This quest is required to complete the following quest(s):

  • None

Abyssal Demon.name: Abyssal Demon
Abyssal Demon.location: Whispering Swamp / Bloodblight Swamp / Fractured Plains
Abyssal Demon.lead: An abyssal demon is a power level 4 mini boss monster that can be found wandering the Whispering Swamp, Fractured Plains and Bloodblight Swamp.
Abyssal Demon.strategy: When fighting an abyssal demon, it will teleport and then attack in quick succession. If fighting with magic, allow for downtime in casting animations to allow for the opportunity to dodge its attacks. In addition, players should seek higher ground whilst fighting the abyssal demon with Ranged or Magic attacks. One of the most effective ways to defeat a abyssal demon is to use fire spells, which causes the demon to lose a lot of HP.
Abyssal Demon.location_html: Although it cannot be consistently found there, there is a rare chance for an abyssal demon to spawn in the north-eastern Fractured Plains.

Black Dragon.name: Black Dragon
Black Dragon.lead: Black dragons, also known as lesser black dragons, are power level 8 dragons that can be found in the Scorned Wilderness raid. There are currently only three black dragon spawns.
Black Dragon.attacks:
• Lunge
  • Tail sweep (if behind them)
  • Fire Claw Slash
  • Poison Blast: The black dragon launches a fire projectile to build up around the three-quarters point.
  • Fire Breath: The black dragon sweeps the area in front of them with their fire breath.
  • Wing Attack: The black dragon flaps its wings, blowing wind at the player, with the second such blast doing damage.
  • Fly: The black dragon can fly into the sky and do a few moves:
    • Fire Breath: The black dragon shoots their breath in a line going away from them. This staggers the player and can easily lock them in to take all of the damage.
Black Dragon.location_html: Within the Scorned Wilderness, they can be found in Dragontail Vines, in the Fragments of Ghornfell, and in The Shattered Stronghold areas.
Black Dragon.journal: If you thought the red dragons were bad, you're in for a rude awakening. The black dragons is a powerhouse of destruction. Every fibre of its being is bred to defend Kuldra and obliterate all threats that get remotely near. Xikotal was the exception. He was a creature of empathy and he struggled with violence that Kuldra made him inflict on the world. When the first of the dragon wars ended, he nestled in with Imaru and the two of them tried to turn tragedy into something beautiful; a gentle utopia, where all life was sacred. This disgusted Kuldra, and she has made sure that none of her black-scaled brood ever suffer the same weakness

Black Knight Guardian.name: Black Knight Guardian
Black Knight Guardian.lead: Black Knight guardians are power level 6 variants of the Black Knight warrior, who wields a shield.
Black Knight Guardian.location_html: Various areas around Dowdun Reach.
Black Knight Guardian.journal: Chaos is an attractive philosophy until you're the one organising guard and patrol rotations. Chaos gains a little asterisk: you need a little organisation to facilitate the chaos. Those on guard rotations know that threats are just as likely to come from within than without. For this reason, veterans would advise the newer knights to glue a mirror to the back of their shield.

Black Knight Sniper.name: Black Knight Sniper
Black Knight Sniper.lead: Black Knight snipers are power level 6 monsters located in Dowdun Reach. When taking too many hits, they will evade back and away from their targets.

Black Knight Titan.name: Black Knight Titan
Black Knight Titan.respawn: Can be respawned by interacting with the symbol in the room
Black Knight Titan.lead: Milliburn Rasmodel, also known as Lord Rasmodel, and the Black Knight Titan is a power level 6 boss monster, released with Dowdun Reach. He is the old commander of the Black Knights within Dowdun Reach, who was resurrected by the Dreaming Stone, and guards the passageway to the Umbral Sands.
Black Knight Titan.journal: The Dreaming Stone had been shattered. Lord Rasmodel, on his knees, heard no voices. For the first time in too, too long, he could hear his own breath. His heart played a welcome beat. For decades, he had felt like he floated above the world. Now he was part of it again. Footsteps. Lord Rasmodel lifted his head wearily. Who would interrupt this moment? Tinging around him was his family. The Rasmodels. They were all there - all the ones he knew, and loved and had met. They were dressed as the finest nobility, the Rasmodels at their height. They had regained their standing - the name meant something again. His father knelt down and lifted Lord Rasmodel's bloody chin. Their eyes met. " Rest," his father said. "We will take it from here." Milliburn Rasmodel, twenty-fifth Lord of Rasmodel, took his retirement.
Black Knight Titan.history:
Milliburn was the eldest son of the Rasmodels' house, a noble house from the mainland, who worshipped Saradomin before rebelling against him. When the Children of Shadows became allied with the family, Milliburn's brother would play pranks on the members who became bodyguards to the nobles. When his father died, he became the head of the house. During his rule, he kept having dreams and visions, which eventually led him to believe that he needed to form the Shadow Knights, believing Imaru, Xikotal, and Fellhollow itself could not be trusted.

After reforming the Children of Shadows into the Black Knights, Milliburn would continue to rule over Dowdun Reach. After the Dragon Rebellion, when Kuldra ordered her dragons to lay waste to the inhabitants of Ashenfall, the Black Knights were able to hold their own against the dragon attacks. Their defences were greatly strengthened thanks to the Dreaming Stone, but it would sow whisper and madness in his and others' minds. After a period of time with the stone, which had caused distrust, Milliburn had decided to destroy it, finally being free of the madness. Before he could do anything else, his family, the Rasmodel house, would appear before him, telling him to rest, that they would take it from here. Now his body remains within the Black Knight's Fortress, controlled by his insanity and unknowingly guarding the way to Umbral Sands.

Black Knight Warrior.name: Black Knight Warrior
Black Knight Warrior.lead: The Black Knight warriors are power level 6 monsters found within Dowdun Reach. They are members of the Black Knights within Dowdun Reach and resides in the Black Knight's Fortress.
Black Knight Warrior.location_html: Various areas around Dowdun Reach.
Black Knight Warrior.journal: Lord Rasmodel rarely entrusted the rookies with any meaningful work. He found that they arrived with chaos in their hearts. They weren't old enough to realise that chaos is an ideal that rarely works in everyday life. So, he would give them the role of "Warriors", and would loosely allocate them an area of the Reach to wander. "Let their cynicism grow," Rasmodel would say. "If the demons or magi don't kill them first, they might harden into one of the good ones."

Blazing Black Knight.name: Blazing Black Knight
Blazing Black Knight.lead: Blazing black knights are power level 6 monsters located in Dowdun Reach. They are a larger variant of the Black Knight Guardian that had an flaming blade that deals Burning build up.

Blightscale.name: Blightscale
Blightscale.lead: Blightscale the lesser green dragon is a power level 5 green dragon located at the south side of the cliffs leading up to the Silverthorn Keep, north-east of the ominous gateway. She is immediately past some willow trees and a small set of ruins. There is a spectral door in the small clearing where he's located. The Binding of Ib is found near some bones in the clearing. Blightscale has the same attacks and drops as a normal green dragon.

Blue Dragon.name: Blue Dragon
Blue Dragon.lead: Blue dragons, also known as lesser blue dragons are power level 6 dragons found in Dowdun Reach. They are said to have lightning-based abilities and drop blue dragon hide upon death.
Blue Dragon.attacks:
• Lunge
  • Tail sweep (if behind them)
  • Electric Claw Slash
  • Lightning Blast: The blue dragon launches a blue lightning projectile to build up around the three-quarters point.
  • Fire Breath: The blue dragon sweeps the area in front of them with their fire breath.
  • Wing Attack: The blue dragon flaps its wings, blowing wind at the player, with the second such blast doing damage.
  • Fly: The blue dragon can fly into the sky and do a few moves:
    • Fire Breath: The blue dragon shoots their breath in a line going away from them. This staggers the player and can easily lock them to take all of the damage.
    • Flame Whirlwind: After a short wind-up, the blue dragon creates a whirlwind of fire below them as they fly into the air. When they come back down, the whirlwind disappears.
    • Lightning Surge: The blue dragon will unleash a surge of electrical energy twice; the second time will expand reach.

Boggs.name: Boggs
Boggs.lead: Boggs is a power level 6 monster that appears with Rat Master Skrexis in The Menagerie.

Buddy.name: Buddy
Buddy.resistance: Crush, Slash, Stab, Range, Air, Water
Buddy.lead: Buddy is a power level 7 summonable kalphite that can be summoned with the pharaoh's sceptre and help players fight against enemies. Buddy can be up for up to 3 minutes as long as it is still alive, and will take another five minutes for it to respawn when recasting the sceptre's special attack.

Carnivorous Chinchompa.name: Carnivorous Chinchompa
Carnivorous Chinchompa.lead: Carnivorous chinchompas are power level 5 monsters located within Dowdun Reach. Like their variants, they explode when in close range.

Chicken.name: Chicken
Chicken.location: Temple Woods, Bramblemead Valley, Dowdun Reach
Chicken.lead: Chickens are power level 1 creatures found in the Temple Woods, Bramblemead Valley, and Dowdun Reach. They are generally passive until you walk into them, provoking them. These creatures are one of the weakest creatures in the game, dealing 7 damage to an unarmoured player.

Chinchompa.name: Chinchompa
Chinchompa.lead: Chinchompas are power level 3 NPCs that will explode upon death.

Corrupted Raven.name: Corrupted Raven
Corrupted Raven.lead: Corrupted ravens are power level 1 birds located in Dowdun Reach, dropping corrupted essence samples for the Biohazard quest. Note that players must kill these corrupted ravens directly and not use Confuse on other monsters, killing these ravens.

Cow.name: Cow
Cow.lead: Cows are power level 2 creatures that roam around Bramblemead Valley and Dowdun Reach. Their damage to an unarmoured player is fairly high at 34.

Curly.name: Curly
Curly.lead: Curly is a power level 6 monster that appears with Rat Master Skrexis in The Menagerie.

Deer.name: Deer
Deer.lead: Deer are power level 1 and 5 creatures that are non-aggressive and too fast to keep up with on foot; they should be killed via ranged or magic attacks. Deer can be alerted and will flee if the player is within 50 metres, and/or if a monster within 50 metres is hit with either ranged or magic attacks.

Delrom.name: Delrom
Delrom.lead: Delrom is a power level 6 lesser demon located under Dowdun Reach, near The Lake.

Desert Devil Kebbit.name: Desert Devil Kebbit
Desert Devil Kebbit.lead: Desert devil kebbits are power level 1 and 7 monsters that are located around Umbral Sands and in Rasthin's Rest. Like their previous counterpart, these kebbit are only aggressive if players bump into them or attack them.
Desert Devil Kebbit.journal: The kebbit of the sands have a strange name, one that implies a connection to the fiery realm of Infernus. This is, weirdly, not actually that far from the truth, because the desert devil is not native to the Umbral Sands, but rather the result of poor security at Dowdun Reach.

Dire Wolf.name: Dire Wolf
Dire Wolf.lead: Dire wolves are power level 3 monsters, found in Fractured Plains and Stormtouched Highlands. Despite not having power level 4 variants, the dire wolf has exceedingly high health for its level. Each attack from the dire wolf will build the Bleed debuff to about 70-75%, which will cause the player to lose up to 32 damage if the Bleed debuff bar is filled.

Dragon Hatchling.name: Dragon Hatchling
Dragon Hatchling.lead: Dragons hatchlings, are power level 8 dragons that can be found in Kuldra boss encounter in the the Scorned Wilderness. They are are like their regular counterparts in combat, with the difference being that killing one will infuse the players in either water anima (blue) or fire anima (red).

Dragon Wolf.name: Dragon Wolf
Dragon Wolf.lead: Dragon wolves are level 5 aggressive NPCs in Ashenfall, located within the region of Fellhollow. They are the product of a dragonkin hybridisation experiment that crossed dire wolves with dragons.
Dragon Wolf.attacks:
• Lunge: The dragon wolf lunges at the player.
  • Breathe Fire: After a wind up with blue flame in their mouth, the dragon wolf breathes fire onto the player.
Dragon Wolf.journal: The unholy fusion of dragon and beast, creations of twisted dragonkin science. These creatures seem somehow resistant to the cursed nature of the region, but they refuse to sit still long enough for anyone to ask them why. Not that they would answer, they have a wolf's mind, not a dragons.

Elite Black Knight.name: Elite Black Knight
Elite Black Knight.lead: Elite Black Knights are power level 6 monsters located in Dowdun Reach. They are elite members of the Black Knights. They are either alone, with another elite Black Knight or with a few hellhound
Elite Black Knight.location_html: Various areas around Dowdun Reach.
Elite Black Knight.journal: Chaos is an attractive philosophy until you're the one organising guard and patrol rotations. Chaos gains a little asterisk: you need a little organisation to facilitate the chaos. Those on guard rotation know that threats are just as likely to come from within than without. For this reason, veterans would advise newer knights to glue mirror to the back of their shield.

Fido.name: Fido
Fido.lead: Fido is a power level 6 monster that appears with Houndmaster Rexiton under The Garrison.

Fuzan.name: Fuzan
Fuzan.lead: Fuzan is a giant red dragon and one of Kuldra's youngest generals and also the fiercest. Fuzan rules over the Umbral Sands, using the Lens from the KotHaar to make the desert unbearable to walk through the day. To reach him, players must do the Icthlarin's Little Helper quest, where they will be led to Fuzan's trial.
Fuzan.journal: Youngest of Kuldra's brood, Fuzan grew up spoilt and childish. Where other dragons sought strategy, family, or some loftier goal, Fuzan only cared about the next dopamine hit brought on by mindless destruction. We've all seen kids like that. As he grew older, he began to seek experience in more dangerous places. He picked fights with other dragons. Bullied the monsters roaming the lands. he brought chaos everywhere he went, in hopes that it might mildly alleviate some of his boredom. In the heart of a volcano, as he gazed into the purest fires, he found something other than amusement to cling onto. he found faith. Faith in a being not of this world: born of celestial fire so bright that it made Fuzan's own mighty flames seem like a mere candlelight in comparison. This being spoke through flames. In her words, were flickering embers. Her laughter the cackle of flames. Her platitudes swirled in the air, carried aloft by ashes. She claimed to be a god, and she promised him that Fuzan would burn hotter, shine brighter, and ignite the world under his own light - rather then spend his life in his mother's shadow. It was an offer too enticing to refuse. Under her Tutelage, Fuzan learned to better wield his own flames and the flames of others. He seized control of the gentle KotHaar and he began marking the garou, igniting their souls as kindling and taking their strength for his own. It is better that he is dead. For everyone's sake.
Fuzan.history:
Finding Purpose

Fuzan was one of Kuldra's children, the youngest and fiercest among them. He grew up spoiled, usually seen as a troublemaker who enjoyed mindless violence. When Kuldra overthrew the dragonkin, Fuzan became one of her chosen generals; the other being Velgar. After laying waste to the human settlements, Fuzan would often find himself bored, usually travelling around Ashenfall to bully other creatures roaming the wilds and picking fights with other dragons. He would often gaze into the flames of The Burning Spire when bored. One day, something gazed back at him - an entity who claimed to be a Goddess would reveal herself to Fuzan, who noted how her celestial flames were brighter than his. The self-called goddess would then offer Fuzan more power so that his flames could burn hotter, shine brighter and ignite the world under his own light so that he wouldn't need to spend his life in his mother's shadow. Convinced by the promise of power, Fuzan would then worship the deity and, under her banner, he learned to better wield the flames - be those his or other's.

Terrorizing Umbral Sands

Fuzan would then head towards Umbral Sands, where he would attack the Moon Garou settlements, forcing them to hide within the shadows. Some who survived an encounter with him would tell the tale of his attacks. After some attacks, Fuzan would go to a empty area of Umbral Sands and pray to the goddess who had taught him the means to control the flames as he wanted. Eventually, he found the KotHaar, and the device they were guarding, the Lens. With his newfound power, he would take control of the Lens, and in turn, the KotHaar. He would then use the KotHaar to move the Lens to his tower, so that he could use it and increase the suns' heat over the desert, making it harder for the garou to be able to roam it freely He would also mark them, igniting their souls and taking their strength for his own.. Even at night, he'll hunt any prey down with some red dragons. Sometime, would force the KotHaar to fight each other, enjoying the violence they commit to each other. Sometime later, Dearg Due would be cursed by Fuzan.

Sixth Age

Centuries after the , with Fuzan continued torment over the garou in Umbral Sands. Velgar and Fuzan, with a legion of dragons, attacks ships that were attempting to come to Ashenfall. Returning to Umbral Sands, Fuzan would continue to terrorize the inhabitant, until some Adventurer(s) would arrive to his territory. With the help of Icthlarin, and the three garou tribes united, the Adventurer(s) would make their way to Fuzan, slaying them and freeing Umbral Sands from their cruelty.

Garou Berserker.name: Garou Berserker
Garou Berserker.lead: Garou berserkers are power level 3, 4 and 8 monsters found within Ghornfell and the Scorned Wilderness raid

Garou Druid.name: Garou Druid
Garou Druid.location: Fractured Plains / Bloodblight Swamp / Stormtouched Highlands / Druid's Cave in the Whispering Swamp
Garou Druid.xp:
Power level 3
  Melee 97
  Magic 74
  Ranged 74
Power level 4
  Melee 134
  Magic 102
  Ranged 102
Garou Druid.lead: Garou druids are power level 3 or 4 monsters. They are highborn garou gifted with the ability to cast spells. According to the garou berserker journal entry, druids exert subtle magical influence over berserkers, manipulating their perception to recognise the druids and their allies as comrades rather than foes.
Garou Druid.strategy: Players are recommended to drink an antipoison potion before attacking a garou druid. The poisoned magic dart is among the most dangerous abilities in a druid’s arsenal, dealing both physical and poison damage. The most effective way to defeat a druid is to quickly close the distance, thereby limiting their attacks to the poison field, which can be easily avoided. Another strategy is to engage them from long range, using powerful ranged or magic to strike from a distance. Avoiding their poisoned dart is strongly advised; with careful timing, the projectile can be completely evaded. When facing a group of garou, it is advisable to prioritise eliminating the druid first, as their healing magic will otherwise prolong the fight.

Garou Exile.name: Garou Exile
Garou Exile.lead: A Garou Exile is a Power level 3 monster located in the Ghornfell region of Ashenfall. They are a variant of the Garou Berserker, but instead are alone or in a group and use daggers to attack. Some attacks do hit heavy, causing players to stagger a bit.

Garou Hunter.name: Garou Hunter
Garou Hunter.lead: Garou hunters are power level 3 or 4 monsters who can attack from up to 30 metres away and will occasionally kneel and prepare a special attack that can hit and inflict the Bleed debuff on the player.

Garou King.name: Garou King
Garou King.lead: The Garou King is a power level 5 mini-boss monster located at the Highlands Castle.
Garou King.journal: Those who complete the rite of the moon, and usurp their leaders, become the kings of the garou. The title of king is gender-neutral, and kings of all genders are recorded across garou history. This is because the mantle of queen has belonged to only two beings: Lougrim and her devourer. When Lougrim first visited the world of the garou, a place known as Antumnos, she was treated as prey. Her hunters were no match for a goddess, of course, and she assumed the forms of powerful predators, forcing them into submission. She fell upon the capital of the garou nation, the city of Magrawn, where she called out a challenge to all the reigning kings of the garou clans. They answered the summons and she defeated each of them together in a single, decisive, battle. From then on, she held the mantle of High Queen of the garou. A title she held until Kuldra devoured her, earning the dragon queen her moniker: God Eater.

Garou Thane.name: Garou Thane
Garou Thane.lead: Garou thanes are power level 3, 4 and 8 monsters with a large tower shield to protect themselves. When attacked, they will block all attacks until their stance is broken, staggering them for three seconds. Their stance breaks after three seconds, and they will attack and be immune to getting staggered.

Ghost Wolf.name: Ghost Wolf
Ghost Wolf.lead: Ghost wolves are power level 4 aggressive NPCs in Fellhollow, encountered if the player entered the soul rift. They have a similar moves to dragon wolves.

Giant Rat.name: Giant Rat
Giant Rat.lead: Giant rats are power level 1-5 creatures found in a variety of areas within Temple Woods, Bramblemead Valley, Fractured Plains and certain dragonkin vaults.

Gnasher.name: Gnasher
Gnasher.lead: Gnasher is a power level 6 monster that appears with Houndmaster Rexiton under The Garrison.

Goat.name: Goat
Goat.lead: Goat are power level 7 creatures found in Umbral Sands.
Goat.journal: Goats should have thrived all over Ashenfall, and yet they seem to have migrated exclusively to the desert. It’s strange, because they aren’t really well suited to the region. They have thick fur, so overheat easily. Their little feet sink into the sand, and quicksand devours a great many of them every day. Yet, no matter how hard you explain to the goats of Ashenfall that they’d enjoy much happier lives elsewhere, the Umbral Sands is where they choose to stay. There is no reason for this. Trust us, we’ve asked. Still, over the years, where they’ve failed to adapt physiologically, they’ve adapted mentally and socially. There are few creatures as stubborn as a goat. They are utterly unwilling to back down from a dangerous area, preferring to power through no matter what the cost. There’s probably some life lesson or metaphor in there, but I’m not sure it’s one worth learning.

Goblin Archer.name: Goblin Archer
Goblin Archer.lead: Goblin archers are power level 2, 6 and 8 monsters located in Brynmoor, Dowdun Reach and the Scorned Wilderness raid.

Goblin Bruiser.name: Goblin Bruiser
Goblin Bruiser.location: Bramblemead Valley, Whispering Swamp, Dowdun Reach
Goblin Bruiser.lead: Goblin bruisers are power level 2, 6 and 8 monsters located in Brynmoor, Dowdun Reach. and the Scorned Wilderness raid.
Goblin Bruiser.location_html: Various areas around Bramblemead Valley and Whispering Swamp.
Goblin Bruiser.journal: The leaders of the goblin tribes by strength alone, the bruisers enjoy nothing more than a life of bullying other goblins around. They are assumed to be the smartest, because if you tell them they’re wrong, you’ll get a fist in the face. They’re the most charismatic, because if you don’t like what they’re saying… well… fist and face return once more. In fact most of their skillset consists of fists approaching faces at high velocity. They are one of the few goblins with brains enough to wedge a large sheet of metal between their vulnerable internal organs and the person poking at them with a sharp object. So in goblin society that makes them an unrivalled genius.

Goblin Poisonshot Archer.name: Goblin Poisonshot Archer
Goblin Poisonshot Archer.lead: A goblin poisonshot archer is a Power level 2 and 3 variant of a Goblin Archer, where they will fire poison arrows at the players, and do a three shot combo as well.

Goblin Runt.name: Goblin Runt
Goblin Runt.lead: Goblin runts areare power level 1, 3 and 6 monsters located in Brynmoor, Bloodblight Swamp and Dowdun Reach

Goblin Warrior.name: Goblin Warrior
Goblin Warrior.lead: Goblin warriors are power level 2, 6 and 8 monsters located in Brynmoor, Dowdun Reach and Scorned Wilderness

Green Dragon.name: Green Dragon
Green Dragon.lead: Green dragons also known as lesser green dragons are Dragons found in Fellhollow. They are monsters that can be found and fought in Emberwood, Dragon's Run, Hope's Fall and Silverthorn Keep.
Green Dragon.attacks:
• Lunge
  • Tail Sweep (if behind them)
  • Claw Slash
  • Poison Spit: The green dragon launches a green poison projectile to build up around the three-quarters point.
  • Fire Breath: The green dragon sweeps the area in front of them with their fire breath.
  • Wing Attack: The green dragon flaps its wings, blowing wind at the player, with the second such blast doing damage.
  • Fly: The green dragon can fly into the sky and do a few moves:
    • Fire Breath: The green dragon shoots their breath in a line going away from them. This staggers the player and can easily lock them to take all of the damage.
    • Flame Whirlwind: After a short wind-up, the green dragon creates a whirlwind of fire below them as they fly into the air. When they come back down, the whirlwind disappears.
Green Dragon.journal: Lesser green dragons are weaker than the generals, but that doesn’t make them easy to defeat. Their cruelty is almost as great as Velgar’s, but they fortunately lack the ambition and tactical thinking that would elevate their threat to greater heights.

Gyrfalcon.name: Gyrfalcon
Gyrfalcon.lead: Gyrfalcons are power level 1 non-aggressive birds that can be found exclusively in the Stormtouched Highlands. Like magpies, they will fly away if you get too close to them.
Gyrfalcon.journal: The gyrfalcon is an agile predator. They silently dart through the air, seeking out small game to hunt. Giant rats are their favourite prey, though their flesh is stringy, they are comparatively large meals, compared to the kebbits and voles of the region. Some Wild Knights would forge bonds with the falcons. They’re raise them from eggs and carefully train them to assist with scouting and hunting. This symbiotic relationship would allow both hunter and falcon to thrive in Ashenfall’s dangerous environment.

Heartworm.name: Heartworm
Heartworm.lead: Heartworms are parasitic minions encountered inside Kuldra during Phase 4 of the Scorned Wilderness Raid.

Hellhound.name: Hellhound
Hellhound.lead: Hellhounds are power level 6 monsters located in Dowdun Reach.

Hellrat.name: Hellrat
Hellrat.lead: Hellrats are power level 6 monsters located in Dowdun Reach.
Hellrat.location_html: Note; Location are accurate, but they do not tell you they are underground, so if they do not appear there in-game, look for a underground passage.

Houndmaster Rexiton.name: Houndmaster Rexiton
Houndmaster Rexiton.lead: Houndmaster Rexiton is a power level 6 variant of the Black Knight guardian. He is located under Dowdun Reach within The Garrison.
Houndmaster Rexiton.journal: Houndmaster Rexiton doesn't realise the power that he wields. If he wanted to, he could trigger a huge power-shift in Dowdun Reach. The hellhounds obey his voice. His key, and his key only, turns in their locks each night. With a pointed word or a neglectful thought, he could cause chaos. Rexiton would never turn on the Reach because, at heart, he is a devout romantic. It's a combination that Lord Rasmodel noticed quickly and capitalised on. Rexiton was devout to both Zamorak and the Reach. He was an idealist who believed that Dowdun could become the centre of Gielinor. With Zamorak in the ascendance, and Dowdun so heavily fortified, he earnestly believed it could become the capital of the known world. Rexiton also wanted nothing more than for everyone to get along. The rifts of Dowdun Reach were seen as temporary to him. If he could form a bond with a hellhound, then the world could drop its squabbles and come together in peace. Lord Rasmodel couldn't think of a more lovable idiot to be in charge of one of the Reach's most formidable weapons.

Imaru.name: Imaru
Imaru.lead: Imaru the Soul-Eater is an undead blue dragon infused with the wild anima of Ashenfall and the energy of the by drinking from the . She was one of Kuldra's generals, who rules over Fellhollow, a boss monster who was introduced with the 0.10 update.
Imaru.journal: Once, Imaru was a gentle creature. She and her mate, the black dragon Xikotal, would dance through the air together, lost in their love. Although the dragon's rage still burned inside her, the cooling power of the water she was infused with, calmed herand brought the reason and clarify that she enjoyed Dragonkin experiments had robbed her of the one thing she craves, to be a mother. So when the humans came to the region, she convinced Xikotal that they should take them under their wing, becoming protectors and, perhaps, even parents to the fragile things. Together, they built a society with peace and cooperation at its core. The villagers thrived, and Imaru and her mate thrived with them. She used magic within her to bless her new pets, making sure that she could protect them wherever they were How cruel a thing is fate? once protector, Imaru became the threat. After being slain by Kuldra, Imaru became a blighted thing. She refused to pass into the afterlife and wedged herself within the river of souls, feasting on the dead of Fellhollow in search of power. Once the guardian of her beloved adopted children, Imaru was lost to everything but the rage and grief. She would have torn apart the world for one more shot at Kuldra. Fortunately, that won't be an option.
Imaru.history:
Early life

Like all other dragons in Ashenfall, Imaru was created by the dragonkin. Imaru was a water dragon, infused with water magic by the dragonkin who created her. Though the rage characteristic of her kind burned within her, her elemental nature tempered it, granting her the reason and clarity that would define her disposition. The dragonkin's experiments had denied her the ability to bear offspring, the one thing she desired above all else.

She and her mate, Xikotal, settled within the region of Fellhollow. When human settlers found their way to the region, it was Imaru who persuaded Xikotal that they should take the settlers under their protection, seeing in the fragile humans the children she could never have. The two dragons at first kept their distance from the settlers, but later befriended them. Imaru and Xikotal helped their new friends build cities, farmland, and control the weather. Those whom she and Xikotal protected were given a blessing, an enchantment woven over each of the settlers. She also appointed guards to protect her and Xikotal when they went into long torpors.

After the Dragon Rebellion, Kuldra had issued an extermination order against the human settlements in Ashenfall, minus a few. She took notice of Imaru's and Xikotal's mercy. Finding this a betrayal, she descended onto the region to handle it herself. Imaru and Xikotal denied Kuldra, rejecting her demands and rising against her, and the humans rose with them. But even with numbers on their side, Kuldra proved too powerful. Imaru witnessed her mate's heart ripped from his chest and devoured by Kuldra. Instead of killing Imaru, Kuldra left her to her grief, considering this punishment enough for disobeying her.

Imaru sought out Ravanna, a sorcerer who had practised in the magical arts, including necromancy. She begged for her beloved back, but Ravanna declined, as she was not powerful enough to reanimate things to that degree. Instead, she offered a different solution: a curse to allow Imaru to take vengeance on Kuldra. Ravanna bestowed a curse that would turn Imaru's grief into power, a blade intended for the Godeater.

Armed with the curse, Imaru attacked Kuldra a second time. Witnesses described a battle of catastrophic force, the land itself weaponised as the two dragons tore at one another. The curse had changed her; her grief and rage had been forged into something that shook even Kuldra's armour. As Imaru pressed the attack, the Blessing began drawing strength from the villagers themselves, leaving those who bore it weakened. Despite everything, Kuldra proved too powerful and killed her. However, due to the very curse put on her, Imaru did not give up. She instead wedged herself, preventing herself from moving on drinking from the River Noumenon and clawed her way out of the underworld, resurrecting herself to continue her vengeance, though that came with a cost: corruption. Imaru caused the river to become blocked, with its waters beginning to leak into the surface of Fellhollow. This gave her a hunger for souls. She gave into it, feasting on those she had sworn to protect and turning them into undead. Soon this rot began spreading further, and even those who had not been blessed began becoming undead, as the necrotic magic infected those bitten.

With Imaru continuing to consume the souls of Fellhollow, her strength grew. Fellhollow became a place of rot and ruin, with undead ruling the region. In her guilt, Ravanna attempted to fix her mistake. Knowing that Imaru would never stop consuming souls, she decided to seal her in the tower to prevent her from spreading to the rest of Ashenfall and Gielinor. After successfully locking her away, she separated the essence of Imaru's curse into three fragments and spread them across Fellhollow, in hope that someone more skilled and powerful than herself would one day use the very curse against Imaru.

Sixth Age

In the Sixth Age, Death would recruit some Adventurer(s) to enter Fellhollow, where they would work with Cathan and search for the curse fragments to confront Imaru. Despite being sealed within her tower, she is was still able to use her specter form to command the tormented souls and ghost wolves to attacking them when they are Soul Rifted, as well as appearing when she grows impatient. After gathering the fragments and removing the seal, the Adventurer(s) confront Imaru, empowered with the same curse, and defeated her, ending her reign in Fellhollow, putting all the souls to rest.

Kalphite Guardian.name: Kalphite Guardian
Kalphite Guardian.resistance: Crush, Slash, Stab, Range, Air, Water
Kalphite Guardian.lead: Kalphite guardians are a larger defensive variant of kalphites in Umbral Sands, and will periodically change to red, blue, and green shades, making them immune to melee, magic, and ranged damage, respectively.
Kalphite Guardian.location_html: Some kalphite guardians only spawn at night.
Kalphite Guardian.journal: The queen is all that matters. Protect the queen at all costs. Those are the only thoughts within the guardian - the only drive, the only reason for living. All their energies, every cell in their bodies, fixated on that singular command. Perhaps this is why they fight with such fervour. When your entire existence is reduced to a single focus, a single command, everything must get a little frustrating. The kalphite do not aspire, they do not dream. They have their place in the hive and they accept it completely. Avisk was fascinated by this. As one of the Aughra, he was always obsessed with the mind and the potential within it. Whereas the other Aughra sought to escape the curse by transferring their consciousness to a single new body, Avisk dreamed of becoming the swarm. The kalphite fascinated him. He saw them as a single entity comprised of multiple individual moving parts and the potential of that structure became his new obsession. When he stole some of the royal eggs from the Kharidian Desert’s hive, he was forced to battle several guardians who were protecting the nest. While they were no match for the power of a dragonkin, they nonetheless earned what passes for Avisk’s respect and he made sure to encourage his new queen to create as many guardians as possible so he could study them further.

Kalphite Queen.name: Kalphite Queen
Kalphite Queen.immune: Can be immune to any attack style.
Kalphite Queen.lead: Kalphite queens are the ruling heart of kalphite hives in the Umbral Sands, creating soldiers, workers, and guardians as needed to ensure the hive survives and thrives.
Kalphite Queen.journal: Power corrupts, and absolute power corrupts absolutely. It is such a human concept, born out of our own selfishness. We see power as a path to cruelty; seeing too many people who abuse that power for their own personal gain. The insect does not think like this. The hive is the power, the control and the source of all that matters to the kalphite. At the heart of the hive sits the queen, the source of all kalphite life in the hive. She creates soldiers, workers, guardians - whatever the hive requires. She does not do so for personal glory, nor wealth, nor control. She does it so that the hive can thrive. Absolute power, zero corruption. The queens in Ashenfall were stolen from the Kharidian hives by the dragonkin Avisk, who wanted to study their insect minds in the hope that he could graft himself onto them, becoming the hive. He wanted absolute power, but it would have led to absolute corruption.

Kalphite Soldier.name: Kalphite Soldier
Kalphite Soldier.resistance: Crush, Slash, Stab, Range, Air, Water
Kalphite Soldier.lead: Kalphite soldiers are a militant variant of kalphite native to the Umbral Sands region, bred specifically to defend their hive. A Kalphite Queen creates them by ingesting adamantite ore and infusing its chemical compounds into a developing larva as she lays her eggs.
Kalphite Soldier.location_html: Some kalphite soldiers only spawn at night.
Kalphite Soldier.journal: There are many people who argue that the military is “in their blood”, and aside from those who were part of secret, medical conspiracy theories, this is not a biological truth. While you can dedicate your life to the military machine, it is a choice, not a certainty. For the kalphite soldier it is a literal reality. They have the military in their blood. Their very genetic structure is designed with the singular purpose – battle. They are pure warriors, with minds that think of nothing else other than the defence of the hive. The queen creates the soldier with intent. When she lays her eggs, she releases certain chemicals harvested from ingested metal ore, in this case adamantite, and it bonds with the growing larvae, becoming something stronger. That is why the soldiers' shells are harder and their mandibles more dangerous, because they are forged in the embryonic sac to be killers.

Kalphite Worker.name: Kalphite Worker
Kalphite Worker.resistance: Crush, Slash, Stab, Range, Air, Water
Kalphite Worker.lead: Kalphite workers are the lowest caste of kalphite, tasked with gathering food, harvesting materials, and constructing and expanding the hive for the queen. While each kalphite possesses its own complex nervous system, but also shares in a broader hive intelligence built from scent signals and sound. Workers are weaker than soldiers, but will still defend their hive fiercely if threatened, even at the cost of their own lives.
Kalphite Worker.location_html: Some kalphite workers only spawn at night.
Kalphite Worker.journal: You could easily mistake the kalphite worker for a dumb bug, and for the most part you’d be right. But, that’s only because you are thinking with a human mind, one comprised of neurons and hard-wired for self-preservation. The kalphite mind is a different beast entirely. Whilst they are individual entities, with their own complex set of neurons, axons and other complicated sciency sounding words, their consciousness is also a collection of pheromone trails, high-frequency chittering, and the strange sort of nonsense only insects understand. The result is an individual that is connected to a great whole. Like an arm that can think by itself… which is a horrible thought - let’s not dwell on it. The worker is the lowest caste of the kalphites, though it’s not really a status thing. Their entire existence is to gather food, harvest materials, and construct bigger and better hives for the queen’s delectation. Unfortunately, that does not mean they won’t attack you if you threaten their hive. They will with as much vigour as they can manage. They care little for themselves: only the hive matters, and they will defend it with their lives.

Karibdos.name: Karibdos
Karibdos.history:
Long before the dwarves arrived in Ashenfall, an ancient and monstrous creature lay dormant beneath the Umbral Sands, something that by any reasonable account simply shouldn't exist. When a dwarven expedition came upon the region's deposits of adamant and other treasures, their approach roused the slumbering beast, and it surged up in an attempt to swallow the entire party in a single strike. Karibdos attacked by drawing its prey into a churning vortex of sand, and several explorers were lost to it before the rest could escape. The survivors' weapons couldn't pierce its hide, and the beast withdrew to its slumber to wait for another chance.

With Karibdos barring the only way forward, the expedition turned back armed with adamant whose true strength had only just been discovered. When it struck again, its teeth shattered against their armour and its hide tore apart under their blades where nothing else had succeeded. No trace of a creature like Karibdos has surfaced in Ashenfall since its death, though some who live in the desert suspect that's only because no one has dug deep enough to find another.

Kebbit.name: Kebbit
Kebbit.lead: Kebbits are a power level 1 animal that resides near kebbit burrows throughout Ashenfall, and are passive creatures unless attacked. As these are the weakest creatures in the game, they deal 15 damage to an unarmoured player.

KotHaar-Hur.name: KotHaar-Hur
KotHaar-Hur.lead: KotHaar-Hur are a power level 7 monsters that are found throughout Umbral Sands. KotHaar-Hur are unarmed and do not have special attacks, but can deal a significant amount of damage with power level 6 armour or less. The following is their attack set:
KotHaar-Hur.journal: There are few beings on all of Gielinor as strange as the KotHaar. They, like their distant cousins the TzHaar, were once members of the TokHaar race, but long ago split from the hive mind to serve a different function: protecting the Lens. Each of the KotHaar is an individual, yet they do not see themselves as a separate organism from one another. They function something like an insect hive, each of the KotHaar fulfilling a specific function, so that the greater community can exist. They have no leaders. No politics. No selfish desires. They exist for one another: a perfect, cohesive whole. Or they did. Fuzan put an end to that. The KotHaar-Hur are workers. Once, they served as the backbone of KotHaar society. They lifted the rocks, they carved out underground tunnels. They are the glue that kept a secret society of obsidian creatures together. Now, the magma that animates them has been turned against them by Fuzan’s Mark, and the KotHaar-Hur turn from labourers to cannon fodder in Fuzan’s twisted games.

KotHaar-Kal.name: KotHaar-Kal
KotHaar-Kal.lead: The KotHaar-Kal are KotHaar monsters found in Umbral Sands. Some appear mainly at night, and will use the following attacks:
KotHaar-Kal.journal: In most societies, the strongest emerge either from training, or natural advantage of birth. For the KotHaar, the strongest are made to be the strongest and to stand as defender for the rest of the community. There is no jealousy over this role. No ambition among the KotHaar to strive to be stronger, faster, better. They know their place and they know that all other members of their society work together to achieve a perfect, harmonious, goal. Or, they did. It was, ironically, the KotHaar-Kal who first fell to Fuzan’s corruption. The dragon saw them and admired the battle prowess and studied them carefully over many days. He saw the way the fire danced within them, like blood vessels… or, in his mind, like strings. Using the mastery over fire that his mother had gifted him, Fuzan seized control of those strings and made the KotHaar-Kal dance to his tune. With such powerful soldiers under his command, it was a small thing to overpower the other KotHaar and force them into his service as well. The other KotHaar were confused at the seeming betrayal of the Kal, but could not comprehend that they might be acting in a way other than their purpose, so they marched toward Fuzan’s embrace without ever stopping to wonder why.

KotHaar-Ket.name: KotHaar-Ket
KotHaar-Ket.lead: KotHaar-Ket is found in Umbral Sands. At below 50% health, they will put up a fire shield that blocks all attacks and then explodes after a short time; however, this can be broken with water damage. The KotHaar-Ket has three types of attacks:
KotHaar-Ket.journal: Whereas the KotHaar-Hur are beasts of burden to the KotHaar community, the KotHaar-Ket are builders, crafters and warriors. They wield great obsidian hammers to shatter rock, pummel stone into shape and to crack the skulls of any foolish creature that might think to endanger KotHaar society. When Fuzan’s power seized control of these creatures, he focused only on their violent role. The dragon delights in watching these hammers smash the bones of any that might stand against him. He has no plan to build cities. No desire to craft wonders. He seeks only to rend everything down to dust, so that his sands might bury the world.

KotHaar-Xil.name: KotHaar-Xil
KotHaar-Xil.lead: The KotHaar-Xil are KotHaar monsters that are found in Umbral Sands.
KotHaar-Xil.journal: Not all threats stay up close and personal. This, the KotHaar learned early on in their existence, so they created the KotHaar-XIl caste to handle more distant threats. Their accuracy is terrifying and they hurl their weapons with such force that it could tear through any armour. In times gone by, they would stand for days on end, at key points around the entrances to their tunnels. Here they would tirelessly keep vigil, never wavering, never getting bored, focused exclusively on protecting the Lens from any that would do it harm, or seek to gain it. Only now do they waver in their task, bound as they are by Fuzan’s will. If you watch them carefully, you might spot their eyes glancing toward Fuzan’s tower, still dedicated to protecting the Lens from danger. Even if Fuzan puppets their actions, the core of their being still sticks to its task.

Kuldra.name: Kuldra
Kuldra.respawn: Entering the Dragon Gate in Kuldra's Sanctum.
Kuldra.lead: Queen Kuldra, also known as the Dragon Queen and the God Eater, is an ancient black dragon with five heads. She is the leader of the dragons ruling over the continent of Ashenfall, and the current High Queen for some of the garou. She is the boss of the Scorned Wilderness raid, and the final boss for Kuldra's Saga.
Kuldra.journal: Kuldra's tale is tragic really. An innocent child, raised by monsters: tormented, tortured, and forced to create legions of children who were all taken from her and then either weaponised or dissected for future study. She found comfort in the gentle warmth of a lover's embrace, only to see him taken from her by those same cruel parents. Only one dragonkin ever showed her warmth, but their mind was distracted by thousand different timestreams and they could never give Kuldra the love that she deserved. A lack of love is like a poison: it seeps into one's soul and infects it with malice. You find yourself unable to believe that love could be real, and from it all the other positive emotions, such as charity, kindness, or hope. Kuldra wasn't born a monster, but she chose to become one and she was determined to be the worst monster she could be. For centuries she has gorged herself on the anima of Ashenfall, building her own power so that she might turn the region's wellspring into a weapon that would decimate the rest of the world. Why? Because the rest of the world is happy, and she needs to see that stopped. Now, she is dead - although her legacy will scar the world for generations to come. Hate breeds only hate, and Kuldra has had plenty of children.
Kuldra.history:
Creation

Kuldra was amongst the first dragons created by the dragonkin Lacrussa and Avisk. When Lacrussa was working on making a better race of dragons, Avisk would force himself into her experiments and suggesting to fuse certain dragons for a better results. He would mess with some of the brood, adding rune essence into the them. Despite Lacrussa's warning in trying to maintain a single headed dragons, Avisk ignored her, which led to several of these brood to die, all but one. Kuldra was born showing no signs of madness for having multiple minds. Instead she found that it would work as one, unified in a way. Lacrussa learns that the dragon was able to spread the rage across herself, weakening the effect, causing her to express other emotion and behaviours, such as curiosity, reason and even wit. This would make Lacrussa want to study her further, keeping her chained. During the study, they would get her off springs and conduct several experiments on them, exterminating the failures. Kuldra would witness this, and slowly plot her vengeance.

Dragon Rebellion

After the Human-Garou War, the goddess Lougrim donated her blood to the dragonkin for their assistance against the human and bandosians. Lacrussa would use this on Kuldra. After gaining Lougrim's blood, she would plot a rebellion against the dragonkin after seeing the continued abuse, despite their assistance in the war. At first, she was hesitant, but it was Velgar who convinced her and was the first to join her cause. When the rebellion started, Lacrussa was slain, along with Brakka, from whom Kuldra stole powers for herself and shared them with Velgar, her most trusted ally, granting him his elemental mastery of earth. Before she could kill Rasthin, the dragonkin, activated the Harmonic Resonator in hope to destroy Kuldra, only for the Dragon Queen to survive. In a battle that fractured the continent itself, Kuldra then attacked Lougrim, who was protecting the garou village. Weak and wounded, Kuldra descended on her without mercy and devouring her body and taking her title of High Queen of the Garou. Some accepted out of fear, but others rejected her rule and left to another region. Having freed her fellow dragons, she sent them out across the continent to wipe out other settlements, other than the garou and goblins.

Sometime during these events, Kuldra caught wind of Imaru's and Xikotal's mercy towards the human settlements in Fellhollow, and as a result, she decided to confront the duo herself. As Kuldra descended on the region, nobles within the region would arm themselves in steel equipment to assist Xikotal and Imaru, in the hope of defending their new home and bring an end to the Dragon Queen. Despite the help and numbers, they failed to bring Kuldra down. With Kuldra's strength and power seemingly unmatched, she would pull Xikotal's heart from his chest and devour it. She would then leave Imaru to grieve, as punishment for disobeying her. However, Imaru would challenge Kuldra a second time, after being infused by a curse placed by Ravanna. However, this was not enough to even stand a chance against Kuldra, who killed her quite easily. Despite Imaru's action, Kuldra had left the humans of Fellhollow alone, their fate met by the resurrected corpse of Imaru some time later.

With Ashenfall settlement destroyed, minus some of the garou and goblins, Kuldra now rules the continent with her dragons.

Sixth Age

During the 14th Year of the Sixth Age, while ruling unchallenged, an expedition had made its way to Ashenfall; her generals had attacked the expedition in her name. After the arrival of a group of adventurers, Kuldra would start gathering pieces of the Harmonic Resonator to cause another explosion that would devour the world. Before she could put her plan into motion and put an end to the world, the adventurer(s) made their way into her sanctum and, through a grueling barrage of her hatchlings trying to protect her from the intruders, was unable to survive after they destroyed her heart.

Kuldra's Heart.name: Kuldra's Heart
Kuldra's Heart.respawn: Re-enters on new raid instance / Reset per raid run
Kuldra's Heart.lead: Kuldra's Heart is the final target encountered during Phase 4 of the Kuldra encounter in the Scorned Wilderness Raid.

Lesser Demon.name: Lesser Demon
Lesser Demon.lead: Lesser demons are power level 6 monsters located under Dowdun Reach. They are incredibly powerful and fast, dealing mostly heavy and fast blows. There are several variants of a lesser demon, shardbound lesser demon and Delrom.

Lost Soul.name: Lost Soul
Lost Soul.lead: Lost souls are power level 2, 3, and 5 aggressive NPCs in Fellhollow, encountered if the player is soul rifting. After a 30 second grace period while soul rifting, power level 2 lost souls appear and attack the player. After 150 seconds, these lost souls become power level 3.

Lurch.name: Lurch
Lurch.lead: Lurch is a power level 6 monster that appears with Houndmaster Rexiton under The Garrison.

Mage of Zamorak.name: Mage of Zamorak
Mage of Zamorak.lead: Mages of Zamorak are power level 6 monsters located within Dowdun Reach. They can cast fire spells, teleport short distances, and call on the Flames of Zamorak under their targets.

Magpie.name: Magpie
Magpie.location: Temple Woods, Bramblemead Valley, Fractured Plains
Magpie.lead: Magpies are power level 1 non-aggressive creatures in Ashenfall. They can be found on most of Ashenfall's territories. They can be scared very easily and fly away when somebody gets near them. Their feathers can be used to create arrows.

Nature Spirit.name: Nature Spirit
Nature Spirit.lead: Nature spirits are power level 5 monsters in Fellhollow, found at willow Groves, who play a role in the quest The Wild Hunt. They have the same moveset as terrorbirds and emit a metallic wail when in close proximity.
Nature Spirit.location_html:
Nature spirits are found in willow groves across Western Fellhollow, such as south of Witchwillow Range, west of Emberwood and west of Dragon's Run. There is an additional willow grove found east of Skekven Kara.

Look for willow tree symbols on the map which are always located around ponds to find nature spirits close by.
Nature Spirit.journal: Nature spirits are part of a natural cycle, they are both the hunter and the hunted and death is as important a part of their essence as living is. In death, they rise again, like plants growing from the nutrients of fallen beasts, only to be hunted and slain again and again. On paper it’s a tragic existence, but this cycle of life and death is vital for the wellbeing of any ecosystem.

Nosey.name: Nosey
Nosey.lead: Nosey is a power level 6 monster that appears with Rat Master Skrexis in The Menagerie.

Patch (Hellrat).name: Patch (Hellrat)
Patch (Hellrat).lead: Patch is a power level 6 monster that appears with Rat Master Skrexis in The Menagerie.

Pip.name: Pip
Pip.lead: Pip is a power level 6 monster that appears with Rat Master Skrexis in The Menagerie.

Plague King.name: Plague King
Plague King.location: Whispering Swamp, Bloodblight Swamp, Vertentis Kara vault
Plague King.lead: Plague kings are power level 2-3 monster, a bigger version of the putrid rats. Plague kings are found in the Whispering Swamp and Bloodblight Swamp, as well as the Vertentis Kara vault.

Putrid Rat.name: Putrid Rat
Putrid Rat.lead: Putrid rats are found in the Whispering Swamp, the Bloodblight Swamp, and inside vaults. Putrid rats can hit the monster and fill up the Poison debuff bar by up to 80% per hit. Thus, two successful hits can poison the player.

Ram.lead: Rams are power level 3 or 4 NPCs that are found in the Fractured Plains and Stormtouched Highlands. Before attacking, rams will lower their horns before charging at the player. If the attack is successful, this will fill up the Bleed bar and inflict 30-32 damage to the player.

Rat King.name: Rat King
Rat King.lead: Rat kings are boss-like versions of the rat monster with higher attack accuracy and higher hitpoints.

Rat Master Skrexis.name: Rat Master Skrexis
Rat Master Skrexis.lead: Rat Master Skrexis is a power level 6 monster located within Dowdun Reach. They are able to cast fire spell, short distance teleport and call on the Flames of Zamorak under their targets.

Raven.name: Raven
Raven.lead: Ravens are power level 1 birds found all over Dowdun Reach.

Razlem, the Deranged.name: Razlem, the Deranged
Razlem, the Deranged.lead: Razlem the necromancer is power level 5 aggressive NPC found in the south-east part of Silverthorn Keep. They guard the scroll Eventide - A New Spawn, which is needed for the quest What Remains is Written, and has a similar moveset to skeletal necromancer.

Red Dragon.name: Red Dragon
Red Dragon.lead: Red dragons also known as lesser red dragons are power level 7 dragons that roam the Umbral Sands.
Red Dragon.attacks:
• Lunge
  • Tail sweep (if behind them)
  • Fire Claw Slash
  • Fire Blast: The red dragon launches a fire projectile to build up around the three-quarters point.
  • Fire Breath: The red dragon sweeps the area in front of them with their fire breath.
  • Wing Attack: The red dragon flaps its wings, blowing wind at the player, with the second such blast doing damage.
  • Fly: The red dragon can fly into the sky and do a few moves:
    • Fire Breath: The red dragon shoots their breath in a line going away from them. This staggers the player and can easily lock them in to take all of the damage.
    • Fire Whirlwind: The red dragon will fly into the air after looking upward and spin, causing a whirlwind of flames. They'll also spit 6 fireballs around the area; on impact, the fire will also form a pool of lava on the ground.
Red Dragon.location_html: Travelling within the Umbral Sands at night can result in a chance encounter with Fuzan, who drops off a red dragon at your location.
Red Dragon.journal: These red dragons are only lesser when compared to Fuzan, the strongest red dragon currently active in the region. Despite their weaker stature to their draconic overlord, the lesser red dragons are still some of the deadliest creatures in the region. Like Fuzan, the red dragons here are fuelled by a desire to destroy. The fire that rages in their bellies yearns to be unleashed upon anything that moves - or doesn’t move (as some poor cacti have discovered). They torment the locals, and delight in their suffering. A few red dragons give themselves grandiose names, in an attempt to claim their own legacy. One dragon, known as The Radiant, torments the Manafem Moon Garou. For years now, The Radiant has destroyed caravans, eaten travellers and brought suffering to the camp, for no reason other than their capacity to do so. Cruelty is a deeply embedded trait in the red dragons of Ashenfall, and they view mercy as a weakness to be exploited.

Reek.name: Reek
Reek.lead: Reek is a power level 6 monster that appears with Rat Master Skrexis in The Menagerie.

Rotridden Cow.name: Rotridden Cow
Rotridden Cow.lead: Rotridden cows are level 5 aggressive NPCs in Ashenfall located within the region of Fellhollow near Withered areas.
Rotridden Cow.journal: Once gentle creatures, the rotridden cows were the few cows that hadn't been filled with an ancestral rage against humanity, for the slaughter of their kin back on the mainland. Unfortunately, this gentle nature made them carriers for the cursed hunger of Imaru and now these cows seek to damage the very souls of their victims, rotting them from within.

Rotridden Rat.name: Rotridden Rat
Rotridden Rat.lead: Rotridden rats are level 5 aggressive NPCs in Ashenfall located within the region of Fellhollow near Withered areas.
Rotridden Rat.journal: These nasty little creatures embody all the viciousness of their living kin, but with the added hatred of an undead dragon. Their bites will wither your soul, threatening to drag you into Imaru's gaze.

Rotsworn Marauder.name: Rotsworn Marauder
Rotsworn Marauder.lead: Rotsworn marauders are level 5 aggressive NPCs in Ashenfall located within the region of Fellhollow near Withered areas.
Rotsworn Marauder.journal: The Scalesworn were heroes. Only the strongest, most skilled and powerful marauders would be chosen by Xikotal to act as guardians of the dragons. They would guard the great beasts as they slept, standing strong against any force that might try to do them harm. They were blessed with the mark of the dragon, granting them some of the power of their draconic masters. These marks would be their undoing, when Imaru refused to stay dead. They became the first of the infected, inflicted with a terrible withering curse that would drag the souls of any they touched into Imaru’s hungry maw.

Rotsworn Necromancer.name: Rotsworn Necromancer
Rotsworn Necromancer.lead: Rotsworn necromancers are power level 5 aggressive NPCs found in Fellhollow. Rotsworn necromancers are able to spawn in rotsworn warriors.
Rotsworn Necromancer.journal: Hatred guides these creatures, a vitriolic disgust at a world too cruel to function. They were once mages who had delved into the secrets of necromancy, desperate for power they were too foolish to wield. The power within them has twisted and rotted, infected by Imaru’s vengeful rage. Their souls have been long hollowed out and now they are driven by a need to infect and corrupt, raising the dead in further service of vengeance.

Rotsworn Reanimator.name: Rotsworn Reanimator
Rotsworn Reanimator.lead: Rotsworn Reanimators are power level 5 undead monsters in Ashenfall located within the region of Fellhollow. They are similar to Rotsworn Zombies but respawn many more times. They also explode on each death, which causes Wither damage in the area.

Rotsworn Thrall.name: Rotsworn Thrall
Rotsworn Thrall.lead: Rotsworn thralls are level 5 aggressive NPCs found during the fight with Imaru at Imaru's Tower. They can appear as rotsworn necromancers, rotsworn warriors, or rotsworn marauders.

Rotsworn Warrior.name: Rotsworn Warrior
Rotsworn Warrior.lead: Rotsworn warriors are power level 5 aggressive NPCs in Ashenfall, located within the region of Fellhollow near withered areas.
Rotsworn Warrior.journal: Foul creatures, warped by Imaru’s terrible hunger. They were once convicts and criminals, now cursed to serve as Imaru’s claws. In the ages past those who had committed the gravest sins were given to Xikotal for conversion. He would breathe into them a new way of thinking, draconic magic creating a fog in their minds that erased their wicked past and offering them a newer future. Some would be farmers. Others might live their lives in service of the village, even taking roles as priests or healers. The strongest would be given new identities, soldiers to stand as the dragon’s forces. They were closest to Imaru when she died and as she drew in the souls around her they were the first to be afflicted. Withered and rotten, these tragic creatures remember nothing but a desire to infect and destroy.

Rotsworn Zombie.name: Rotsworn Zombie
Rotsworn Zombie.lead: Rotsworn zombies are power level 5 undead monsters in Ashenfall located within the region of Fellhollow near withered areas. Similar to standard zombies. Each rotsworn zombie respawns an additional time to fight the player. Additionally, they explode on death, which causes Wither damage in the area.
Rotsworn Zombie.journal: What is worse than a shambling corpse that years to feast on all your precious fleshy parts? A shambling corpse that’s infected with a terrible rot that will tear your soul apart if you let it. These zombies were once the most faithful followers of Imaru, her chosen servants. Each of them was branded with a special mark that would allow her to gift them a small semblance of her power. As humans they were healthier, lived longer and they thrived under her care. Yet when Imaru’s hunger spread from the underworld, it was these unfortunates that fell first to this terrible affliction. Now they act as extensions to her hunger, sharing the rot with any unfortunate enough to cross their path.

Rufus.name: Rufus
Rufus.lead: Rufus is a power level 6 monster that appears with Houndmaster Rexiton under The Garrison.

Sergeant Blister.name: Sergeant Blister
Sergeant Blister.lead: Sergeant Blister is a power level 7 variant of the Black Knight guardian. They are located under Dowdun Reach within The Garrison. They must be defeated to obtain the Dreaming Stone Shard.
Sergeant Blister.journal: You wanna know why they call me Blister? 'Course you do. You'd well to listen up. People love to gripe and fight in 'ere. Lotsa madness, lotsa grievances - it's gonna 'appen. But they know not to fight wiv'out Blister. I get called tout suite. I'm the one who handles the bets. You wanna make some extra dirt from a fight? You come to me. I give fair odds. Why Blister? I'm the one who grows fat an' happy from all the friction in this place. Like a blister on your foot, ain't it?

Shardbound Lesser Demon.name: Shardbound Lesser Demon
Shardbound Lesser Demon.lead: Shardbound lesser demons are power level 6 variants of a lesser demon. They are located in Dowdun Reach under The Library and The Demon Gate. They must be fought and defeated in order to obtain the Dreaming Stone Shard

Skeletal Archer.name: Skeletal Archer
Skeletal Archer.lead: Skeletal archers are power level 5, 6, and 8 monsters found in Fellhollow, Dowdun Reach and the Scorned Wilderness raid.
Skeletal Archer.journal: By the time you’ve heard their creaking bones, it’s already too late. Despite their lack of sinew, sensory organs, or anything that should make them this dead, the skeletal archer is surprisingly deft. In life they were scouts, hunters or Wild Knight archers, in death they’re simply something best avoided.

Skeletal Hoplite.name: Skeletal Hoplite
Skeletal Hoplite.lead: Skeletal hoplites are power level 5 aggressive NPCs found in Fellhollow.
Skeletal Hoplite.journal: In life the hoplites named themselves in honour of the legendary forces of Saradomin, back on Hallow. They took their identity from the sacred texts, creating a disciplined and loyal legion of skilled warriors. Now, that discipline has all but faded. They forget the shield walls, or the turtle formation. They forget the bonds they once shared with their friends. Now they only remember that a spear must be thrust forward, preferably into someone else.

Skeletal Marauder.name: Skeletal Marauder
Skeletal Marauder.lead: Skeletal marauders are power level 5 and 6 aggressive NPCs in Ashenfall located within the region of Fellhollow and Dowdun Reach.

Skeletal Necromancer.name: Skeletal Necromancer
Skeletal Necromancer.lead: Skeletal necromancers are power level 5 aggressive NPCs found in Fellhollow. Skeletal necromancers are able to spawn in skeletal warriors.

Skeleton.name: Skeleton
Skeleton.lead: Skeletons are a type of undead monster found in Fellhollow.

Soulstone Sentinel.name: Soulstone Sentinel
Soulstone Sentinel.lead: Soulstone sentinels are power level 5 aggressive NPCs in Fellhollow, encountered if the player enters a spectral door. They have a similar attack mechanism like the skeletal hoplites.

Spectral Bird.name: Spectral Bird
Spectral Bird.lead: Spectral birds are power level 1 non-aggressive spirit birds found within the region of Fellhollow, on ruined buildings. They look like spiritual versions of gyrfalcons.

Spectral Chinchompa.name: Spectral Chinchompa
Spectral Chinchompa.lead: Spectral chinchompas are spectral enemies that can be found within the region of Fellhollow. They are enemies mainly used in the quest Things That Go Boom In The Night and drop spectral chinchompa skulls.
Spectral Chinchompa.location_html:
They are spawned in certain locations in Fellhollow, these locations are:

  • South Emberwood's druid circle.
  • Witchwillow Range's willow tree grove.
  • In another willow tree grove north of Hope's Fall.
  • West of Doric's camp, where the first statue is before entering the cave.
    • Another is further west, near the shore of the Lake of Lost Souls.
  • In the south-eastern wood of Silverthorn Keep
  • In another willow tree grove in Silverthorn Keep.
  • Most eastern part of Silverthorn Keep, where a purification pool is located when heading into the keep.

Stormpact Demon.name: Stormpact Demon
Stormpact Demon.lead: The Stormpact demon is a power level 6 variant of a lesser demon located under the Grand Hall in Dowdun Reach.

Summoner Flament.name: Summoner Flament
Summoner Flament.lead: Summoner Flament is a power level 6 monster located within Dowdun Reach. They are able to cast fire spell, short distance teleport and call on the Flames of Zamorak under their targets.

Terrorbird.name: Terrorbird
Terrorbird.lead: Terrorbirds are power level 3 and 8 monsters found within the Fractured Plains and Scorned Wilderness that will shriek when the player is at least 5–10 metres away. This will send nearby garous and other monsters nearby towards the player. The terrorbird will also attack the player with five quick attacks with its beak that knock back the player if within five metres of the terrorbird. A terrorbird can be summoned and mounted using the mount mechanic.

Tiny.name: Tiny
Tiny.lead: Tiny is a power level 6 monster that appears with Houndmaster Rexiton under The Garrison.

Tok-Xil.name: Tok-Xil
Tok-Xil.lead: Tok-Xil is a KotHaar mini-boss that is found in Umbral Sands.
Tok-Xil.journal: The Elder Gods are not subtle in their creations, and this is best exemplified in the Tok-Xil. Not considered part of the KotHaar caste, as such, this creature is more like living artillery, built purely for destruction. In aeons past, these creatures would blast apart mountains, decimate forests and banish creatures back to nightmares. The world was a darker, scarier place, and needed deadlier and deadlier defences to push the evil back. Recently - and by recently I mean in the last few thousand years - there has been much less need for the Tok-Xil in Ashenfall. They still stood as the guardians of the Lens, but it has been a long time since they last saw combat. Fuzan, of course, changed all that. Now, the Tok-Xil roam the desert sands, obliterating everything in their path. They are uncaring engines of destruction, slaying any living creature in their path.

Ulgo the Zogre.name: Ulgo the Zogre
Ulgo the Zogre.lead: Ulgo the zogre is a unique zogre found in Coalridge Pass who guards the Coclear Malificarum, a scroll needed for the quest What Remains is Written. They have the same attacks as a normal zogre. Their drop table is nearly identical with Ulgo the zogre having a higher chance to drop the Shard of Smoky Glass and dropping Ascension Shard (Power Level 6) instead of power level 5 shards.

Vault Archon.lead: Vault archons are vault mini boss monsters that attack with Ranged styles.

Vault Overlord.name: Vault Overlord

Vault Overlord.attacks:
• Rapid spin attack: The Overlord will spin, closing the distance. This attack is designed to wear down stamina. Simply dodge out of the way; blocking will rapidly drain the player's stamina reserves.
  • Standard fist slam: A single-handed slam, easily blocked, can be parried to make the Overlord collapse.
  • Double-fisted slam: This will break your block and stun the player. This will also stun the overlord, whether it hits or not; dodge the attack, then retaliate while the overlord is incapacitated.
