regions.name: Fellhollow
regions.lead: Fellhollow is a power level 5 region in Ashenfall, ruled over by Imaru, the Soul-Eater. The region includes underground spaces and is infested with all manner of undead monsters. Death will make an appearance in this region.
regions.history:
Pre-Withering

Fellhollow was founded by Amalgamated refugees from Brynmoor, displaced during the Schism, a period of violent conflict in which those deemed 'impure' were persecuted, killed, and expelled from their homes. The violence drove communities north past the garou and down into the earth, emerging in the region that would become their new home during the period of peace brokered between the humans and the garou in the Third Age. Former Bandosian ogres from the campaigns in Ghornfell, abandoned when Bandos withdrew and with no war left to fight, joined the settlers in the same period. For the Amalgamated among the founders, Fellhollow represented a marked contrast to the persecution left behind.

Two dragons already inhabited the region: Imaru and her mate Xikotal. Though initially distant, both eventually approached the settlers as neighbours and extended their protection over the community. Dragonkin experimentation had stripped Imaru of the ability to bear children, and the settlers provided both dragons with cause to take on a guardianship role. Imaru's elemental affinity with water brought rain to the region's crops, while Xikotal's influence calmed the winds, resulting in plentiful harvests and a growing population. Blessed purifying pools were created across the region to ward off illness and corruption, and a magical Blessing was woven over each settler that bound the people of differing backgrounds together and served as a source of shared health and strength.

Emberwood grew into a multi-faith community unlike anything else on Ashenfall, with Saradominists and Zamorakians living and trading side by side. The villagers honoured their draconic guardians in daily life, weaving patterns of blue and black into their clothing in tribute to the dragons' dances in the sky. A civilian military force, the hoplites, formed within the village, naming themselves after the legendary Saradominist forces of Hallow and training together each week. The Wild Knights established a fortress at Silverthorn Keep to the east.

Dowdun Reach, a Zamorakian faction based across the mountains, maintained an isolationist stance despite the peace secured by the region's draconic guardians. Xikotal brought gifts of coal and iron ore to Dowdun Reach, hoping to soften the faction's isolationism. Its lord Rasmodel accepted the materials and used them to arm a new private military force instead. The resulting Shadow Knights, established by formal edict, ensured Dowdun Reach's continued separation from Fellhollow, and would in time become the Black Knights.

The peace ended when Kuldra, the Godeater, arrived in Fellhollow. Kuldra's campaign against humanity extended to any dragon that sheltered it, and the cooperation between the region's draconic guardians and its settlers was not permitted to stand. Xikotal was killed, his heart torn out and devoured by Kuldra before she departed the region. The loss was felt across the entire community through the Blessing, the region falling silent.

The Withering

Following Xikotal's death, a grief-curse was embedded in Imaru by Ravanna, an Emberwood necromancer who had settled in the region. The curse was designed to amplify Imaru's power into something capable of destroying Kuldra, but the attempt failed. Kuldra withstood the attack without difficulty and Imaru was struck down.

Rather than passing into the Afterlife, Imaru anchored herself within the using the curse, wedging herself in the passage between the living world and the Underworld. From there she began consuming the souls of the dead to accumulate power, causing the Noumenon's waters to bleed into the living world. The Blessing, which had bound the community together, was turned into a conduit through which the souls of Fellhollow's living population were drawn toward Imaru.

The Scalesworn, Xikotal's most devoted guardians, fell first. The draconic marks they bore became an entry point for the curse, making them both the first to turn and the first vector through which the affliction spread to others. Necromantic energy washing back through the Blessing then animated the dead throughout the region, filling them with an insatiable hunger that spread further through the population. Researchers in Dowdun Reach measured the spread at roughly a hectare a day, slowed only by mountains and bodies of water, and projected full contamination of Fellhollow within two weeks. The hunger did not stop at the living. The substance of the region itself was consumed over time: food tasted of nothing, campfires felt cold, and trees were hollowed from within.

As the village fell regardless, priests of all faiths prayed together over the bones of the dead buried beneath the soil, erecting a multi-faith barrier that sealed Emberwood shut. To the east, the Wild Knights held their positions at the village gates before retreating into Silverthorn Keep and sealing themselves inside. Imaru's Tower shattered, and those who had dwelt near it were lost in the lake of grief that formed around it. None of these defences held. The Withering eventually claimed those inside the keep, and the defenders who had fought hardest against the undead became the undead themselves.

Three curse seals, each containing a fragment of Ravanna's curse, were placed across the region in an attempt to provide a future means of challenging Imaru. The curse, which made Imaru powerful, also represented the only way to make her vulnerable, a challenger who gathered all three shards would carry enough of it to overcome her invulnerability. Dowdun Reach sealed all connecting pathways to Fellhollow and posted guards at their crypt as a warning system. For centuries afterward the region remained locked in this state, its dead unable to pass on and its souls endlessly consumed, while Death himself found his ability to reap souls in the region entirely blocked.

Sixth Age

Following the defeat of General Velgar in Ghornfell, the Wise Old Man discovered a necromantically sealed door in a passage near Ashien's Watch. After studying the magic, the passphrase was passed to the player, granting access to what lay beyond. Beyond the door lies the Forgotten Temple, where the player is met by Death. The Withering has blocked Death's ability to reap the souls of Fellhollow, and the player is tasked with investigating and resolving it, directed first to Postie Pete to undergo soul rifting, then to Cathan, who had already been investigating a necromantic ritual site in the region.

Through the standing stones left by Ravanna, the history of Imaru's fall is uncovered and the three curse seals are located across Fellhollow. Absorbing a shard from each, the player accumulates enough of the curse to make Imaru vulnerable to attack. Imaru is then confronted and defeated in her tower, ending her centuries-long consumption of Fellhollow's dead. With her hold on the region broken, Death is able to begin clearing the enormous backlog of souls trapped since the Withering began. Following this; the entrance to Dowdun Reach is unlocked, allowing the player to progress.
regions.geography:
Fellhollow is comprised of the subregions;

Forgotten Temple

Is located in the underground part that separates Fellhollow and the Fractured Plains. Death, Muncher, and Postie Pete resides here.

Bleakfields Valley

Is the starting area of Fellhollow. The valley contains a withered village, a graveyard, willow groves, and the standing stones left by Ravanna as part of her attempt to contain Imaru's curse.

Lake of Lost Souls

Is the north eastern part of Fellhollow. Its waters are drawn from pools corrupted by the , poisoned by Imaru's hunger and carrying the essence of the river of the dead within each drop.

Dragon's Run

Is the north western part of Fellhollow that houses a green dragon. The area contains withered ruins, the remnants of settlements consumed by the Withering.

Dragon's Run features an agility course, Grave Run.

Emberwood

Is the most western part of Fellhollow, home to the village founded by the original settlers. Before the Withering, the region was a kaleidoscopic wonder of colour shaped by the Anima Twist, its streets filled with laughter and song while Imaru and Xikotal danced across the skies above. The village is now sealed behind a prayer barrier erected by the priests of Emberwood at the height of the Withering, its icons binding the barrier in place and containing the withered villagers within.

Witchwillow Range

Is the south western part of Fellhollow. The range is home to willow groves, each connected to a pool of water and once inhabited by nature spirits. The spirits in these groves have been corrupted and drained by the Withering, and now wander as hostile creatures, consumed by Imaru's hunger. The subregion also contains the ruins of a fountain.

Hope's Fall

Hope's Fall is a Rotsworn infested area of Fellhollow. In the centre stands Imaru's Tower, sealed off and inaccessible until the player has gathered the three curse shards left by Ravanna across the region. Ravanna placed one of her curse seals within Emberwood's heart, describing it as an anchor made from the suffering of the villagers.

Coalridge Pass

Coalridge Pass is an area within Fellhollow that houses several skeletons, zogres, dragon wolves, green dragons and other notable enemies. The region contains many coal nodes nearby, located either on the ridge walls or in caves, and the ruins of a miner's cottage are evidence of the working community that once operated here. It is located north-west of Silverthorn Keep and north-east of the Lake of Lost Souls.

Silverthorn Keep

Silverthorn Keep is an area within Fellhollow that houses several skeletons, zogres, dragon wolves, green dragons and other notable enemies. It is the location of one of the Wild Knights fortresses and the ominous gateway that leads into Dowdun Reach. During the Withering, the keep's defenders held the gates against the undead horde before sealing themselves inside, unleashing volleys of arrows from the walls in a last stand that ultimately failed. Ravanna placed one of her three curse seals here, guarded by the keep's last surviving protector.

regions.name: Dowdun Reach
regions.lead: Dowdun Reach is a power level 6 mountainous region in Ashenfall located south of Silverthorn Keep in Fellhollow, accessible through its gatehouse. Players must first complete Withering Heights to gain access to this region.
regions.history:
The Children of Shadows

The keep and its settlement grew from the Children of Shadows, a Zamorakian order who chose the mountains, then called the Dowdun Mountains, as their meeting ground.

The region's value was secured through an accidental finding. A young Zamorakian mining rock for a raven habitat struck a mithril seam and tried to conceal the discovery, but she was found out and killed. Mutiny followed until the order stabilised, at which point the Children of Shadows held the only known source of mithril on Ashenfall. The order's mining operation belonged to the peacetime that followed the Human-Garou War, when the four major faiths of Emberwood coexisted. Since the order believed manual labour was below them, goblins were press-ganged into hauling the ore out of the mountain in exchange for scraps of food. Mithril itself was withheld from both arms and armour by strict policy. The Children deliberately kept the supply short to keep its value high, treating it as a bribery currency used to influence those who could further Zamorak's goals. The smiths within the order lived dual lives, openly forging deliberately dulled weapons to arm the Saradominists in Bramblemead while covertly delivering superior goods to their own pilgrims in the Dowdun Mountains.

The Rasmodels

During the and the Human-Garou War, the Rasmodels, a noble house who migrated from the mainland, arrived in Ashenfall and settled within Brynmoor. The family first operated within the Temple Woods and Bramblemead, and their standing gave the Children of Shadows access to circles the order could not otherwise reach, with members of the order serving the family as its first bodyguards. The order made the mistake of dismissing the family as preening peacocks, and the Rasmodels moved deliberately into leadership seats within the Children's own ranks until the family and the order had become one and the same. With that influence came demands, and more of the Children were assigned to the family as personal bodyguards. The family's reputation for poisoning their rivals grew alongside that influence. When one of the family was finally caught in the act, the whole house was banished north to Dowdun Reach, and they took their most loyal bodyguards with them. At Dowdun Reach, the Rasmodels moved freely through the region and continued operating as they had before. Their scheming eventually overreached. The youngest Rasmodel was caught poisoning a sleeping official, and what remained of the family's standing collapsed overnight. They were barred from the rest of the Reach, restricted to a single part of the keep, and survived only because their bodyguards had grown loyal enough that moving against them was too dangerous.

Dowdun Reach grew into a settlement in its own right, home to the Rasmodels, the Zamorakians, and the goblins pressed into their service. When the head of the family died, his eldest son Milliburn worked to restore the family's lost pride, taking charge of the keep's training and quartermasters, and was duly elected Master of Dowdun Reach. The Children took to calling him Lord Rasmodel, the name used for him hereafter. The new Lord Rasmodel slept poorly. His dreams spoke to him in unfamiliar words, in a dull and interminable voice, and he came to suspect the Archmage Alric of being behind his restless nights. That restlessness hardened into resolve. Milliburn raised a new martial order, the Shadow Knights, who would later be known as the Black Knights. The order grew from his deep distrust of Fellhollow and its dragons Imaru and Xikotal, and his own bodyguards formed its core. For armour, the order drew on a precedent set within the Children generations before. Sadia Vulketra, a member who feared an eventual Saradominist reprisal, had already worked with the Amalgamated blacksmith Vesk to produce the first suit of steel gear in the Fellhollow area, starting with a black horned helm. Outfitting the Knights in bulk demanded materials, and these came from an unexpected source. Xikotal brought the Zamorakians an offering of coal and iron as a misguided attempt to draw them into the wider Fellhollow community. The gift instead fuelled and fortified their separation from it. The keep's marksmen kept watch for dragons above all else, and their eagerness had to be violently curbed after an incident during one of Imaru's diplomatic visits.

Mystic cloth, a humming fabric that the keep's magi believed had come from Zamorak himself, was long reserved for the Archmage and his council. That changed when a cleric from Emberwood, an attaché of Imaru and Xikotal, arrived at a trade meeting wearing the cloth. Alric burned the contract and cast the envoy from the top of the keep, and the cloth was afterwards freed for any common magi to wear. As the cloth became more plentiful in the Reach, Lord Rasmodel permitted its trade with carefully chosen partners, which brought the Children of Shadows into their first dealings with an offshoot of the garou, and a friendship of sorts grew between Lord Rasmodel and the Moon Garou merchants. The Moon Garou's physiology kept them beyond the usual methods of infiltration, so Lord Rasmodel turned to Alric, who proposed that the humming cloth itself could be worked to surveil the Moon Garou. Meanwhile, the goblins of the Reach had been promised gold, food, and passage back home to the Felldip hills, and received only scraps, so calls to rise up against Lord Rasmodel and Alric circulated among them.

The Dreaming Stone

As the Dragon Rebellion tore through Ashenfall and the rest of the subcontinent fell to dragons, Lord Rasmodel and his knights held the Reach and protected those within its walls. During the Rebellion, Avisk had preserved his intellect within a stone as the rest of the Cabal died or awaited destruction. Members of the Children of Shadows who pursued arcane knowledge found the stone buried beneath the desert sands and brought it to Dowdun Reach, where the mages studied it for its power and called it the Dreaming Stone. From inside the stone, Avisk whispered to the Children of Shadows to amuse himself, gradually pushing them into turning on one another.

When Fellhollow was falling to the Withering plague, the Reach's response was to cut itself off entirely. A research group within the keep reported that the surrounding mountains should hold the contamination out, though waterways and crevices still posed a risk. Every pathway to Fellhollow was severed and the Reach closed to the outside world. Knights were stationed in the crypt as an early warning, since the dead rising there would be the sign that the plague had breached the mountains. The Shadow Knight snipers' standing orders were to shoot any draconic presence on sight, with the lone exception of lesser blue dragons, which were to be spared to preserve the local balance. The deaths of Fellhollow's guardians changed the keep's smithing as well. The black metal of the knights' arms was steel treated by a process akin to vulcanisation, work Xikotal had once carried out himself as a gift to the isolationist knights. After the dragon's death the work passed to demonic methods, whose poorer results made the original dragonfire metal prized within the Reach.

Within the sealed Reach, the Dreaming Stone's power was eventually turned to fuelling a demon portal, and the Mages of Zamorak were soon summoning demons in growing numbers. The wizard Valerius wrote of the undertaking as an attempt to summon beings from another world in the hope of learning from them. Meanwhile, the Black Knights operated under two sets of orders. The first set was simple. Any demon that broke free of its summoner was to be put down, and the mages were to be protected. The second set was kept secret. It held what the order called the 'Demon's Share', a policy under which the knights were to allow one mage to die before stepping in whenever a demon went rogue, used in practice to keep the mage population trimmed. Above even that, the knights' highest standing order was to destroy the demon portal outright if the summonings ever got beyond control. Archmage Alric uncovered the arrangement, coming to Lord Rasmodel with a ledger showing one hundred and seventeen magi deaths across one hundred and seventeen incidents, exactly one mage lost each time, and raging at what the numbers proved. Lord Rasmodel's answer went out the next day. The Black Knights were now to allow two magi to die with each incident.

The Dreaming Stone had always been a point of contention, and the breaking point came when a demon appeared in the middle of a Black Knight training session and killed the unarmed recruits. Alric and Lord Rasmodel argued the matter out in the war room. When they emerged, control of the Dreaming Stone and the demon portal's power belonged to Lord Rasmodel, and the magi had lost most of their authority.

Alric refused to accept losing command of the Dreaming Stone. Denial is the first tenet of The Gospel of Zamorak, and Alric's faithful lived by it. They secretly redirected the stone's power so that its energy spread to every room of the keep instead of flowing along a single line. The rerouting coincided with a separate scheme of Alric's to capture demon souls in enormous numbers and use them to supercharge the demon portal. The tens of thousands of stored demon souls bled into the walls of the fortress itself rather than powering the gateway, and demons could summon themselves anywhere within it. Alric claimed this outcome as his plan all along, warning his magi that nowhere in the Reach was private any longer and that an avernic would be listening whenever someone spoke against them. The rerouting caused other problems too. Overloaded energy tethers set off sudden fires and magical accidents, which the magi pinned on Lord Rasmodel and his knights. Later effects were worse. With the altered flows now running through sleeping quarters, residents stopped dreaming properly, tempers grew short, and a sickness of voices spread outward from the magi wing. The afflicted either fell unconscious or heard competing voices fighting inside their own minds.

The madness spread into the order itself. Black Knight numbers fell as more knights succumbed, and the order's charter forbade resignation. Among the afflicted was a soldier Lord Rasmodel had known long before, whose rambling mimicked the droning voice of his own dreams. Lord Rasmodel resolved to see the stone destroyed, blaming its whispering for the madness of his order and accusing Vulketra and his fanatics of needing its power for their own schemes.

Milliburn shattered the Dreaming Stone with his warhammer. The voices that had plagued him for decades briefly ceased. The reprieve was brief, and the afflictions that followed were worse than before. The magic released in the breaking twisted the fortress's residents, prolonging their lives and cursing them with madness. His family appeared around him in their finery, and his father bade him rest. The twenty-fifth Lord of Rasmodel retired. He remains within the keep as the Black Knight Titan. The keep's demons felt the aftershocks as well. Some fell still, as though a controlling force had been cut from them, while a subset gathered the scattered shards and fought one another over their stockpiles, becoming the shardbound. The shards themselves lie scattered across the Reach and continue to whisper. Groups of the afflicted would travel together and kill whoever they met, and the elite Black Knights were deployed to put them down during the worst outbreaks.

Sixth Age

In the Sixth Age, adventurers who have driven the withering from Fellhollow are directed onward by Death and find the keep standing between them and the Umbral Sands. During Black Knight's Fortress, the adventurer works alongside the Wise Old Man and Doric to uncover the secrets of Dowdun Reach and unlock the way through to the desert. Thirteen shards of the Dreaming Stone are gathered from across the region and the stone is made whole once more. The restored intelligence names itself Avisk, blames the cthonian for the keep's state, and lowers the barrier blocking the way onward. With the keep's gatekeeper defeated, the door to Umbral Sands is opened.

During Biohazard, Zanik enlists the adventurer to investigate the corruption afflicting the region's residents. Samples gathered from the corrupted ravens point to a cthonian infection, and its source is traced high up in the Reach. There the adventurer finds Putrilius, one of the last of the cthonian demons that once ruled Infernus, who admits to being part of the madness while holding the mind of the Dreaming Stone responsible for how far it spread. Zanik hopes the demonic corruption can be kept contained within Dowdun Reach.

Sealed nodestone portals lie strewn across the Reach, and during What's Theirs is Mine! the adventurer unclogs them while helping Doric track down a thieving mage, with the Dreaming Stone's magic completing their restoration.

regions.name: Umbral Sands
regions.lead: Umbral Sands is a desert region of Ashenfall, ruled by the red dragon Fuzan. Its sun burns so fiercely that the player suffers Scorch in direct light and must build shelter or keep to the shade by day, while by night Fuzan and his red dragons take to the hunt. To cross the open sands the player can summon a magic carpet, which can be earned after earning the trust of a garou tribe. The KotHaar and kalphites make their home here, along with vultures, alongside three Moon Garou clans that are far less hostile than the garou tribes elsewhere on the continent. Icthlarin can be found at the Alcarrid Oasis. Adamantite and yew are gathered across the desert, and the region holds the materials needed for adamant equipment, red dragonhide armour, and infinity robes.
regions.history:
Since the creation of Gielinor, Umbral Sands was an empty region inhabited only by the KotHaar, who had been tasked with safeguarding a powerful device used by the Elder Gods, the Lens. The device ensured the sun gave off a temperature that let the world thrive rather than burn. The KotHaar were also given a tunnel system so that they might return to the on Karamjah and be reborn when needed. The desert at the time was far greener, with grass and other flora. Shortly after Guthix departed from Ashenfall and sealed it within a veil, a group of dragonkin known as the Cabal arrived and, over time, spread through the different regions. Avisk kept one of his many laboratories here, experimenting on the kalphites he had brought from the mainland to study, fascinated by their hive mind.

Sometime during the , shortly after Lougrim's defeat by Kuldra during the Dragon Rebellion, a faction of the garou split off and wandered towards Umbral Sands, where they struggled to adjust to the sandy region. There they discovered Elidinis, the River Goddess associated with the moon. A lost garou cub found her at a previously unmapped oasis, she gave it water and comfort. Looking upon these poor mortals, the goddess taught them how to live within the desert, showing them how to build, plant, and place mirrors to guard against supernatural threats. Over time the garou raised great cities and became known as the Moon Garou. Once they could thrive without her, Elidinis left Gielinor for the stars. Sometime after her departure, Fuzan found the Moon Garou and began to terrorise them.

Eventually, a new entity appeared, the "Sun Demon", also known as the Queen of Ashes. She came before Fuzan, claiming to be a god and promising to teach him to wield his fire well enough to outshine even his mother. Fuzan accepted, and with her teaching he learned to control not only his own flames but those of the KotHaar, turning the magma that animated them against their nature. He also broke the tunnels by which they had once returned to the Elder Kiln, cutting them off from rebirth. Though puppeted, the KotHaar never forgot their charge, and still turn toward the Lens they were made to protect. Fuzan used this power to torment the Moon Garou, razing the cities they had raised and scattering the survivors into far-flung tribes so that no single hunt could take them all. Rather than destroy the remnant outright, he branded them with his Mark, which drew on their strength to feed his own. Those who bore it were spared his fire, but the dying were compelled to walk out into the sands as an offering. The Sun Demon, meanwhile, recruited followers of her own, reshaping those who worshipped the sun and its flames into devotees. The cursed wolf Dearg Due also came to roam the desert in this age. Fuzan ordered the KotHaar to move the Lens to his tower, where he used it to cast a barrier over the entrance and to raise the region's temperature. Soon the region became impossible to cross without the heat killing those who dared, and any who braved it by night would find Fuzan hunting with one or two red dragons.

After the God Wars, Fuzan continued to rule until the Sixth Age, when the veil over Ashenfall lifted. The Adventurer, having braved Brynmoor, Ghornfell, Fellhollow, and Dowdun Reach, arrives in Umbral Sands, and with the help of Icthlarin puts an end to Fuzan's reign.
regions.geography:
Umbral Sands consists of several subregions.

Alcarrid Oasis

In the north of the region, the Alcarrid Oasis is the first area the Adventurer reaches from Dowdun Reach. It is home to the Alcarrid clan, the youngest of the region's three Moon Garou clans, and to Icthlarin.

Dunes of Uzzer

To the north-east lie the Dunes of Uzzer, home to the Uzzer clan, who are known for their weaving and teach their children to work patterns into tapestries together. The archaeologist Lehran studies the Forbidden Scrolls here, piecing together the true history of the Moon Garou.

Manafem Plains

To the west, the Manafem Plains are home to the Manafem clan, whose people seldom brave the open dunes. By day the Scorch makes travel deadly, and by night they are hunted by a red dragon called The Radiant, which destroys their caravans and preys on travellers.

The Burning Spire

In the south stands The Burning Spire, Fuzan's volcano and the seat of his power, where the corrupted Lens is kept. Within it lies the Cave of Screams, where the KotHaar are forged and bound in thrall to Fuzan.

regions.lead: The Scorned Wilderness is RuneScape: Dragonwilds' first raid. This raid contains the Dragon Queen Kuldra as well as all monsters you have previously encountered.
regions.history: After arriving to Ashenfall long ago, the Dragonkin created a device called the Harmonic Resonator within the area now known as the Scorned Wilderness. The device's purpose was to gather raw anima for the Dragonkin, who would create an empire with it. Centuries after the creation of the device, Rasthin would activate it to destroy Kuldra, shattering the land. Kuldra survived, and now hunts for the pieces of the device to activate and lay waste to the rest of the world.

User:AFloofyDoggo/sandbox.lead: It is located north-east of the mainland continent in RuneScape.
User:AFloofyDoggo/sandbox.html:
Ashenfall is the continent in Gielinor that RuneScape: Dragonwilds is set in. It is divided into various regions, each of which contains different creatures, monsters, and biomes.

It is located north-east of the mainland continent in RuneScape.

Regions

  • Brynmoor
  • Ghornfell
  • Fellhollow
  • Dowdun Reach
  • Umbral Sands

Geography

Ashenfall is divided into five major territorial divisions: Brynmoor in the south, Ghornfell in the north, Fellhollow to the far north, and with the Umbral Sands in the far south divided from Fellhollow by the mountainous region of Dowdun Reach. The geography becomes more wild and dangerous as one travels further inland, with the Anima Twist phenomenon growing stronger deeper into the continent.

Brynmoor

The southern territories of Ashenfall include:

  • Temple Woods
  • Bramblemead Valley
  • Whispering Swamp

Ghornfell

The northern territories include:

  • Fractured Plains
  • Bloodblight Swamp
  • Stormtouched Highlands

Fellhollow

The far northern territories include:

  • Bleakfields Valley
  • Forgotten Temple
  • Dragon's Run
  • Emberwood
  • Witchwillow Range
  • Hope's Fall
  • Lake of Lost Souls
  • Silverthorn Keep
  • Coalridge Pass

Dowdun Reach

South of Silverthorn Keep, but north-east of Ghornfell, this region includes:

  • The Approach
  • The Courtyard
  • The Nexus
  • The Library
  • The Grand Hall
  • The Garrison
  • The Pastures
  • The Menagerie
  • The Bastion

Umbral Sands

South-east of The Bastion and directly east of Ghornfell, this region includes:

  • Alcarrid Oasis
  • Dunes of Uzzer
  • Manafem Plains
  • The Burning Spire

Unique phenomena

Anima Twist

After the Elder Gods created Gielinor, and prepared to sleep while their eggs consumed the planet's anima slowly, they discovered some impure, "wild" anima which they disliked, and they used the continent of Ashenfall to "vent out" the impure anima from the world. This resulted in the Anima Twist phenomenon enveloping the continent, with its effects getting stronger further into the continent. The Anima Twist affects not only the environment, but the creatures and people living on it, as well as magic itself. This results in common materials like wood and stone being capable of lasting hundreds or even thousands of years, and the inhabitants of the continent to become Amalgamated, creatures that would be enhanced with elemental properties due to the land's wild anima. The effects of the Anima Twist can be observed in the transformed wildlife, with wolves developing manes made of leaves, deer possessing reed-like fronds, and trees displaying leaves in unusual hues resembling sunset.

Dragonkin vaults

Hidden across Ashenfall are numerous dragonkin vaults, ancient facilities containing lost knowledge and technological wonders. These vaults are protected by guardians created by the dragonkin Lacrussa, using refined rune essence.

Inhabitants

Garou

Garou are bipedal lion-like beings who once worshipped the moon goddess Lougrim. Their society is divided between noble-born (larger, stronger, capable of magic) and common-born.

Amalgamated

Humans and other creatures affected by the Anima Twist can develop elemental mutations, becoming known as the "Amalgamated". These traits can include fiery skin, leafy hair, or other magical characteristics. A newcomer to the continent is unlikely to change, but each generation born on Ashenfall carries a chance of becoming Amalgamated. Throughout Ashenfall's history, the Amalgamated faced persecution from "pure" humans.

Goblins

Goblins are green-skinned humanoids who were brought from the mainland by their "God of War" Bandos, during the Third Age. They were abandoned in Ashenfall when he retreated from his battle against Velgar; they now worship Velgar as their new "Big High War God".

Ogres

Ogres are large humanoids who sought refugees from war. They were turned into zogres when Imaru infected the region with necrotic energy.

Dragons

Dragons (Draconis rex) are a dangerous race of reptiles with wings and the ability to use a fiery breath attack. After being cursed by the Elder God to guard her most powerful artefact, a creed of dragonkin known as the Dactyl wished to create a race that would be similar to them, but without suffering the Curse's effects. In Ashenfall, a group of dragonkin refugees known as the Cabal would also create and empower their own dragons, using them as slaves. Today, they roam across Ashenfall, all servants of Kuldra. Every dragon currently living on the continent descends from Kuldra. They fall into two tiers, with the lesser green, blue and red dragons found across Ashenfall weaker than the named generals.

Undead

Undead are creatures that have died and were reanimated through magic. These creatures resides within Fellhollow, controlled by the dragon general Imaru.

Humans

Human were among the first inhabitants of Gielinor and Ashenfall, brought over by Guthix. Although they were seemingly wiped out in Ashenfall, today an expedition had led new humans to explore and reside in Ashenfall.

Elves

Elves are pale humanoids brought to Gielinor by their goddess . Some had travelled to Ashenfall, exploring and even settling within the region.

KotHaar

KotHaar are lava creatures that were left in Umbral Sands by the Elder Gods to guard the Lens.

History

Creation

During the creation of Gielinor, the Elder Gods shaped Ashenfall for the sole purpose in filtering and venting the impure, wild anima they wished to keep separate from the stream of anima that nourished their eggs, giving rise to the Anima Twist that pervades the continent. Servitors accompanied them to Gielinor and stood guard over Ashenfall's hidden treasures long before any other race reached its shores. These guardians had once belonged to the but broke away from the collective mind of their race to take up a duty of their own, the protection of the Lens, a device that regulates the temperature of the sun so that life may thrive. These servitors became known as the KotHaar.

Discovery

During the , the god of balance, Guthix, discovered Ashenfall and explored it with some of his followers. After some time, they founded a village in Bramblemead Valley to settle in and explore the wondrous continent. Here, he found the land was rich with unique anima. Guthix discovered strange rocks hovering through the air. Sensing that the stones held magical properties, Guthix took instant interest and began to experiment on them with several of the humans. He took great joy in the work, and the strange rocks that would become known as rune essence and his early experiments seemed to lift his usually grim demeanour. After several experiments and failures, Guthix began to expand his experiments, bringing the to assist him. He was finally successful, binding the air itself into the essence, creating the first air rune. His followers on Ashenfall soon began Runecrafting themselves before any on the mainland even knew of runes. Guthix would then travel to the mainland to share his discovery there, using the Stone of Jas to create more and stored them for his followers to use there. On Ashenfall, the Guthixians that travelled there with him would start forming small settlements and villages over time.

As the humans grew to inhabit their new homes, a strange phenomenon began to occur. Their beards turned to leaves, their skin glowed like fire, and some took on the qualities of the elements, becoming Amalgamated and gaining elemental abilities. These Amalgamated humans were viewed as "impure" and "imperfect" by some of the human settlers there, suffering persecution and even being murdered by the humans who feared them in an event known as the Schism. When Guthix returned, he was horrified to learn of the widespread persecution and slaughter of the Amalgamated humans. As such, he took some of the humans with him, those who had not fallen to cruel prejudices. He would then task the Wild Knights, an order of skilled humans that were safeguarding the Amalgamated humans, to uphold their oath in protecting both the humans from the wild, and the wild from the humans. As he left, he placed a veil over Ashenfall, hoping to hide the continent before he, too, hid himself. But, the veil was not as good as the god had hoped, as the Cabal, a group of dragonkin and outcasts among their kind settled in Ashenfall in the early second age Only five dragonkin are known to have been part of the group. Lacrussa was a Dactyl scientist who gained the elemental power of ice and water, created the vault guardians, and experimented with dragons. Viika was a "time swept" seer with prophetic abilities. Brakka was a Nodon architect who gained the elemental power of earth and built a great tower. Rasthin was a Necrosyrte who drew the elemental power of fire from Ashenfall's mysterious vents and created a device known as "Jas Moksha" to share elemental powers with her fellow Cabal members. Avisk was an Aughra who gained the elemental power of air and experimented on the minds of living creatures. Avisk lives on to this day as the Dreaming Stone. Like their kin in the mainland, the Cabal would experiment in creating more and new draconic creatures, such as dragon wolves. They had marvelled at the wild anima flowing through the continent on arrival and set out to claim it. To draw on it they built the Harmonic Resonator, a device that harnessed raw anima and granted them immense power, and on that power they forged an empire.

The God Wars

Ashenfall was mostly untouched by the world until the Third Age. On the mainland, the God Wars raged on, forcing plenty of people to seek refugee elsewhere. Saradominist missionaries arrived on the continent, intent on escaping the God Wars and on winning the abandoned Guthixians over to their faith. Unbeknownst to the Saradominists, Zamorakian spies were also in their midst, posing as labourers and other menial servants. The missionaries lived near the cliffs, where they could look back towards their old home but also mixed with the villagers of Bramblemead, eventually setting up the Temple of Saradomin in place of their previous encampment. The first Runecrafting Guild was created on the continent, where Saradominist wizards of the guild would research the magic of the land. Initially, the Saradominists and Guthixians maintained a symbolic alliance known as the Bronze Advisors, represented by bronze armour. During this period, druids wore pins of copper while Saradominist priests wore tin pins, materials that combined to form bronze. This alliance was protected by bronze-armoured warriors who upheld traditions and punished those who blasphemed against either faith. The Bronze Advisors offered counsel from both Saradominist and Guthixian viewpoints, order and balance side by side. Meanwhile, the Zamorakians, having formed a cult known as the Children of Shadows, plotted in secret, recognising the potential of the dragonkin vaults, hoping to bring a weapon home with them. Their hold over the region was further secured when a young Zamorakian discovered a mithril seam in what would become known as the Dowdun Mountains. Rather than weaponise it, the Children of Shadows treated mithril as a tool of influence, keeping it scarce to preserve its value as a means of bribery.

The garou, a race originally from Antumnos, arrived on Ashenfall from the mainland, led by their moon goddess, Lougrim. They settled primarily in the highlands of what would later be known as Ghornfell. The garou's arrival created a new dynamic on Ashenfall. The garou maintained their territories and traditions. The garou society was built upon strength and practised the sacred tradition of the right of challenge, where leadership was earned through combat prowess rather than birthright. The garou initially claimed The northern territories of Ghornfell, a region rich in natural resources. Early encounters between humans and the garou were violent as they would attack travellers on sight before an initial treaty was made, this was a misunderstanding on the garou's part as they thought the humans consented to being hunted. Their presence and continued devotion to their goddess fostered envy among the abandoned Guthixian humans even as an initial peace treaty was made. The treaty opened a few years of peace in which the humans of Bramblemead and the garou of Ghornfell traded. Brakka, at some point during this period, used the garou for slave labour to build his tower before learning how to siphon anima and gaining the power to control the earth itself, making slave labour obsolete. The timing of the tower's construction is not recorded, and the enslavement may have taken place either before or during the Human-Garou War.

Things seemed peaceful, and the God Wars were contained to the mainland. However, the people of Ashenfall would soon find their own conflict. There was a power shift, at first amongst themselves, with Saradominist leaders attempting to overthrow the Guthixian druids and push them elsewhere within the continent. The bronze-clad inquisition applied Saradomin's laws whenever they conflicted with Guthixian practice, and they went from purging shrines of monsters to purging them of Guthixians. The Duke of Brynmoor, on the counsel of his priests, expelled the remaining Guthixian followers to the forests and caves. The druids rebelled, and the bronze-clad enforcers were sent against them rather than the saradomists. Eventually the Guthixian influence on Ashenfall fell to nothing as the saradomnists set their eyes on conquest.

The Human-Garou War

The early truce with the Guthixians held for now but with the saradomnists in charge, the truce could not hold. The Saradominist humans had started to encroach on garou lands in search of iron and other resources that had been depleted in the Bramblemead Valley. As the humans cleared the area of trees and animals to mine for iron, they attracted the attention of garou hunting parties. These parties viewed the presence of the Saradominists as a slight against their sovereignty. Small skirmishes between the hunting parties and the humans became commonplace, but they rarely resulted in significant casualties due to their bronze armour. However, these small skirmishes escalated into an all-out war when Kessel, a fire-touched amalgam, struck down a young garou prince.

The war between both sides was at a stalemate as the Whispering Swamp acted as a buffer between the two factions, often drowning and ensnaring those who attempted to breach the no man’s land. The humans, feeling desperate, devised a plan to goad the god of war, Bandos, into joining the conflict. Saradominist priests met with emissaries of Bandos, leveraging their knowledge of an ancient slight between the garou goddess and Bandos that occurred aeons ago on another world. They proposed an alliance to confront the garou and their goddess. Eager to take revenge on Lougrim, Bandos agreed to the plan and arrived at Ashenfall with his followers. With the Bandosians' assistance, the humans began pushing the garou back, forcing their goddess to form an alliance with the dragonkin and place herself in their servitude for future experimentations. In turn, the dragonkin unleashed their creations in the battle to support the garou, including massive wyrms that darkened the sky and dragons with elemental powers. This shift changed the tide of the war, forcing Bandos to personally confront one of the dragon generals, Velgar, who was stationed atop Brakka's great tower. The war god stormed the tower and challenged Velgar to single combat, but the dragon's stone-touched flesh turned his blows aside, and though Bandos cut a great scar down Velgar's side the wound was not fatal. In a display of arrogance, Bandos then cast aside his armour and protective wards and came close to throttling the dragon bare-handed. Velgar broke the hold by calling a venom-laden rock down from the sky against the god's temple, then caught the staggered Bandos in a breath of anima-infused poison that sapped his strength.

Weakened and fearing death, Bandos made a "tactical retreat", abandoning his followers on Ashenfall. Velgar was left wounded by the exchange, and his blood, warped by the magic his queen had granted him, had become a toxin. In jubilant rage he spilled it across the fertile plains in the south-east of Ghornfell, a refuge where garou fleeing the conflict had grown fields of wheat and barley, and the corrupted land became the Bloodblight Swamp. The war also claimed the life of Ulv, a mute outcast of Bramblemead, and the finest hunter in the region. he was friends with the necromancer Ravanna The two were inseparable, and Ulv's death at the hands of a garou patrol left Ravanna grief-stricken. Then, using the souls of slain garou, her grief-born curse tore through the Stormtouched Highlands, twisting the clouds into screaming things filled with fractured spirits. The resulting storm destroyed countless settlements instantly and has raged ever since. Bandos' retreat led to confusion among his goblin followers. At first the goblins continued their war without Bandos' guidance, but soon as they began to recognise the strength of the dragons and the defeat of Bandos, the abandoned goblins began to worship the dragons, naming Velgar as their new Big High War God.

Uneasy Peace

With the garou victory, Lougrim would keep the peace with the humans while assisting the dragonkin in their experimentation and the dragonkin returned the dragons to their chains and servitude. As a goddess in tune with the natural world, Lougrim was a source of great vitality, and the dragonkin drew her blood and stored it in urns hidden across the continent, intending it to be the linchpin of their great endeavours. The dragonkin bred dragons to safeguard what they had built, servants and weapons made to obey. Kuldra was shaped and tested and broken to the purpose of birthing a perfect race. She was not necessarily the first dragon the Cabal made, and others may have come before her, but she was the one they settled upon, and the dragonkin recorded only those experiments that proved at least partly successful. She is the oldest of the dragon generals. Lacrussa bred the clutch she came from, and Avisk meddled with it, working rune essence into the eggs in an attempt to give the dragons a greater mind, one that might function as a swarm. Every other subject died. Kuldra alone survived, and she survived changed, growing the many heads that Lacrussa insisted no sane dragon should ever bear. Her own first offspring were judged failures and destroyed. Only then did the dragonkin turn Lougrim's blood on Kuldra herself, feeding it to her and raising her to the brink of divinity. The dragon was therefore the work of two dragonkin at once, carrying the energy of rune essence and Avisk's swarm in her skulls and a goddess's divinity in her blood. Kuldra was made to lay a multitude of eggs, and clutch after clutch was taken from her before she ever saw them. She is mother to the dragons active on Ashenfall today, Velgar among them, though she knows that brood only as blood and holds no attachment to any of it. Fuzan came later, and Kuldra kept that egg and raised the whelp herself, the one dragon she mothered in any real sense. Lacrussa recorded the red-scaled whelp as a disappointment and wondered aloud whether the fault lay with the father. For the time being, the humans and garou held an uneasy truce.

Despite this truce, the garou remained hostile towards the human settlers who were leaving the southern settlements in search of new lives elsewhere. Humans made their way through an underground passage and emerged in Fellhollow, where the dragons Imaru and Xikotal befriended them, helping them raise their city and assisting them in other means, where Imaru would use her magic to bring in rains, while Xikotal would calm the winds, in exchange for a few sheep and cows. Imaru, whom dragonkin experiments had denied the motherhood she craved, also placed a "Blessing" upon the settlers, a magical bond that let her protection reach them anywhere. Some of the Wild Knights would join in settling within Fellhollow, creating Silverthorn Keep to the west. The ogres, one of Bandos' abandoned followers, settled peacefully in Emberwood alongside the humans there, building a camaraderie that promised a new age of prosperity.

Not every settlement was founded in good faith. The Rasmodels, nobility from the mainland, schemed in the Temple Woods and Bramblemead until their operations were exposed and the family was exiled to Dowdun Reach. During this time, the Children of Shadows had planted themselves into the Rasmodels house, where they would attempt to influence the noble household, only to be slowly turned into bodyguards and warriors of the Rasmodels. Over time the Rasmodel family came to dominate the Children of Shadows entirely, with Milliburn Rasmodel eventually rising to become Lord Rasmodel, Master of Dowdun Reach. Growing paranoid about Fellhollow's intentions, he established an order of knights outfitted with steel forged from coal and iron given to him by Xikotal as a gesture of goodwill. They would be formed into the Shadow Knights, and eventually the Black Knights.

Far to the east, in the sands, the dragonkin Avisk pursued a design of his own. He plotted to make himself immortal. He had already completed his work on the Avisk crystals, allowing him to preserve his consciousness within them, but he also began developing a means of transferring himself into a perfect vessel, a kalphite queen. Where his fellow Aughra sought to escape the dragonkin curse by moving their minds into a single new body, Avisk meant to become the swarm entire. His work, however, would soon be interrupted by the coming hostilities.

Dragon Rebellion

Near the end of the Third Age, the Dragon Rebellion began when Kuldra led the dragons against their dragonkin masters. In the years leading up to her betrayal, Kuldra sought counsel and may have considered other options. Ultimately, however, she was swayed by the advice of her most trusted ally, Velgar, who insisted that brutality was the only language their masters would understand. Velgar, however, also had personal reasons to support the rebellion, having suffered as a beast of burden under Brakka, despite his innate combat prowess. When the war against the goblins and humans brought dragons into the conflict, Velgar was finally allowed to join the battle. He slaughtered without mercy, decimating settlements and entire platoons with barely any effort. However, once the fighting subsided, Brakka rewarded Velgar's brutality with further servitude, forcing him to haul materials for reconstruction efforts. When Velgar was recruited by Kuldra to overthrow their master, he immediately accepted her scheme, becoming her first ally aside from Fuzan.

The rebellion proved successful. Kuldra confronted Brakka at his tower, crushing him and consuming his anima-rich soul to steal his power. After defeating him, she bestowed his elemental mastery upon Velgar, teaching him to absorb the power of the anima font and transforming him into a dragon infused with earth magic. As a final mockery, Velgar claimed Brakka's monument as his lair. This tower would come to be known as Brakka's Folly. Kuldra turned on the dragonkin who had made her and devoured them one after another until only Rasthin was left alive. In desperation Rasthin released the Harmonic Resonator against her, a cataclysm meant to destroy the Dragon Queen. Ashenfall was broken by it and Kuldra survived. After freeing herself and other dragons from dragonkin control, Kuldra set her sights on expanding her power. She would challenge Lougrim next, though not in the fair combat that garou tradition demanded. The battle between Kuldra and Lougrim was cataclysmic, causing the entire continent to buckle beneath their fury. Kuldra emerged the victor through ambush. Garou accounts long held that the two met in honest combat, a version of events that the Forbidden Scrolls recovered by the Moon Garou would later expose as false. Kuldra never called a challenge at all. She waited until Lougrim had drained her strength protecting garou settlements from the dragons' flames, then fell upon the exhausted goddess and gave her no chance to resist. Her many heads tore the goddess limb from limb, swallowing the pieces of her divine flesh. The victory crowned her as the new High Queen of the Garou and earned her the name God Eater. While much of garou society bowed to the new queen out of fear, others fled, abandoning their homes to escape her tyranny. These dissenters looked to the moon for guidance and became the Moon Garou. Their long migration carried them over woodland and mountain range at the cost of many lives, and ended in the deserts of Umbral Sands as Avisk was finishing his work.

The rebellion cut Avisk's work short. Plundering the stores of the late Lacrussa, he built the Dreaming Stone, a crystal vessel vast enough to contain the whole of his mind, and prepared to cast his thoughts into the Kalphite Queen and command the swarm through her. As the rebels closed in, Avisk transferred himself into the stone with the scheme still unfinished, forfeiting his body so that his intellect would endure. Of the Cabal, he alone escaped in this way while his colleagues perished or went into hiding. Avisk built more than one such vessel. Copies of the crystal, each holding his consciousness, remain across Umbral Sands, and destroying one only forces his mind into another. The Dreaming Stone itself was swallowed by the sands, where it would lie for an age.

The Golden Age of the Moon garou

The garou are woodland creatures by nature, and the dunes tested them sorely. For a time they wandered godless, though a god already dwelt amongst the dunes undetected. Elidinis, a goddess of the rivers, growth, and fertility, had arrived on Ashenfall at some unknown time and settled within Umbral Sands. The two peoples remained strangers until the day a cub vanished into the desert. The searchers discovered the cub unharmed at an oasis no garou had ever mapped, in the company of a singing, silver-furred stranger whom they mistook for one of their own kind. Elidinis presented herself as a river goddess associated to the moon, from a different , and the Moon Garou soon gave her their devotion. Garou histories preserved her under the name El-Idahn-Inees. Under her care the Moon Garou mastered desert life, learning from her how to build in stone and raise crops from the arid ground. To ward off supernatural dangers, she entrusted them with the mirrors, each carrying a sliver of solid moonlight at its core. The mirrors are of elder creation, though they are not elder artefacts. Their camps swelled into the giant walled cities of the Old Kingdom, where bright tapestries hung above the streets as shelter from the blowing sand, libraries kept the accumulated writings of their people, and festivals filled the year with light, song, and feasting. In shaped stone the Moon Garou raised dwellings, temples, and monuments meant to endure long after their makers. Elidinis would then depart Gielinor, trusting that the civilisation she had raised could now stand without her. The Old Kingdom flourished without her, entering a golden age in which a people once defined by the hunt turned instead to art, scholarship, and magic.

Destruction of Settlements

While the exiles built their new lives in the desert, the lands they had fled did not fare well. With Lougrim replaced by Kuldra, the uneasy truce between the garou and humans would not last. Kuldra had a deep hatred for humanity, holding them weak, petty and flawed, and she called for their destruction. The dragons began to decimate human settlements, burning cities to the ground, murdering lords and knights, and forcing survivors to flee into the wilderness and other regions.

Fellhollow

Within Fellhollow, Imaru and Xikotal defied the Dragon Queen, sheltering the settlements from the destruction. The Blessing that bound the dragons to their people would prove to be both gift and curse. Kuldra herself descended upon the region, demanding humanity's destruction, But they declined. Imaru, Xikotal and the settlers would fight against Kuldra in hope to defend their home. But she proved too powerful, aside from defenders, Xikotal fell in the battle that followed along with his rider. The Dragon Queen tore his heart from his chest and ate it before Imaru's eyes, sparing Imaru so that she would live with the loss. Consumed by grief, Imaru sought a way to bring Xikotal back from the dead, seeking the assistance of the necromancer Ravanna. However, Ravanna did not have the power to resurrect him. Instead, she proposed creating a curse born of Imaru's sorrow and grief, one that would give her the power to consume the Dragon Queen's soul and exact her revenge.

The curse was not enough, Kuldra had proven more powerful than imagined, defeating Imaru with ease. Even in death, Imaru craved revenge for her fallen mate and children. She wedged herself in the using the curse Ravanna had given her, fuelled by her own sheer rage and will. While in the underworld, she drank from the to gain more power and claw her way back from death. However, this resurrection came with a terrible cost. She became twisted with an insatiable hunger for souls and turned against the very people she had once protected. The "Blessing" that linked them was now used against them, and their souls were pulled from their still-living bodies. These soulless husks began to reanimate. Soon the settlements in Fellhollow would fall, and the region would become a land of rot and wither where the undead roamed. The Wild Knights were pushed back towards their keep, while Emberwood sealed itself behind a barrier. Dowdun Reach, shielded by the Dowdun Mountains, sealed all connecting pathways to Fellhollow and posted guards at the crypt as an early warning against breach. Four priests of Saradomin, Zamorak, Armadyl, and Guthix united to keep the Withering both in and out of the town. Those who were disciples of Imaru came to believe she was blessing the humans, willingly transforming them into undead. The necrotic magic spread like a virus, eventually turning even the ogres into zogres and infecting the Wild Knights as well. Those who tried to escape found the passage to Dowdun sealed off. Ravanna, the one who cursed Imaru, would attempt to fix her mistake and seal the dragon away. She split the curse into three fragments, in hope that in the future, someone can use the power of the curse against Imaru to put her soul to rest.

Dowdun Reach

Arcane researchers among the Children of Shadows recovered the buried Dreaming Stone and bore it back to the keep. The recovered vessel brought instability alongside its power. A faction within sought to weaponise it, while Archmage Alric' used it to power an infernal demon gate, which failed, causing its demonic souls to bleed into the fortress walls. The Black Knights would defend the region against the dragons, under standing orders that any draconic presence beyond the lesser blue dragons be shot on sight. Though the stone had come to power much of the keep itself, Lord Rasmodel, whose mind it had preyed upon for decades, ultimately took his warhammer to the Dreaming Stone and broke it. The consequences proved worse than the affliction. The energies released by the shattering, together with the parasitic remnants of a demon, seized the lord and remade him as the Black Knight Titan, a being part Rasmodel, part Avisk, and part avernic, who stood guard over the passage to Umbral Sands until the Sixth Age.

Umbral Sands

The Moon Garou of Umbral Sands met their own destruction. Fuzan, Kuldra's youngest child, owed his fire to his mother, who had taken it from the dragonkin's Harmonic Resonator, would begin to terrorise the garou. Deep inside a volcano, Fuzan encountered an otherworldly entity of celestial fire who claimed godhood, a being the garou would come to know as the Sun Demon. The Forbidden Scrolls place her arrival just after Fuzan's own, and the young dragon became her devoted worshipper. She schooled him in mastery over fire, and with that power he bent the KotHaar, to his will. Fuzan also collapsed the underground tunnels by which the KotHaar had once returned to the Elder Kiln, cutting them off from their cycle of rebirth. He also ordered them to move the Lens to his lair, where he would use the device to increase the suns' temperature over Umbral Sands, turning the region into a scorching desert. He brought down the cities of the Old Kingdom, destroying even the monuments in which their history was kept, and the survivors split into far-flung tribes, reasoning that no single hunt could catch them all. Rather than exterminate the remnant, Fuzan branded the garou with his seal. The Mark siphoned their strength to feed his power, and in return most were spared his fire.

Rediscovery

During the 13th year of the Sixth Age, with Guthix dead and the veil that concealed Ashenfall weakened by time, the continent was rediscovered. An expedition was assembled, and adventurers from across the realm answered the call, among them Dionysius the Wise Old Man, Vannaka the Slayer master, Zanik of the , Doric the master smith, and Cathan, a rising rookie forging his reputation. The voyage was cut short as the ship neared Ashenfall. A massive green dragon descended upon it, destroying the expedition and leaving only a handful of survivors. Those who lived washed ashore and began to explore the land, scavenging what they could to construct a lodestone, an anchor to the mainland and a beacon to call for reinforcements. Word spread once the lodestone was activated, and new and old adventurers arrived from the mainland to face the draconic threat and confront the Dragon Queen. While Dionysius, Vannaka, Doric, and Zanik prepared for their arrival, Cathan set off alone, determined to slay the dragon Velgar without aid.

Once a base is established and resources are gathered, the search for Cathan begins. He has recruited goblins to his cause and learned of a challenge horn, but he is captured by a garou and sacrificed before Velgar before the materials can be gathered. Cathan assists in the crafting of the challenge horn regardless, despite being dead. Velgar is confronted and slain, bringing peace to Brynmoor and avenging those the dragon killed.

After Velgar's defeat, Death arrives in Fellhollow with Postie Pete and Muncher and opens the way into the Forgotten Temple, a location he claims so that he might speak with the adventurers. Dionysius supplies the incantation that opens the door, and Death asks that Fellhollow be entered and that Cathan be found. Cathan is in Death's employ, and has been set to finding a way to confront Imaru and end her torment. The seal placed upon her is uncovered, the fragments are located and their power harnessed, and the undead dragon is defeated, freeing Fellhollow, Imaru, and the tormented souls.

After a period of rest, Death speaks of a colleague waiting in Umbral Sands, though the way onward is blocked in Dowdun Reach. The Wise Old Man and Postie Pete give greeting on arrival in the region and explain the barrier that bars the way to the next. The fortress is explored, and Vannaka, Zanik, and Doric are assisted in their search for the pieces of the Dreaming Stone. The barrier is bound to the stone itself, so the only road to the desert runs through repairing Avisk. With the thirteen shards recovered and the stone made whole, Avisk lowers the barrier himself and thinks little of the effort, then invites the adventurers to surrender their minds to him so that he might deal with the Black Knight Titan in their stead. The offer is declined, and the Black Knight Titan, the transformed Lord Rasmodel, is fought and put to rest, opening the path to Umbral Sands once Doric has opened the door.

With the way opened, the desert is entered. An envoy asks that his oasis camp nearby be visited, and Fuzan is seen on patrol over the region before the Alcarrid Oasis is reached. There, Icthlarin is attempting to obtain the mirror lenses from the Moon Garou tribes so that he might raise a relay to focus a beam of sunlight on Fuzan's Tower and open the way to the dragon. The Moon Garou refuse him, and he asks instead that their trust be won and their lenses acquired. The search crosses the whole of the desert, through kalphites and KotHaar, ancient secrets, and strange sights, until all three lenses are gathered. The mirror relay is raised and the way to Fuzan's Tower is opened, though not without struggle. Hordes of KotHaar hold the tower, but the summit is reached and the red dragon is slain. Icthlarin is given the head of Fuzan, and names the final challenge, Queen Kuldra herself.

Kuldra is gathering the remnants of the Harmonic Resonator to unleash a second cataclysm, one that would consume the whole of Gielinor. Guided by Saradomin, General Zilyana has come to Ashenfall seeking champions to face the Dragon Queen and stop the end of the world.

Notable characters

Expedition members

  • Cathan - A privileged youth who lost a leg in a childhood adventure, but was trained by mentors to become a warrior. He came to Ashenfall seeking adventure.
  • Vannaka - A mysterious slayer master trained under . His origins are unknown, but he seems to have some connection to Ashenfall.
  • Zanik - A cave goblin who was the first of her kind to brave sunlight and meet humans. Now searches for a lost tribe on Ashenfall.
  • Wise Old Man (Dionysius) - Once a legendary adventurer who performed great deeds but turned to crime in his later years.
  • Doric - A dwarven blacksmith and legendary craftsman.

Allies

  • Death - A guardian of Guthix and the Grim Reaper of Gielinor. Death arrived to Ashenfall and request assistance from the Adventurer(s) in dealing with Imaru and the undead corruption in Fellhollow
  • Muncher - Death's undead hellhound pet who accompanied the reaper to Fellhollow.
  • Postie Pete - A postman of Gielinor who arrived to Fellhollow, informing the adventurer(s) on Wither and soul rifting.
  • Icthlarin - The Menophite god of the dead, who arrived to assist the Moon Garou and their blight.

Native rulers

  • Velgar - A green dragon, Kuldra's progeny and one of her most feared generals. He rules over Brynmoor and Ghornfell
  • Imaru - An undead blue dragon who rules over the Fellhollow region.
  • Milliburn Rasmodel - Also known as Lord Rasmodel and the Black Knight Titan is the leader of the Black Knights and Master of Dowdun Reach.
  • Fuzan - A red dragon and one of Kuldra's generals. He rules over Umbral Sands
  • Kuldra - Also known as the Dragon Queen and the God Eater, she devoured the garou goddess Lougrim, and now rules over the dragons and garou.

Past rulers

  • Lougrim - The goddess of the garou, she ruled over the garou territories in Ghornfell before being devoured by Kuldra.
  • Lord of Bramblemead - A lord who resides in the Keep of Blue Flames, who watches over the village and surrounding area of the region.

Bloodblight Swamp.name: Bloodblight Swamp
Bloodblight Swamp.lead: Bloodblight Swamp is a hazardous region located in the eastern part of Ghornfell on the continent of Ashenfall. The area is characterised by its poisonous green mists, corrupted water, toxic environment, and exploding plant traps, all created by the blood of General Velgar. Players are recommended to bring an antipoison potion when travelling through the region, as entering the swamp automatically fills the poison debuff bar up and eventually will poison/damage the player.
Bloodblight Swamp.html:
Bloodblight Swamp is a hazardous region located in the eastern part of Ghornfell on the continent of Ashenfall. The area is characterised by its poisonous green mists, corrupted water, toxic environment, and exploding plant traps, all created by the blood of General Velgar. Players are recommended to bring an antipoison potion when travelling through the region, as entering the swamp automatically fills the poison debuff bar up and eventually will poison/damage the player.

History

The Bloodblight Swamp was once a very different place. The garou seeking refuge from the war with the goblins retreated here and found peace. They farmed the fertile plains, raised families, and made this place their home. They spent their days farming wheat and barley safe from the war. But it wouldn't remain untouched forever. The god Bandos stormed Brakka's Folly and challenged General Velgar to a battle to the death. Bandos, full of pride and underestimating the dragon's strength, chose a greataxe to fight Velgar. Despite Velgar's rock-like hide, Bandos managed to cut a great scar down his side. Feeling confident, Bandos threw aside his weapon, armour and protective ward, moving in to wrestle the great dragon. He nearly succeeded. Bandos wrapped his arms around the dragon's neck. Velgar, in a bid to escape, called down a poison-filled rock from the heavens and cast it at Bandos, striking him in the temple. As the god reeled, he released Velgar, allowing the dragon to breathe a jet of anima-infused poison at Bandos. Bandos breathed in the toxins and felt weakness for the first time in centuries. The god retreated rather than face death; a decision he framed as "tactical" rather than cowardice. Velgar, victorious but still enraged from the battle, spilled his blood over the surrounding landscape, forever corrupting the plains and garou within with his hate-filled venom.

Bramblemead Valley.lead: Bramblemead Valley is a power level 2 area in Ashenfall, Brynmoor located east of Temple Woods.
Bramblemead Valley.html:
Bramblemead Valley is a power level 2 area in Ashenfall, Brynmoor located east of Temple Woods.

Description

Bramblemead Valley is located in the south-western region of Ashenfall, south of the Whispering Swamp and west of the Fractured Plains. The valley contains the village of Bramblemead, which is now abandoned and overrun with monsters. Goblins occupy the region, and rats infest the ruins. The once-fertile farmland is now bloodstained.

The valley landscape is predominantly green and forested, with several waterways running through it.

History

Bramblemead Valley was founded in the First Age by the god Guthix and his followers. During the Third Age, most of the settlement converted to the worship of Saradomin.

Under Saradominist influence, the Keep of Blue Flames was constructed in the architectural style favoured by Saradomin's followers, featuring an ordered shape to symbolize the god of order. The keep was governed by a local lord under the guidance of the high priest.

The valley was once a centre of human activity and learning in Ashenfall, with institutions dedicated to magical research and monster hunting. Eventually, the area was abandoned and overrun by hostile creatures.

Following certain incidents involving cats and crossbow limbs, a superstition developed in Bramblemead that it was bad luck to house cats and crossbows together. The supposed reasoning ranged from practical concerns about feline safety to increasingly absurd fears, including the notion that cats might somehow develop opposable thumbs and weaponize crossbows against their owners. What began as harmless folklore took a darker turn when the conflict with the garou intensified. As Bramblemead's demand for crossbows increased dramatically, families faced a choice between keeping their pets or acquiring the weapons they needed for defence. Most chose the latter. Over time, domestic cats became increasingly rare on Bramblemead's streets. Local folklore later attributed Bramblemead's destruction to feline revenge, though most historians dismiss such claims. Not all cats faced the same fate. Mittens, unlike most of his Bramblemead contemporaries, lived comfortably in his blacksmith's forge and never learned to fear crossbows. The superstition eventually ended in Fellhollow with the introduction of steel crossbow limbs. The superior durability of steel construction apparently eliminated whatever problems had sparked the original belief, and cats once again found acceptance in human households. The dragon Xikotal became particularly fond of feline company, surrounding his lair with hundreds of cats whose purring helped lull him to sleep.

Chaktan Kara.name: Chaktan Kara
Chaktan Kara.lead: Chaktan Kara is the dragonkin vault found in the Stormtouched Highlands. It can be reached by following the river upstream. Upon reaching the end of the river, there are vines that need to be cut through, and then stone boulders that need to be cleared. Walkthrough

  • Entryway, to the right (North is a locked door, the end room).
  • Main entryway (looking south the stairs with the bars at the top are where the lever is to open the final door, the hallway has a patrolling vault guardian hulk.
  • Heading down the southern hallway, the room to the left has two giant rats and a treasure chest hidden behind the stairs.
  • Continuing down the hall, turn right around the corner to enter a large multi-level room. Beware, there are three vault guardian hulks; use the stairs to your advantage to either range them or put them into a chokepoint to take them on one at a time. If engaging with melee, it is advised to cast Tempest Shield and Enchant Weapon: Fire before entering if you have them.
  • Below the entrance to the large room, there is another chest hidden there. Exit the room through the southern door.
  • There are three fire traps in the hall; time dodge rolls past each set, and they can heavily damage you if caught inside. Continue following the hall to reach the next area.
  • There is a spike room, to the west is a small room with a rat in it, you can use the spikes to dispatch it, otherwise there is no loot there, continue up the stairs on the north side.
  • Continue straight down the hall; going west is a dead end, and there are two rats to fight. Just past the doorway is a room with three vault sentinels. They attack with ranged, so using cover with your own ranged attacks, or holding up a shield and countering, is very effective to take them out. It is also advisable to cast buffing spells before engagement as with any fight where you are outnumbered.
  • After defeating the guardians, you can grab a vault core, these are essential for high-level recipes and lodestones. Be careful as they weigh 50 kg and can easily overencumber you if you have also been looting other resources from the vault.
  • There is another chest to be found, just off to the left from the statue.
  • Continue east out of the room, careful of the traps. The fire can deal more damage than the spikes, but dodge rolls will get you safely past all of them. As the spikes are laid out in a diamond with the points against the walls, the spikes are thinnest there and thus easier to pass if sticking to the wall.
  • Once past the traps, you will be in a room with three routes (two clearly visible and one that can be missed), up the stairs to the end boss or south to some optional treasure. North contains a spike room with four rats and no treasure.
    • If you stand on the rubble seen in the image facing south, you can see an opening on the wall which can be reached with Windstep. Go there, and you will find the second vault core, some treasure, and a lever which you can pull to open a shortcut.
  • To get to the final boss, follow the stairs to the top, pull the lever, and go through the gate to the starting room that opens, and a new large door will open that contains the boss and his treasures.
  • There is a side path for additional treasure, going south first instead of up the stairs that lead to the boss, around the corner to the left is a lever, pull it to open a gate that is past the fire traps.
  • After pulling the lever, make your way past two fire traps.
  • Past the gate are two goblin runts waiting inside to ambush; however, they are much weaker enemies and should not pose much threat.
  • After disposing of the goblins, the treasure is just past some more spike traps.
  • Back to the main path behind the previously locked door awaits The vault overlord, who is a vault hulk but with much more health and damage. Remember to buff up and cast combat spells before entering to make the fight more manageable, and to save energy to block or dodge.
  • After defeating the vault overlord, you can grab the last vault core and loot the chest.
