Emberwood.name: Emberwood
Emberwood.lead: Emberwood is a ruined village in the Fellhollow region of Ashenfall. The village was protected by a divine barrier maintained by shrines to the gods: Saradomin, Guthix, Zamorak and Armadyl. Emberwood is a collapsed village surrounding a small lake that once powered the settlement's mill. All structures have missing roofs and are in a state of ruin. A large cemetery surrounds the cathedral. A smaller circular lake lies to the north-east, featuring a large stone with a Shrine of Saradomin. The village is sealed by a magical barrier that can only be opened by obtaining blessings from the god shrines located around the area.
Emberwood.html:
Emberwood is a ruined village in the Fellhollow region of Ashenfall. The village was protected by a divine barrier maintained by shrines to the gods: Saradomin, Guthix, Zamorak and Armadyl. Emberwood is a collapsed village surrounding a small lake that once powered the settlement's mill. All structures have missing roofs and are in a state of ruin. A large cemetery surrounds the cathedral. A smaller circular lake lies to the north-east, featuring a large stone with a Shrine of Saradomin. The village is sealed by a magical barrier that can only be opened by obtaining blessings from the god shrines located around the area.

History

The village was envisioned as a potential utopia where multiple faiths could work side by side, with both Amalgamated and non-Amalgamated villagers coexisting peacefully under the protection of two great dragons.

Emberwood was protected by two dragons: Imaru and Xikotal. Imaru's most faithful followers were branded with special marks that granted them enhanced health and longer lifespans, and she created purification water blessed with her magic to protect the population from illness and corruption.

When the withering curse struck the village, priests from all four faiths united to erect a protective barrier. Using the power of prayer from bones buried in the soil, they created a barrier of belief to contain the withered villagers. The barrier was bound to religious icons and could only be opened when all the shrines worked together. Imaru's grief and rage transformed the once-peaceful village into a prison, with a piece of the curse placed at its heart.

Locations

Cathedral

The cathedral contains a purifying pool and is surrounded by a large cemetery. A chest in the graveyard west of the cathedral spawns several skeletal enemies when opened for the first time.

The Mill

A collapsed mill that once utilised the central lake for power.

Ruined Homes

Several small collapsed homes and shacks shacks are scattered throughout the village. One shack north-east of the cathedral contains the thorny irit root and lazily-penned diary.

God Shrines

Armadyl's Shrine

Located south-west of Emberwood village, found in the middle of a small lake, guarded by three ghosts:

  • Suspicious ghost
  • Shady ghost
  • Snickering ghost

The shrine requires identifying a crime, perpetrator, and motive to unlock.

Guthix' Shrine

Located far west of Emberwood village at a large stone circle where a green dragon made its home. A chest is located behind one of the south-western standing stones.

On the southern side, inside one of the henges, is a spectral door that requires being soul rifted to enter. It leads to an area where soul stone can be mined, requiring a steel pickaxe.

Saradomin's Shrine

Located east of the barrier, the shrine is missing the symbol of Saradomin, which can be found within the water just west of the shrine.

Zamorak's Shrine

Located north-east of the barrier, within a church. Players must Windstep or build their way to the top in order to enter the church and activate the shrine.

Dragonkin Vault

Kalistrakthen Kara is located at the far western edge of the region, with a small pond featuring a rune essence geyser and nature spirit.

Factions

The Hoplites

The primary military force was composed of farmers and artisans rather than nobility, naming themselves after the legendary Saradominist hoplites from the world of Hallow. Through years of training, they developed exceptional unit cohesion, forming impenetrable shield walls and coordinated formations, with their training sessions concluding with communal barbeques hosted by retired hoplites. When the Withering began, however, the hoplites' unity became a fatal weakness as infected members turned on their comrades from within the ranks.

The Wild Knights

Elite warriors who ventured into dangerous territories to face monsters warped by the Anima Twist, with their mages employing magic pragmatically against threats that ordinary villagers were unaware of.

Children of Shadows

A Zamorakian cult whose self-proclaimed warlocks performed dark rites in darkened basements, though these rituals had no actual effect. Despite their ineffective rituals, the order made practical contributions, with member Sadia Vulketra forging the first steel gear in Fellhollow out of concern that they needed greater defensive strength against potential Saradominist threats.

Druids

Guthixian druids performed rituals around the standing stones, wearing enchanted amulets in hopes of strengthening their bond with nature.

Magical community

Despite having less funding than the tower to the south, Emberwood had a significant spellcasting community. The mages developed alternative methods to strengthen their magical abilities, with the amulet of Magic being particularly popular among practitioners.

Notable residents

Bilar Amaris

Bilar Amaris was a renowned hunter known for his skill with the bow and ability to take down nearly any prey.

His death, while resulting in a sparsely attended funeral, led to an important development in Emberwood's crafting traditions. The dragonhide armour he wore proved remarkably durable despite his fatal injuries. Villagers recovered the armour and leatherworkers studied and improved upon the design, eventually making green dragonhide armour standard equipment for the village's best hunters.

Fractured Plains.name: Fractured Plains
Fractured Plains.lead: The Fractured Plains is a power level 3 area in Ashenfall, found just north of the Whispering Swamp.
Fractured Plains.html:
The Fractured Plains is a power level 3 area in Ashenfall, found just north of the Whispering Swamp.

Description

The Fractured Plains is located in the eastern central region of Ashenfall, east of the Stormtouched Highlands and north of the Whispering Swamp. The region is characterised by reddish grass and lush forests with multiple paths running through it. A notable feature is the presence of a strange purple energy flow cutting through the northern part of the region.

The anima in this region is less stable than in Brynmoor, causing more pronounced Anima Twist effects. The local flora takes on the hues of dragonfire, creating a visual effect similar to an inferno when summer winds blow through the area.

A shattered tower stands in the distance, still containing ancient dragonkin magic. This structure serves as the lair of General Velgar, a dragon whose roars can be heard throughout the region.

The Fractured Plains gained their name from the cataclysmic battle between the goddess Lougrim and the Dragon Queen Kuldra. This conflict literally fractured the landscape as described in historical records: Using his newfound elemental powers, Brakka constructed a massive tower that would later become known as Brakka's Folly. Despite having abilities that could have benefited the entire continent, he chose to create a monument to his own glory. The construction of this tower relied not only on Brakka's elemental powers but also on the forced labour of garou slaves.

Atop a mesa in the Plains, something crystalline glistens in the moonlight, accompanied by a mournful sound carried on the wind, hinting at the presence of Elves at some point.. Garou regularly patrol the pathways, and wolves guard the woods, terrorbirds are present.

History

Upon discovering the continent of Ashenfall, the architect Brakka saw Ashenfall as an opportunity to create a new dragonkin empire similar to Orthen, one not chained by the conventions of the elder dragonkin. Rasthin taught Brakka how to obtain magical power from the anima vents located throughout the continent; Brakkka used this new technique to gain mastery over earth. Brakka used this new power, along with slave labour from the garou, to build a great tower, a monument to his hubris known as Brakka's Folly.

Brakka met his end in the very tower he had built, slain by the Dragon Queen, Kuldra After defeating Brakka, Kuldra absorbed his power bestowed it upon her loyal general, Velgar who had been used as a beast of burden after the Human-Garou War. As recompense, Velgar took Brakka's tower as his own, renaming it Velgar's Rise. One of the most defining moments in the history of the Fractured Plains was the battle between the Dragon Queen Kuldra and the garou goddess Lougrim. This fierce confrontation literally reshaped the landscape fracturing and reshaping it into what we see today, a great chasm surrounds Velgar's Rise. The culture of the garou changed significantly under dragon rule, becoming more brutal and focused on survival of the fittest rather than traditional values. Under Lougrim, they used to carefully select targets, but now the garou patrol the area, attacking anyone on sight.

Runecrafting Guild.name: Runecrafting Guild
Runecrafting Guild.lead: The Runecrafting Guild, also known as the Wizard's Guild, Wizard's Tower, and Magic Institute, was the centre of magic research, study, and experimentation for Saradominist wizards on Ashenfall. It is also the first known Runecrafting Guild in Gielinor's history, having been founded some time in the Third Age. Some Knights of Saradomin had to be permanently stationed at the guild to address the perils often created by the wizards. The wizards were rarely seen outside the guild, focused on creating and studying powerful spells. Nowadays, the guild is inhabited by goblins, like most of the Brynmoor region.

Stormtouched Highlands.html:
The Stormtouched Highlands is a power level 4 mountainous region located in the north-western part of Ashenfall. The area is characterised by a perpetual magical storm that strikes with hateful fury at any who walks these lands. The region is home to well-trained garou warriors and is littered with the bones of ancient wyrms created by the dragonkin Lacrussa.

History

The perpetual storm that gives the Highlands their name is the result of desperate sorcery used during a long, drawn-out war. The thunder is described as hateful and spiteful, striking any who walk the land as if driven by the vengeful fury of its long-dead caster.

The region was once home to gargantuan dragons, created through the "mad science" of the dragonkin Lacrussa. These titan wyrms were powerful enough that they could have ended the God Wars themselves. Fortunately, these creatures are no longer living, with only their massive bones remaining scattered throughout the highlands.

Temple Woods.lead: Temple Woods is an area in Ashenfall. It serves as the starting area for adventurers, and contains the Temple of Saradomin.
Temple Woods.html:
Temple Woods is an area in Ashenfall. It serves as the starting area for adventurers, and contains the Temple of Saradomin.

Description

Temple Woods is situated at the peak of a cliff overlooking the Bramblemead Valley. The main structure in this area is the Temple of Saradomin, which dates back to the Third Age. The temple's walls and stained glass windows remain intact despite their age. A faint trace of priestly magic keeps more dangerous elements from entering the temple.

North-west of the temple is a windmill. The timber creaks despite its sails no longer turning. At night, creatures patrol around the windmill's exterior.

History

The Temple Woods area was first settled during the Third Age by followers of Saradomin who arrived on the continent during a that affected much of the world. These settlers established a small settlement at the cliff's peak.

The expedition members eventually integrated with the villagers of Bramblemead Village, moving from their camps into the village. As the settlers abandoned their temporary structures, they began construction of the Temple of Saradomin.

Now, millennia later, the temple serves as a sanctuary against the wild frontiers of Ashenfall and functions as the home base of the current expedition team.

Whispering Swamp.name: Whispering Swamp
Whispering Swamp.lead: The Whispering Swamp is a power level 2 region in Ashenfall that serves as a natural buffer between the human territories of Brynmoor and the garou domain of Ghornfell. Named for the eerie whispers that bubble up from its fetid waters, the swamp holds memories of past conflicts in its murky depths.
Whispering Swamp.html:
The Whispering Swamp is a power level 2 region in Ashenfall that serves as a natural buffer between the human territories of Brynmoor and the garou domain of Ghornfell. Named for the eerie whispers that bubble up from its fetid waters, the swamp holds memories of past conflicts in its murky depths.

Description

The region is said to be haunted, and thick fog hangs over it, limiting visibility. Those who wander it at night speak of whispers bubbling up from the fetid water, and of a coldness that reaches beneath warm clothing into bone and blood. Ancient trees of spiteful nature wrap their roots around the bones of adventurers, villagers, and warriors alike, indifferent to goblin, human, or garou. journals tell of tiny stones that occasionally bubble to the surface, black as midnight and cold to the touch and an ancient horror walks the region.

Despite the dangers, the swamp is rich with resources for crafting. Globs of swamp tar collect in places, clay deposits are scattered throughout, and herbs such as harralander and marrentil grow. Swamp weed gathered here can be processed into textile, and bittercap mushrooms grow sparsely across the region, with greater abundance found within the Druid's Cave and western cave. The murky water hinders movement, and putrid rats infest the shallows. Goblin hunters keep sentries on ruins throughout the region. The region only contains one lore scrap - the torn journal page The region also houses a memorial candle for the Mirror, Mirror quest this item can be found in the eastern basin.

History

When war broke out between humans and garou, the swamps formed a natural boundary between the two factions. The muddy water was difficult to fight in, and neither side enjoyed the idea of drowning on the battlefield. Now, the swamp retains the memories of that conflict in its murky depths.

The necromancer Abraxus wandered the Whispering Swamps in his youth, drawn by the swamp's reputation as ancient and haunted and by a magic unlike any other part of Ashenfall. He sought forbidden secrets others dared not pursue, exploring its vaults and caves and battling goblins in the mists, yet never found the power he sought there.

In the Sixth Age

Prior to the events of Dragon Slayer, the explorer Cathan sought a "blue-flamed door" within the swamp with the help of the goblin Spitfoot, believing it held the secret to General Velgar's destruction.

A garou druid steals one of two halves of a Bandosian amulet containing a prophecy of Bandos, and flees to the swamps leaving the reliquary filled with fetid water and mud. Zanik, sensing a "strange presence in the swamps" near the ruins to the north-east, identifies the amulet as one of the war god's safeguards and warns of darker powers, older than the gods, that might claim it now that Bandos is dead.

The spirit of Kay is encountered in the swamp beside a drifted boat. An adventurer who tried to row out at the lake near the temple at Bramblemead, she was killed by a dragon's tail; the boat carried her remains into the swamp on its own.

Black Knight's Fortress.name: Black Knight's Fortress
Black Knight's Fortress.lead: Black Knight's Fortress is the seventh primary quest and the third in the main storyline of RuneScape: Dragonwilds. In this quest, the Player must delve into an ancient mountainous fortress after defeating the revenant dragon Imaru in order to gain access to the Umbral Sands.
Black Knight's Fortress.html:
Black Knight's Fortress is the seventh primary quest and the third in the main storyline of RuneScape: Dragonwilds. In this quest, the Player must delve into an ancient mountainous fortress after defeating the revenant dragon Imaru in order to gain access to the Umbral Sands.

Quest Overview

Walkthrough

Part I: The Dark Fortress...

Speak to Death in the Forgotten Temple. He will mention about how you did well in Fellhollow, but that there is more for you to do. A colleague of his is waiting for you in the Umbral Sands to help him, but instructs you to speak to Cathan to gather allies and investigate. You can find Cathan east of Fellhollow, near the ominous gatehouse in the south of Silverthorn Keep.

Speak to Cathan, who greets you, and he will comment about how the adventure never ends. He will then right to it and explain how he has been investigating the ominous gatehouse and, while it leads to some fortress, it is blocking the way to the Umbral Sands. He tells you how he wanted to scout out the place more all spooky-like, but made the mistake of mentioning it to the Wise Old Man. Knowing how he is like, Cathan mentioned about how he murmured some stuff like "amateur hour wards" and "rubbish defences" before storming down the passageway. Cathan will inform you that, if you want to go after him, to look for him in some sort of central point (like a nexus or something). Go through the open gateway and enter through the ominous door (Image right).

Note: This will play a small intro cutscene to the area.

You will then arrive within The Approach. Traverse southward through this new region until you enter The Courtyard where you will meet the Wise Old Man.

Part II: Shadows Within

Speak to the Wise Old Man, who will mention about how you had an easier time getting here than they did and walloping a few troublesome people. He'd then mention about how he was hoping to hunt down another dragon to whittle down Kuldra's forces, but complains about the fortress full of Zamorakians in the way. Despite the bothersome trouble in the way, he mentions how great it is that you're here to help get them moving again. Troubling thing is, he mentions how the way is blocked by someone called "the gatekeeper" and he isn't sure who or what it may be. Despite not being aware of who or what it is, the Wise Old Man tells you that Doric is currently working on dispelling a nasty magical barrier further ahead in the Nexus. He then says how it might be a good idea to make a base camp here first.

After making a base camp, follow the path leading up into the fortress. Arrive at The Nexus and speak to Doric. Once you speak to him, he will mention about how crazed the Black Knights are along with how they look like they should have all died long ago. He mentions how the problem is that you are all stuck here and he has everything to get the door open. As far as Doric can tell, everything seems to be connected to a great big stone next to him. He says that it looks broken and, theorising a way to get past the door, might need to fix it using some missing pieces. Inspect the stone.

This will reveal a small dialogue from the stone itself describing how it is broken, shards of itself are missing, and that you should find the missing pieces to repair it. It will then give you authorisation to look around the keep and to access the Nexus nodes scattered around Dowdun Reach.

Part III: Shard Hunting

Item(s) needed: Spade, Pickaxe, Logging Axe.

After inspecting the Dreaming Stone, you will discover that there are thirteen shards (marked on your map with yellow circles) that are needed to repair it. These shards are scattered throughout Dowdun Reach and require you to either interact with characters, scenery objects, or solve puzzles to acquire them. While most are above-ground, there are three that are kept underground. Once you have collected all thirteen shards, head back to the Dreaming Stone.

Note: You can make it easier to take them down by leading them into the spiral staircase. Despite the player needing to interact with the doorway to phase through, the lesser demons can walk through the doorway as if it is not there.

South-WestInteract with ValeriusGo to the top of the staircase (a floor above where Valerius can be found) and West, past the blue dragon, and veer right as soon as you pass under the cliff. Equip your spade and dig in front of the gargoyle statue to uncover the glass owl. Return this item to Valerius to acquire this shard.
The Menagerie
LocationInteract typeDetails
South
  • Dig with spade
  • Cut down vines w/ mithril logging axe

Find three levers to unlock the door. The first lever is inside of the broken down roof of the tiny house (located next to the windmill). You'll need to cast Windstep to reach the roof, then use your spade here to dig it up and interact with it. The second lever is inside of a cave nearby protected by a thorny vine wall along the rock wall to the right of the shard. You will need a mithril or better logging axe to chop these vines. The third and final lever is on the top level of the nearby stone ruins, located beside the air anima vent. You'll need to use Windstep to reach this level.

This area is guarded by a lesser blue dragon.

South-EastStandard interact

Follow along the lower area cliffs to reach an area where you can jump across. You'll also locate a group of hellhounds on your way there, but you can either ignore them or defeat them until you locate a series of beams. Traverse the beams by jumping up to the next level until you reach the top where you'll need to jump across to the stone rock where the shard is located. Note: You'll need plenty of air runes to use Windstep for this particular jumping puzzle.

An alternative way is to equip your leggings of lightness and use Windstep from where you received the previous shard from finding the three levers, down to the cliffs. Be sure not to jump and head down, instead, fall with the spell and the leggings to avoid damage.

The Pastures
LocationInteract TypeDetails
NorthMine a granite deposit

Reach the highest part of the goblin-infested fortress. In the middle of the area, there is a granite deposit that hides the shard. You can either avoid or defeat the blue dragon here to get to the shard, but you can use the Rocksplosion spell to quickly interact with the shard.

EastInteract buttonDefeat the goblins in the immediate area of the shard before interacting with it.
Underground Shards

These are located underground, they can be completed in any order.

The Crypt (underground)
LocationInteract TypeDetails
The CryptDig with spade/shovel

Navigate to The Crypt in the underground region. Before searching for the shard, defeat the zogre here. This will save you trouble later. Interact with the note next to the goblin corpse to learn that the shard is buried in a grave. Dig at any of the graves until you uncover the shard. Note: The location of this shard is randomized for every world.

The Demon Gate (underground)
LocationInteract TypeDetails
The demon gateDefeat 2x shardbound lesser demon

Navigate to the lowest part of the region. There is a lever-activated elevator that will take you down to the demon gate region. For easier traversal later, interact with the nearby nodestone to connect it to the Nexus. Navigate through the pathways until you reach the stone structure and defeat the two lesser demons guarding the shard.

The Lake (underground)
LocationInteract TypeDetails
The LakeSpeak with Offalfoot

He will ask you to give him one of the fish nearby (requires an empty inventory slot), so you'll need to grab one from the nearby pool of fish. This will give you an unusual trout and give this trout to Offalfoot. He'll give you the shard. Note: You do need a fishing rod (the highest level is recommended) and this can be done with level 1 Fishing. You will encounter Delrom when traversing to through this location.

Part IV: Remember the Titans

Interact with the Dreaming Stone. It will say that it is restored, but it will reveal that it was evil! It will claim that its name will rattle in your tiny skull like the echoes within a cave. The Dreaming Stone then reveals its name to be Avisk the eternal whose mind had ever graced the Aughra, but as it tries to enslave you and become its thrall, it seemed stunned. This will reveal two dialogue options (both of which are about destroying the stone), but choose option one. This will force the crystal to acknowledge your logic and, in its own way, apologise for being overzealous and how it happens when you've been alone in the psyche of Black Knights for too long. It then blames the Cthonian before taking down the barrier.

It then warns you to be wary of Lord Rasmodel (aka the Black Knight Titan) as it had a bit of a mishap when he smashed the Dreaming Stone to pieces. Now, he's got some of the Dreaming Stone , some of a demon, and a whole lot of anger issues. End the dialogue and the Dreaming Stone will be fully repaired.

Interact with the newly-dropped Barrier and you'll arrive in The Bastion. Head up all the stairs (be mindful of some gaps which can be Windstepped) until you reach the top. Enter into the Bastion building and, just past a barrier, slay the boss. Interact with the barrier to fight the Titan. After defeating him, return to the Dreaming Stone.

Note: The barrier may not allow you to teleport through if you have not unblocked all of the nodestones; with the exception of The Bastion.

Part V: To the Umbral Sands!

Talk to the Dreaming Stone/Avsik. It will remark how impressive it was that you slew the Titan and that when he finds himself a new body to walk among the world again, he'd like for you to work with him. Aside from that, he remarks about how the gate to the Umbral Sands hasn't been opened in a long time, so he'll need time to get it unstuck. He also pleads for you to be patient - and to stay your hammer - as he will help get you into the desert soon. He then gives you a reward (read: bribe) for not smashing him to pieces with your hammer.

Congratulations! Quest Complete!

Rewards

  • 1x Black Knight's Fortress reward pack
    • 1x Tome of the Titan
      • +750 XP to Magic, Ranged, and Attack
    • 1x Titan's wrath
  • Recipe to creating the Titan's wrath 2h sword

Transcript

Required to Complete

This quest is required to complete the following:

Walkthrough

  • Entryway, to the right (North is a locked door, the end room).
  • Main entryway (looking south the stairs with the bars at the top are where the lever is to open the final door, the hallway has a patrolling vault guardian hulk.
  • Heading down the southern hallway, the room to the left has two giant rats and a treasure chest hidden behind the stairs.
  • Continuing down the hall, turn right around the corner to enter a large multi-level room. Beware, there are three vault guardian hulks; use the stairs to your advantage to either range them or put them into a chokepoint to take them on one at a time. If engaging with melee, it is advised to cast Tempest Shield and Enchant Weapon: Fire before entering if you have them.
  • Below the entrance to the large room, there is another chest hidden there. Exit the room through the southern door.
  • There are three fire traps in the hall; time dodge rolls past each set, and they can heavily damage you if caught inside. Continue following the hall to reach the next area.
  • There is a spike room, to the west is a small room with a rat in it, you can use the spikes to dispatch it, otherwise there is no loot there, continue up the stairs on the north side.
  • Continue straight down the hall; going west is a dead end, and there are two rats to fight. Just past the doorway is a room with three vault sentinels. They attack with ranged, so using cover with your own ranged attacks, or holding up a shield and countering, is very effective to take them out. It is also advisable to cast buffing spells before engagement as with any fight where you are outnumbered.
  • After defeating the guardians, you can grab a vault core, these are essential for high-level recipes and lodestones. Be careful as they weigh 50 kg and can easily overencumber you if you have also been looting other resources from the vault.
  • There is another chest to be found, just off to the left from the statue.
  • Continue east out of the room, careful of the traps. The fire can deal more damage than the spikes, but dodge rolls will get you safely past all of them. As the spikes are laid out in a diamond with the points against the walls, the spikes are thinnest there and thus easier to pass if sticking to the wall.
  • Once past the traps, you will be in a room with three routes (two clearly visible and one that can be missed), up the stairs to the end boss or south to some optional treasure. North contains a spike room with four rats and no treasure.
    • If you stand on the rubble seen in the image facing south, you can see an opening on the wall which can be reached with Windstep. Go there, and you will find the second vault core, some treasure, and a lever which you can pull to open a shortcut.
  • To get to the final boss, follow the stairs to the top, pull the lever, and go through the gate to the starting room that opens, and a new large door will open that contains the boss and his treasures.
  • There is a side path for additional treasure, going south first instead of up the stairs that lead to the boss, around the corner to the left is a lever, pull it to open a gate that is past the fire traps.
  • After pulling the lever, make your way past two fire traps.
  • Past the gate are two goblin runts waiting inside to ambush; however, they are much weaker enemies and should not pose much threat.
  • After disposing of the goblins, the treasure is just past some more spike traps.
  • Back to the main path behind the previously locked door awaits The vault overlord, who is a vault hulk but with much more health and damage. Remember to buff up and cast combat spells before entering to make the fight more manageable, and to save energy to block or dodge.
  • After defeating the vault overlord, you can grab the last vault core and loot the chest.

Agility.name: Agility
Agility.lead: Agility is a support skill that allows players to reduce stamina drain, improve mobility, and navigate Ashenfall more efficiently through passive world benefits, active traversal mechanics, and skill spells. At certain levels of this skill, players will be able to increase their carry weight, access shortcuts, and reduce stamina drain on jumping and sprinting.

levelling.desc: Execute a short, horizontal aerial dash to cross gaps and evade attacks in combat.

levelling.name: Breakfall

sections.title: Experience Calculation
sections.html:
Experience Calculation

Experience is earned based on the amount of damage dealt to an enemy (except for the training dummy). If the attack is normal, players will receive 25% of the damage value as Attack experience. If the attack is a critical hit, players will instead receive 50% the damage value as Attack experience.

Construction.levelling_html:
See experience for a table of the experience required to reach each level.

Levelling Construction grants access to both passive benefits as well as unlocking spells and other abilities. When you build an object and then break it, you will no longer receive Construction experience for building that object until the world is reset. An effective way to quickly train Construction is to walk backwards while building something with a low cost in a straight line (such as chairs). Once you've run out of supplies, destroy all of them, exit the world, and load back in. Once the world has been reset, players can reach the desired level by repeating this process.

sections.title: Mechanics
sections.html:
Mechanics

See Buildings/Mechanics for a complete explanation of the building interface.

Players can press the "B" key (default binding) to access the building menu. There, players can select from various Structures to place in-game. All structures have durability, which can be damaged and eventually destroyed by monsters, such as during goblin raids. To repair any damaged object, enter the repair interface by pressing the "T" key (default binding) and then interacting with the structure.

Farming.name: Farming
Farming.lead: Farming is one of the skills in Runescape: Dragonwilds and allows players to grow various plants. The skill was released as part of the 0.10 Fellhollow update.

levelling.name: Seed Recovery Chance
levelling.desc: Increases the chance to recover seeds from all plants by 0.3% per level, up to 29.4% at level 99.

levelling.name: Plant Cure
levelling.desc: Unlocks the ability to create plant cures at the cooking range! Use plant cures to heal your plants from disease.

levelling.name: Rain Catcher
levelling.desc: Collects and filters rain water into usable clean water over time.

levelling.name:
Compost Bin
Compost Bucket
levelling.desc: Unlocks the compost bin and compost bucket recipes. These allow for creating and using Normal compost to boost the yield and disease resistance of your plants.

levelling.name: Uproot
levelling.desc: Channelling the power of the earth, summon a spectral surge that gently coaxes ripe plants from the soil. Within a small radius, all fully grown crops and wild plants are instantly harvested and drawn towards you.

levelling.name: Tree Farming
levelling.desc: You are skilled enough at farming to now grow trees! Trees can be planted directly into the ground and seeds can be found while chopping down trees and from birds nests.

levelling.name: Water Barrel
levelling.desc: Unlocks the water barrel, which stores Clean or dirty water collected from watering cans for later use.

levelling.name: Humidify
levelling.desc: Conjure water magic to create a rain cloud that travels forward, instantly watering any farming plot that it passes over with clean water.

levelling.name: Well
levelling.desc: Unlocks the ability to build a well! A well provides a limited amount of clean water per day. Wells refill in the morning.

levelling.name: Harvester
levelling.desc: With greater mastery over the land, the caster's reach extends even further. Harvester expands Uproot's range to a wider radius.

levelling.name: Speedy Farmer
levelling.desc: You've become more adept at watering and composting your plants. You can now do so with less penalty to your movement speed!

levelling.name: Iron Secateurs
levelling.desc: A pair of gardening Secateurs that boost your harvesting yield while equipped.

levelling.name: Large Water Barrel
levelling.desc: Unlocks the large water barrel, which stores even more Clean or dirty water collected from watering cans for later use.

levelling.name: Cleansing Rain
levelling.desc: Upgrades the Humidify spell, causing the conjured rain cloud to cure any diseased plants it passes over while watering them.

levelling.name: Scarecrow
levelling.desc: Unlocks the scarecrow for protecting your farm from feathered annoyances.

levelling.name: Super Compost Bin
levelling.desc: Unlocks the super compost bin which produces super compost, for an even better yield boost and disease resistance of your plants.

levelling.name: Rapid Growth
levelling.desc: Advances plant growth by one stage. Cannot be reapplied until the plant grows further.

levelling.name: Mucksplosion
levelling.desc: Not for the squeamish gardener! This spell harnesses Earth magic to summon a bubbling compost volcano, showering your beloved plots with rich, nourishing fertilizer.

levelling.name: Overgrowth Aura
levelling.desc: Increases the range of the Rapid Growth spell.

levelling.name: Farming Cape
levelling.desc: A true showcase of skill mastery. Unlocks the ability to craft and wear the Farming skillcape.

Fishing.name: Fishing
Fishing.lead: Fishing is a skill that released on 21 April 2026 alongside the 0.11.1 update and is Dragonwilds' eleventh skill. Magic.name: Magic
Magic.lead: Magic is one of the skills in Runescape: Dragonwilds and was released in Update 0.8. Magic is one of the three combat styles players can use. Combat spells can be cast to efficiently fight monsters from a distance, whereas utility spells have numerous uses.

levelling.name: Reduced Magic Stamina
levelling.desc: Reduces the cost of magical stamina drain by 0.5% per level.

levelling.name: Air Magic
levelling.desc: Summon the unrelenting force of air! Equip air runes to unleash the power of wind against an enemy, dealing high single target damage and knocking your enemies down!

levelling.name: Secondary Attacks
levelling.desc: Charge up and release powerful secondary staff spells.

levelling.name: Water Magic
levelling.desc: Conjure the supportive power of water! Equip water runes to damage and slow your enemies while also healing yourself and your allies. Kills with water magic have a chance to spawn water orbs.

levelling.name: Surge
levelling.desc: Channel arcane power into your dodges, travelling further and evading longer as a result.

levelling.name: Arcane Expertise
levelling.desc: Unlocks an additional powerful magical attack at the end of staff magic combos.

levelling.name: Runic Refund
levelling.desc: Your greater understanding of magic gives you a 30% chance to preserve runes when attacking with magic.

levelling.name: Fire Magic
levelling.desc: Wield the destructive forces of fire. Equip fire runes to deal medium damage to enemies in a large area and build up Burning on them to reduce them to ash

levelling.name: Afterimage
levelling.desc: Distract your enemies by leaving behind an illusionary image for a short time when you use your first Surge charge.

levelling.name: Confuse
levelling.desc: Twist the minds of lesser enemies, making them unable to distinguish between friend and foe for a limited time.

levelling.name: Magic Potion
levelling.desc: Unlock the recipe for the magic potion at the brewing cauldron.

levelling.name: Magic Focus
levelling.desc: Allows crafting of magic focus at the crafting table, which can be used to imbue magic staves to increase their damage!

levelling.name: Greater Confuse
levelling.desc: The Confuse spell now works on a wider variety of creatures.

levelling.name: Enfeeble
levelling.desc: Weakens the attacks of the targeted opponent.

levelling.name: Vengeance
levelling.desc: A spell that reflects incoming damage back at the enemies.

sections.title: Experience mechanics
sections.html:
Experience mechanics

Players who deal regular damage will receive 0.25 \times damage\ dealt experience depending on the maximum health of the enemy. Players who deal critical damage will receive 0.5 \times damage\ dealt experience, depending on the maximum health of the enemy. For example, if a player deals 88 regular damage to a chicken, the player will only receive 5 Ranged experience, since the maximum health of the chicken is 20 hitpoints (20 hitpoints x .25 experience factor = 5 experience).

Players can also earn more experience by targeting the monster's weak points. Below is a list that shows the area on the monster:

sections.title: Rune Altar
sections.html:
Rune Altar

The rune altar is a crafting table used to craft runes using rune essence. Its menu displays options to select which rune you want to craft, a slider for how many you want to craft (from 1 to 50), and has two different methods to do so—Attune and Auto Craft:

  • Attuning is a two-step process involving Attunement and Infusion and can award the maximum available XP and rune essence to runes ratio of 1:10.
  • Auto Crafting instantly crafts runes but only awards 25% of the XP and requires Efficiency upgrades to get the 1:10 ratio.

sections.title: Anima Vents
sections.html:
Anima Vents

Anima vents can be found throughout Ashenfall, and produce sounds and runes specific to their type. The player can siphon runes from them using rune essence at any level, making them a source of runes that the player may not yet be able to craft. Like other resource nodes, they respawn after 3 in-game days.

Each normal node will turn 10 rune essence into 100 runes and 40 XP, or 70 XP with 45% XP Boosts. With Lesser Anima Siphoning at level 46, the runes will increase to 120, a ratio of 1:12, and with Greater Anima Siphoning it will further increase to 150 per 10 rune essence, or a ratio of 1:15.

Anima vents have a chance to be concentrated, which means they will have triple the available runes as long as they player has triple the available essence. With the previous two abilities, that means that the player can get up to 450 runes and 120/210 XP for only 30 rune essence from a concentrated vent with Greater Anima Siphoning. Also with Greater Elemental Spirits at level 64, the Summon Elemental Spirits spell from level 19 will indicate any concentrated vents.

In addition, starting at level 34, there is a 1/5 chance while siphoning for a Pure Essence rock to appear, which will float in the air and move quickly. It disappears after a short time, but by hitting it with a combat spell, arrow, or bolt, it will provide 700 XP and 20-30 additional runes that match the vent as well as 20-30 additional nature and law runes.

And finally, with Runes to Rune Essence at level 61 and especially with Runes to Rune Essence Upgrade at level 81 giving back 40% and 60% of the rune essence, the player can interact with every anima vent they come across and almost entirely refund the rune essence consumed, gaining free siphon XP as well as a chance for a Pure Essence rock. Even if they don't have any rune essence on hand, they can generate some with the spell using runes that don't weigh anything and from the rune Pouch which is separate from the inventory.

buildings.name: 45° Stairs
buildings.description: Simple stairs used to go up or down.
buildings.lead: 45° stairs is a constructed item that is not required to have a roof and does not require a stable foundation. Since the stairs are at a 45° angle, players who wish to connect two floors in their house will need to place the bottom of the stairs at the furthest edge of the bottom floor and connect it to the base of the top floor; this will use two stairs. The square tile and the wall are both 4 metres long (in either direction), such that the measurement for each stair is approximately 2.8 metres long.

buildings.name: Armour Mannequin
buildings.description: A mannequin on which you can mount armour on.
buildings.lead: An armour mannequin is a buildable object at level 40 Artisan, which players can mount up to five pieces of armour. Players can quickly swap armours at mannequins and can even store some capes on them (Pioneer's cape the dragonbane cape and Fellhollow cape). If a certain piece of equipment is already on a mannequin, players can add another piece of the same type. For example, if the reinforced helmet is on the mannequin, players can also add a Dragonkin mage hood. This results in only the latter being shown.

buildings.name: Ash Chest
buildings.description: A small chest to store items in.
buildings.lead: The ash chest is a small storage container for up to 32 item slots. Players can unlock the small chest by receiving ash logs in their inventory for the first time and unlocking the skill perk Creature Comforts. Players can also name their chest, up to 16 characters long. To craft or process an item without having the required items in their inventory, players must have the required items in their chest and check the "Linked" checkbox in the chest interface. This will allow players to craft up to a 12-metre radius away from the chest.

buildings.name: Bed
buildings.description: A comfortable bed to sleep in and skip the night.
buildings.lead: The bed is a buildable piece of furniture used to rest and set the player's respawn point in the world. If used at night, players will skip to daytime and regain their full rest meter; if used during the day, players will lie in place and slowly regain their rest meter over time. The bed requires 8 ash planks and 4 rough cloth to craft, and must be under a roof and enclosed with three walls to be used.

buildings.name: Crafting Table
buildings.description: A simple crafting station equipped with an array of primitive tools. It is used to craft equipment and other important resources.
buildings.lead: The crafting table can be used to create and repair tools, weapons, ammo, armour, and capes. It does not have any indoor/outdoor restrictions and can be placed without a foundation.

buildings.name: Crate
buildings.description: A simple crate.
buildings.lead: A crate is a tier 1 constructed object that does not have restrictions to build indoors/outdoors and does not require a foundation to build. The crate is the smallest storage container for up to 16 item slots. To craft or process an item without having the required items in their inventory, players must have the required items in their crate and check the "Linked" checkbox in the crate interface. This will allow players to craft up to a 12-metre radius away from the crate.

This may be useful in Ghornfell or Brynmoor, where lightning strikes can occur during rainy weather (e.g., Stormtouched Highlands).

buildings.name: Lodestone
buildings.description: A powerful plinth for teleportation.
buildings.lead: A lodestone is a platform that allows the player to travel if another lodestone is placed elsewhere. When the first lodestone is built, the inactive lodestone in the Temple starting area becomes active as well. Teleporting between two lodestones costs a varied amount of law runes, depending on the distance of the target lodestone and the weight of the player.
buildings.html:
A lodestone is a platform that allows the player to travel if another lodestone is placed elsewhere. When the first lodestone is built, the inactive lodestone in the Temple starting area becomes active as well. Teleporting between two lodestones costs a varied amount of law runes, depending on the distance of the target lodestone and the weight of the player.

Permanent locations

Teleportation costs

Teleporting between two lodestones costs an amount of law runes based on the distance between them and the amount of weight carried, with a minimum cost of one law rune. Note that the number shown on the lodestone map is calculated by the following:

Law\, runes = (Distance\, to\, target\, lodestone\, \div 1000) \times (Total\, weight\, \div 1000)

For example, teleporting 8000 meters (the length of 2000 square tiles) while weighing 400 kilograms would require 8 \times 0.4 = 3.2 law runes which rounds to 3.

Restrictions

Players cannot build lodestones in instanced areas, inside Dragonkin Vaults, or in specific areas in Ashenfall.

Dowdun Reach

Most areas within Dowdun Reach prevent the players from building lodestones, with the exceptions of The Approach, The Pastures, The Menagerie and The Courtyard. Refer to the image on the side.

Players can also build multiple sawmills with the sawing end within two metres, and have the processed planks go into the same storage. buildings.name: Mystic Forge
buildings.description: Used to craft magic weapons and for ascending masterworks and vestiges.
buildings.lead: The mystic forge is a crafting station that allows for the creation of staves, other weapons, and more powerful capes, and uses ascension cores in ascending masterwork weapons and vestige armour. This replaces some of the functionality of the smithing anvil and crafting table.
buildings.html:
The mystic forge is a crafting station that allows for the creation of staves, other weapons, and more powerful capes, and uses ascension cores in ascending masterwork weapons and vestige armour. This replaces some of the functionality of the smithing anvil and crafting table.

The mystic forge is unlocked upon obtaining a bronze bar in the player's inventory.

Ascension Upgrades

Players can ascend their masterwork weapons and armour by collecting ascension cores through defeating enemies that drop ascension shards and creating them in the mystic forge or the cores directly through the Nightmare Crucibles. In order to start ascending weapons and armour, players will need at least 1 ascension core of the next power level available in either their inventory or chest along with a suitable item to ascend. This item must first be placed within the slot to ascend (it still stays in the inventory).

Ascending a masterwork weapon or armour piece consumes the core to bring it to the highest power level available to the player (<4 to 4, 4 to 5, 5 to 6, etc) and, if the player has multiple cores to reach the current highest power level in the game, the weapon or armour piece will require ascending twice to consume the cores needed to ascend to the highest power level in the game. It is worth noting here that weapons and armour that are already the highest power level cannot be ascended until a new major update.

buildings.name: Oak Chair
buildings.description: A sturdy, fancy chair.
buildings.lead: An oak chair is a type of furniture that is unlocked after creating oak planks. Players can place decorations and can also sit on top of the chair.
buildings.html: An oak chair is a type of furniture that is unlocked after creating oak planks. Players can place decorations and can also sit on top of the chair.

buildings.name: Oak Chest
buildings.description: A moderately sized chest to store items in.
buildings.lead: The oak chest is a large storage container for up to 48 item slots. Players can unlock the creation of the large chest after receiving oak logs for the first time. To craft or process an item without having the required items in their inventory, players must have the required items in their chest and check the "Linked" checkbox in the chest interface. This will allow players to craft up to a 12-metre radius away from the chest.
buildings.html:
The oak chest is a large storage container for up to 48 item slots. Players can unlock the creation of the large chest after receiving oak logs for the first time. To craft or process an item without having the required items in their inventory, players must have the required items in their chest and check the "Linked" checkbox in the chest interface. This will allow players to craft up to a 12-metre radius away from the chest.

Players can also lock their chest by opening the interface and checking the Private checkbox at the bottom.

buildings.name: Oak Farming Plot
buildings.description: A plot made from Oak logs. Plants found in Ghornfell grow better in this plot.
buildings.lead: The oak farming plot can be used to grow plants with seeds through the Farming skill. To obtain this plot recipe, collect oak logs.
buildings.html:
The oak farming plot can be used to grow plants with seeds through the Farming skill. To obtain this plot recipe, collect oak logs.

It is the best plot to grow plants found within the Ghornfell region, like the following:

  • Dwellberry seeds
  • Onion seeds
  • Tomato seeds
  • Kwuarm seeds
  • Swamp weed seeds
  • Snapdragon seeds
  • Toadflax seeds

buildings.name: Oak Shelf
buildings.description: Sturdier shelves for displaying things in your home.
buildings.lead: An oak shelf is a tier 2 decoration. It can only be built on Creative Mode worlds.

buildings.name: Ore & Stone Storage
buildings.description: A high-capacity storage for stones and ores.
buildings.lead: Ore & stone storage is a storage container for storing stones and ore, unlocked at 58 Mining. Unlike the lumber storage that will automatically pickup planks from a sawmill, the ore & stone storage will not automatically pick up ores and stone processed from a kiln, furnace, grindstone, stonecutter, or blast furnace. The ore & stone storage has the same capacity as an oak chest and less capacity than an iron chest, despite it both taking up more space and being made from materials available later in a player's progression.
buildings.html:
Ore & stone storage is a storage container for storing stones and ore, unlocked at 58 Mining. Unlike the lumber storage that will automatically pickup planks from a sawmill, the ore & stone storage will not automatically pick up ores and stone processed from a kiln, furnace, grindstone, stonecutter, or blast furnace. The ore & stone storage has the same capacity as an oak chest and less capacity than an iron chest, despite it both taking up more space and being made from materials available later in a player's progression.

Note that the ore & stone storage does not store rune essence, limestone, gypsum, ground materials, Gems, Salvage Piles, and clay or glass products.

buildings.lead: The postbox is a buildable scenery item found in the "Crafting" building tab, given to players as a reward for completing the Letters for the Dead secondary quest. The post box can also give you a letter. Delivering the letter give you 50 soul fragments.

Players cannot open the rain catcher's interface unless there is at least one unit of rain stored inside the catcher.

buildings.name: Rune Altar
buildings.description: Used for crafting Runes, the magical stones needed to cast magic.
buildings.lead: The rune altar is a crafting table used to craft runes, which are required to cast spells. To make runes, players need rune essence, which comes from essence geysers around the world, as well as from goblin packs, garou packs, and vault guardians. It does not have any special conditions to function.

To make runes, players need rune essence, which comes from essence geysers around the world, as well as from goblin packs, garou packs, and vault guardians. It does not have any special conditions to function.

Runes can be auto-crafted quickly or attuned by playing a simple minigame for more experience.

buildings.name: Sawmill
buildings.description: The Sawmill processes wood into planks!
buildings.lead: The sawmill is currently used to make ash planks and oak planks out of ash logs and oak logs. If a lumber storage is placed within five metres of the saw end, the planks will be deposited directly into it. It processes very slowly, so it is recommended to keep it filled while doing other tasks, or to fill it just before sleeping to process a whole stack instantly. It must not have a roof above it to function.

It must not have a roof above it to function.

The sawmill is unlocked upon obtaining a bronze bar.

buildings.name: Scarecrow
buildings.description: A wooden friend to protect your crops and keep you company in the fields.
buildings.lead: A scarecrow is a buildable object unlocked at level 55 Farming. It is meant to prevent bird-type mobs from landing in your planters.
buildings.html: A scarecrow is a buildable object unlocked at level 55 Farming. It is meant to prevent bird-type mobs from landing in your planters.

buildings.name: Side Table
buildings.description: A tiny table.
buildings.lead: Side table is a type of furniture that is unlocked after creating ash planks. Players can place decorations on top of the side table.
buildings.html: Side table is a type of furniture that is unlocked after creating ash planks. Players can place decorations on top of the side table.

buildings.name: Smithing Anvil
buildings.description: A Blacksmith's Anvil. Required for working with metals.
buildings.lead: The smithing anvil was used to create and repair higher-level tools, weapons, ammo, armour, and capes. It required a roof above it to function. It was removed on 23 June 2026 in Update 0.12.0 and replaced with blacksmith's bench, armour bench, and mystic forge.

buildings.name: Spinning Wheel
buildings.description: A spinning wheel can spin fibres such as flax or fleece into threads for crafting.
buildings.lead: The spinning wheel is unlocked when players harvest from flax plants and receive flax for the first time. It is used to process fibres and furs into threads that can be used for crafting. It processes somewhat slowly, so it is recommended to keep it filled while doing other tasks. It requires a roof above it to function.

It processes somewhat slowly, so it is recommended to keep it filled while doing other tasks. It requires a roof above it to function.

There is an advanced version of this spinning wheel that grants a secondary slot for spinning thread.

buildings.name: Square Foundation
buildings.description: Place on the ground to create the foundations for a larger structure.
buildings.lead: Square foundations are constructed objects that are not required to have a roof or a stable foundation. Note that the square foundation has eight points of contact: four at the corners and four on the bottom of each vertical beam. Players can only build up to six square foundations, either stacked on top of each other or side by side, without a stable foundation in between (or at the bottom of the stack). The square foundation is 4 metres long on both sides (which includes the frame surrounding the tile).
buildings.html:
Square foundations are constructed objects that are not required to have a roof or a stable foundation. Note that the square foundation has eight points of contact: four at the corners and four on the bottom of each vertical beam. Players can only build up to six square foundations, either stacked on top of each other or side by side, without a stable foundation in between (or at the bottom of the stack). The square foundation is 4 metres long on both sides (which includes the frame surrounding the tile).

A square foundation is not recommended for building floors in a two-floor player-built house, as the bottom legs will make it hard for players to move around the house. It may be recommended to use square tiles without legs on the bottom.

buildings.name: Square Tile
buildings.description: Sturdy surface used to create floors.
buildings.lead: Square tile is a constructed item that is not required to have a roof and does not require a stable foundation. A square tile is 4 metres long in both the x and y directions, making the area 16 square metres. Note that this measurement accounts for the frame surrounding the tile.
buildings.html: Square tile is a constructed item that is not required to have a roof and does not require a stable foundation. A square tile is 4 metres long in both the x and y directions, making the area 16 square metres. Note that this measurement accounts for the frame surrounding the tile.

buildings.name: Standing Torch
buildings.description: A torch that can be placed on surfaces.
buildings.lead: A standing torch is a constructed object that can be built either indoors or outdoors, and requires a horizontally flat foundation (e.g., another standing torch, a square tile, or on the top end of a thin or thick beam). The standing torch has two points of contact, one at the base and one at the base of the fire. Players can only stack up to five torches on top of each other before the structure becomes too unstable.

Players can only stack up to five torches on top of each other before the structure becomes too unstable.

buildings.name: Stone Range
buildings.description: A sturdy pot over a campfire that can be used to combine ingredients to make better meals and infuse water with berries or other ingredients.
buildings.lead: A stone range can be built using 8 ash logs, 12 stone, and 3 animal bones. It is a lower-tier version of the cooking range. To unlock the recipe for the stone range, players must first build and interact with a campfire, or collect an animal bone in their inventory.

buildings.name: Stonecutter
buildings.description: A must have for those desiring a castle
buildings.lead: The stonecutter is a buildable processing station where players can input 2 stone pieces to create 1 stone block, which is used to make power level 3 building pieces. The recipe and ability to build a stonecutter are unlocked after obtaining a steel bar in their inventory for the first time.

buildings.name: Storage Ledger
buildings.description: Swiftly unload your inventory into linked storage that contains matching items.
buildings.lead: Storage Ledger is a building that enables players to quickly deposit items into storage containers that have "linked" enabled.
buildings.html:
Storage Ledger is a building that enables players to quickly deposit items into storage containers that have "linked" enabled.

Its function serves to limit the need to manually open every storage container, and instead automatically depositing items into the appropriate container.

buildings.name: Super Compost Bin
buildings.description: Deposit all of your unwanted nutrient rich food or plant matter to turn it into Super Compost over time.
buildings.lead: A super compost bin is a buildable object unlocked at level 60 Farming. Unlike the regular compost bin, it will only accept a smaller pool of items, which includes willow logs, in order to produce super compost, which can be taken out of the bin with an empty compost bucket.

buildings.name: Tannery
buildings.description: A rack that slowly processes animal hide into leather.
buildings.lead: A tannery can be built using 2 coarse thread, 4 animal bones and 12 ash logs. It allows for refining animal hides into leather. It processes somewhat slowly, so it is recommended to keep it filled while doing other tasks. Players must collect an animal bone to unlock the tannery.

The tannery can be upgraded by placing a tanner's kit next to it. This allows the creation of products that require two materials, most notably hard leather. There is an upgraded crafting station, the advanced tannery which allows you to create products that require three materials.

buildings.name: Training Dummy
buildings.description: A wooden friend to take all your frustrations out on.
buildings.lead: A training dummy is a constructed object, unlockable at level 37 Attack, that acts as a non-combative NPC with 400 hitpoints. Upon losing all its hitpoints, the training dummy will be knocked down for a few seconds, pop up again, and restart at full health. Note that bows and staves will lose regular durability as if attacking a monster. However, melee weapons do not lose durability, even if using the melee weapon's special attack.

Note that the wall is 4 metres long in both the horizontal and vertical directions.

buildings.name: Wall-mounted Torch

Players can choose to build either the cabin-like or the baroque-like version with the same requirements.

buildings.name: Well

This well must be built outdoors and on top of land for it to be placed. The well replenishes to its full capacity at midnight, and players cannot destroy the well whilst there is water stored inside.

concepts.title: Guide for new players
concepts.lead: New to RuneScape: Dragonwilds? This guide introduces the core gameplay systems, survival mechanics, and activities you'll encounter in Ashenfall. It provides an overview of essential topics – including quests, skills, exploration, combat, crafting, and progression - to help new players get started and build a strong foundation.
concepts.html:
New to RuneScape: Dragonwilds? This guide introduces the core gameplay systems, survival mechanics, and activities you'll encounter in Ashenfall. It provides an overview of essential topics – including quests, skills, exploration, combat, crafting, and progression - to help new players get started and build a strong foundation.

Getting started

To get started on your adventure, you must first purchase the game from your preferred platform. Here is a list of places where you can buy the game:

PC/DesktopConsole
Jagex LauncherXbox Store
SteamPlaystation Store
Epic Games StoreNintendo eShop
Also available on...

Xbox Game Pass (Premium and Ultimate)

Playstation Plus (Plus Extra and Premium)

All links, unless otherwise specified, automatically link to the UK storefronts.

Once you have purchased the game, launch the game and you'll be able to create your character, create a new world save, and modify settings. To create a character, go to "Characters" and decide which character mode you want to be. Know that you will be able to still create a character if you first clicked on play and entered whether on solo or online. Currently, there are three character modes:

  • Normal: A standard version of the game where you can play the game in a normal mode, access hard mode versions of the game, and play in public or dedicated servers.
  • <b>Custom mode</b>: A version of the game that lets you customize the world to fit how you want to play. It allows you to scale health, stamina, resistance, and even become invulnerable.
  • Creative mode: A version of the game that allows you to play in a world without any restrictions, granting unlimited resources.

After creating a character and world, or joining a friend's world, you'll automatically begin the tutorial quest First Steps. Now, you can skip the tutorials, and the quest will have you meet the Wise Old Man in Bramblemead Village, but it is advised that new players go through the tutorial to learn the basics of the game. Once you complete the tutorial (or skip it), you will then be able to start the first primary quest, Dragon Slayer.

The basics

RuneScape: Dragonwilds is a game built on Unreal Engine 5 developed by Epic Games. Unlike its older predecessors, who use a custom game engine, this game uses real-time mechanics to run everything. Every in-game day is roughly 24 minutes, with a majority of that time (~19 minutes) being daytime. Actions in the game take different lengths of time to accomplish. For instance, freshly cut trees (if the stump remains) take roughly three in-game days (~72 minutes) to respawn.

To navigate the continent, there is a compass in the top-middle section of your HUD/UI. This will show you nearby dragonkin vaults, kebbit burrows, claimed beds, and player markers (both placed on the World Map and player indicators). All distances in the game are indicated as "meters" or "XXXXm" to inform you of how far you are from specific points, including your claimed bed.

To access your World Map, use the (default: M) key or (default: view) button. This shows all the locations you have discovered while leaving the rest covered in grey fog.

To travel fast throughout the continent, and even access newly discovered regions, players must unlock the building recipe for lodestones. To unlock this recipe, players must first acquire a vault core in a vault.

Starting out

After creating your first character and world, you will appear inside of a ruined temple in the temple woods sub-region of Brynmoor. The lodestone behind you is inactive until you either place your first lodestone or discover another lodestone. Aside from you in this temple, there is one other person there: the Wise Old Man. Speak to him to continue the tutorial quest or skip it entirely and meet him in the nearby Bramblemead Village. It is highly recommended for first-time players of this game to continue the tutorial instead of skipping it as it will help you get used to the game mechanics.

For combat, there are small kebbits, swift deer, violent goblins, and beefy cows in this region that you can kill. For skilling, interact with special hotspots (Fishing/Agility), build plots (Farming), or chop trees (Woodcutting) to gain experience.

Quests

Quests can help you understand the game's story and explore, like First Steps and Dragon Slayer, which help you adventure deeper into the continent of Ashenfall or unlock special mechanics like The Wild Hunt. There are three types of quests that can be completed in the game: Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary. Both Primary and Secondary quests offer tutorials (ex: First Steps and Shrimp Catcher, respectively), but Tertiary quests can only be completed during Primary quests. The only quest, before the full release, to feature Tertiary quests was Icthlarin's Little Helper.

Lore Scraps

Lore Scraps help you understand and learn Ashenfall's history, as well as Gielinor's. These scraps can be found in the Journal interface, where you can read all the items and lore scraps you find.

Skills

Skills are essential in the game as they give the character passive buffs (ex: less stamina used during sprinting), unlock skill-specific recipes (ex: angler's hat), or enable usage of powerful skill spells (ex: windstep). While skills do not actively allow you to gain access to specific regions of the game (like Fellhollow), they do allow you to access fast travel outside of lodestones.

Exploration

Players will start with the basic adventurer's tunic and adventurer's leggings as their armour and a simple torch as their off-hand.

The tutorial gives players their own weapons and starter tools made from loose stones and teaches them what they must do. In Brynmoor, the starting region, players can only acquire up to power level 2 gear before needing to head northward towards Ghornfell and unlock bronze and iron (power level 3 and 4, respectively) gear. Players who greatly explore the continent of Ashenfall will also come across sanguine urns, which can be interacted with to increase the player's total health pool by 10 points. While exploring the continent, you will learn over time the stories that take place here, or, if you like skipping dialogue, all the various monsters Ashenfall has to offer.

Building

To start building, players will need a form of lumber as their primary resource, as well as any other basic items that building structures, furniture, and decorations will require. Certain structures cannot be placed due to certain restrictions mentioned below.

Players cannot build:

  • Inside vaults
  • Either outdoors or indoors (depending on the structure)
  • With no supporting structure below
  • Higher than the structure's limit
  • In most of Dowdun Reach, save for places like The Courtyard.
Build health

Structures built with ash logs as the primary ingredient have 100 building health, whilst structures built with oak and willow logs have higher building health. Defensive structures, such as the pallisades gates and pallisade walls, have at least 2000 and 6000 health, respectively.

Combat

Ashenfall is full of creatures, some hostile, others friendly. From kebbit to dragons, killing monsters provides combat experience and useful loots. Certain monsters have a power level tied to the region they are in. For example, Ghornfell is a power level 3 - 4 region, where monsters, such as the garou, have a power level of 3 or 4. Here, you also have your own power level that greatly depends on the armour you are wearing. During and after the tutorial, your character will start with power level 0 armour and power level 1 weapons, like the Adventurer's Tunic and Stone Club, respectively.

Killing monsters will level up the specific combat skill you used to kill, which is Attack, Magic, and Ranged. Here, the combat system relies on your movement (default: W,A,S,D) keys or joystick (if using controller), your primary action (default: primary left button) mouse or controller (default: RT) button, secondary action (default: secondary right button) mouse or controller (default: LT) button and evade (default: CTRL) key or controller (default: B) button.

Staying safe

This game, while not purely multiplayer like its predecessors, does allow multiple players (4-6 players) to play the same world. Players can open up servers to the public, and some who join may not be completely good actors, so here are some tips to help you stay safe:

  • Enable locked/private chests.
  • Use totems to protect your builds.
  • Set up passwords for your server if you want only trusted friends online.
  • Make sure Gravestone protection is enabled, which will prevent players from looting it.
  • Be cautious of trading in another world; be sure you are certain that the player you are exchanging items with can be trusted.

What's next

Now that you have the basics down, here are some next steps to enhance your RuneScape: Dragonwilds experience:

  • Set a goal, decide what you want to achieve, whether it is completing the first Saga, building a structure or town, or gathering all the vestiges.
  • Complete quests to explore new areas within Ashenfall, level up your skills to better gather resources!
  • Experiment with the game; see how the game functions with different methods of builds, travel, or playstyle!
  • Stay updated by keeping an eye on official RuneScape: Dragonwilds updates, patch notes, and announcements!
  • Most importantly, have fun! RuneScape as a whole is about enjoying yourself, whether it be the survival game RuneScape: Dragonwilds, its MMO precursors - ' or '!

Conclusion

There is so much to explore in Ashenfall, from quests to skilling and combat. Set goals, build smart habits with refilling on food, drinks, and potions, whack a few goblins if you can, and enjoy the tales to come. Remember to follow the rules of the game and respect other players. See you in Ashenfall and Happy scaping!

concepts.title: Power level
concepts.lead: Power levels are an indication of how strong a player, monster, or piece of food is. Players can see their current power level at the bottom right of their inventory, and power levels for monsters can be seen to the left of their health bar. Each region in Ashenfall has a power level, which most of the monsters in that region inherit.

Player Power Levels

Monster hitpoint scaling

A monster's base hitpoints can scale based on the region's power level. This hitpoint value is determined for all monsters in a region when the player enters that region, and the power level icon will change based on the player's average power level, determined by their armour. The formula that calculates the monster's base hitpoints is shown below:

Hitpoints = Region\, Power \, Level\, \times \, Monster's\, Base\, Hitpoints

Power level 1 monsters (e.g., chickens, kebbits, etc.) do not scale their hitpoints; those are always at their base value, regardless of the region's power level.

concepts.title: Health
concepts.lead: Health determines how much damage a player or a monster can take. Upon first arriving in Ashenfall, players have 100 maximum health. However, scattered across Ashenfall, there are currently 21 sanguine urns that will offer a +10 permanent boost to health. The maximum health a player can have is 310. Health regeneration is negatively affected by having low sustenance.
concepts.html:
Health determines how much damage a player or a monster can take. Upon first arriving in Ashenfall, players have 100 maximum health. However, scattered across Ashenfall, there are currently 21 sanguine urns that will offer a +10 permanent boost to health. The maximum health a player can have is 310. Health regeneration is negatively affected by having low sustenance.

Effects

  • Currently, the maximum amount of health players can have is 310.
  • Every 25 sustenance will increase the player's natural health regeneration by 0.5/sec, up to a maximum of 2.0/sec, and a minimum of 0.5/sec.
    • Health will regenerate after no player damage is taken for 11 seconds.

Damage events

Damage to the player can come from many sources, including enemies, falling a large distance, damage-over-time (DOTs), or the environment.

Enemies

Damage from enemies will scale rapidly based on the relative player: enemy difference in power level, and the player's defensive level against the used attack style. In addition, the published health on the monster pages assumes the player is wearing power level 1 armour. See monster hitpoint scaling for more information.

Fall damage

Falling a large distance will significantly damage the player, scaling exponentially to the distance fallen. Jumping from 11 metres below will start to damage the player by one to two hitpoints.

  • Leggings of lightness is the only item to reduce fall damage.
  • Windstep significantly reduces fall damage.
  • Encumbered or player weight does not affect fall damage.

Damage over time (DOTs)

  • Poison: Deals either 3 HP/s, or 4 HP/s, depending on the source, over an average of 8–10 seconds.
    • Can be negated and protected against with antipoison, or accumulation rate reduced with Fungal Fortitude.
  • Bleed: Once gauge is full, deals 30-32 damage in one second.
    • The accumulation rate is reduced with Coagulated if the player eats a meat pizza.
  • Burning: Deals 4-8 damage over 6 seconds.
  • Soulscourge: Once the gauge is full, it deals 10 damage over five seconds.
  • Starvation/dehydration: Either 1 HP/s for either 0 sustenance or hydration, or 2 HP/s for both 0 sustenance and hydration.
  • Scorch: Works similar to Soulscourge.

Traps

Traps within dragonkin vaults damage the player when mistimed or overlooked. These include: Spike Traps and spear traps. Ways to avoid taking damage include casting the Windstep if there is enough overhead clearance or timing the retraction of the trap.

Death

Death occurs when a player's health reaches zero. In a standard death, a player will appear at the last respawn point they set before dying (claiming a player-crafted bed for the first time, or the church at the start of the game if no bed is claimed), keeping their cape, all equipped armour, arrows/bolts, and runes at the time of death. All other items are placed in a gravestone close to the location of death. There is no time limit for the player to return to their grave.

Upon retrieving all items from the player's gravestone, the game will attempt to place the items back into the player's inventory in the orientation they were at death, placing items into the same hot-bar slots at the time of the player's death.

  • Gathering any items during the run back to the player's grave will interfere with the game's placement of the items into the previous hot-bar locations.
  • Dying before reaching the first gravestone will create a second gravestone working exactly as the first, if the player had items with them that would go into one.
  • Upon death, sustenance, hydration, and rest will all be reduced.
    • Sustenance and hydration will be reduced by 10/100, unless the player is already at or below 35/100; in this case, they will be reset to the minimum of 25/100.
    • Rest will be reduced by 15/100, unless the player is at or below 40/100; in this case, it will be reset to the minimum of 25/100.
  • In the event no respawn point was set by the player, or a previous respawn point was removed by destroying the claimed bed, the player will respawn in the starting chapel.

Notes

  • Upon reaching 0 sustenance or hydration, the player will start taking damage until reaching 1 health; the player cannot die from having 0 in either of these attributes. This damage can stack with 0 hydration and 0 sustenance, making the player's health drop even more quickly to 1, however, this still cannot kill the player.
    • Health lost with either 0 sustenance or hydration occurs at a rate of 1 HP/s.
    • Health lost with both 0 sustenance and hydration occurs at a rate of 2 HP/s.

concepts.title: Sanguine Urn
concepts.lead: Sanguine urns are an interactable scenery item that gives the player 10 health to their total health pool. These urns can be found very easily through the world map and the icon can be found on the compass within 50–60 meters. Some of these urns can be found in caves or underground areas, but not in vaults.
