Journal

This journal entry is within the Tutorials section of the in the Knowledge part.

The dragonkin discovered a unique and powerful resources in their time on Ashenfall, the blood of a goddess - Lougrim. She was a moon deity, in-tune with the natural world, the forest and a source of great vitality. Her blood carries some of those properties. If imbibed, even small amounts of blood, centuries old, can enhance one's vital spark, making you hardier and healthier. You can take more damage and survive greater threats, overcome the most dangerous challenges. The blood was kept in a number of urns, which were separated and hidden across Ashenfall, in hope that the resource wouldn't easily be destroyed. It was to be a linchpin in their great endeavours, until Kuldra laid those lofty dreams to rest. Once they were buried, deep within the earth, but time, and other, more mysterious source, have brought them to the surface just in time for your arrival. Anyone, and by that, I mean you, dear reader, can use the power of these urns for yourself. Explore Ashenfall and seek out these hidden locations; take the power of the goddess for your own. Whilst the blood may be weaker than before, it will still make you healthier, increasing your ability to stand against the great threat of Ashenfall.

concepts.title: Stamina
concepts.lead: Stamina is used for most actions, such as determining how long a player can run. Stamina is consumed from actions relating to skills (mining or woodcutting), attacking (melee, magic, and ranged), using special attacks, blocking, running, dodging, and jumping. It is displayed as a bar underneath the health bar at the bottom of the screen. Hydration affects stamina regeneration, and rest affects the maximum stamina a player has.
concepts.html:
Stamina is used for most actions, such as determining how long a player can run. Stamina is consumed from actions relating to skills (mining or woodcutting), attacking (melee, magic, and ranged), using special attacks, blocking, running, dodging, and jumping. It is displayed as a bar underneath the health bar at the bottom of the screen. Hydration affects stamina regeneration, and rest affects the maximum stamina a player has.

Cost

Stamina is depleted in varying amounts depending on the player's action.

  • The maximum stamina a player can have is 100.
  • All costs below are calculated without permanent skill levelling perks or other stamina reducing effects.
    • To use a special attack, the player would need to be at least level 8 Attack. This would give them five 1% stamina cost reduction perks from the Attack tree, meaning a special attack from a warhammer would cost: 40 x 0.95 = 38.
    • Unarmed attacks are unaffected by skill levelling perks.
  • After the player takes no stamina-requiring actions for 3s, stamina regeneration will begin. This is the base regeneration delay.
    • The player can reduce this delay through perks, such as the 1/3 magic armour set bonus - see below. Regeneration rates rely on hydration status.
  • If a stamina cost were to bring the player below 0 and the player currently has >0 stamina points, the action will still be usable, and instead the player will be brought to 0.
    • Although the stamina gauge only shows whole numbers, the gauge and calculations are actually decimal numbers.
      • The gauge value shown will always be rounded down; however, the decimal remains.
  • Dodging can animation cancel most player animations in the game.
    • E.g., a player can cast Abyssal Snare, and just as the cast animation completes, dodge to avoid enemy mechanics.
      • This can outright cancel player actions, so timing is imperative.
  • Stamina-reducing perks will not stack on each other if they are applied towards the same skill.

concepts.title: Hydration
concepts.lead: Hydration is a player attribute which determines how thirsty they are - if a player is low on hydration, their stamina regeneration will be negatively affected. To increase hydration, players can drink water or infusions.
concepts.html:
Hydration is a player attribute which determines how thirsty they are - if a player is low on hydration, their stamina regeneration will be negatively affected. To increase hydration, players can drink water or infusions.

Effects

  • The maximum hydration a player can have is 100. Attempting to consume another drink will make the top of its in-game infobox say, CANNOT CONSUME.
  • Immediately after taking a drink for hydration, the player receives an invisible perk (buff) that stops the degradation of hydration for 60s.
    • Interestingly, this timer begins upon clicking the drink and starting the use delay timer of 2s, not after this delay is completed, as one would assume. In this way, the buff is only 58s long + the 2-second use delay timer.
  • Hydration status slowly dwindles over time. When equal to or less than 25/100, hydration dwindles at half the rate:
Hydration levelDwindle rate
>25/100(1/11)/s, or 1pt/11s
≤25/100(1/22)/s, or 1pt/22s

This means going from 100-0 hydration takes 1,375s (22m 55s).

  • If the player has less than or equal to 25/100 rest, hydration will dwindle more quickly (1s faster per point lost at base rate):
≤25/100 rest
Hydration levelDwindle rate
>25/100(1/10)/s, or 1pt/10s
≤25/100(1/20)/s, or 1pt/20s

At this rest threshold, the player would instead go from 100-0 hydration in 1,250s (20m 50s)

  • Every 25 hydration will increase the player's natural stamina regeneration:
Hydration levelStamina regeneration
100/1006.0/s
75/1004.5/s
50/1003.0/s
25/1001.5/s
0/1000.75/s
  • Upon reaching 0 hydration, the player will start taking damage until reaching 1 health; the player cannot die from having 0 hydration. The damage can stack with 0 sustenance, making the player's health drop more quickly to 1, however this still cannot kill the player.
    • At 0 hydration, the player will lose 1 HP/s.
    • At both 0 hydration and 0 sustenance, the player will lose 2 HP/s
  • Like sustenance, while at 0 hydration, the player cannot use the spell Eye of Oculus. This means when building large structures or player homes with the use of Eye of Oculus, hydration, and sustenance items are required.
  • Like with sustenance but unlike rest, upon death hydration will be reduced by 10/100, unless the player is already at or below 35/100; in this case, it will be reset to the minimum of 25/100.
  • After a full night's rest, hydration is reduced:
    • 65-100: Hydration reduced by up to 40, randomly
    • 25-65: Hydration reduced randomly by up to 40, to a minimum of 25
    • 0-25: Hydration maintained at current value.

Player Announcements

Upon reaching certain thresholds of hydration, a player announcement on screen will display:

25/100: Your throat feels dry. You could do with a drink of water.

5/100: Your lips crack and your heart races from dehydration.

0/100: You are critically dehydrated. Your body can't take much more of this.

concepts.title: Scorch
concepts.lead: Scorch is a status effect that builds while in direct sunlight in the Umbral Sands and falls off in shade or at night. When the meter fills, it will drain 1 health and 1.5 hydration per second.
concepts.html:
Scorch is a status effect that builds while in direct sunlight in the Umbral Sands and falls off in shade or at night. When the meter fills, it will drain 1 health and 1.5 hydration per second.

The perk Frosted Flavours from cactus water, the Cooling infusions, monkfish skewers and Umbral kebab and the armour desert hood, desert robes, and desert robe legs provide Scorch resistance. The more sources of Scorch resistance a player has, the longer they can remain in direct sunlight. The armour provide a bit better resistance than the perks, but they all stack. The time a player can remain in direct sunlight before being afflicted by Scorch is as follows:

Additionally, the Scorch build up is reduced to about half near sunrise (around 7:30 AM in-game) and sunset (around 8 PM in-game).

concepts.title: Death
concepts.lead: Death occurs when a player's hitpoints reach 0. Upon dying, a system message in the chat interface will say, "USERNAME has died". In a standard death, players can have multiple gravestones and can retrieve their items at any time. In addition, players will retain their skill experience. In a hard mode death, players can only have one gravestone; not claiming their items from their first gravestone and dying again will delete all of the items in the previous gravestone.
concepts.html:
Death occurs when a player's hitpoints reach 0. Upon dying, a system message in the chat interface will say, "USERNAME has died". In a standard death, players can have multiple gravestones and can retrieve their items at any time. In addition, players will retain their skill experience. In a hard mode death, players can only have one gravestone; not claiming their items from their first gravestone and dying again will delete all of the items in the previous gravestone.

Respawning

After dying, players in both normal and hard difficulty worlds will either spawn back at their claimed bed or the lodestone inside Wise Old Man's temple if no bed has been claimed.

Types of Death

Players can die from the following:

  • Combat from an enemy or another player with the PvP setting on
  • Falling - either from cliffs or other high areas
  • Poison
  • Burning

concepts.title: Durability
concepts.lead: Durability is a property of equippable items in RuneScape: Dragonwilds - the durability of tools, weapons, armour, and shields will decrease as they are used in combat. There is no loss of effectiveness associated with loss of durability, but an object will break when it reaches zero. Durability can be repaired either at the facility where the object was made, such as a smithing anvil or crafting table, or by the use of the Magical Mending spell. It should be noted that repairing at a facility requires raw materials, while the Magical Mending spell consumes only runes, and as such is likely to be the economical option. However, Magical Mending will only restore half of the tool's maximum durability. For example, if a logging axe is at 234/1200, using Magical Mending on the item will add 600, leaving the durability at 834/1200.

concepts.title: Inventory
concepts.lead: The inventory allows players to view and organise their collected items. There is a standard weight limit of 400 for the inventory which includes items in the players primary inventory, hot-bar, and armour slots.
concepts.html:
The inventory allows players to view and organise their collected items. There is a standard weight limit of 400 for the inventory which includes items in the players primary inventory, hot-bar, and armour slots.

Players, through levelling Agility, can unlock perks to increase the weight limit by 75 units, to a maximum of 550.

Effects

  • The inventory has 5 sections: 8 hot-bar slots, 5 armour slots, 24 primary inventory slots, 24 rune pouch slots, 24 quiver slots and 24 quest item slots.
  • On death, all items stored in the primary inventory will be lost to a gravestone (see page for specifics of death mechanics); the armour and shield that are currently equipped will be kept along with runes and key items.
  • Items in the primary inventory, hot-bar, and armour slots can be dropped, moved, or split via a key-bound user hot-key.
  • Activating any usable item (such as food, drinks, packs, or armour) places it on a delay timer of 2 seconds before an item in the same stack can be used again.
    • This precludes swapping armour sets rapidly, such as is commonly done in the RuneScape universe. However, with accurate mouse moments, armour can instead be clicked and dragged into the appropriate armour slot in the inventory, bypassing this delay timer.
    • A stack of items, when used, will not open the stack, but just 1 item in the stack. To use a stack more rapidly (such as when opening goblin packs or bird nests), the stack can be split into separate inventory spaces. Each separate stack has its own delay timer which can drastically reduce the amount of time required.
    • Items can also be used inside of containers such as chests.

Over-Encumbrance

If the player's combined inventory and armour weights exceed their carrying capacity, they will become Encumbered.

  • Encumbered players cannot run or jump, and move at 60% normal speed.
    • Other speed penalties (such as using items or trudging through water) stack with the Encumbered speed penalty.
    • This speed penalty does not scale based on weight (so 401/400 will incur the same penalties as 1000/400).
  • Encumbered players no longer pick up nearby items automatically. The player may still pick up items manually, but this further increases the player's weight.
    • The exception to this rule is the complete prevention of the player taking from bushes, or picking vegetables and flax, while Encumbered.
  • The leggings of lightness are currently the only armour piece that increases the player's weight limit, increasing it by 50 (to 600 maximum).
    • Depending on the player's Agility level, this can vary from 450 maximum carry weight to 600 max.
  • The terrorbird mount can increase player's weight limit to 200
  • If the player becomes too tired through rest depletion, the maximum weight decreases by 100 (to a base of 300).
  • Encumbrance has no maximum limit; however, carrying more weight increases how many law runes will be consumed when utilising a lodestone teleport.

concepts.title: Compass
concepts.lead: The compass is an overhead interface where players can navigate and find their respawn point/bed, death marker, active main/side quests, and the NPC markers needed for those active quests. The compass features four cardinal directions, north, south, east, and west, with a distance to the markers in metres. Players can also view other players if they are in a multiplayer world. Casting the Summon Stone Spirits spell can display nearby clay and ores up to 200m.

concepts.title: Lodestone
concepts.lead: A lodestone is a platform that allows the player to travel if another lodestone is placed elsewhere. When the first lodestone is built, the inactive lodestone in the Temple starting area becomes active as well. Teleporting between two lodestones costs a varied amount of law runes, depending on the distance of the target lodestone and the weight of the player.
concepts.html:
A lodestone is a platform that allows the player to travel if another lodestone is placed elsewhere. When the first lodestone is built, the inactive lodestone in the Temple starting area becomes active as well. Teleporting between two lodestones costs a varied amount of law runes, depending on the distance of the target lodestone and the weight of the player.

Permanent locations

Teleportation costs

Teleporting between two lodestones costs an amount of law runes based on the distance between them and the amount of weight carried, with a minimum cost of one law rune. Note that the number shown on the lodestone map is calculated by the following:

Law\, runes = (Distance\, to\, target\, lodestone\, \div 1000) \times (Total\, weight\, \div 1000)

For example, teleporting 8000 meters (the length of 2000 square tiles) while weighing 400 kilograms would require 8 \times 0.4 = 3.2 law runes which rounds to 3.

Recipe

Recipe Build Menu · Construction 80 xp
32 × Stone, 20 × Rune Essence, 1 × Vault Core → 1 × Lodestone

Recipe tree

Restrictions

Players cannot build lodestones in instanced areas, inside Dragonkin Vaults, or in specific areas in Ashenfall.

Dowdun Reach

Most areas within Dowdun Reach prevent the players from building lodestones, with the exceptions of The Approach, The Pastures, The Menagerie and The Courtyard. Refer to the image on the side.

concepts.title: Anima
concepts.lead: Anima is the living energy of the universe and all living beings, and the source of magic. After the created Gielinor, and prepared to sleep while their eggs consumed the planet's anima slowly, they discovered some impure, "wild" anima which they didn't like, and they used the continent of Ashenfall to "vent out" the impure anima from the world. This resulted in the Anima Twist phenomenon enveloping the continent, with its effects getting stronger further into the continent, this event is known as the Anima Twist. The Anima Twist affects not only the environment, but the creatures and people living on it, as well as magic itself. This results in common materials like wood and stone being capable of lasting hundreds or even thousands of years, and the inhabitants of the continent to become Amalgamated, creatures that would be enhanced with elemental properties due to the land's wild anima. The effects of the Anima Twist can be observed in the transformed wildlife, with wolves developing manes made of leaves, deer possessing reed-like fronds, and trees displaying leaves in unusual hues resembling sunset.
concepts.html:
Anima is the living energy of the universe and all living beings, and the source of magic. After the created Gielinor, and prepared to sleep while their eggs consumed the planet's anima slowly, they discovered some impure, "wild" anima which they didn't like, and they used the continent of Ashenfall to "vent out" the impure anima from the world. This resulted in the Anima Twist phenomenon enveloping the continent, with its effects getting stronger further into the continent, this event is known as the Anima Twist. The Anima Twist affects not only the environment, but the creatures and people living on it, as well as magic itself. This results in common materials like wood and stone being capable of lasting hundreds or even thousands of years, and the inhabitants of the continent to become Amalgamated, creatures that would be enhanced with elemental properties due to the land's wild anima. The effects of the Anima Twist can be observed in the transformed wildlife, with wolves developing manes made of leaves, deer possessing reed-like fronds, and trees displaying leaves in unusual hues resembling sunset.

Affected wildlife

  • Deer - Deer were affected by the surrounding anima, making their hides valuable and versatile as armour, such as leather armour.
  • Giant and putrid rats - Rats gorge on plants that are infused with wild anima, making their bodies more aggressive, larger, and dangerous over time. In some poisonous areas such as the Whispering Swamp and Bloodblight Swamp, giant rats would also feast on the poisonous plants and become even stronger and poisonous.
  • Wolves - Wolves were infused with anima, making them faster and stronger through their teeth. Many Brynmoor villagers were killed because of this phenomenon, and Wild Knights would hunt them down to prevent further attacks. Some wolves would absorb more ambient anima, making them stronger than their regular counterparts, turning into dire wolves. The strength of the dire wolves would make the Wild Knights respect their power, leaving the wolves alone.
  • Wild lapulis vines - Wild lapulis vines absorbed the magic into their plant cells and have become sentient, prepared to shock villagers and adventurers alike.

Amalgamated

The Anima Twist not only affected wildlife and the fauna, but also local villagers, who also absorbed the anima. The Amalgamated were often seen as less than human and were the subject of significant violence. The Wild Knights often risked their lives to sneak into towns and rescue Amalgamated from their persecution. However, the prejudice eventually culminated in a great schism where humans fought to purge Ashenfall of the Amalgamated.

See also

  • Wild anima

concepts.title: Dragonkin Vault
concepts.lead: Dragonkin vaults or vaults are special dungeons that can be found within the continent of Ashenfall. These vaults contain deadly traps, rats, goblins, and vault guardians. However, there are blueprint recipes and other rewards hidden in each vault in the form of a treasure chest in every vault. If a player dies inside a vault, a gravestone will be placed at the outside entrance. It should also be noted that all players will need to discover the locations of these vaults in order for them to appear on your map.

Journal

Hidden across Ashenfall are the Vaults, the ruined remains of dragonkin research. Each contains lost knowledge or riches, sealed away so that none but their jealous masters may possess them. Paranoid and wary of intrusion by the "lesser races", the Dragonkin of Ashenfall filled each of the vaults with an array of deadly traps and they created servitor guardians. Although time has whittled away at most of the mysteries, the cruel claws of entropy rending secrets to shreds, there still remain pieces of powerful knowledge that bold adventurers might be able to salvage.

concepts.title: Vault Core
concepts.lead: A vault core can be found on pedestals in dragonkin vaults. Their primary use is to make lodestones, which serve as a teleport location that can be travelled to from any other lodestone the player has placed on the map. They are also components of several masterworks, such as the abyssal whip and dragonblight shield. Note that these respawn in their plinths every three in-game days, so their quantity is not limited.
concepts.html:
A vault core can be found on pedestals in dragonkin vaults. Their primary use is to make lodestones, which serve as a teleport location that can be travelled to from any other lodestone the player has placed on the map. They are also components of several masterworks, such as the abyssal whip and dragonblight shield. Note that these respawn in their plinths every three in-game days, so their quantity is not limited.

Products

Item sources

Journal

A heart of alchemically modified rune essence. Layers of complex enchantments and veins of anima run through this core. It allows it to absorb ambient anima from its surroundings, which in turn powers the various functions of the vault guardian servitors. This marvel of dragonkin science had revolutionary potential. The ability to create power sources that thrived off of the ambient anima of the region. Ashenfall, with it’s surfeit of magical power, was the perfect place for such technology, and the dragonkin would apply it to all of their arcane machinery.

concepts.title: Vault Shard
concepts.lead: Vault shards are items used in crafting several items and can be obtained from vault guardians found in dragonkin vaults.
concepts.html:
Vault shards are items used in crafting several items and can be obtained from vault guardians found in dragonkin vaults.

Products

Item sources

Journal

A shard of rune essence, refined and manipulated by dragonkin alchemy. Tiny lines, like veins, run through the shard in very specific patterns, allowing the precise control of anima flow through the construction. When used correctly, these shards can create magical circuits, allowing the vault guardians to move, sense and attack with impunity. It was the dragonkin Lacrussa who discovered this technology, and it paved the way for powerful servitors to be constructed. Ultimately, she would consider the technology a failure, albeit a useful one.

concepts.title: Ascension Shard
concepts.lead: Ascension shard is a basic item used to craft ascension cores, which are in turn used to upgrade masterwork weapons into stronger forms.
concepts.html:
Ascension shard is a basic item used to craft ascension cores, which are in turn used to upgrade masterwork weapons into stronger forms.

Item sources

Power Level 4

Power Level 5

Power Level 6

Power Level 8

Journal

Avisk was many things, arrogant, manipulative, cruel, but he was also a genius. Within the dreamscapes of the nightmare crucible, he found a way to reshape matter, reforging it into its ideal form. He took weapons and moulded them into stronger versions. He took a staff and re-imagined it stronger and more deadly. Using the stuff of nightmares, he found a limited way to reshape the world. We are, perhaps, fortunate that it was limited to such small scales. These shards are a part of that power. When combined with a fully realised core, they can upgrade legendary equipment into stronger versions of itself. A power we should hope Kuldra never finds.

concepts.title: Ascension Core
concepts.lead: Ascension cores are items used and crafted in the mystic forge to ascend masterwork weapons from their base power level to the next tier. They are made by combining ascension shards or by collecting them as rewards for completing Nightmare Crucible instances in Umbral Sands. For most cores, players can gain core shards by killing mini-bosses (such as red dragons, green dragons, and blue dragons).
concepts.html:
Ascension cores are items used and crafted in the mystic forge to ascend masterwork weapons from their base power level to the next tier. They are made by combining ascension shards or by collecting them as rewards for completing Nightmare Crucible instances in Umbral Sands. For most cores, players can gain core shards by killing mini-bosses (such as red dragons, green dragons, and blue dragons).

The only core that cannot be crafted thus far is the power level 7 ascension core, which can only be acquired by completing the Nightmare Crucible.

Recipe

Journal

Imagine, if you will, what you could do if you could harness your dreams. If you could take an ideal, refine it and reforge it using the power of the imagination. Such a technology is terrifying in its potential, and Avisk was the first to explore its possibilities. This core is a part of the nightmare, refined and reforged over and over again, then condescended into a singularity and sealed within dragonkin technology. It is a mote of potential, waiting to be released. The technology is limited for now. Avisk was only able to use it to improve his existing equipment, as well as to empower the beasts he trapped in the nightmare dreamscape. Fortunately, limited as it might be, you should find this technology particularly useful, as it will allow you upgrade and improve some of your more unique equipment, such as masterwork gear.

concepts.title: Mystic Forge
concepts.lead: The mystic forge is a crafting station that allows for the creation of staves, other weapons, and more powerful capes, and uses ascension cores in ascending masterwork weapons and vestige armour. This replaces some of the functionality of the smithing anvil and crafting table.
concepts.html:
The mystic forge is a crafting station that allows for the creation of staves, other weapons, and more powerful capes, and uses ascension cores in ascending masterwork weapons and vestige armour. This replaces some of the functionality of the smithing anvil and crafting table.

The mystic forge is unlocked upon obtaining a bronze bar in the player's inventory.

Recipe

Recipe Build Menu · Construction 12 xp
6 × Bronze Bar, 20 × Ash Logs, 8 × Coarse Thread, 1 × Vault Core → 1 × Mystic Forge

Products

Ascension Upgrades

Players can ascend their masterwork weapons and armour by collecting ascension cores through defeating enemies that drop ascension shards and creating them in the mystic forge or the cores directly through the Nightmare Crucibles. In order to start ascending weapons and armour, players will need at least 1 ascension core of the next power level available in either their inventory or chest along with a suitable item to ascend. This item must first be placed within the slot to ascend (it still stays in the inventory).

Ascending a masterwork weapon or armour piece consumes the core to bring it to the highest power level available to the player (<4 to 4, 4 to 5, 5 to 6, etc) and, if the player has multiple cores to reach the current highest power level in the game, the weapon or armour piece will require ascending twice to consume the cores needed to ascend to the highest power level in the game. It is worth noting here that weapons and armour that are already the highest power level cannot be ascended until a new major update.

concepts.title: Garou Chit
concepts.lead: Garou chit are currency used by the Moon Garou in Umbral Sands.
concepts.html:
Garou chit are currency used by the Moon Garou in Umbral Sands.

Item sources

Garou chit can be found inside chests within the Umbral Sands region as well as from selling items to a garou merchant. Only a few items can be sold for chit, and the three available merchants have separate lists for what they will purchase from the player.

Strategy

When starting off, players can obtain a substantial amount of chits by completing the various side quests unlocked during the Umbral Sands main quest, Icthlarin's Little Helper.

An efficient way to farm garou chit after unlocking the appropriate merchants is to sell surplus materials with limited utility at this point in the player's progression, such as maple logs and coarse animal fur.

One of the most effective materials to sell is leather from dragons, as they have no further use beyond the few weapons and armour made from them: Each of the 5 green dragons drop 6-8 green dragon hide which can be processed into 12-16 green dragonhide leather worth 100 garou chit each, the 3 blue dragons drop 6-8 blue dragon hide which can be processed into 12-16 blue dragon leather worth 120 garou chit each, and the 5(ish) red dragons drop 6-8 red dragon hide which can be processed into 12-16 red dragonhide leather worth 140 garou chit each!

That's 18,720 to 24,960 garou chit for farming all of them, which can easily be done in a day, and once every four or five days! While farming for dragon's rare drops like the amulet of glory, this can be a substantial source of garou chit in the meantime. That's not to mention the dragon teeth and dragon blood as well as other drops that can also be used in other recipes or valuable items, such as cooling ferocious infusion and draconic leather.

Another efficient method involves completely clearing the north-westernmost area of the desert of kalphite eggs to harvest kalphite ichors. Clearing the entire zone, including the cave leading to the nearby kalphite queen, yields approximately 800 ichor, which can be sold to Iasadair for roughly 12,000 garou chit. Using a fast weapon such as keris or a hard-hitting crush weapon like an adamant warhammer or mace, together with an air enchantment speeds up the process considerably. The whole process takes about 20 minutes and can be done every day as the eggs respawn daily.

An additional way to farm garou chit for free is to purchase dragonwolf hide from Iasadair - The Merchant for 45 chit and make it into draconic leather and sell it back for 60 chit. This is also a decent way to gain Artisan experience.

Journal

Currency is a relatively new concept for the garou who, through most of their history, relied on a barter system based around hunting. As the Moon Garou settled into less hectic lives, they needed a means of trade that everyone had access to, and so created the chits to do so. These chits are formed from tiny scraps of adamantite, melted down and then stamped with the branding of the tribes. A fun fact about them is that both sides have garou heads on them, one male and one female, so you can flip as many heads in a row as you want.

concepts.title: Currencies
concepts.lead: Currencies are items that can be exchanged and are used for various transactions in RuneScape: Dragonwilds. There is no main form of currency in the game, as only five known shops take different currencies.
concepts.html:
Currencies are items that can be exchanged and are used for various transactions in RuneScape: Dragonwilds. There is no main form of currency in the game, as only five known shops take different currencies.

In-game currencies

There are currently three types of currencies used in-game:

  • Soul fragments, which can be collected within Fellhollow by killing undead or completing quests within the region and can be used in Death's Exchange.
  • Infernal fragments, which can be collected within Dowdun Reach by killing Black Knights, demons or completing quests within the region, and can be used in Evil Emporium.
  • Garou chits, which can be collected throughout Umbral Sands and used to trade with merchants.

concepts.title: Mount
concepts.lead: Mount is a mechanic that was introduced with the release of Fellhollow. It was highly requested by players who wanted a faster means to travel through Ashenfall.
concepts.html:
Mount is a mechanic that was introduced with the release of Fellhollow. It was highly requested by players who wanted a faster means to travel through Ashenfall.

Mechanics

When on a mount, players can travel through terrain, and their stamina lasts longer as well. There are two base mount versions: the terrorbird and magic carpet. If the player is attacked, dealt damage, or is building up Wither, the mount will vanish.

Types of Mounts

The list below are of the different types of mounts and their functions:

  • Terrorbirds: Terrorbird mounts are unlocked upon completing The Wild Hunt. Terrorbirds give +200 carry weight, making them good for travelling when gathering supplies.
  • Magic carpets: Magic carpets are unlocked upon completing the first section of Icthlarin's Little Helper. They do not give bonus weight, but do make traversing through Umbral Sands easier, and are much faster in the desert compared to other mounts. They are also lighter, taking less fall damage and allowing higher jumps.

Variants

The list below are of different types of colour variant of mounts, their lore and how to obtain them:

Terrorbirds
ImageNameRequirementsMisc. information
Terrorbird
  • The Wild Hunt

The nature spirits of Ashenfall serve a purpose, one denied to them by the encroaching Wither. It may seem counterintuitive to have to slay these spirits in order to bind them, but that's what nature is. It's hunt and be hunted. Kill and be killed, life is a perpetual cycle - Everything chained together.

  • This variant is automatically unlocked when completing The Wild Hunt.
Infernal blightbeak
  • Partial completion of Icthlarin's Little Helper
  • 9999

This Breed of terrorbird was the bane of most normal human residents. They would raid farms, culling livestock and devouring grain. They would storm through settlements, smashing to pieces anything within their reach. Only the Black Knights of Dowdun Reach had any success in training them, and only such madmen would even try to.

  • Bought from Domri - The Merchant.
Crimson crybaby
  • The Wild Hunt
  • Partial completion of Icthlarin's Little Helper

A breed created by a Zamorakian priest who found them far less terrifying than he had hoped. Instead of bringing fear to the masses, these terrorbirds would whimper and sob whenever forced to do any manual labour. He named the breed "crybaby" in frustration, though it remains disappointingly apt.

  • Dropped from red dragon, KotHaar-Kal, kalphite guardian or found in chests in Umbral Sands.
Mossbeak hunter
  • Partial completion of Withering Hights
  • 2000

While many terrorbirds were bred for speed, the mossbeak hunter was bred to pursue. Wild Knights would raise them to chase down dangerous prey, tiring their quarry our from their terrorbird's almost limitless stamina.

  • Bought from Death.
Springdown runner
  • The Wild Hunt

The springdown runner was bred for the races. It was quick, focused and not easily distracted by various tricks of the watching crowd. While nowadays there's less of that racing instinct, this breed of terrorbird still enjoys a good run around.

  • Dropped from green dragons, zogres, soulstone sentinels and chests found in Fellhollow.
Grassfoot screecher
  • The Wild Hunt

Druids in Brynmoor would rear these birds not as mounts, but as guard dogs for their sacred sites. The terrorbirds were raised to be quick, silent and merciless in their defence of the groves.

  • Dropped from green dragons, zogres, soulstone sentinels and chests found in Fellhollow.
Leafwood strider
  • The Wild Hunt
Oakfeather raptor
  • The Wild Hunt
  • Partial completion of Withering Heights
  • 2000

A green-feathered variant of the terrorbird, popular with the Wild Knights back in the earliest days of Bramblemead. They would raise the raptor from the moment they hatched, so that the bird could imprint on the knight and create a bond of loyalty unlike any other.

  • Bought from Death.
Coastal sunbeak
  • The Wild Hunt
  • Partial completion of Black Knight's Fortress
  • 2000

Raised along the beaches and coastal regions, the Sunbeak is a colourful terrorbird variant who enjoyed a more fish heavy diet then most.

  • Bought from Evil Emporium.
Summerbellied wagtail
  • The Wild Hunt
  • Partial completion of Black Knight's Fortress

This friendly breed of terrorbird is so named because they wag their tails in the presence of their handlers. They delight in playful displays of affection, such as jumping up and down, or attempting to chew someone's face off. Oh, how sweet.

  • Dropped from blue dragons, lesser demons, elite Black Knights and chests found in Dowdun Reach.
Eclipseborn sharpbeak
  • The Wild Hunt
  • Partial completion of Black Knight's Fortress

Legends says that this breed of terrorbird appears only during a solar eclipse. They are said to possess magical powers; the exact nature of which varies with each telling. In truth, they can hatch just like any terrorbird does and possess no known metaphysical capabilities.

  • Dropped from blue dragons, lesser demons, elite Black Knights and chests found in Dowdun Reach.
Sunkissed clawfoot
  • The Wild Hunt
  • Partial completion of Black Knight's Fortress

These bright yellow creatures love nothing more than ferreting out strange green herbs with their sharp claws. They enjoy running around plains, making screeching noises.

  • Dropped from blue dragons, lesser demons, elite Black Knights and chests found in Dowdun Reach.
Astralbeak warbler
  • The Wild Hunt
  • Partial completion of Black Knight's Fortress
  • 2000

Named after the stars, rather than the runes, the astralbeak warbler is a strange beast. On nights where the sky is clear and the moon absent, this breed of terrorbird loves nothing more than to raise its head to the heavens and warble strangely haunting melodies.

  • Bought from Evil Emporium.
Zamorakian pledgesaddle
  • The Wild Hunt
  • Partial completion of Icthlarin's Little Helper
  • 9999

Popular with the Black Knights of Dowdun Reach due to the dark and sinister colour schemes. Many of the knights would ride into battles atop these creatures, screaming about the power of chaos as they went.

  • Bought from Domri - The Merchant.
Scorchsummer ashbeak
  • The Wild Hunt
  • Partial completion of Icthlarin's Little Helper

This breed is so named because the breeder's daughter thought they were sunburned when she first saw the chicks. Bright pink and screeching, she immediately put them in buckets of water, only to face the wrath of their mother.

  • Dropped from red dragon, KotHaar-Kal, kalphite guardian or found in chests in Umbral Sands.
Applefeather mosstail
  • The Wild Hunt
  • Partial completion of Icthlarin's Little Helper

This brightly coloured breed of terrorbird gets its name from the apple orchard where the breed was first reared. The owner of the orchard had little imagination for colour combination, so when he saw red and green together the only thing that came to mind were the apples right in front of him. This is in no way similar to the naming process used by the narrative designers.

  • Dropped from red dragon, KotHaar-Kal, kalphite guardian or found in chests in Umbral Sands.
Magic Carpets
ImageNameRequirementsMisc. information
Magic Carpet
  • Partial completion of Icthlarin's Little Helper

A carpet, woven from enchanted thread. Summon it to carry you across the desert. Unlike terrorbirds, the carpet will glide smoothly across the desert, showing you a whole new world of sandy sight.

  • This variant is automatically unlocked when completing a section of Icthlarin's Little Helper.
Uzzerian umber
  • Partial completion of Icthlarin's Little Helper

The light umber tone is handcrafted by Uzzer children as part of their daily lessons. The youngsters gather round and work together to weave the complicated pattern throughout the tapestry as a means of teaching them patience as well as some useful life skills. If you look very carefully, you can see where the garou cubs have found clever ways to sneakily weave in swear words, personal symbols and odd little doodles to amuse themselves. This way, each of the carpets is unique, if not entirely desirable.

  • This variant is unlocked when studying the MOUNT: Uzzerian Umber vestige dropped from Tok-Xil in Umbral Sands.
Manafem midnight
  • Partial completion of Icthlarin's Little Helper
There are currently no known drop sources or acquisition methods available for this item.
Scorchweave Rug
  • Partial completion of Icthlarin's Little Helper
There are currently no known drop sources or acquisition methods available for this item.
Moonsilk Weave
  • Partial completion of Icthlarin's Little Helper

Legends tells us that this carpet is woven from the silk of the moon spirits of the Umbral Sands. It is said that they create those silken threads only on clear nights when the moon is full and the stars look down and give them permission. These rare carpets, therefore, only appear in times of great peace and tranquility. Traits that the Umbral Sands have not seen in some time.

  • This variant is unlocked when studying the MOUNT: Moonsilk Weave vestige dropped from Kalphite Queen in Umbral Sands.

concepts.title: Worlds
concepts.lead: Worlds are separate versions of Ashenfall created by players. Each world can have up to four players, and can have player-versus-player combat enabled/disabled. They can be played solo, opened to friends, or advertised on a public world list.
concepts.html:
Worlds are separate versions of Ashenfall created by players. Each world can have up to four players, and can have player-versus-player combat enabled/disabled. They can be played solo, opened to friends, or advertised on a public world list.

Creating a world

Players can create a world by clicking on "Create World", taking them to the Wise Old Man's temple.

Selecting a world type

Players can choose from the following types of worlds:

  • Play solo - Players can choose this type to open a private world. Players can open this world type to friends whilst playing solo.
  • Play with friends - Players can play with friends from their Steam friends list.
  • Play with community - Players can advertise their world to the public worlds list.
  • Dedicated servers

Worlds

Regardless of the type of world players choose, they can still choose whether the world is available only to the player, to the player's friends, or to the public. In addition, players can enable Friendly Fire, allowing players to have player-versus-player combat.

Modes

Standard Mode

Standard mode is the default option when starting a world. This will include only basic settings and difficulties, both of which cannot be adjusted after creating a world.

Creative Mode

Creative Mode is a game mode that allows players to play without any restrictions. It allows the player to be invincible, have unlimited resources, and roam the map to build and explore.

Custom worlds

Custom mode allows the player to set the difficulty and settings whilst playing the game.

Settings

World name

Players can choose a world name, limited to 16 characters. Spaces and special characters will still count in the 16-character limit and will be stripped out (e.g., -, ~, !, @, _, etc.)

Difficulty

Players can choose the difficulty of the world. The main differences between Normal and Hard are listed below:

NormalHard
Hydration, sustenance, and restNever reduces health below 1%Rates decrease faster and can reduce health to 0%
Skill XPRetained on deathSkill XP beyond the player's current level is lost on death
Enemy attacksDeals standard damageDeals 15% more damage to the player
Death mechanicsMultiple gravestonesOnly one gravestone can be active; dying again will make the oldest gravestone lost on death
Weaknesses & resistancesStandard weaknesses and resistancesWeaknesses and resistances both increased by 10%
Friends worlds

Friends in the player's Steam friend list who are also playing RuneScape: Dragonwilds will display the world name, friend name, players, type, PvP enabled/disabled, and last played, similar to the public worlds list. Ensure the world is not full when entering; otherwise, players will receive an error that the world is full. Note that setting a world to friends only will not be shown on the public worlds list.

Public worlds

The public worlds list includes the world name, the player who created the world, players online (of up to four players), the type of world (public or offline), PvP enabled/disabled, and last played. These can also include dedicated servers.

concepts.title: Creative Mode
concepts.lead: Creative Mode is a type of world that allows players to play in a world without any restrictions. It allows the player to have unlimited resources, undetectable by any aggressive/passive monsters, and roam the map to build and explore. Players can still fall to their death whilst in Creative Mode, but will not sustain any negative status effects, such as Poison or Wither. The character also does not need to upkeep any hydration, sustenance, or rest, or otherwise experience interruptions to impede creatively expressing themself.
concepts.html:
Creative Mode is a type of world that allows players to play in a world without any restrictions. It allows the player to have unlimited resources, undetectable by any aggressive/passive monsters, and roam the map to build and explore. Players can still fall to their death whilst in Creative Mode, but will not sustain any negative status effects, such as Poison or Wither. The character also does not need to upkeep any hydration, sustenance, or rest, or otherwise experience interruptions to impede creatively expressing themself.

Starting a creative world

Players can choose the type of world upon opening the RuneScape: Dragonwilds Steam client. From here, players can create a world and select "Standard", "Custom" or "Creative". Players can create up to 8 character slots.

Creative world features

Building

  • All building pieces will be unlocked.
  • Buildings will not have any material costs.
  • Players will have an infinite carry weight.

Crafting

  • All crafting recipes will be unlocked.
  • Crafting will not require materials.

Skills

  • All skills will be maxed.
  • Spells will not require runes or have cooldowns.
  • Lodestones will not have rune costs.

Environment and survival

  • Hunger, thirst, and endurance will always be full.
  • No world events will spawn (e.g., dragon attacks and hunted events)
  • No aggressive monsters will attack the player.

Stability

Stability is tied to the type of foundation players use in their building; the better the material, the higher players can build. In addition, players can toggle stability on or off when creating a world.

Settings

Building

Players can enable No Building Stability, where structures have no stability attribute, and players can build higher structural buildings. This setting is off by default.

Environment

Players can enable Friendly Fire, where players can attack each other. This setting is off by default.

concepts.title: Dedicated Servers
concepts.lead: Dedicated servers allow players to host persistent game instances of RuneScape: Dragonwilds, independently of their own game client. Players have several options for hosting their dedicated server, such as using Shockbyte, a web-based option, hosting at home on their computer, or using cloud hosting.

Dedicated servers allow players to host persistent game instances of RuneScape: Dragonwilds, independently of their own game client. Players have several options for hosting their dedicated server, such as using Shockbyte, a web-based option, hosting at home on their computer, or using cloud hosting.

Hosting options

ShockbyteAt HomeCloud
Setup difficultyEasyHardHardest
PriceSetDepends on electricity costs/RAMDepends on capacity
Game updatesSecuredManual backupsManual backups

Shockbyte

Pricing

Players can choose to rent a dedicated server on Shockbyte through these manually hosting plans listed below:

Pricing per month (USD)MonthlyQuarterlyAnnually
Ashwood (2 players - 3GB RAM)$9.99$8.99$7.49
Iron (4 players - 4GB RAM)$14.99$13.49$11.24
Anima (6 players - 5GB RAM)$19.99$17.99$14.99
Configuration

After purchasing a plan, players must enter configuration values. To do so, go to the config page:

Then click on RuneScape: Dragonwilds Settings.

More information about configuration settings can be found here. Optionally, players can set the World to one from their personal library. More information can be found here. Once players have set those values, write down the World Name and start the server.

Hosting at home

Dedicated servers will only run on a 64-bit operating system. Both Windows and Linux are supported, and the required RAM is 2 GB + 1 GB per player. The server can support up to 6 players, so the total required RAM is 8GB.

Ports

Dedicated servers use ports starting with 7777 by default (known as the Game Port), and the second server will use 7778 (known as the Secondary Port). However, players must ensure that the port(s) are reachable directly. This means the player's firewall, router(s), and ISP must forward UDP through those ports.

You can edit the default port by passing -port=1234 into your RSDragonwildsServer.sh execution.

Please note the following:

  • Every router between you and your ISP will need port forwarding.
  • Some ISPs will prevent you from doing port forwarding altogether. Some will have admin tools that allow you to do it. Others will require you to contact their Client Support.
  • Portforward.com has a lot of details on how to forward ports.
  • If your server appears in other players' server lists but is not joinable, then Port Forwarding likely failed somewhere.
Installing the game

The RuneScape: Dragonwilds - Dedicated Servers client is free and available on Steam. Players can download the Steam product directly or use the following CMD command line:

steamcmd +force_install_dir C:\MyInstallFolder +login anonymous +app_update 4019830 +quit

Next, run the client via Steam, or locate RSDragonwilds.exe in the dedicated server product folder and run it.

Players are strongly encouraged to add the following launch options when running: -log -NewConsole

Players who enter this command in the Launch Options will see a console feedback window that tells them exactly what's happening on the server. To do so:

  1. Go to Steam > RuneScape: Dragonwilds Dedicated Server.
  2. Right-click and select Properties
  3. Set the launch option to -log -NewConsole
Ensuring versions match

If the dedicated server is no longer visible, use the logs to verify that the current game version matches the dedicated server version. Mismatches are likely to occur whenever an update or hotfix is released. You can find the version your dedicated server runs at the top of its logs.

Players can find the client version in the top-left corner. Note that the version is formatted as such:

Hosting in the cloud

Cloud server providers are pending and will be scheduled for a later update.

Configuration values

Dedicated servers require several settings to be configured properly. Changing those values while the server is running will result in those changes being lost.

Linux configuration values can be found under: Files > RSDragonwilds > Saved > Config > Linux > DedicatedServer.ini

Windows configuration values will need to be copied from Linux and created in: Files > RSDragonwilds > Saved > Config > WindowsServer > DedicatedServer.ini

Mandatory configuration values are:

  • Owner ID: this is your RuneScape: Dragonwilds Player ID. It can be found in-game at the bottom of the Settings Menu. The server will not start without your owner ID.
  • Server Name: the name of your server, no matter what world it may run in.
  • Default World Name: Upon startup, your dedicated server will create a default world. This configuration value lets you decide how it should be named.
  • Admin password: Anyone who knows this password can enter the Server Management tab in the Pause Menu > Settings menu. They will be considered as Admins until the Admin Password is changed again. You can see the list of people who used the Admin Password to access the Server Management screen by opening Files > RSDragonwilds > Saved > Config > Linux > DedicatedServer.ini.

Optional configuration values are:

  • World password: This will supersede any password stored in the world. Can be left empty if you want anyone to join your world.

Finding my Dedicated Server

To find the created dedicated server, go to the Public tab of the Worlds screen:

In the search tab, type the world name. Note that the world name is case sensitive.

After a few seconds, the created server should appear. If the server cannot be loaded:

  • Check if the server and clients are using the latest version of the current game. Note that Shockbyte servers automatically restart to the latest server version.
  • Make sure the world name is currently running.
  • Ensure the mandatory configuration variables have been set.
  • Look at the console log to see if there are any errors. RAM errors may occur, indicating that the allocated RAM for home-hosting servers may be insufficient.
    • Logs for the server itself can be found in C:\Users\%userprofile%\AppData\Local\RSDragonwilds\Saved\Logs as well, this may help with troubleshooting. For advanced troubleshooting, send these logs to ModMail on the Official RuneScape Dragonwilds Discord.

World management

When a dedicated server starts, it loads the latest .sav file available in C:\Users\%userprofile%\AppData\Local\RSDragonwilds\Saved\Savegames. If the folder doesn't contain a .sav file, the dedicated server will create a default Standard world with the default config.ini values applied.

How to: Move a world to my Dedicated Server

When copying an existing world save to your dedicated server, DO NOT CHANGE THE FILE NAME.

If you have already done this, either copy the world save file with the original name, or rename it BACK to its original name.

Verify that the server is saving the world correctly by checking that character progress is maintained when leaving and rejoining the server, and that restarting the server keeps buildings and objects. The server will need to be restarted. If the server was started with an edited filename, progress will be lost.

  1. Ensure your dedicated server is stopped.
  2. Back up every file from C:\Users\%userprofile%\AppData\Local\RSDragonwilds\Saved\Savegames to a safe location (on the dedicated server drive, the player's own drive, or the cloud).
  3. Empty all contents from the C:\Users\%userprofile%\AppData\Local\RSDragonwilds\Saved\Savegames. DO NOT delete this folder!
  4. Copy your local world .sav file from your hard drive: C:\Users\%userprofile%\AppData\Local\RSDragonwilds\Saved\SaveGames to your dedicated server hard drive (separate from the C: drive)RSDragonwilds/Saved/Savegames.
  5. Start the server.

How to: Create a new world with custom settings

  1. Run your local RuneScape: Dragonwilds via Steam.
  2. Create a new world with all the custom settings you need (Standard, Custom, Creative, etc).
  3. Enter the world and make sure the player's surrounding textures are loaded (wait approximately 1–2 minutes).
  4. Exit the world by pressing the and clicking on Exit Game.
  5. Back up every file from RSDragonwilds/Saved/Savegames to a safe location (on the dedicated server drive, your own drive, or the cloud).
  6. Empty all contents from the C:\Users\%userprofile%\AppData\Local\RSDragonwilds\Saved\Savegames. DO NOT delete this folder!
  7. Copy your local world .sav file from your hard drive: C:\Users\%userprofile%\AppData\Local\RSDragonwilds\Saved\SaveGames to your dedicated server hard drive (separate from the C: drive)RSDragonwilds/Saved/Savegames.
  8. Start the server.

How to: Back up saves

It is very important to back up saves before updating your current dedicated server to the latest update. Please see the following to ensure you can save your archived saves:

  1. Go to RSDragonwilds/Saved/Savegames
  2. Copy any world save you want to back up elsewhere on the dedicated server drive, on your personal computer, or in the cloud.
  3. You can rename the files to include the backup save in their names to make things simpler.

User management

Dedicated servers divides users into three categories:

RoleAssigningPermissions
OwnerPlayer ID matching the Owner ID set in configCan ban/unban anyone offline or online.
AdminPlayers with the admin password (can enter in the Server Management page)Can ban regular players who are online, but cannot unban.
Regular userPlayers who have the World NameCannot ban or unban any player, including the admins or the owner.

Known issues

  • Inviting a player to your dedicated server via Steam Invites doesn't currently connect as intended.
  • Changing dedicatedserver.ini values while the server is running will result in those changes being lost.
    • You will need to search for the world file name in your server browser, not the server name plus the suffix (e.g., .sav)
    • For example, if your world file name is Dragonwilds_World1.sav, you will need to make sure the world name value is Dragonwilds_World1.
  • The server binaries are not available separately from the game.

concepts.lead: Hardcore mode is a feature planned for a future update, which would aim to make the base game experience much more difficult. It will primarily feature "permadeath"; a player who dies will not respawn, and a new world or character would need to be started from scratch.
concepts.html:
Hardcore mode is a feature planned for a future update, which would aim to make the base game experience much more difficult. It will primarily feature "permadeath"; a player who dies will not respawn, and a new world or character would need to be started from scratch.

While not currently confirmed, other features have been suggested that may be included, such as more aggressive, powerful, and plentiful enemies, or more punishing hydration, sustenance, and rest.

concepts.title: Nightmare Crucible
concepts.lead: The Nightmare Crucible is a combat activity found within the Umbral Sands region of Ashenfall. It is meant to act akin to ''s and ''s in where the player fights against all of the toughest enemies Ashenfall has to offer thus far.
concepts.html:
The Nightmare Crucible is a combat activity found within the Umbral Sands region of Ashenfall. It is meant to act akin to s and s in where the player fights against all of the toughest enemies Ashenfall has to offer thus far.

To unlock a Nightmare Crucible, the player must use a corresponding item, called an Engram, whose title matches the Crucible of interest. An Engram only provides a single attempt to a given Crucible: - Single player: win or lose, the crucible will re-lock once the player enters it once. - Multiplayer: The crucible will only remain open as long as at least one player remains in it.

If the player dies while inside a Crucible, their gravestone will appear outside the crucible entrance.

The interior of Nightmare Crucibles are wide open, flat areas with almost no obstacles, save for the small Reward Pedestal in the center, and no safe spots for ranged or magic users. There is enough space to run around the arena in a circle and fight enemies from afar, but there is nowhere to hide. It is sometimes possible, depending on the player's positioning, to attract the attention of only a subset of the enemies in a given Crucible at a time.

Location

Enemies to Defeat

Note: The level of the enemies are based on the location of the Nightmare Crucible.

Umbral Sands

Nightmare Crucible of Humiliation - in Dunes of Uzzer (Northeast) - Unlock with Crucible Engram of Humiliation

  • 1 x blue dragon
  • 1 x green dragon
  • 1 x red dragon

Nightmare Crucible of the Hounded - in Manafem Plains (Southwest) - Unlock with Crucible Engram of the Hounded

  • 2 x zogre

Nightmare Crucible of Betrayal - in The Burning Spire (Southeast) - Unlock with Crucible Engram of Betrayal

  • 1 x Black Knight Titan
  • 1 x green dragon or abyssal demon

Nightmare Crucible of Helplessness - in Alcarrid Oasis (Northwest) - Unlock with Crucible Engram of Helplessness

  • 2 x garou thane
  • 1 x green dragon

Rewards

Enemies in Nightmare Crucibles do not drop anything upon defeat.

Upon killing all monsters in the Nightmare Crucible, one ascension core is rewarded by interacting with the reward pedestal. In multiplayer sessions, additional players do not receive additional ascension cores. In general, one engram corresponds to one ascension core, assuming the crucible is cleared.

Note: Currently there is a bug where if Buddy, summoned from the Pharaoh's Sceptre special attack, is alive, the challenge is not counted as completed. Player must wait for Buddy to despawn for the challenge to complete.

You can despawn Buddy by casting your special with the pharaoh's sceptre

concepts.title: Combat
concepts.lead: Combat is an event in RuneScape: Dragonwilds in which two or more players and/or creatures fight. Combat is based around a randomly generated numbers in the form of "damage", which deplete a target's life points. The damage done by the parties involved is determined by several factors, including weapons and equipment.
concepts.html:
Combat is an event in RuneScape: Dragonwilds in which two or more players and/or creatures fight. Combat is based around a randomly generated numbers in the form of "damage", which deplete a target's life points. The damage done by the parties involved is determined by several factors, including weapons and equipment.

Players can influence their effectiveness in combat in many ways, such as boosting their combat via perks.

Combat

The three combat classes in RuneScape: Dragonwilds are melee, ranged, and magic.

Melee

  • Melee armour offers a -% in block stamina cost, +% in crit chance after blocking, and a +% on damage to staggered opponents on all three sets.
    • Melee armour also has a greater defence against melee attacks, while having the weakest defence against magic attacks.
  • Melee weapons have 3 damage types: slash, stab, and crush.

Ranged

  • Ranged armour offer a +% stealth speed, -% in ranged attack stamina cost, and a +% to weak point damage on all three sets.
    • Ranged armour also has greater defence against range attacks, while having a equal defence stats in magic and melee.
  • Ranged weapons has one damage type: ranged.

Magic

  • Magic armour offers a -% stamina regen delay, +% magic attack speed, and +% in magical crit change.
    • Magic armour also has a greater defence against magic attack, while having the weakest defence against melee attacks.
  • There are three spell damage types: air, fire, and water.

Combat variables

There are several variables in combat that moderate an entity's performance. Life points are possessed by players and foes, whereas the other mechanisms are used in foes sparingly or restrictively.

  • health - Health represent how much damage a player or creature can withstand. When an entity loses all its life points, it dies. A player's maximum life points is at 100. The primary method of recovering life points is either staying outside of combat for regen, or eating food. Armour also provides reduction to how much damage you can receive.
    • sanguine urn - Sanguine urns are items found within Ashenfall that boosts max health by 10. Collecting them all would provide 310 total health.
  • stamina - Stamina represents how much energy a player has to be able to attack, dodge or block. If a player runs out of stamina, they will be unable to attack or dodge and blocking will cause them to stagger (parrying can regain some stamina). The Primary method of recovering stamina is allowing it to regen on its own. There are perks that grants some reduction to stamina.
  • special action - Special action represent how much power a player has and can use. Certain weapons allow players to do special actions, where it would cost 25, 33, or even 50% of their special action energy.

Combat stats

Combat stats are levels that determines a player's benefit when fighting in one of the three combat styles. In RuneScape: Dragonwilds, players have three of the following combat style and benefits:

  • Attack - Per level, it decreases the cost of stamina when using melee weapons, and grants benefits at certain levels:
    • At level 5 you unlock the ability to parry.
    • At level 8 you unlock the ability to use use weapon special actions.
    • At level 11 you unlock the spell Tempest Shield.
    • At level 16 you unlock the spell Weapon Expertise.
    • At level 20 you unlock the spell Enchant Weapon: Fire.
    • At level 23 you unlock the ability Adaptability.
    • At level 30 you unlock the spell Enchant Weapon: Air.
    • At level 30 you unlock the item whetstone.
    • At level 50 you unlock the spell Enchant Weapon: Water.
    • At level 99 you unlock the Attack cape.
  • Ranged - Per level, it increases the chances of retrieving your arrows or bolts from enemies' loot when they die and grants benefits at certain levels:
    • At level 3 you unlock the ability Quick Action.
    • At level 8 you unlock the ability Trick Shot.
    • At level 12 you unlock the spell Snare.
    • At level 15 you unlock weapon poison (called Toxic Behaviour in-game).
    • At level 18 you unlock Hunter's Sense.
    • At level 22 you unlock weapon barbs (called Make 'Em Bleed in-game).
    • At level 25 you unlock the spell Spectral Arrows.
    • At level 30 you unlock the ability Crossbow Trick Shot.
    • At level 35 you unlock the ability to create enchanted crossbow bolts.
    • At level 40 you unlock the Venomous Trapper effect of Snare.
    • At level 45 you unlock fire oil to create fire arrows
    • At level 99 you unlock the Ranged cape.
  • Magic - Per level, it decreases the cost of stamina when attacking with magic and grants benefits at certain levels:
    • At level 5 you unlock the ability Secondary Attacks.
    • At level 7 you unlock the ability to cast Water magic.
    • At level 11 you unlock the spell Surge.
    • At level 16 you unlock the ability Arcane Expertise
    • At level 20 you unlock the perk Runic Refund
    • At level 21 you unlock the ability to cast Fire magic.
    • At level 25 you unlock the perk Afterimage from the Surge spell.
    • At level 30 you unlock the spell Confuse
    • at level 39 you unlock the item magical focus.
    • At level 44 you unlock the perk Greater Confuse from the Confuse spell.
    • At level 99 you unlock the Magic cape.
  • Artisan - Per level, it decreases the durability loss on equipment, that includes weapons and armour.
    • At level 56 you unlock the spell Magical Mending.
    • At level 99 you unlock the Artisan cape.
Stamina reduction

Within RuneScape: Dragonwilds there are method of reducing stamina when using combat from devouring food or drinks that provide additional perks, such as Infusions. Infusions can be created by using the Cooking skill, and provides benefits such as stamina reduction when using one of the three combat style.

Combat Equipment

In RuneScape: Dragonwilds, combat equipment, such as armours and weapons provide additional stats boosts to help you either do more damage, or reduce the damage you will receive. Using good equipment is essential to combat, as well as dodging and parrying.

Weapons

Weapons are items held that uses the either one or both hands to use and contributes on the player's base damage, damage multiplier and/or attack speed. Each weapon have a different power level that determines their stats. The higher the power level the greater the stats is. Some weapons, like bows and crossbows have their own base damage, which is increased when using ammunition, which adds a damage multiplier.

Certain weapons, like black sword or the zombie axe have special effects that does better damage against certain enemies.

Armour

Armours are items worn by the players that increases their defence against certain attack style, reducing incoming damage while providing buffs as well.. They also have a set effect which requires all three of the same combat style to unlock all three effect. Each armour have different power level that determines their stats. The higher the power level the greater the defence is.

Trinkets

Trinkets are items worn by the players that grants additional effects to the wearer, such as the ring of recoil, which deflects certain percentage of damages back to the attacker(s), or the salve amulet, which increases damage to undead enemies. The ring of life provides a teleport back to your bed when your HP is reduces to 1.

Special Action

Most, if not all weapons have the ability to use a special action, this is an ability that allows the player to use the max damage of their attack, at the cost of their Special Action Bar. Some like the abyssal whip or the crystal bow allows a special attack that provides extra damage with other effects, like staggering or extra damages. A good numbers of weapons have special actions, they are

  • Swords
  • Greatswords
  • Daggers
  • Greataxes
  • Warhammer
  • Maces
  • Scimitar
  • Staves

Damage

There are different type of weapon damages, including buffs, they are:

  • Stab
  • Slash
  • Crush
  • Ranged
  • Fire
  • Water
  • Earth
  • Burning
  • Bleed
  • Poison
  • Immunity

    There are also critical damage, resistance damage and weak to damage, which both indicates when a target is receiving critical damage, is resistance to a damage type, or is weak to the damage type.

Weak spots

Some enemies have spots around them that usually allow players to deal critical damage; these are called weak spots. Note that there is no cooldown for critical damage when targeting the monsters' weak spots.

concepts.title: Parry
concepts.lead: Parry is an unlockable ability at level 5 Attack, where players can unlock the ability to parry incoming attacks to prevent damage, and stagger the attacker for roughly 3 seconds. Most enemies are staggered by different amounts, except for bosses such as Velgar. After a successful parry, there is a minimum delay of 0.550s where the player finishes the parry animation and cannot initiate an attack.

concepts.title: Stagger
concepts.lead: Stagger is a combat mechanic where the player or monster stumbles and is unable to retaliate for some time.
concepts.html:
Stagger is a combat mechanic where the player or monster stumbles and is unable to retaliate for some time.

Mechanics

Stagger affects enemies differently, with this brief stun lasting either longer or shorter. Some enemies are immune. An enemy can be staggered via:

  • Abyssal whip's special action will stagger non-immune enemies
  • A warhammer's special action will stagger non-immune enemies
  • Parrying an enemy strike

When either the player or monster is staggered after being blocked by a parry, the incoming damage to the attacker is dealt 25% more damage.

The player can be staggered via:

  • Blocking while stamina is depleted.
  • Attempting to block an unblockable attack (without the use of Tempest Shield):
    • Garou berserker "red attack"
    • Vault guardian hulk's double slam attack

concepts.title: Critical Strike
concepts.lead: Critical strikes deal an additional 25% increased damage from base damage roll (125% base damage).
concepts.html:
Critical strikes deal an additional 25% increased damage from base damage roll (125% base damage).

Mechanics

The player’s critical hit chance affects the rate at which each attack can critically hit, dealing 25% more critical hit damage (x1.25). The base critical hit chance is 10%, and this rate (not damage) can be improved through perks.

To calculate the damage multiplier of an attack or event, the following formula is used:

  • For example: (( 1 - 0.10) \times 1.00) + (0.10 \times 1.25) indicates a 10% critical strike chance, no base damage boosts, and all critical strikes deal 125% damage. In this example (the baseline for all players), the equation would equal 1.025, meaning on average (true statistical average over many events) each attack deals 1.025x more damage per swing than displayed in the chart below due to critical strikes and base damage boosts.

    The amulet of accuracy can increase the critical strike damage of Ranged attacks by 15%.

concepts.title: Poison
concepts.lead: Poison is a status effect that environments and monster attacks can cause. Poison can be cured and prevented with antipoison potions. It will also naturally recover over time, though this can be dangerous as it will deal roughly half the player's health bar during the process. Inflicted Poison will do either 3 damage/second or 4 damage/second, depending on the source.
concepts.html:
Poison is a status effect that environments and monster attacks can cause. Poison can be cured and prevented with antipoison potions. It will also naturally recover over time, though this can be dangerous as it will deal roughly half the player's health bar during the process. Inflicted Poison will do either 3 damage/second or 4 damage/second, depending on the source.

The perks Antipoison, Antipoison II, and Fungal Fortitude help prevent Poison buildup from the environment and grant some resistance to poison-based attacks.

Sources

  • Monsters that can cause Poison status include putrid rat and garou druids. Velgar fires poison when the player is spotted during his random Patrols.
  • Poisonous environments can be found in the Bloodblight Swamp and the vault within the swamp. Generally, the entire region will cause Poison to build up and cause continuous poison damage unless otherwise prevented/cured with potions.
  • A melee weapon or arrows coated with weapon poison
  • Parrying enemy attacks with the dragonblight shield

concepts.title: Burning
concepts.lead: The Burning debuff applies 8 damage per second for 6 seconds (48 damage total) to the player's health. Its duration can be reduced by dodge rolling or entering water.
concepts.html:
The Burning debuff applies 8 damage per second for 6 seconds (48 damage total) to the player's health. Its duration can be reduced by dodge rolling or entering water.

Burning can be applied by:

  • Fire traps
  • Campfires (non-player)
  • Fire magic, a player-casted fire spell

Runes are retained if you happen to die.

Food is a type of item primarily used to replenish sustenance. Some foods can be consumed raw, such as redberries, but most food must be cooked to be eaten. A campfire or grill can be used to cook raw ingredients, and a stone range or cooking range can be used to combine ingredients into meals. Food with high sustenance to weight ratios will allow you to carry more while adventuring.
concepts.html:
Food is a type of item primarily used to replenish sustenance. Some foods can be consumed raw, such as redberries, but most food must be cooked to be eaten. A campfire or grill can be used to cook raw ingredients, and a stone range or cooking range can be used to combine ingredients into meals. Food with high sustenance to weight ratios will allow you to carry more while adventuring.

Most foods also provide health, however, there is a 2 second delay between eating food, and consuming more than 100 sustenance will start to build Over Eating - eating 200 sustenance over the cap will trigger the effect, preventing the player from eating any additional food for 15 seconds. Because of this, when looking for ideal healing foods, food with higher health to sustenance ratios should be preferred, and not just which food heals the most. Additionally, food with higher health to weight ratios will also allow you to carry more while adventuring.

Some foods also provide perks, useful effects such as Knowledgable Nourishment, which increases the player's experience gain in all skills by 10%. The duration of these perks can be reset with the use of Internal Alchemy, but the player can only maintain one to three perk(s) from food. Any previous perk will be overwritten by the most recently consumed food. Additionally, only one source of food can provide the perk(s). For example, the player cannot eat two one-perk foods to have them both. However, the player can eat any other food that does not provide a perk without overriding the previous perk(s).

The default sort for the following tables is based on region and Cooking progression, and separated into a table for food without perks, food with perks, one for all food, and then the facility lists for the campfire and cooking range. Burnt food is only included in the campfire facility list. Use the Header sorts on the relevant table to find the food you're looking for. For example, use the perk-less food table and sort by health to sustenance Ratio to find food that will restore as much health as possible in a short time without triggering Over Eating or overriding any active perks.

concepts.html:
Armour describes items worn in the head, chest, leg, or cape slot to defend against damage from melee, ranged, or magic-based attacks. Most armour pieces have durability which degrades either during combat or other sources of Damage, such as falling or failing vault traps.

Armour is classified under three classes, representing the RuneScape combat triangle, and provides additional set bonuses for wearing multiple pieces within the same class type.

Shields

Shields are equipped in the off-hand and allow players to block and parry incoming attacks.

  • Blocking reduces the incoming damage from the attack of a monster by the block value of the equipped shield.
  • Parrying is when the beginning of a block coincides with the timing of an attack of a monster. An audible "clang" will sound, and the enemy becomes staggered as long as they are not immune (e.g., Velgar).
