concepts.title: Weapons
concepts.lead: Weapons are items that can be used to deal damage to enemies or to other players in a PvP-enabled server. Their damage types are represented by the RuneScape combat triangle, and can come in 3 types - Melee, ranged, and magic. They are crafted via various furniture such as the crafting table, blacksmith's bench, fletching bench, mystic forge. They can be repaired there as well if their durability drops or they break. The various foes in the world are weak to and resist certain types of attacks, so a varied arsenal is paramount for ease of exploration in Ashenfall.
concepts.html:
Weapons are items that can be used to deal damage to enemies or to other players in a PvP-enabled server. Their damage types are represented by the RuneScape combat triangle, and can come in 3 types - Melee, ranged, and magic. They are crafted via various furniture such as the crafting table, blacksmith's bench, fletching bench, mystic forge. They can be repaired there as well if their durability drops or they break. The various foes in the world are weak to and resist certain types of attacks, so a varied arsenal is paramount for ease of exploration in Ashenfall.

Various monsters and chests within the world have a chance to contain recipes for new weapons, which can be read and then crafted at their respective workshop.

  • See stamina for a breakdown of the stamina costs for using each weapon, or combat for a complete list of the damage per second for each weapon and style, enemy weaknesses, etc.

Melee Weapons

Melee weapons are currently split into two categories: one-handed and two-handed weapons.

Attack Combos shown include the bonus attacks awarded by Weapon Expertise, unlocked at 16 Attack.

  • 1-handed and 2-handed weapons can utilise the block mechanic without a shield.

Ranged Weapons

Ranged weapons are currently split into three categories: shortbows, longbows, and crossbows.

  • Shortbows can be effectively used at both close and moderate ranges, but do less damage than their counterparts.
  • Longbows are very high-damage, long-range weapons, but difficult to use at close range.
  • Crossbows are one-handed and do moderate damage, but are only effective at relatively short range.

Shortbows

Shortbows can either be drawn, or quick-fired with a reduction in range and damage. They have the lowest per-shot damage of the ranged weapons and moderate range, but the fastest fire-rate when quick-firing.

Battlestaves

Battlestaves can expend a large amount of magical energy at once through a secondary attack, based on the rune used. This consumes 5 runes per cast.

    • Air: Stuns and knocks back enemies. Increases damage and stun based on charge time.
    • Fire: Breathe fire in a cone in front of you. Increases duration, not damage, of the cone based on charge time at 2-5 ticks of damage.
    • Water: Conjures a bubble of magic water that damages all enemies around the player when released. It then creates a field of magic water that heals allies standing on it over time. Increases both the first damage and the duration and size of the field based on charge.

concepts.title: Drop table

Note that the rarity is based on the cache's drop table system, and is represented as a float value over 100 (e.g., rate = 4.5 means that the rarity is 4.5/100).

concepts.title: Spawning
concepts.lead: Spawning is the in-game creation of an entity, such as a non-player character (NPC) or an item. Respawning is the recreation of an NPC, resource node, or item, after its death, destruction, or use. Despawning is the instantaneous destruction or removal of a resource, such as destroying a tree stump. The time it takes for an entity to spawn/respawn depends on the game's internal time mechanic. Respawn times shown in the wiki refer to in-game times.
concepts.html:
Spawning is the in-game creation of an entity, such as a non-player character (NPC) or an item. Respawning is the recreation of an NPC, resource node, or item, after its death, destruction, or use. Despawning is the instantaneous destruction or removal of a resource, such as destroying a tree stump. The time it takes for an entity to spawn/respawn depends on the game's internal time mechanic. Respawn times shown in the wiki refer to in-game times.

Spawning

There are different spawning mechanisms, such as:

  • After creating their character on the character creation menu, the player will spawn inside the Temple of Saradomin.
  • Summoning Velgar by using the challenge horn on the dragonkin altar at Velgar's Rise

Respawning

Several respawn mechanisms include:

  • Monsters can respawn between one to three days, depending on the type of monster and their location.
  • Several resources can respawn in their resource node between half an in-game day to three in-game days.

Resource nodes

Respawn point

Respawn points are places where the player has set their on-death placement. For example, "claiming" a bed or bed roll after building it can set their respawn point if they die anywhere in Ashenfall.

concepts.title: Character creation
concepts.lead: Character creation is an interface where players first customise their character's appearance before starting the tutorial.
concepts.html:
Character creation is an interface where players first customise their character's appearance before starting the tutorial.

Character name

Players can choose up to a 16-character name without spaces. Note that the name is capitilisation sensitive.

Body type

There are two types that players can choose from: type A (masculine) or type B (feminine).

Skin tone

Players can choose one of the eight skin tones. The top right option (#A28A7A) is selected by default.

Face

There are four options players can choose from:

  1. (Default) Cheeks and nose are narrow, following a slight V-shape.
  2. Includes a slightly wider version of the cheeks and nose, and fuller lips
  3. Includes a slightly rounded version of the cheeks and nose (still following the V-shape) and thinner lips
  4. Includes a longer, vertical version of the cheeks and nose (still following the V-shape) and thinner lips)

concepts.lead: The Settings screen can be found whilst starting the RuneScape: Dragonwilds client. Below are features that players can adjust to enhance their gameplay:
concepts.html:
The Settings screen can be found whilst starting the RuneScape: Dragonwilds client. Below are features that players can adjust to enhance their gameplay:

Gameplay

Gameplay

Hide Chat

Players have the option to hide the chat overlay completely. To do so, they must confirm their choice by clicking on the box on the right. This option is disabled by default.

Gravestone Protection

Players can choose to prevent other players from accessing their gravestone. This option is disabled by default.

Screen Shake

Players can choose to disable or enable screen shake during combat. This option is enabled by default.

Camera

Sensitivity X

This option controls the generic mouse sensitivity along the x-axis across the game. Players can adjust the setting by dragging the pointer across the bar. Sensitivity X is set to five by default.

Sensitivity Y

This option controls the generic mouse sensitivity along the y-axis across the game. Players can adjust the setting by dragging the pointer across the bar. Sensitivity Y is set to five by default.

ADS Sensitivity X

This option controls the mouse sensitivity when aiming down sight (ADS) along the x-axis. Players can adjust the setting by dragging the pointer across the bar. ADS Sensitivity X is set to five by default.

ADS Sensitivity Y

This option controls the mouse sensitivity when aiming down sight (ADS) along the y-axis. Players can adjust the setting by dragging the pointer across the bar. ADS Sensitivity Y is set to five by default.

Invert X / Horizontal

This option can invert the horizontal axis of the mouse or joystick. Players can confirm their choice by clicking on the box on the right.

Invert Y / Vertical

This option can invert the vertical axis of the mouse or joystick. Players can confirm their choice by clicking on the box on the right.

Controls

Press To Sprint

Players can press the Sprint key to toggle sprinting on and off, rather than holding it.

Video

Quality

Auto Detect (Quality)

Players who click the APPLY button will automatically apply the best video quality for their computer configuration.

Auto Detect (Performance)

Players who click the APPLY button will automatically apply the best video performance for their computer configuration.

Quality

Players have five options that can drastically change the level of graphics in the game up to the level they select:

  • Auto - Very low (default)
  • Low
  • Medium
  • High
  • Very high
    • Choosing this option will enable Nanite.
  • Epic
    • Choosing this opition will enable Nanite.
Upscaling Mode

Upscaling mode is an algorithm used to improve visual fidelity. Players can choose to adjust this by clicking on the side buttons to change to:

  • TSR (Balanced) - This option is set by default. This contains a good balance of image quality and performance, often a solid all-around choice.
  • DLSS (Best) - Renders the game at a lower resolution than the target display resolution.
  • FSR (Fast) - Prioritises performance, may have a softer image quality.
  • NIS (Fastest) - Heavily prioritises performance, can look sharper, but might have more artefacts.
  • Off - Disables any upscaling.
Upscaling Quality

Upscaling quality is how the game changes visual fidelity whilst moving around in-game. The options below depend on the setting chosen above:

  • TSR (Balanced)
    • Quality (default option)
    • Ultra Quality
    • Performance
    • Balanced
  • FSR (Fast)
    • Quality (default option)
    • Ultra Performance
    • Performance
    • Balanced
  • NIS (Fastest)
    • Auto - Balanced (default option)
    • Quality
    • Ultra Quality
    • Performance
    • Balanced
  • Off
    • Auto - Quality
Anti-Aliasing

Players can choose the anti-aliasing quality. Anti-aliasing smooths jagged edges in the display.

  • Epic

Nanite

Players can choose to turn on to improve an object's geometry detail. Nanite is turned off by default.

Recommended below are lists of GPUs that can handle Unreal Engine 5's Nanite mode:

  • NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Ti, 4080, or 4090
  • AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT or 7900 XTX:

Display

Graphics API

Players have three options to adjust their graphics level in-game:

  • DX12 (default)
  • DX11
  • Vulcan
Resolution

Players can adjust their resolution in the game if the Display Mode setting is set to Windowed or Full Screen. Several options can appear based on the following Display Mode adjustments:

  • Full Screen Windowed
    • 1,920x1,080
  • Windowed
    • 1,280x720 (default)
    • 1,600x900
  • Full Screen
    • 1,280x720 (default)

Display Mode

Players have several options that display the game on their screen.

  • Full Screen Windowed (default)
  • Full Screen
  • Windowed - This will allow players to change the Resolution setting between 1,280x720 and any higher resolutions, depending on the player's graphics card.
Frame Rate Limit

Players can change the frames per second (FPS) to several thresholds:

  • Dynamic (default)
  • 30 frames per second
  • 60 frames per second
  • 90 frames per second
  • 120 frames per second
  • 140 frames per second
Brightness

Players can adjust their brightness based on the calibration screen after clicking on OPEN CALIBRATION. This screen will pop up three RuneScape: Dragonwilds logos, with the logo on the left adjusted by the adjustment bar below.

Sharpness

Players can adjust the sharpness from 10 (default) to 100, only if the Upscaling Mode option is set to FSR (Fast) or NIS (Fastest).

Depth of Field

Players can adjust the depth of field in the game; this is set to 100 by default.

Bloom

Players can adjust the bloom that controls the hazy glow around light sources; this is set to 100 by default.

Frame Generation

Players can turn on Frame Generation only if the Upscaling Mode option is set to FSR (Fast). Depending on the player's graphics card, this may improve the image quality.

VSync

Players can turn on Vertical Synchronisation (VSync) to eliminate screen tearing.

Advanced

GPU Crash Debugging

Players can automatically report GPU Crash Debugging if the Steam client crashes. Note that enabling this feature has a small performance cost.

Audio

Players can adjust the Master, Music, SFX, and Dialogue volume. Note that all these options are set to 100 by default.

Accessibility

Language

Players set their language from its default setting, English (United Kingdom), to Spanish, French, Italian, or German.

Font Size

Players can set their font size from its default setting, Normal, to Large or Small.

Enable Profanity Filtering

Players can enable or disable the profanity filter, applying to in-game chat and players' signs. This can optionally apply to usernames and server names.

Filter Usernames

Players can check this box to apply the profanity filter (if set to enabled) to usernames. Note that usernames will not be filtered in the server users list, so players can copy the usernames for reporting purposes. This option is set to disabled by default.

Strong profanities

This option determines the strength of the profanity filter if Enable Profanity Filtering is set to enabled. This option is set to Always by default.

  • Always - will always filter entries, even if they are in the middle of a word. For example, if "cat" is in a profanity, then "scatter" would be filtered to "s***tter" and "catfish" is filtered to "***fish".
  • '''Filter if full word" - will only filter entries that are surrounded by blank spaces or punctuation. For example, if "cow" is a profanity, then "coward" will be unaltered, but "cow" will be filtered to "***".
  • Ignore - will ignore the strong profanity filter list.

Mild profanities

This option determines the strength of the profanity filter if Enable Profanity Filtering is set to enabled. This option is set to Filter if full word by default.

  • Always - will always filter entries, even if they are in the middle of a word. For example, if "cat" is in a profanity, then "scatter" would be filtered to "s***tter" and "catfish" is filtered to "***fish".
  • '''Filter if full word" - will only filter entries that are surrounded by blank spaces or punctuation. For example, if "cow" is a profanity, then "coward" will be unaltered, but "cow" will be filtered to "***".
  • Ignore - will ignore the strong profanity filter list.

Also filter German

This option determines if the filter will also include words added to the German profanity list.

Also filter Spanish

This option determines if the filter will also include words added to the Spanish (Castilian) profanity list.

Also filter Spanish (Latin America)

This option determines if the filter will also include words added to the Spanish (Latin America) profanity list.

Also filter French

This option determines if the filter will also include words added to the French profanity list.

Also filter Italian

This option determines if the filter will also include words added to the Italian profanity list.

Also filter Portuguese (Brazil)

This option determines if the filter will also include words added to the Portuguese (PT-BR) profanity list.

Social

Players can choose to either kick, ban, or unban players in their friends/banned list. Note that players in the Steam's friend list are also listed in the settings' Friends List.

Updates

Updates that begin with "Eye on Ashenfall" from either the Steam client or the official RuneScape: Dragonwilds website are posted here.

Legal

Data Collection

Update Privacy Settings

Players can update their Steam Privacy Settings by clicking on the UPDATE button. This will take players to a separate window in-game where it goes over the player activity and game diagnostics for the player. Make sure to confirm the choices selected and see here for more information.

Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information

Players who choose to opt out of selling their personal information in the UK are linked here (and here for players in the US) to Jagex's privacy policy websites.

Epic Account Services

Update EOS Settings

Players can update their EOS settings by clicking on the UPDATE button. This will lead players to an in-game popup where players can either choose to continue playing with Epic Games or play offline instead. For more info, players are directed to click on the link on the bottom-right of the screen.

The interface, or user interface (UI), is the screen containing different buttons which, when clicked, display different pieces of information.

concepts.html:
The interface, or user interface (UI), is the screen containing different buttons which, when clicked, display different pieces of information.

Upon spawning in a world for the first time, players can see the following:

  • Status - located at the bottom left of the screen and includes (from left to right):
    • Hydration
    • Sustenance
    • Rest
  • Health and stamina bar - located at the bottom middle of the screen
  • Inventory bar - located at the top right of the screen
  • Quick action bar - located at the bottom right of the screen and includes:
    • Chat - default keybind is the key
    • Map - default keybind is the key
    • Quests - default keybind is the key
    • Build Menu - default keybind is the key
    • Inventory - default keybind is the key
  • Aiming reticle - located at the centre of the screen
  • Compass located at the top middle of the screen
  • A sundial widget on the top right of the screen that will notify the time of day

Inventory

Players can access their items through either the hotbar on the top right-hand side of the screen or by pressing the key on their inventory. After pressing the key (or other key, depending on the key bindings), players can access their inventory and their armour slots. The number on the bottom right of every item indicates the current number of items the player has. All items have a stack limit and can be determined by clicking and dragging each item to another inventory slot. Items have a stack limit of 1, 25, 50, 99, or 999.

In addition, a yellow bar indicates the player's weight. If the player goes over 400 (or 450 with the leggings of lightness), the bar will become red, and the player will become overencumbered. The player will be unable to dodge attacks, run, or walk slower.

Items may have interactable icons to the top-right of each item. This may include:

Buildings

Players can choose any buildings by pressing the default button on their keyboard and switch to different types of structures/decorations:

Spells

Players can quickly choose a spell by pressing the default button, opening the quick spells menu. Players can hover over the spell's rune requirements and description to get a better understanding of the spell before casting, and to determine if the player has the required runes before casting. Players can also choose the spells based on their Magic level. After levelling up in a skill, players receive a spell in their spell's main menu.

Players can also drag and drop several spells from the spell's main menu if they have the required level. The quick spells menu can only hold up to 12 spells and can be rearranged at any time.

concepts.title: Player-versus-player
concepts.lead: Player-versus-player combat, or PvP, can be enabled for a world when creating or editing one. When the option is enabled, players can fight each other, rather than just other monsters.
concepts.html:
Player-versus-player combat, or PvP, can be enabled for a world when creating or editing one. When the option is enabled, players can fight each other, rather than just other monsters.

Creating a world

When creating a world, world owners have the option to turn on Friendly fire, enabling PvP for the world. The world owner can change this setting at any time whilst hosting the world. World owners must make sure to click on "Edit World" after making the PvP adjustment.

Mechanics

Players can attack each other whilst in Ashenfall, vaults, or other instances (such as the boss fight with Velgar) through melee, ranged, and magic. If a player kills another player, the player who dealt the kill can access the player's gravestone and get their items. If a player dies and the world owner closes the world, the player who died will not be able to retrieve their items.

concepts.title: Steam Achievements
concepts.lead: Steam achievements (also called "tasks") are specific standalone challenges/milestones within RuneScape: Dragonwilds. Players can complete specific achievements through in-game actions, such as completing certain quests or defeating special monsters (like bosses). The global completion rate is fetched and published at 12-hour intervals starting at 00:00 UTC.

concepts.title: Saga
concepts.lead: Sagas are major narrative arcs in RuneScape: Dragonwilds, told through the game's primary quests. Each saga follows a central storyline that unfolds across the continent of Ashenfall. Most regions contain a single chapter dedicated to their local narrative; however, Wrath of Velgar is an exception, beginning in Brynmoor before continuing into Ghornfell, making it the only chapter to span multiple regions.
concepts.html:
Sagas are major narrative arcs in RuneScape: Dragonwilds, told through the game's primary quests. Each saga follows a central storyline that unfolds across the continent of Ashenfall. Most regions contain a single chapter dedicated to their local narrative; however, Wrath of Velgar is an exception, beginning in Brynmoor before continuing into Ghornfell, making it the only chapter to span multiple regions.

Sagas

Kuldra's Saga

Kuldra's Saga is the first saga to be released alongside RuneScape: Dragonwilds. It follows the player's arrival in Ashenfall and their efforts to confront Kuldra and her dragons. It takes place during the Sixth Age, following the events of , and establishes the beginning of the player's journey across the continent of Ashenfall.

The Story So Far, is a lore scrap entry that provides an overview of the events preceding the start of the game.

Chapter 1: Wrath of Velgar
"They swooped down from the skies and decimated the landing party. Whole teams of people, gone, just like that. "Queen Kuldra bids you welcome," they laughed, as our comrades drew their final breath''.''" - ''[[Wise Old Man]]''

This is the opening chapter of Kuldra's Saga, Wrath of Velgar. Upon arriving in Ashenfall, the player emerges from an ancient, ruined Saradominist temple and is introduced to essential survival techniques by several notable characters, including the Wise Old Man, Doric, Vannaka, and Zanik. After completing this introductory training, the player sets out across the region of Brynmoor, battling goblins and other hostile creatures to acquire stronger equipment before confronting the dragon general Velgar at his tower within Ghornfell.

The chapter concludes with the player defeating Velgar and delivering his severed head to the Wise Old Man outside the tower.

Chapter 2: Beyond the Grave
"Welcome to Fellhollow. The whole region is infected with a terrible withering. Some dread curse that untethers the soul and drags it to the River Noumenon without ever sailing upon it, preventing the dead from moving on. This cannot stand''.''" - [[Death (Grim Reaper)|''Death'']]

Beyond the Grave is the second chapter of Kuldra's Saga. It follows the player's journey into the region of Fellhollow after the defeat of Velgar, here the players will be introduced to Death. Here, they will learn of Imaru and the plague she had unleashed within the region centuries ago and will be asked to slay her in order to restore the region. Here the players discover the Wither effect and how to enter it, and escape it. Players will be facing all kinds of undead when in the region, even green dragons, preparing themselves before they face Imaru.

The chapter concludes with the player defeating Imaru and the delivering her severed head to Death.

Chapter 3: Madness of Zamorak
"Full of angry Zamorakians. Quite the bother. Good thing you're here though, you can get us moving again. The way is blocked by something called the Gatekeeper. Not sure what it is, or who it is, but it's in the way. There's a nasty magical barrier before we can even reach them, but Doric's working on it as we speak." - [[Wise Old Man]]

Madness of Zamorak is the third chapter of Kuldra's Saga. It follows the player's journey to Dowdun Reach after the defeat of Imaru. Here, the player will be asked to help Doric unlike the barrier that blocked them from entering the next region. They'll have to located shards of the Dreaming Stone in order to restore it and undo the barrier. Players will be facing Black Knights, mage of Zamorak, blue dragons and more in order to prepare and repair the stone and fight against the Black Knight Titan.

The chapter concludes with the player's defeating the Titan and bringing his broken sword to Doric to prove their victory.

Chapter 4: Fire of Fuzan
''"Souls are coming to me from Umbral Sand at a faster and faster rate. My good friend Death informed me that the culprit is Fuzan, a dragon tyrant of these dunes." - [[Icthlarin]]''

Fire of Fuzan is the fourth and penultimate chapter of Kuldra's Saga. It follows the player's journey to Umbral Sands after defeating the Black Knight Titan. Here, they will be asked by Icthlarin to assist them in rebuilding his mother's mirror to lead them into Fuzan's lair. The player will be tasked to gain the trusts of the Moon Garou in order to gain the pieces needed for the mirrors. Players will be facing kalphites, red dragons, KotHaar and other dangers within the region to prepare for their fight against Fuzan.

This chapter concludes with the player defeating Fuzan and his trials, as well as delivering his head to Icthlarin.

Chapter 5: Rage of Kuldra
''"The lord of the skies has fallen, slain by Kuldra..."'' - Dragon Gate

Rage of Kuldra is the fifth and final chapter of Kuldra's Saga. It follows the player's journey through the Scorned Wilderness raid after defeating Fuzan and liberating the Umbral Sands from his tyranny. Here, they will be able to open the Dragon Gate north-west of Velgar's Rise and speak to Commander Zilyana to discover that Kuldra plans to destroy all of Gielinor by using strange discordant anima waves created by the Harmonic Resonator. This will force them to fight through hordes of black dragons, goblins, garou, undead, and solve puzzles using anima itself to bring the fight to the god-eater herself.

This chapter, and this saga, concludes with the player killing Kuldra and delivering her head to Zilyana.

Future Sagas

It was revealed by Mod Dutch in the RuneFest reveal Twitch stream that Kuldra's story isn't the conclusion for the of game, there are future sagas planned for the game. The next saga is planned to focus on a multi-year journey, one being to discover the ancient magic guarding the continent of Ashenfall and potentially revealing the continent to the rest of Gielinor. More information on this new saga will be revealed at RuneFest 2026.

Blood Crystal Saga

It has been revealed that the new Saga is Blood Crystal Sagalink, which will be introduced in 2027, more information will be revealed in RuneFest 2026. It was revealed in the 1.0 dev blog that this new saga will also introduce new skills.

concepts.title: Buildings/Mechanics
concepts.lead: Building mechanics are ways that players can create building structures/objects, general decorations, and other types of furniture. Players can start building by pressing the default button on their keyboard to unlock the building interface.
concepts.html:
Building mechanics are ways that players can create building structures/objects, general decorations, and other types of furniture. Players can start building by pressing the default button on their keyboard to unlock the building interface.

Placement

Upon clicking on an unlocked type of structure, players can choose the area to place the object and can rotate it as the object is previewed (assuming players have the required materials). Players can rotate the previewed structure with the following:

Key pressDirection
Scroll wheelRotation along the Z-axis
Alt + scroll wheelTowards/away from the player
Shift + scroll wheelUp/down from the world's surface

Repair mode

If a structure has visible signs of damage (at 50% health or below) or if the structure is below 100% health, players can fix it with its base material. For example, a square foundation requires one ash log if the structure is below 100%.

Players will need to ensure the structure's health stays above 1%. Otherwise, the structure will collapse, leaving behind the base materials used to build it.

Ghost mode

Players can create ghost-like structures without the required materials, either on a solid foundation or a wall. Ghost mode is useful for determining whether an object can be stable without building with physical materials on hand. After placing the object, this creates a pseudo-structure that can be built whenever the player has the required materials. To destroy the pseudo-structure, players can go to their build menu, toggle "Repair mode", and click the scroll wheel to dismantle the structure. To build the pseudo-structure, click on the key.

Ghost mode will not work in the temple at Temple Woods, vaults, and inside instanced areas.

Cycle snapping mode

Players who enable cycle snapping mode can see either the object's full points of contact when connecting structures, the object's most critical points of contact, or no points of contact. This also works with ghost mode, as players can see the points of contact with the pseudo-structure. Cycle snapping mode will only be enabled if players are hovering over the previewed object with another built object.

Note that only house structures will have cycle-snapping mode; any decorations, such as barrels, will not show points of contact on their outlines.

No snapping

No snapping allows the player to not allow the object to be automatically placed to another built object. This may be useful for abstractly placing objects without the object moving automatically.

Basic snapping

Basic snapping allows the player to see the most critical points of contact. For example, a wall and a square tile will display four points of contact on each corner, and a floor will also display four points of contact

Advanced snapping

Advanced snapping allows the player to see all of the points of contact. For example, a wall and a square tile will display 13 points of contact, with three between the corners.

Stability

Objects that do not have a solid foundation underneath will display a yellow outline (warning) around the previewed object and a red outline (prohibited) around the previewed object. Certain structures, such as a wall or floor, can be built up to six structures above the ground without a foundation. In addition, directly stacking objects above each other will perform the same action, depending on the constructed object. For larger constructions, using multiple foundations on the ground is necessary to expand the stable building area. This also adds redundancy, preventing a total collapse if one anchor is accidentally removed.

Areas with non-stable foundations include the temple at Temple Woods, vaults, and inside instanced areas.

When placing a foundation or anything on the ground, all basic snapping points for the desired structure must be in contact with the ground at the same time. This means any structure (or the tent from casting Summon Shelter) must be on flat land. Otherwise, a red UNSTABLE will pop up on the screen.

Block types and stability

Beams and foundations are the best blocks to use for anchors as they provide the greatest amount of stability. Thick and thin beams offer the same stability and can provide the upper-constructed objects a stable defence if the bottom of the structure is broken. Walls and stairs, when used as anchors, provide less stability than beams or foundations.

The material used for the anchor block dictates the build's stability limits. Ash objects allow for a structure 5 blocks high and 3 blocks wide. The travel distance for stability is about 4-5 blocks from the anchor. Oak is a superior anchor material, permitting builds of up to 8 blocks high and 5 blocks wide. Stone and above provide support up to 7 blocks wide. It also provides a stable travel distance of 6-8 blocks without a foundation.

General base building tips

  • Prioritise oak structures: While adventuring in Ashenfall, there are higher-tier materials that can be used to create bases. As you advance your Construction level, you gain access to higher-tier buildings and foundations, but these buildings become more expensive. To be cost-effective in terms of resources for a starter base in a new area/region, it is best to use Oak structures as the resources are quicker to acquire.
    • You can also use the highest-tier material available to you, but it takes time to acquire a substantial amount of resources to construct these structures.
    • In case you don't have enough resources to make a base completely out of Oak material, you can always use Ash without impacting overall stability limits.
  • Beware of false anchors: A block may appear green and seem to be on (or in) the ground, but it might not be a true anchor providing its own stability. This can severely limit the player's build and may be related to a known issue of placing beams on cliffs. Be cautious when deleting any anchor to avoid an unexpected structural collapse.
  • Use beams for framing: Beams are recommended for creating the main frame of a build because they make it easy to visualise and trace stability paths.
  • Roofs: Roofs are often difficult to place due to stability limits at the top of a building. Plan to have less roof space, potentially reducing the building height by a floor or two to accommodate a decent-sized roof. Frequent support beams running up from anchors are needed for larger roofs.
  • Leverage different beam types and sizes:
    • Long vs. short beams: It is best to use long beams for the main structure, but supplement them with short poles where needed. Short poles can sometimes provide extra building room at their unique snapping points.
    • Angled beams: Using 45° beams (or other angled beams, depending on the player's structure) can help expand the buildable area by filling in gaps between horizontal and vertical beams. They are also useful for anchoring structures into the cliffside.

concepts.title: Bed
concepts.lead: The bed is a buildable piece of furniture used to rest and set the player's respawn point in the world. If used at night, players will skip to daytime and regain their full rest meter; if used during the day, players will lie in place and slowly regain their rest meter over time. The bed requires 8 ash planks and 4 rough cloth to craft, and must be under a roof and enclosed with three walls to be used.

Experience chart

The following graph plots each point with x being the level and y being the experience:

Formulae

The amount of experience required to advance to level L is calculated using a piecewise function:

\text{Total XP}(L) = \begin{cases} \lfloor c \sum_{i=1}^{L-1} \lfloor i + 300 \cdot 2^{i/7} \rfloor \rfloor & \text{if } 1 \le L \le 93 \\ 342,568 + \lfloor 52,560.5(L - 93) \rfloor & \text{if } 94 \le L \le 95 \\ 14,241(L - 95)^2 + 81,114(L - 95) + 447,689 & \text{if } 96 \le L \le 99 \end{cases}

Following this piecewise function would provide the graph:

Levels 1-93

The first part of the piecewise function utilises , taking the previous level's experience and adding an exponentially growing term, using:

\lfloor i + 300 \cdot 2^{i/7} \rfloor

Levels 94-95

Levels 94 and 95 are approximately linear, starting at level 93 (342,568 experience), then jumping to level 94 (395,129 experience) by 52,561, and to level 95 (447,689 experience) by 52,560.

Levels 96-99

Calculating the quadratic coefficients

Levels 96 to 99 use the quadratic equation, f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c, where a is half of the second difference (a.k.a, taking another difference after subtracting the difference needed from level 95 to 96 and level 96 to 97). This is shown with the following:

f(96) - f(95) = 543,044 - 447,689 = 95,355
f(97) - f(96) = 666,881 - 543,044 = 123,837
123,837 - 95,355 = 28,482
a = \frac{28,482}{2} = 14,241

Calculating the determinant (b)

Since c is the starting value at level 95 (447,689 experience), use f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c and substitute f(x) for level 96 (with 543,044) to get the b coefficient:

543,044 = 14,241 + b + 447,689
b = 81,114, making the following function from level 96 to 99:

14,241(L - 95)^2 + 81,114(L - 95) + 447,689

concepts.title: Gathering
concepts.lead: Gathering skills (or just "gathering") is a category of skills within RuneScape: Dragonwilds that allow the players to interact with scenery items to acquire resources or materials.
concepts.html:
Gathering skills (or just "gathering") is a category of skills within RuneScape: Dragonwilds that allow the players to interact with scenery items to acquire resources or materials.

Overview

While these skills are strictly non-combative in nature, they allow the player to acquire resources that cannot be acquired in massive quantities in a short amount of time or not acquired through monster drops. These skills also have their own special type of tools that enable the player to get experience.

Mining

Mining is a gathering skill that pertains to mining ore nodes or certain rocks (such as stone boulders and granite deposits) with a pickaxe. At a high enough level, it is possible to acquire gemstones from certain ore nodes while mining.

Woodcutting

Woodcutting is a gathering skill that pertains to chopping down trees to acquire logs using a logging axe. By creating better logging axes using higher-tiered materials (such as bronze or iron), one can chop down stronger trees and weaker tress faster.

Farming

Farming is a gathering skill that pertains to growing and harvesting crops. By planting seeds in planters (or tree seeds on the ground), using watering cans, and compost, one can gather specific resources that would otherwise be hard to collect easier. At a high enough level, it is possible to create a higher version of compost and create a tool that creates a small increase to crop yields.

Fishing

Fishing is a gathering skill that pertains to catching fish in specific fishing spots. By using nets to trawl for fish closer to shore and cast using rods (with bait) to catch fish from far away, one can gather a renewable food source.

concepts.title: Whetstone
concepts.lead: A whetstone can be used to give a 15% damage multiplier on a player's equipped melee weapon for 10 minutes, and can be used in conjunction with damage-boosting spells, such as Enchant Weapon: Fire. Its recipe is unlocked after reaching level 40 in the Attack skill.
concepts.html:
A whetstone can be used to give a 15% damage multiplier on a player's equipped melee weapon for 10 minutes, and can be used in conjunction with damage-boosting spells, such as Enchant Weapon: Fire. Its recipe is unlocked after reaching level 40 in the Attack skill.

Recipe

Recipe Blacksmith's Bench · Artisan 0 xp
5 × Granite, 10 × Stone → 1 × Whetstone

Recipe tree

Journal

The blade is not just a weapon in the wilds of Ashenfall, it’s a tool. Sometimes it’s the difference between seeing tomorrow and having a very bad today. Dwarves have always understood the importance of properly maintaining one’s equipment. They turned the care for their weapons into a ritual of almost religious significance. Blades would be cleaned, serviced and sharpened so that they might cut through deadlier dangers and challenge greater threats. The whetstone is a simple device, but one that served as a backbone of this ritual. A smith would learn to gently sharpen the blade to the thinnest edge possible, treating it almost like a competition. They would boast and brag with each other about the sharpness of their blades. A popular dwarven myth speaks of the Prime Whetstone, capable of sharpening a blade to the point that no armour or metal could withstand it. Sadly, or perhaps thankfully, no evidence exists to provide any truth to the myth.

concepts.title: Magical Focus
concepts.lead: A magical focus is an unlockable item at level 39 Magic, where players can imbue their equipped staff with a 15% damage multiplier for 10 minutes. Players can also stack the damage boost with a lesser Magic potion, making the player's staff also equipped with a 25% increased chance of a critical hit.

Recipe tree

Journal

The wizard Mallory was never as good as he had hoped to be. He was proficient in spellcasting and his rote memory was excellent, but the power of his spells always fell a little short. His advancement through the ranks was due more to being around long enough than anything else, and he never quite earned the respect of his peers. That was until the day he created the focus. Mallory had always been good at making things. He enjoyed the simpler magic of crafting, and he found you could weave small threads of magic into the construction of something, breathing just a little bit more life and wonder into it than before. True craftsmanship, he believed, carried a little bit of the creator’s soul in it. The focus proved this theory and elevated it further. By creating a focus and subconsciously imbuing it with a bit of his essence, it facilitated a smoother, more fluid, channel of magic through the body. This resulted in spells of greater potency. Tragically, after sharing his knowledge with the other wizards, he was murdered by his mentor, who claimed the knowledge as his own. Karma is a stern judge, however, and the offending wizard later found himself being swallowed whole and digested by a dragon. Just punishment, I’m sure Mallory would agree.

concepts.title: Surge
concepts.lead: Surge is a Magic spell that grants players the ability to quickly dodge incoming attacks from monsters and vault traps. Upon casting, players receive three Surge dodges, which are displayed on the top-right of the health bar with a two-minute countdown.
concepts.html:
Surge is a Magic spell that grants players the ability to quickly dodge incoming attacks from monsters and vault traps. Upon casting, players receive three Surge dodges, which are displayed on the top-right of the health bar with a two-minute countdown.

Activating a Surge charge causes the player to travel eight metres away from the direction they are currently facing. This distance can be obstructed and shortened by walls or other environmental barriers.

After reaching 25 Magic, the perk Afterimage is unlocked, where players can leave behind an illusory image for 10 seconds after using the first Surge charge. This will allow the player to temporarily avoid strikes as the enemy will target the illusory image instead. After 10 seconds, the enemy will lock on to the player.

concepts.title: Tempest Shield
concepts.lead: Tempest Shield is a Attack spell that produces an invulnerable shield for one minute that acts like any other equipped shield. However, this will release a powerful wind burst when the time ends if the shield is raised, knocking nearby foes to the ground. It can be invaluable before the player has access to stronger shields such as the iron shield, since most stronger attacks will still pierce damage through shields before that, while the Tempest Shield will still fully protect the user even when barehanded (provided they are blocking).
concepts.html:
Tempest Shield is a Attack spell that produces an invulnerable shield for one minute that acts like any other equipped shield. However, this will release a powerful wind burst when the time ends if the shield is raised, knocking nearby foes to the ground. It can be invaluable before the player has access to stronger shields such as the iron shield, since most stronger attacks will still pierce damage through shields before that, while the Tempest Shield will still fully protect the user even when barehanded (provided they are blocking).

It is recommended to always cast it before an encounter (as there is usually scarcely time to cast it once already in battle), as it can often be the difference between a close fight or an easy one. The invulnerability and knockdown can be vital in gaining an opening on an opponent, and using it even when not engaging with melee can be advisable, to leave open the option to back away on low hitpoints with a safe frontal shield.

concepts.title: Enchant Weapon: Air
concepts.lead: Enchant Weapon: Air is a Attack spell that imbues a held melee weapon with a wind enchantment for two minutes. While this enchantment is applied, the held melee weapon will appear to have a silvery sheen with small wind breezes flowing around it and have their attack speed increased. This enchantment does not stack with other weapon enchantments, but does stack with whetstones and lesser Attack potions.
concepts.html:
Enchant Weapon: Air is a Attack spell that imbues a held melee weapon with a wind enchantment for two minutes. While this enchantment is applied, the held melee weapon will appear to have a silvery sheen with small wind breezes flowing around it and have their attack speed increased. This enchantment does not stack with other weapon enchantments, but does stack with whetstones and lesser Attack potions.

Currently, the Hitsplat is not registering every damage fast enough, causing one damage to stack over the other.

Mechanic

  • Your melee weapon speed increases, combos that takes about 4-5 seconds, will take 3-4 seconds.
  • When active, your weapon will do an additional 33% air damage based on your weapon damage.
    • Example, you do 116 damage, the enchantment will do 39 damage.
    • Special attacks/actions also becomes faster.

concepts.title: Enchant Weapon: Fire
concepts.lead: Enchant Weapon: Fire is a Attack spell that imbues a held melee weapon with a fire enchantment for five minutes. While this enchantment is applied, melee weapons will have a chance to apply Burning to enemies with each critical hit. This enchantment does not stack with other weapon enchantments, but does stack with whetstones and lesser Attack potions.

  • The weapon will act as a Torch, a lightsource.
  • Every critical hit, the enchantment will cause burn damage to enemies who are not immune to burn damage.

concepts.title: Spectral Arrows
concepts.lead: Spectral Arrows is a spell that is unlocked at level 25 Ranged causing arrows fired from two-handed bows to penetrate multiple targets. Arrows fired with this enchantment bypass Ranged resistances and immunities (including fire arrows against KotHaar), but they cannot be recovered. This enchantment cannot be cast on crossbows.

Arrows fired with this enchantment bypass Ranged resistances and immunities (including fire arrows against KotHaar), but they cannot be recovered. This enchantment cannot be cast on crossbows.

concepts.title: Internal Alchemy
concepts.lead: Internal Alchemy is a spell that is unlocked at level 20 Cooking. When used, it refreshes any active perks from food or infusions. It also provides the health from the refreshed perk food. This spell does not affect perks received from potions or other perk-giving items.
concepts.html:
Internal Alchemy is a spell that is unlocked at level 20 Cooking. When used, it refreshes any active perks from food or infusions. It also provides the health from the refreshed perk food. This spell does not affect perks received from potions or other perk-giving items.

This spell has a cooldown of 210 seconds, which means that any food or infusion perk that lasts longer can be extended indefinitely by casting this spell before those perks expire. 10 nature runes are cheaper than any food or infusion, so this is an effective method of saving valuable ingredients.

For example, only clean water and dried cadavaberries are needed to maintain hydration and sustenance and this spell can maintain the more valuable perks from the more expensive foods and infusions.

Due to the long cast time of this spell, players will need at least 6 seconds left on their current buffs for them to be refreshed; otherwise they will run out and the spell will be wasted.

Journal

The druid Gastritix often struggled with Bramblemead dishes. Something about the rustic cooking troubled her stomach and she would find herself in constant distress. Even bread, simple as it was, would leave her doubled over in agony and there were many times where she regretted that day's meal. So it was that she created a spell, which would speed up her digestion to near instant speed, granting her the energy needed to survive, but somehow preventing her normal stomach issues. Thereafter, with this spell in her repertoire, she became a noted local chef, finally able to enjoy a good meal.

concepts.title: Magical Mending
concepts.lead: Magical Mending is a spell that will partially repair weapons, tools, or armour placed on the floor in its area of effect by adding half of the durability back into the equipment. This does not consume resources to do so, other than the runes to cast the spell. It will affect all targetable equipment in range. Upon completion of the spell, the equipment will be placed back into the closest player's inventory automatically if possible. Be careful attempting to use it in a dangerous area as the gear will rarely be in the same inventory spots as before, and will need time sorting and re-equipping.
concepts.html:
Magical Mending is a spell that will partially repair weapons, tools, or armour placed on the floor in its area of effect by adding half of the durability back into the equipment. This does not consume resources to do so, other than the runes to cast the spell. It will affect all targetable equipment in range. Upon completion of the spell, the equipment will be placed back into the closest player's inventory automatically if possible. Be careful attempting to use it in a dangerous area as the gear will rarely be in the same inventory spots as before, and will need time sorting and re-equipping.

Journal

Skilled craftspeople are worth their weight in gold. The ability to repair broken equipment, and weaponry, was a core part of any craftsperson's trade. But, in the wilds of Ashenfall, such trades lacked the excitement and adventure of more whimsical professions. Hunters, warriors and druids, were the roles that everyone wanted, and so it was that fewer and fewer apprentices took up the hammer. As such, smiths would focus on creating new equipment, and tools, leaving repairs on the backburner for sometimes weeks at a time. Frustrated, the druids created a solution to this problem. Using a variation on the ritual that preserved wood, timber, and stone, the druids could turn back the clock on a piece of equipment, returning it to a healthier state. Over time, more people began to favour less deadly professions, and the spell would be used in only the most dire situations.

concepts.title: Windstep
concepts.lead: Windstep is a spell that is unlocked at level 5 Agility, allowing the player to reach higher ledges by jumping up to 16 metres high. In addition, the spell can be cast to act as a slow-fall effect when trying to go from high to low places. However, the slow-fall effect will not mitigate fall damage completely, but will reduce it dramatically to survive a fall that would normally kill the player. Players have seven seconds to use the spell before it disappears.
concepts.html:
Windstep is a spell that is unlocked at level 5 Agility, allowing the player to reach higher ledges by jumping up to 16 metres high. In addition, the spell can be cast to act as a slow-fall effect when trying to go from high to low places. However, the slow-fall effect will not mitigate fall damage completely, but will reduce it dramatically to survive a fall that would normally kill the player. Players have seven seconds to use the spell before it disappears.

At level 40 Agility, the spell gets the Wind Stomp perk, which allows a staggering effect on near by enemies when landing.

Journal

The air can be wrapped as a cloak around you, making heights much less scary to face. Once, long ago, young druids would use windstep to hurl themselves from atop the highest mountains, descending to the ground below. Higher and higher they would climb, each trying to outdo the other. Until the inevitable finally intervened. Since that tragic day, it has been well known that there is a limit to the height at which Windstep might protect someone. They call it the splat-limit, because druids are very bad with names.

concepts.title: Recall
concepts.lead: Recall is a spell unlocked at level 57 Agility that lets players summon and teleport back to a runic marker on the ground. At level 70 Agility, players unlock the Reactive Recall perk. This automatically triggers upon receiving fatal fall damage, protecting the caster.
concepts.html: Recall is a spell unlocked at level 57 Agility that lets players summon and teleport back to a runic marker on the ground. At level 70 Agility, players unlock the Reactive Recall perk. This automatically triggers upon receiving fatal fall damage, protecting the caster.

concepts.title: Dragon Rebellion
concepts.lead: The Dragon Rebellion is an event that took place in Ashenfall during the end of Third Age of Gielinor. It started shortly after the war between the garous and the humans, with the creation of Kuldra. The dragons were returned to their chains by their masters, the dragonkin, after assisting Lougrim and the garou in their war. With the dragons returned to chains they were forced to work in repairing damaged fortresses. Kuldra would witness this and start recruiting not only her own children, but other dragons. One of these dragons, Velgar would eagerly accept Kuldra's scheme without hesitation, being the first to join her war.
concepts.html:
The Dragon Rebellion is an event that took place in Ashenfall during the end of Third Age of Gielinor. It started shortly after the war between the garous and the humans, with the creation of Kuldra. The dragons were returned to their chains by their masters, the dragonkin, after assisting Lougrim and the garou in their war. With the dragons returned to chains they were forced to work in repairing damaged fortresses. Kuldra would witness this and start recruiting not only her own children, but other dragons. One of these dragons, Velgar would eagerly accept Kuldra's scheme without hesitation, being the first to join her war.

As the war commenced, Brakka was amongst the dragonkin killed by Kuldra, who devoured him and shared his essence with Velgar. Her gaze then turned to Lougrim, in a battle fractured the continent itself, Kuldra fought and killed Lougrim, devouring her body and taking her title of High Queen of the Garou. Having freed her fellow dragons, she sent them out across the continent to wipe out the human settlements.

concepts.title: Sixth Age
concepts.lead: This page covers the event of the Sixth Age of Ashenfall told in the lore scraps, and is the current timeline of the game. For the full history of the world, click .
concepts.html:
This page covers the event of the Sixth Age of Ashenfall told in the lore scraps, and is the current timeline of the game. For the full history of the world, click .

The Sixth Age is the current age of Gielinor. It followed the Fifth Age.

Events

The Sixth Age began with the death of Guthix by the hands of , which saw the return of the gods, as the of Guthix were destroyed. It wasn't until a decade later that a group of powerful heroes forged an alliance and the Edicts.

Dragonwilds

It is in this age that the events of the game begin, with an expedition team setting off to explore the newly rediscovered continent of Ashenfall. However, the expedition team was attacked by dragons, wiping out most of team. The surviving team members, Wise Old Man, Zanik, Doric, Vannaka, and Cathan, set off to explore the continent, setting up base camps as well as building a lodestone so new people can be brought in from the mainland. It is here where the game starts, with the player being teleported into the continent to help slay the dragons.

concepts.title: Commander Zilyana
concepts.lead: Commander Zilyana is a character who appears alongside the Scorned Wilderness.
concepts.html:
Commander Zilyana is a character who appears alongside the Scorned Wilderness.

History

This section is a simplified explanation of their history. To learn more, check her

Pre-Ashenfall

Zilyana is a from who arrived in Gielinor near the end of the , as one of Saradomin's finest warriors, giving her the rank of Commander. During the war, she led the forces of Saradomin, even participating in the battle of , defending it from Zamorak's forces. She fought against their commander, , but was overpowered by the demon, mortally wounded and left for dead. Saradomin arrived to her aid and teleported her to a secret location, where he keeps the . With it, Saradomin healed her so she could continue to fight under his name.

Sometime after the battle, Saradomin dispatches her with several soldiers to the to assist a flock of that were delivering the blade of the and were pinned by Zamorakian forces. Arriving at the temple, the Armadyleans, led by , were assisted by her and Bandosians led by . Although an alliance was formed after the sword was shattered to prevent K'ril from obtaining it, Zilyana would spy on all three sides, using amulets she received to listen in on their plans and manipulate the battle in her favour, although this did not last long. While all four sides began to fight each other, one of Guthix's , with several other druids, would cast a powerful spell to freeze the four factions, imprisoning the icyene in there.

During the late Fifth Age, the prison thawed out, and the armies would continue to fight; Zilyana would continue her attempt to reclaim the sword pieces for Saradomin. Although sometime later, she learns that god of wisdom was evicted from Gielinor by the god of balance and could not return due to the . But this would soon change when Guthix's resting place was discovered; she was amongst the factions' leaders to head there to slay Guthix. Despite failing to kill the god, as that deed was stolen by , Saradomin was still able to return, leaving the resting place with Zilyana to start planning for the return of other gods. In the Sixth Age, Zilyana was tasked with doing other things, but she remained as the commander of Saradomin's forces, even escorting him to Sliske's , the finale of his , and assisting in the against the Elder Gods.

When the Edict of Guthix was by the and their allies, Saradomin appointed , his daughter, as his successor to the Saradominist kingdoms. Despite disagreeing with this, she accepted it after seeing the wisdom in his choice, remaining in to ensure her safety.

Traveling to Ashenfall

During her time on the mainland, Zilyana received guidance from Saradomin to head to Ashenfall and seek aid in stopping Kuldra's attempt to destroy the world.

concepts.title: Black Dragon
concepts.lead: Black dragons, also known as lesser black dragons, are power level 8 dragons that can be found in the Scorned Wilderness raid. There are currently only three black dragon spawns.
concepts.html:
Black dragons, also known as lesser black dragons, are power level 8 dragons that can be found in the Scorned Wilderness raid. There are currently only three black dragon spawns.

Attacks

  • Lunge
  • Tail sweep (if behind them)
  • Fire Claw Slash
  • Poison Blast: The black dragon launches a fire projectile to build up around the three-quarters point.
  • Fire Breath: The black dragon sweeps the area in front of them with their fire breath.
  • Wing Attack: The black dragon flaps its wings, blowing wind at the player, with the second such blast doing damage.
  • Fly: The black dragon can fly into the sky and do a few moves:
    • Fire Breath: The black dragon shoots their breath in a line going away from them. This staggers the player and can easily lock them in to take all of the damage.

Location

Within the Scorned Wilderness, they can be found in Dragontail Vines, in the Fragments of Ghornfell, and in The Shattered Stronghold areas.

Drops

ItemQtyRarity
Black Dragon Hide10-12Always
Dragon Blood6-12Always
Dragon Tooth6-12Always
Discordant Residue12-15Always
Ascension Shard (Power Level 8)8-12Always

Journal

If you thought the red dragons were bad, you're in for a rude awakening. The black dragons is a powerhouse of destruction. Every fibre of its being is bred to defend Kuldra and obliterate all threats that get remotely near. Xikotal was the exception. He was a creature of empathy and he struggled with violence that Kuldra made him inflict on the world. When the first of the dragon wars ended, he nestled in with Imaru and the two of them tried to turn tragedy into something beautiful; a gentle utopia, where all life was sacred. This disgusted Kuldra, and she has made sure that none of her black-scaled brood ever suffer the same weakness

See also

  • Kuldra
  • Xikotal

concepts.title: Kuldra
concepts.lead: Queen Kuldra, also known as the Dragon Queen and the God Eater, is an ancient black dragon with five heads. She is the leader of the dragons ruling over the continent of Ashenfall, and the current High Queen for some of the garou. She is the boss of the Scorned Wilderness raid, and the final boss for Kuldra's Saga.
concepts.html:
Queen Kuldra, also known as the Dragon Queen and the God Eater, is an ancient black dragon with five heads. She is the leader of the dragons ruling over the continent of Ashenfall, and the current High Queen for some of the garou. She is the boss of the Scorned Wilderness raid, and the final boss for Kuldra's Saga.

Deity Info

History

Creation

Kuldra was amongst the first dragons created by the dragonkin Lacrussa and Avisk. When Lacrussa was working on making a better race of dragons, Avisk would force himself into her experiments and suggesting to fuse certain dragons for a better results. He would mess with some of the brood, adding rune essence into the them. Despite Lacrussa's warning in trying to maintain a single headed dragons, Avisk ignored her, which led to several of these brood to die, all but one. Kuldra was born showing no signs of madness for having multiple minds. Instead she found that it would work as one, unified in a way. Lacrussa learns that the dragon was able to spread the rage across herself, weakening the effect, causing her to express other emotion and behaviours, such as curiosity, reason and even wit. This would make Lacrussa want to study her further, keeping her chained. During the study, they would get her off springs and conduct several experiments on them, exterminating the failures. Kuldra would witness this, and slowly plot her vengeance.

Dragon Rebellion

After the Human-Garou War, the goddess Lougrim donated her blood to the dragonkin for their assistance against the human and bandosians. Lacrussa would use this on Kuldra. After gaining Lougrim's blood, she would plot a rebellion against the dragonkin after seeing the continued abuse, despite their assistance in the war. At first, she was hesitant, but it was Velgar who convinced her and was the first to join her cause. When the rebellion started, Lacrussa was slain, along with Brakka, from whom Kuldra stole powers for herself and shared them with Velgar, her most trusted ally, granting him his elemental mastery of earth. Before she could kill Rasthin, the dragonkin, activated the Harmonic Resonator in hope to destroy Kuldra, only for the Dragon Queen to survive. In a battle that fractured the continent itself, Kuldra then attacked Lougrim, who was protecting the garou village. Weak and wounded, Kuldra descended on her without mercy and devouring her body and taking her title of High Queen of the Garou. Some accepted out of fear, but others rejected her rule and left to another region. Having freed her fellow dragons, she sent them out across the continent to wipe out other settlements, other than the garou and goblins.

Sometime during these events, Kuldra caught wind of Imaru's and Xikotal's mercy towards the human settlements in Fellhollow, and as a result, she decided to confront the duo herself. As Kuldra descended on the region, nobles within the region would arm themselves in steel equipment to assist Xikotal and Imaru, in the hope of defending their new home and bring an end to the Dragon Queen. Despite the help and numbers, they failed to bring Kuldra down. With Kuldra's strength and power seemingly unmatched, she would pull Xikotal's heart from his chest and devour it. She would then leave Imaru to grieve, as punishment for disobeying her. However, Imaru would challenge Kuldra a second time, after being infused by a curse placed by Ravanna. However, this was not enough to even stand a chance against Kuldra, who killed her quite easily. Despite Imaru's action, Kuldra had left the humans of Fellhollow alone, their fate met by the resurrected corpse of Imaru some time later.

With Ashenfall settlement destroyed, minus some of the garou and goblins, Kuldra now rules the continent with her dragons.

Sixth Age

During the 14th Year of the Sixth Age, while ruling unchallenged, an expedition had made its way to Ashenfall; her generals had attacked the expedition in her name. After the arrival of a group of adventurers, Kuldra would start gathering pieces of the Harmonic Resonator to cause another explosion that would devour the world. Before she could put her plan into motion and put an end to the world, the adventurer(s) made their way into her sanctum and, through a grueling barrage of her hatchlings trying to protect her from the intruders, was unable to survive after they destroyed her heart.

Drops

ItemQtyRarity
Kuldra's Head1Always
Queenslayer's Reward Pack1Always
Lougrim's Staff1Always

Journal

Kuldra's tale is tragic really. An innocent child, raised by monsters: tormented, tortured, and forced to create legions of children who were all taken from her and then either weaponised or dissected for future study. She found comfort in the gentle warmth of a lover's embrace, only to see him taken from her by those same cruel parents. Only one dragonkin ever showed her warmth, but their mind was distracted by thousand different timestreams and they could never give Kuldra the love that she deserved. A lack of love is like a poison: it seeps into one's soul and infects it with malice. You find yourself unable to believe that love could be real, and from it all the other positive emotions, such as charity, kindness, or hope. Kuldra wasn't born a monster, but she chose to become one and she was determined to be the worst monster she could be. For centuries she has gorged herself on the anima of Ashenfall, building her own power so that she might turn the region's wellspring into a weapon that would decimate the rest of the world. Why? Because the rest of the world is happy, and she needs to see that stopped. Now, she is dead - although her legacy will scar the world for generations to come. Hate breeds only hate, and Kuldra has had plenty of children.

concepts.title: Kuldra/Strategies
concepts.lead: This is a strategy guide to defeating Kuldra. Depending on the player's world difficulty, please refer to the relevant strategy section.
concepts.html:
This is a strategy guide to defeating Kuldra. Depending on the player's world difficulty, please refer to the relevant strategy section.

Inventory Preparation

Kuldra is a power level 9 boss monster of the Scorned Wilderness raid.

Foods/Drinks

For your fight against Kuldra, may it be first or multiple encounters, you'll want the following suggested items in your key bind hotbar slot or inventory:

  • Stuffed Catfish which restores 200 health per consumption.
    • It is suggested to also have the Undead Delight which restores 180 health and grants the Sea Life perk, regenerating 3 health every second 1,200 seconds (20 minutes.)
      • If you wish not to grind for Undead Delight, Eggs Royale also grants the Sea Life perk and heals 120 health.
  • Use any infusions that buff your combat style.
    • Infusions do not stack, so pick one that reduces stamina on your combat style action, or dodging.
    • Or you can drink the Pumpkin Spice Infusion for the Soul food perk, to have it and Sea Life active. (Soul Food perk will not stack if it is from another food.)
  • In the final phase, Antipoison Potions can be useful. As the incoming attacks are new and the summoned mobs can easily combo a player out, Super Antipoison Potions may be excessive, so the standard 300s duration can suffice.

Optional additions

If fighting in hard difficulty, or wanting to speed up the fight in normal difficulty, it is advised to have these items:

  • Whetstone enhances any melee weapon held by +2 for ten minutes.
    • In addition, lesser Attack potion can be added for the Focused Strikes perk for ten minutes.
  • Magical Focus enhances staff and wand damage output from spell attacks by 15% for ten minutes
    • In addition, lesser Magic potion can be added to increase the chance of landing critical hits with combat spells by 25% for ten minutes.
  • Super Antifire Potion to grant Antifire perk to defend against her energy breath.

Runes and Spells

Although Kuldra cannot be attacked directly, her Dragon Hatchlings can. They have the same resistance as regular dragons.

You can also use spells to enhance your abilities against Kuldra.

  • Surge would allow you to dodge attacks at a greater distance three times, costing no stamina.
  • Tempest Shield for melee, crossbow and wand users, as it blocks more variety of attacks, even unblockable ones.
  • Enchant Weapon: Air to increase the attack speed and damage of your equipped melee weapon if using melee.
  • Spectral Arrows increases their damage done and is worth maintaining over the course of the fight if using Ranged.

Internal Alchemy is optional to have, as it is able to refresh active food and drinks buffs, but only if you're willing to spend about 4–5 seconds of casting time, which can leave you open for attacks.

Presets

Based on the player's preferred combat style, the inventory layout should appear like this:

Strategy Guides

Kuldra has a total of four phases, the first three requiring you to hit her with the device's blast a total of six times before she starts the next phase. Unlike previous bosses, Kuldra cannot be damaged by players themselves. Instead, Players must use the Anima Cannon to do enough damage on her before being able to enter her body and attack her heart.

Main attacks

Kuldra's many heads will have basics abilities fired on you as you are charging up the Anima Cannon. Her main head will shoot a beam of energy out of her mouth across the arena. After that, at random, each head will begin their attack before she does her beam attack again. Green will spit a sludge of poison; Red will shoot 5 fireballs into the air, landing in random areas while one of them is targeted where you last stood; White will shoot a lingering ice shard into the arena where it will attempt to freeze the player; and Blue will shoot lightning at your position.

Dragon Hatchlings

During the first three encounters, a Dragon Hatchling will fly into the arena each phase and attack you. They are just like regular dragons, though exactly like the (Air Skeletons) that grant Anima, killing them will grant you the anima element they carry to either activate the Anima cannon, or activate the Anima Orb Dispenser.

Phase 1

In this phase, Kuldra will use her main attack calmly, giving you enough time to dodge and plan your move. You'll first need to get rid of the blue dragon hatchling that will appear, as killing it will allow you to absorb water anima for the Anima Pylon and the dispenser. There is also a earth Crystallized Anima for players to use for the dispenser. You will need to use the Anima Orb on the cannon twice and fire a total of 6 anima blasts at her. At the end of this phase, all hatchlings will automatically die. Commander Zilyana will then appear and summon a barrier around her (like in the raid) for your protection. Make sure you hide within it or you will take rapid damage from Kuldra's special attack.

Note: You can carry an Anima Charge and the (Orb) at the same time, allowing Players to quickly gather the Orb and then deposit their Charge to reduce time spent waiting for new orbs to appear. Players also cannot carry anima orbs between phases as they will drop after Zilyana protects you from Kuldra's attack.

Phase 2

At the start of this phase, you will be teleported to a new platform where you will need to repeat the same Anima Cannon process as before. Kuldra will start with her primary breath attack more aggressively and quickly, it is advised that you dodge and avoid them first before attempting to reactivate and use the cannon. Kuldra's red head attack will now do 7 spots of her fireballs; the green head will shoot two poison sludge at your previous position; the white will use two ice shards; and the blue will continue to shoot lighting (count the amount?). In this phase, a red dragon hatchling will appear. Killing it will allow you to absorb the Fire Anima in you for the pylon.

If you have multiple people, you can stagger Anima deposits by doing Fire into the first Pylon > Fire into the (Orb Spawner) > Air into the second Pylon, then gather Anima as needed and create/carry orbs from there.

Phase 3

At the start of this phase, you will be teleported to a secondary floating platform. If you happen to have a lingering Anima charge from the previous phase, you can deposit it into the Orb Dispenser. From here, jump to the platform housing the Anima Orb Dispenser. Continue platforming across two more floating islands to reach the main arena platform. Be careful of the attacks from Kuldra's various heads, as (at least the Lightning attack) they can interrupt you mid-jump.

Upon landing on the main platform, Kuldra will immediately launch all of her main attacks aggressively and simultaneously. Focus entirely on dodging these incoming attacks for the first few seconds before attempting to set up the cannon or manage hatchlings. Hatchlings will spawn shortly after this initial onslaught as either blue or red variants (double check spawning priority).

This phase features two distinct Anima Pylons: Water and Fire.

  • Water Pylon: Collect an Anima Orb from the dispenser, insert it into the Water Pylon, and activate it. Doing so unlocks the gate leading to the Fire Pylon.
    • Gate Skip (Optional): You can skip opening the gate by using the Windstep spell on the broken pillar to the right of the gate, then jumping over the stone wall. Note: You must be imbued with Fire Anima before jumping over the wall. To return from the Fire Pylon back over the wall, jump on the green gems located to the left.
  • Fire Pylon & Cannon: The Fire Pylon already contains an Anima Orb. Activating the Fire Pylon fully powers the Anima Cannon.

Once the Anima Cannon is online, load and fire it at Kuldra. After taking sufficient damage (6 hits), Kuldra will be stunned. A bridge will be created that leads directly to her platform, where you can 'Enter' the main head's mouth to begin the final phase.

Phase 4

The final phase has you entering Kuldra's body and attacking Kuldra's Heart. In here, you will have to reduce the Heart to 0 hp, while handling the various Heartworms (do the Heartworms cause the Earth Spike attack?) that spawn as well as the Poison AoE attacks. Without the worms (verify if poison attacks only appear without worms), Kuldra can use poison explosion to damage the player, so it is advised that you use activate your Antipoison II buff and dodge. The lower her HP, the more explosions she causes. Additionally, keep an eye out for the worms as they do respawn. Once you see the hp reach 0, run to the exit as fast as you can. (specific ). There exists a safe spot within the tunnel entrance that allows Players to safely attack the Heart with ranged or magic, letting them avoid most of the poison explosions, with Heartworms rarely/occasionally spawning in the tunnel.
