  • (when within the tunnel)

concepts.title: Scorned Wilderness
concepts.lead: The Scorned Wilderness is RuneScape: Dragonwilds' first raid. This raid contains the Dragon Queen Kuldra as well as all monsters you have previously encountered.
concepts.html:
The Scorned Wilderness is RuneScape: Dragonwilds first raid'. This raid contains the Dragon Queen Kuldra as well as all monsters you have previously encountered.

In order to enter this zone, players will have to first complete the quest Icthlarin's Little Helper and start the Regicide quest. The entrance to the zone is located in the north-western area of the Fractured Plains in Ghornfell.

History

After arriving to Ashenfall long ago, the Dragonkin created a device called the Harmonic Resonator within the area now known as the Scorned Wilderness. The device's purpose was to gather raw anima for the Dragonkin, who would create an empire with it. Centuries after the creation of the device, Rasthin would activate it to destroy Kuldra, shattering the land. Kuldra survived, and now hunts for the pieces of the device to activate and lay waste to the rest of the world.

Raid Info

Rasthin's Rest

This area of the Scorned Wilderness is the only buildable area in the entire zone. It is considered a safe hub, where players can build a base to return to when needing to rest, craft or repair. Players who make a bed here and as their spawn point will not experience any Warband Raids, being one of the few locations that are safe from raiding and hunting parties.

Dragontail Vines

Head into Dragontail Vines and head up the path. You will come across Runite ore deposits and Luminite ore deposits along the way, so it is highly recommended that you mine some up. In order to progress further, you will need to charge up an Anima Pylon with air anima. There is a floating crystallised shard of anima behind you to your right surrounded by three runite ore deposits. Siphon the shard and fill up your charge meter all the way to gain thirty seconds of anima infusion. Head back to the pylon and charge it using the anima you have to unlock the pathway to the next area.

Head down the newly formed anima bridge to the next area where Kuldra will appear along with Zilyana. Kuldra will begin attacking you with an elemental attack, but Zilyana will appear and tells you to get closer to her so she can protect you from the attack. Once you are close enough to her, she will save you from the ensuing attack and, thus, opening the way further into her lair. In this area, she will use an attack to inflict Soulscourge.

Head up the way to a white barrier. This will require you to charge up with Air anima once more, with another air shard nearby to siphon, in order to pass through. When you pass through, you will encounter a black dragon along with some skeletal archers and zombies. Defeat them all to collect discordant residue. Aside from the residue, you will need to siphon some Earth anima next to pass through the barrier.

Once you pass through, head down the vine pathway to another area. This time, defeat the zombies in the area and siphon some water anima from a nearby water anima shard. Pass through the blue barrier and defeat the air-infused skeletal warriors to get enough air anima charged up to collect an orb from the Anima Orb Dispenser nearby. Go up the stairs and pull the nearby lever to unlock the path back around to the anima pylon. This pylon will require you to fill it up with anima again, but you can either fill it up with air or water anima to unlock the next area.

Go down the pathway and you will find a Zilyana Teleporter. Activate it and Zilyana will be able to take you back here if you choose the option "Fragments of Ghornfell" in the options. A small notification will pop up in the top middle of your screen saying that you have reached an extraction point.

Fragments of Ghornfell

Head further into the fragment and defeat the garou and goblins within the area. Once you have done that, head up the stairs to defeat another black dragon along with the garou thane, beserker, and goblin bodyguards. Once you defeat them, you will be able to use the central anima platform to attune to earth anima and unlock a nearby door. It is important to note that, beyond this door, lay a Sanguine Urn which can increase your total health pool by ten points. After collecting the urn, head back south down the stairs to continue through the fragment. There will be goblins and garou in this area, so prepare well. After clearing out all of the garou and goblins in the area, head up to the north-western tower and climb up the tower. Find a lever next to some thorny vines and interact with it. Chop up the vines too before going back down to the fire anima platform. Charge up your anima infusion meter fully and get up to the top of the tower within thirty seconds to acquire an anima orb from the dispenser.

With your new orb, head back down to the two anima pylons blocking the way into the next area. Use the orb on the broken anime pylon to activate it. Once you have done that, it will light up red. This means that, to open the way forward, you will need both fire and air anima. For the fire anima, head back to the platform mentioned earlier and charge up. As for the air anima, there is a graveyard nearby behind a barrier of water anima that you can use to lure the air-infused skeletons out of and kill to acquire a sufficient charge. Once you have charged both pylons, the way forward will open. Head into the church and turn left to fight against some skeletons, a necromancer, and an archer.

Clear out any enemies you see and head down the path. There is a route that is covered in poison emitters (like in the Bloodblight Swamp) and another path that is somewhat fragmented and covered in luminite. Either way will take you to a bridge that will lead you into an underground castle ruin. You will have to fight through numberous goblins, skeletons, some putrid rats, and an Abyssal Demon.

Note: There is another Sanguine Urn in this area that can be acquired, but requires some parkour to get to. It is on the way to the Abyssal Demon.

Once you have defeated the Abyssal Demon, head out and you will have another extraction point. Activate the teleporter once more to unlock this area.

The Shattered Stronghold

Blocking your way into this area is a water anima barrier. Use the nearby crystallised water anima shard to infuse yourself with a sufficient charge of water anima to pass through the barrier. Once you pass through the barrier, quickly run to Zilyana as she will protect you from Kuldra's attack. Once the attack is done, head into the nearby doorway near the water barrier. Enter through the doorway and you will come across a fire-breathing gargoyle statue that will spew flames for a moment. To the right is a pathway to a crystallised air anima shard surrounded by rats and a PL 9 Rat King. It is recommended to defeat the rats here before siphoning the shard as they will attack you while siphoning. Collect enough for a sufficient charge and make your way up to the floor above where the gargoyle statue is and pass through the air anima barrier on the other side of the walkway.

After passing through the barrier, head down the stairs and pull on the lever first before engaging in a fight with the rats and Garou Thane. They will be charged with air anima which can be used at the nearby dispenser to acquire an anima orb for the pylon. Once you get the orb, head to the pylon to activate it. It will require fire anima to charge, so head around the crumbled tower to a breakable wall. Use your pickaxe on it to destroy it and head inside. Siphon the earth anima shard and head up the stairs and turn right towards an earth anima barrier. Pass through the barrier and use the lever nearby to unlock a shortcut back and defeat the garou within before attempting to siphon the fire anima shard as they will have a PL 9 garou thane among them.

Return to the pylon with the fire anima charge and it will open the way to the next area. As there is a black dragon in this area and some wild jade vines, it is recommended to deal with the closest jade vine so you don't get poisoned while fighting the black dragon. Once you defeat the dragon and head further down the path, keeping in mind of the garou and wild jade vines in the area, activate the teleporter.

Cataclysm Keep

Unlike in the previous areas, this area is more fractured and has less safe areas. Walk across the roots and small land chunks, minding the garou thane, and traverse through the shattered pathways to the other side. Once you have gotten through the pathway, reaching the other side, head through the doorway. This will lead you into a room with three vault guardians (two hulk and one sentinel), which can be easily defeated. Head past this to a puzzle that must be solved in order to continue further.

In this area, you can find a Sanguine Urn. It will require you to solve a jumping puzzle in order to reach.

After you activate all of the pylons, you will need to press the buttons in order for the path to be opened. The order is as follows: Air, Water, Earth, and Fire.

Once you open the path, head up the stairs and reach the teleporter to activate it.

Kuldra's Sanctum

When you reach this zone, there are a few Runite ore deposits along with Luminite ore rocks in this area as you reach closer to the Dragon Gate. Interact with the gate and you will be taken into the boss arena where you will face Kuldra.

concepts.title: Ancestral Robes
concepts.lead: Ancestral robes is a power level 8 magic armour piece, crafted using materials found within the Scorned Wilderness raid zone.
concepts.html:
Ancestral robes is a power level 8 magic armour piece, crafted using materials found within the Scorned Wilderness raid zone.

Stats

Recipe

Recipe Armour Bench · Artisan 100 xp
4 × Vis Cloth, 2 × Black Dragon Leather, 2 × Rune Bar, 2 × Harmonised Compound, 2 × Draconic Vis Wax → 1 × Ancestral Robes

Recipe tree

Journal

Long ago, there were people in Ashenfall. Not humans, not elves, nor anyone you might remember, but sentient beings with a life, a culture and a civilisation all of their own. No trace of them remains today. More and more of the Kobalios began to take more than their fair share. The Wellspring was never-ending, but it would only release at a steady rate. Only so much could be consumed at any one time, and fewer and fewer of the Kobalios were able to enjoy it. In their desperation, they used rituals and spells to draw more anima from the Wellspring than it gave, and this caused a tiny crack to appear in the skein of creation. From this crack, smoke rose and filled the bellies of the greediest of the Kobalios. The effect of the smoke was subtle, but deadly. It left a hole in the heart of the infected that made them yearn for more and more anima; to feast deeper and deeper upon the Wellspring, regardless of how it might impact their kin.

It can be ascended at a mystic forge with ascension cores. Note, if you ascend the Abysmal Whip to power level 8, and upgrade it to the Abyssal Whip, it will be brought down to Power Level 7.
concepts.html:
The abysmal whip is a power level 4 one-handed melee weapon that can be created at a blacksmith's bench. The recipe, Abyssal Remains, can be acquired by killing an Abyssal Demon. It can be ascended at a mystic forge with ascension cores. Note, if you ascend the Abysmal Whip to power level 8, and upgrade it to the Abyssal Whip, it will be brought down to Power Level 7.

This weapon's special effect is that regular attacks also build up bleed, and after five rapid hits, it will proc 28 damage at power level 4 and 40 damage at power level 7, despite only listing 25 for each. As this weapon deals slash damage, compared to swords, its attacks are slightly slower but slightly harder; however, its forward lunge distance is much shorter, and since enemies are knocked back significantly by most attacks, they will often be knocked out of this weapon's combos. It also does not have increased block without a shield compared to other similar weapons.

Journal

We've all heard of it. We've all wanted it... the Legendary Abyssal Whip! The fabled weapon that heroes and adventurers have been seeking for an age! You have taken it one step further. You have asked the question, "How hard could it be to make your own?". All you need is a spine from an Abyssal Demon! It comes pre-segmented and it's made from some of the hardiest organic material known to mortalkind. You just need to kill the demon, twist the shoulder, sever a tendon, and Io - your very own Abyssal Whip... right? Wrong. Turns out, it's a bit more involved than you expected, and this "weapon" demonstrates that all too well. Still, not all is lost. Perhaps there is a way, a method, to turn this... "thing" into something that lives up to it's legend.

The Fight Cave is a dangerous combat activity located within The Burning Spire, in Umbral Sands. It is introduced during the quest, Icthlarin's Little Helper, and is required to complete the quest's version of the cave before being able to do the real one.

activities.html:
The Nightmare Crucible is a combat activity found within the Umbral Sands region of Ashenfall. It is meant to act akin to s and s in where the player fights against all of the toughest enemies Ashenfall has to offer thus far.

To unlock a Nightmare Crucible, the player must use a corresponding item, called an Engram, whose title matches the Crucible of interest. An Engram only provides a single attempt to a given Crucible: - Single player: win or lose, the crucible will re-lock once the player enters it once. - Multiplayer: The crucible will only remain open as long as at least one player remains in it.

If the player dies while inside a Crucible, their gravestone will appear outside the crucible entrance.

The interior of Nightmare Crucibles are wide open, flat areas with almost no obstacles, save for the small Reward Pedestal in the center, and no safe spots for ranged or magic users. There is enough space to run around the arena in a circle and fight enemies from afar, but there is nowhere to hide. It is sometimes possible, depending on the player's positioning, to attract the attention of only a subset of the enemies in a given Crucible at a time.

Location

Enemies to Defeat

Note: The level of the enemies are based on the location of the Nightmare Crucible.

Umbral Sands

Nightmare Crucible of Humiliation - in Dunes of Uzzer (Northeast) - Unlock with Crucible Engram of Humiliation

  • 1 x blue dragon
  • 1 x green dragon
  • 1 x red dragon

Nightmare Crucible of the Hounded - in Manafem Plains (Southwest) - Unlock with Crucible Engram of the Hounded

  • 2 x zogre

Nightmare Crucible of Betrayal - in The Burning Spire (Southeast) - Unlock with Crucible Engram of Betrayal

  • 1 x Black Knight Titan
  • 1 x green dragon or abyssal demon

Nightmare Crucible of Helplessness - in Alcarrid Oasis (Northwest) - Unlock with Crucible Engram of Helplessness

  • 2 x garou thane
  • 1 x green dragon

Rewards

Enemies in Nightmare Crucibles do not drop anything upon defeat.

Upon killing all monsters in the Nightmare Crucible, one ascension core is rewarded by interacting with the reward pedestal. In multiplayer sessions, additional players do not receive additional ascension cores. In general, one engram corresponds to one ascension core, assuming the crucible is cleared.

Note: Currently there is a bug where if Buddy, summoned from the Pharaoh's Sceptre special attack, is alive, the challenge is not counted as completed. Player must wait for Buddy to despawn for the challenge to complete.

You can despawn Buddy by casting your special with the pharaoh's sceptre

Journal Entry

Nothing discovered yet...

activities.html:
Statues of Saradomin is an activity that can be started in the Bramblemead Valley, east of Crasorak Kara.

Locations

Walkthrough

The activity requires the player to find three statues of Saradomin and insert gemstones into them:

  1. Whispering Swamp: The statue is in the north-west corner of the swamp. The statue requires an opal to be inserted in exchange for the opal emblem
  2. Fractured Plains: The statue is in the central portion of the plains, east of the tower and west of a lake, on the lower side of a small cliff. The statue requires a jade to be inserted in exchange for the jade emblem
  3. Stormtouched Highlands: The statue is in the north-east portion of the highlands, along the cliff edge. The statue requires a sapphire to be inserted in exchange for the sapphire emblem.

Once all emblems are collected, return to the statue to receive a Saradominist cloak.

updates.title: We're leaving Early Access and launching on consoles on September 15th!
updates.subtitle: Mark your calendars, book your time off work, whatever you have to do - it's time!
updates.html:
RuneScape: Dragonwilds is leaving Early Access and arriving onto consoles on September 15th for PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S!
And yes, we've got crossplay.

Launching simultaneously across PC and consoles for the first time, the full release will include the brand-new Scorned Wilderness update, as well as all our content so far including our upcoming Umbral Sands expansion arriving later this Summer.

Wishlist us, or grab Dragonwilds and join us for the rest of our Early Access journey on Steam here!

What is RuneScape: Dragonwilds?

Dragonwilds is a lovingly hand-crafted Survival RPG adventure set in the legendary world of RuneScape. Players must forge a foothold in a hostile, deeply magical land under the looming shadow of ancient Dragons. You'll grind 13 unique skills all the way to level 99, embark on magical and strange quests and explore a beautiful, hand-crafted world, all of which is deeply immersed in the iconic RuneScape lore. Battle the Black Knights, towering Zogres, Chromatic Dragons, Kalphites and more across an enormous continent filled with perilous vaults, ruthless dragons and boundless mysteries.

Use the magic in the air of Ashenfall to summon a spectral axe to fell trees in an instant! Blink away from danger in a cloud of magic. Turn bones into... peaches? Conjure a tornado of fish from a lake! Explode ore veins with a snap of your fingers! Jump really high! Your Skill Spells will turn surviving into thriving.

Build breathtaking homes with our incredible building system to fortify yourself against the ever-present Dragon threat. Use hundreds of unique building pieces to create a truly unique home with countless possibilities!

What's Happened In Early Access?

When Early Access launched in April 2025, you had one dragon to slay and a continent waiting to be explored. A lot has changed since then!

In December, Fellhollow arrived - our first Major Update! A hauntingly beautiful realm, enlisted in the service of Death, himself. You faced Imaru, a corrupted guardian dragon, learned to farm with a magical twist, and even got to ride a Terrorbird. Wheeeee!

Then in March, Dowdun Reach opened its doors. A dense, dangerous Zamorakian fortress packed to the chaos-worshipping gills with Black Knights, Blue Dragons, and Mithril-tier gear. Speaking of gills, we added Fishing to the game, Skill caps hit 99, Runecrafting got a much-needed overhaul, and dedicated server support let you get more friends hooked into the chaos. Get it? Hooked?

Ah, comedy. Anyway, most recently, we've shared the Kuldra's Saga roadmap, setting the stage for Umbral Sands, the Scorned Wilderness, and our ultimate showdown with the Dragon Queen herself. We're ready to build the final pieces of this Saga of RuneScape: Dragonwilds together with our amazing community and deliver an experience we're truly proud of to so many of you on PC AND Consoles!

What's on the Roadmap?

Umbral Sands is launching on Steam Early Access later this month, and introduces our largest region to date, alongside an additional tier of gear for players to craft, wear and survive in - including iconic Infinity Robes and Red Dragonhide.

Forge yourself into a Dragon-slaying weapon of war in the Fight Caves, and challenge yourself against Ashenfall's most fearsome foes in the Nightmare Crucible.

We're adding the Agility skill to give you more ways to navigate the world. We're building out our minor updates month on month with a selection of QOL Fixes driven by player feedback, as well as quests, items, and additional items for you to build and decorate with!

Take on every challenge to prepare yourself for the final clash with Kuldra, the God-Eater dragon queen, in the Scorned Wilderness raid! We'll be delivering this final update for Early Access alongside our full release onto all platforms, including iconic Rune armour, and so much more. We're so ready to show you everything that's coming your way on PC and consoles on September 15th.

Want to get the latest news? Sign up to our mailing list to be the first to find out more about RuneScape: Dragonwilds. Check out our socials for all the news we’re yet to share. Wanna dive right in and start asking questions? Great! Check out the official Reddit, or Discord too.

updates.title: 0.12.1 and the Road to Release
updates.html:
"She is here: the pinnacle of dragon creation, the queen, fused with divine blood and now housing the elemental power of my kin." - Rasthin

Hello adventurers!

Our road to the end of Kuldra's Saga is clear. Our 0.12.1 update will be the last stop before we put you face to face with the God-Eater herself. Darkness gathers. Wild magic storms overhead. The only way out is through.

We're going to be sharing a full breakdown of Agility, as well as a Dev Diary condensing 0.12.1's features very soon ahead of it's release at the end of this month. Firstly though, let's talk about Scorned Wilderness.

Until now, we've shipped Major Updates that are expansive continents that add a new region, rich with resources, quests, secrets and lore for you to explore at your own pace. These expansion-like updates have grown the world and set the stage for the adventures you'll be undertaking within it. Scorned Wilderness is not like these updates. Scorned Wilderness represents the culmination of our learnings from everything we've built within RuneScape: Dragonwilds so far - but it is not the end. Our journey is only beginning, and we're excited to share more about what's coming after Scorned Wilderness once we launch it. Rest assured, our intentions are the same as they always have been - to keep delivering more of the game you love, at a pace that delights and excites you.

We've referred to it so far as a "Raid" because we know that for those of you chasing Twisted Bows, ending up at the toothy end of Zebak, or who've earned the scars from the Liberation of Mazcab, RuneScape Raids mean something. We agree.

For those of you unfamiliar with RuneScape raids, we've got you. A Raid is typically a high-end challenge pitched against a player, or groups. You'll be subjected to a gauntlet, delving into a dungeon, raiding a tomb, or... say... charging into an Anima storm to take down a God-Eater. We're the latter. A raid includes unique mechanics or combat challenges testing your mettle and survival skills to hold out against onslaughts of enemies as you fight for a foothold and every inch of ground gained is a victory in itself. Ultimately, you'll rise to the challenge and earn the right to challenge the boss.

Our first Raid pits you (and your cadre of adventurer allies, if you so wish) against a landscape that was ripped apart by wild anima, and the fury of Black Dragons. You will traverse across floating islands, fighting through attacks by the God-Eater herself to reach her. Each of her tyrannical, terrible heads channels the fury of Gielinor's dragons - but she is more than the sum of her parts. Those of you who have slain countless Dragons on the Gielinor mainland will recognise some of her attacks. She shares heritage with other Dragonkin experiments, but she is more.

Beyond Kuldra, you'll be able to harvest resources to craft Ancestral Robes, Black Dragonhide gear and of course, Rune Armour. Claim your rewards for a dragon-slaying job well done, and you'll be able to gear yourself up with some new kit that will let you roam the entirety of Ashenfall in relative safety and security. For now, anyway...

Killing Kuldra will ensure you get the latest version of the Dragon Shield as you've come to expect with the previous Dragons, and then a Cape to wear with pride. There is also going to be a selection of pieces of the iconic Dragon armour - glorious, resplendent and red, including the Dragon Scimitar and the Dragon Crossbow. There's a few extra secret goodies on that RDT (that's a Rare Drop Table to you and me) that we're not spoiling yet - you'll have to slay that Dragon and get spooned to find them out.

We're excited to keep working on finishing up what is undoubtedly our most vertical, most anima-warped update to date. We're really excited to get it into your hands, and for you to be able to enjoy the entire RuneScape: Dragonwilds experience so far with new combat, new movement, and so much more. With that in mind, while we've aimed to share things early, give you sneak peeks and even some deep dives in things like blog posts, we're going to be making a conscious choice NOT to spoil the Raid.

We'll be sharing more about our work towards the release, including our process for finding and fixing bugs, and the changes we're delivering to change combat and movement from minute one, but the Raid is something else entirely.

It's going to be something you can only experience for the first time once, so we want it to be totally new, and completely engrossing. We hope you can understand, and we're excited to see you taking on the God-Eater when it launches on September 15th.

- The RuneScape: Dragonwilds Team

updates.title: Changing the Abyssal Whip
updates.html:
"How hard could it be to make your own? ...It comes pre-segmented, pre-made from some of the hardiest organic material known to mortal-kind. Perhaps there is a way, a method, to turn this... thing into something that lives up to the legend."

Since we launched RuneScape: Dragonwilds into Early Access, we've been home to an iconic weapon. A tool of death, with a huge legacy. From its introduction in 2005, to the Falador Massacre, to today, the Abyssal Whip has always been a goal for players looking for a mid-game weapon to increase their damage potential.

When we initially launched out of Alpha testing, the Abyssal Whip was our first blush at making an iconic piece of RuneScape gear. It, and the Granite Maul, were ways for us to show our potential when it came to bringing those iconic weapons to life in a new way. Until now, it has been available after confronting the Abyssal Demons in the Swamps around Ghornfell and sourcing the recipe from a Dragonkin Vault. That meant that players in Dragonwilds could get their hands on an iconic "power weapon" very early in the game - and you told us clearly, that it felt like it was too early in the game to wield such power. We agree.

With the 1.0 release of RuneScape: Dragonwilds, the Abyssal Whip will be a Tier 7 Power Weapon.

To better live up to the Abyssal Whip's legacy and expectations, the journey to create the Abyssal Whip will now ask far more of you.

At the same time, we faced an issue - Abyssal Demons now lacked a chase reward, and we wanted to avoid giving you the Abyssal Spine as a component for a recipe you wouldn’t be able to use for dozens upon dozens of hours of playtime between the Ghornfell Swamps and Umbral Sands. So the Abyssal Demons are getting a change:

Abyssal Demons will now drop a new Whip Vestige Weapon called the Abysmal Whip.

They will also still drop the Abyssal Spine as they did previously. The Abysmal Whip is Power Level 4 - and does not have the special attack. It still applies a buildup of Bleed Damage, however. You can upgrade this Abysmal Whip with Ascension Cores, should you choose - but there is another way.

The Abysmal Whip will replace all existing versions of the Abyssal Whip you currently own in the live game, and this Whip will be an ingredient you use later on.

As an aside, Abyssal Demons will also drop Tier 4 Upgrade Shards to help you bring other pieces of equipment up in power should you so choose.

The Abyssal Whip, the real deal, will now need to be discovered as a recipe in Umbral Sands, in the shadow of the Burning Spire. Successfully sourcing this recipe will unlock the true, Masterwork Abyssal Whip. Complete with Special Attack, full damage and all of the existing effects that the Abyssal Whip offers - only more so.

TL;DR:

  • Abyssal Whip is moving from PL4 -> PL7 to better match its legacy and player expectations.
  • The Abysmal Whip will now replace any existing Abyssal Whips you own in-game, and the recipe reward is earned by killing Abyssal Demons.
  • Abyssal Demons now drop Tier 4 Upgrade Shards as an additional reward.
  • The Masterwork Whip recipe is situated in the Umbral Sands.
  • The Abysmal Whip is a required ingredient to upgrade the Masterwork Abyssal Whip. You must awaken the dark power of this tool of death.

We're excited to share more about the 1.0 release very soon, and we hope you're excited by experiencing the complete Kuldra's Saga from start to finish with all of the changes coming alongside the Raid.

updates.title: Kuldra's Saga - The Roadmap Update
updates.html:
It's been a while since we talked in detail about our roadmap, and we're checking in with you about our journey ahead!

Hello Adventurers - it's been a while since we talked in detail about our roadmap, and we're eager to check in with you about our progress so far, our journey ahead and changes we're making to deliver the best possible experience every step of the way. So, let's talk Roadmap!

The Headlines

  • Umbral Sands will be launching in late June.
  • Our Minor Updates will continue to deliver more quests, rewards and content every month.
  • We're bringing the Agility Skill forward to release in July.
  • The Prayer Skill is moving to our Winter Update.
  • The Scorned Wilderness will be launching in September, on more platforms.
  • In December, we'll be delivering Prayer alongside the next update we're currently developing - currently under the name "Luminance". Oooh.

Now, let's deep dive into everything coming in more detail.

What's Coming

Umbral Sands

This Major Update brings Ashenfall's largest region to date, alongside everything you've come to expect from these kinds of updates. We'll be adding an additional tier of material progression, including Adamant Armour, Infinity Robes and Red Dragonhide. Complete quests to help Icthlarin root out the cause of the chaos that has corrupted the sands of this region. Cross the sands on a Magic Carpet, and introduce the chitinous carapace of the Kalphites to cold steel- I mean, Adamantite. We'll also be introducing a new in-game challenge called the Nightmare Crucible. A heightened challenge that pits you against the toughest enemies Ashenfall has... so far.

Want to prove your mettle even more? The Fire Caves are a wave based combat challenge that pits you against the might of the desert, culminating in a showdown with the tempestuous and incendiary Fuzan. And yes, there's a cape.

Agility

We're pulling forward Agility as a skill for a range of reasons. Firstly, we've heard so much feedback about the jumping feeling... off. With that in mind, the team has been working on ways to improve the experience including vertical jump height, in-air control and feel. We're currently tinkering with ways to make this feel better, and we don't want to wait to fix this. Bundling in this change with a broader reassessment on how we look at Agility feels like a natural fit.

Our aim with agility is to deliver on your expectations of a skill - Abilities, Skill Spells, Stat Upgrades and bonus unlocks that change how you engage with the world around you. When you think Agility, most of you would be right to think "laps". Our aim is to build on that idea of practicing courses to create traversal challenges - paths marked along a space that challenge your movement abilities to reward you with XP, asking you to do more with an expanding toolset of agility spells and ability upgrades as you progress further into the world.

We know that Agility Shortcuts have been a part of RuneScape from its conception, but we're focused on the core skill system and what it can offer you beyond just the occasional shortcut at this stage. All of this should come together to open up new opportunities, new movement tech, and new rewards for you to earn.

Prayer

Prayer is going to be a Combat and Support Skill that allows you to unlock powerful passive effects, boosting combat capabilities, restoring health, improving resource gathering efficiency- and yes: protecting against specific damage types. Bury bones, build an Altar within your base, unlock your first prayer slot and start toggling on your chosen prayer. Running low on prayer points? Refill your prayer points at Altars in the world, or at home... but be on your guard, as some enemies will sap prayer points on-hit. Expect skill spells, buffs, passive unlocks, stat upgrades and extra unlocks along the way, drawing on the rich RuneScape history for some inspiration.

Scorned Wilderness

Work is really moving along with Scorned Wilderness, and we're excited to be delivering the climactic confrontation of Kuldra's Saga. This includes the Runite Tier, as well as filling out the Skill Tracks for existing skills to 99 with more features. We're also working alongside its development to bring the experience to more platforms. We have mentioned this a few times since we launched into early access, but as we approach this release, we'll share more information, so stay tuned.

Minor Updates

In August, we are electing to not release a minor update to do our due diligence on refining the experience for the Scorned Wilderness release, as well as support for more platforms. We want this release to be the absolute best update yet, and we're taking the additional time to make sure that this release feels as big and smooth as our scaly God-Eater herself. The entire team are piling on to this update to deliver something we're really proud of. This means that August will not have a minor update, but once Scorned Wilderness releases, we're back to our monthly cadence, so look forward to those!

Winter Update

Our next major update after Scorned Wilderness is being designed out already, and we're excited to see what it's bringing alongside Prayer. For now, we're focused on Kuldra's Saga, but rest assured - there is more RuneScape: Dragonwilds on the way. Like the other major updates, this will be a free update for all players with a bunch of cool content to get involved with. We'll share more about it in detail at RuneFest, so be sure to tune in to the livestream or be there on the day to find out more.

(Still thinking of coming to RuneFest? Tickets are on sale now, and there's still some spaces available!)

As we continue to work on developing RuneScape: Dragonwilds, we're continually reminded how lucky we are to have such an amazing community around us. Feedback is coming through to us every day across Steam, our socials, our Discord and our Reddit. We're thrilled to continue to work on this project and share our working with so many of you. Thank you, as always.

updates.title: Dragonwilds 2026 Summit Wrap-up
updates.html:
Overslept? Just want to see it all again? Whatever your reason, here's a recap of the RuneScape: Dragonwilds Summit.

2026 is shaping up to be a monumental year for us on RuneScape: Dragonwilds. From our initial launch, we've been floored by the support and enthusiasm we've seen. Bringing something new (and, more frighteningly, DIFFERENT) to the world of RuneScape was always going to be a challenge and our modest team has been continually thrilled, motivated and humbled by the support, passion and creativity we've seen. We've continued to iterate from our release into Early Access (what we referred to as our 0.7 build) and since then we've released three updates to bring us to 0.10, with the release of Fellhollow. If you've not played Fellhollow yet, I would encourage you to stop reading at once and go get involved, it's really rather good if we can say so ourselves.

Beyond The Grave

But, since Fellhollow launched, we've not been bankstanding. We're focused on delivering our promise of small but still impactful updates. These "Minor" updates (using Steam's naming conventions, here) deliver more quests, more rewards and new activities for you to discover and complete. If you're waiting between Major Updates to jump into game, you'll have hours of content waiting for you if you need to grind your way up to the next Dragon General and progress forward. These include new quests and activities that will take you across Ashenfall, reward the curious and test the brave. If you're revisiting between updates, you'll be able to snag rewards like new gear, capes and decorations to celebrate your progress. I wish I got a cape to celebrate my progress.

We aim to deliver these Minor Updates month on month, with the Quest and Activities Team building out more for you to get stuck into while other parts of the Dragonwilds team are building out our next expansion. These may vary in size or content, but the intent is to ensure that we're growing the world and expanding our wealth of content month after month, while you gear up for the next fight. Speaking of which...

Dowdun Reach

Once Imaru has been toppled, your focus will turn towards the ominous gatehouse that lurks in the far corner of Fellhollow.

A vast, interconnected fortress awaits. Once a stronghold of Zamorakian worship, this imposing keep has collapsed into a frenzy of ruin and madness. Truly, Chaos reigns. From community feedback, we know that you've been excited to see more interiors, explore more buildings and battle your way through a more densely packed area with hidden paths, secrets and side quests. Good news - Dowdun Reach has you covered. You'll plunge into the heart of a keep fraught with danger, mystery and magic. Oh joy.

Black Knights walk these halls, and they hold the line against their once-trusted allies - Zamorakian Mages. As paranoia and fear eroded the shared bond of this place, and the shadows lengthened, the Keep is now fragmented. Splinter groups of each order hold their ground with cruel ferocity, and they certainly won't like someone just walking in and nosing around. Drawing on the rich history of Zamorakian lore in Gielinor, Dowdun Reach is bringing a new challenge to our adventurers to see if they're truly ready for what lies ahead. We'll be sharing more about the kinds of rewards and gear you'll uncover throughout March, on the Road to Dowdun.

As part of Dowdun Reach, we'll be actioning a long-requested community feature. We'll be raising the level cap of all skills to 99 - even though the skills aren't finished yet. We've heard from you about wanting to grind out levels and not waste XP, even with the content still due to be added as we continue to grow and develop Ashenfall. With that in mind, we'll be raising the level cap and then continually backfilling content into these skills. If you've already reached the required levels, these will automatically unlock as we add the content in. Enjoy not worrying about XP waste! And, yes, of course - you'll be able to claim a Skill Cape when you get that final ding!

That's not all - we're also refactoring Runecrafting to be more of an activity. We've all spent plenty of time in the Rune essence mines or the Runespan or generally farming Rune Essence and filling chest after chest with delicious, moreish runes. Between you and me, I reckon they've got the texture of shortbread. We're creating a more dynamic experience where your inputs and actions affect your yield. Beyond that we've added Anima Vents. These are attuned to particular elemental types of the Anima that surges forth from the heart of Ashenfall, and you'll be able to use these to your advantage, hone your skills and produce a wealth of runes as a result.

Umbral Sands

Coming this summer, our next Major Update brings you to the Umbral Sands. In the sand oceans beyond Dowdun Reach, the Red Dragon reigns supreme.

From the very beginning, Gielinor has had its fair share of desert regions and we want to honour the heritage of these wonderful regions of RuneScape. We're drawing heavily from the rich history of Kharid-Et, Menaphos, and Sophanem to create a ruined landscape that feels innately RuneScapey, while offering you something different.

In the daytime, the sun itself is the greatest threat. It's corrupted rays drain life with every moment of exposure. Only shade or night offer safety. Build shelter, move carefully, and plan your steps carefully under the burning sky - but beware... Fuzan, the fiery Red Dragon rules with tempestuous, incandescent fury. The winged monstrosity that rules the night isn't the only thing you need to worry about, though.

These once thriving lands now shiver with the chittering whispers of Kalphites - great chitinous insects that burrow within the sands of Ashenfall, and emerge to pluck unsuspecting victims from the surface. RuneScape players will know Kalphites well, but for those of you new to all this - they're mean, green, biting machines. Fighting through the life-sapping sun and overcoming the Kalphite brood will bring you to Fuzan's Tower, rising from the heart of a volcano. A dark spire encircled by rivers of magma and obsidian, and at the base, a cavern, rife with Kot-Haar. Golem-like creatures of living stone, wrought into existence by an Elder God's magic.

There are also a handful of NPCs that will offer some respite from the isolation of the dunes. A sect of Garou, weathered against the inclement and Anima-infused weather have driven into the Sands and have forged a life in the desert. Earn the trust of these hardened nomadic travellers who have endured, take on quests and arm yourself for battle, or... just mine Adamant Ore and gather Yew Wood and arm yourself.

There are whispers of a place lurking within the Umbral Sands, twisted by the sinister corruption of the sun, where evil lurks in innumerable droves and great warriors have fallen in battle. Those seeking the glory of combat call it... The Nightmare Crucible. More on that later this year.

Scorned Wilderness

The end of Kuldra's Saga is coming - but we're still very early in developing our ideas here. We want this to represent a cataclysmic site of ancient power, where Anima has ravaged the landscape and uprooted the very elements from the earth. What form that takes, and how it challenges you, is something we're developing, testing and exploring as you read this very blog. What we can tell you is this: Kuldra must die.

Face off against the God-Eater and bring down their tyrannical reign as you muster your allies, drive into the wilderness to acquire Rune Armour and delve into the heart of the Anima storm. We're very excited to bring players along for the ride with how we round out Kuldra's Saga, and we'll be sharing more as we get a clearer vision of what this looks like.

Beyond The Spire

We've set ourselves a challenge with this year's roadmap. It's ambitious, exciting and the kind of roadmap we can be really proud of. We have a vision for what we want RuneScape: Dragonwilds to become and it's been informed and guided by your feedback, discussions and suggestions. What comes after is the next chapter of Dragonwilds, and we can't wait to share more with you at RuneFest. For your feedback, support and being part of this community - thank you so much.

updates.title: Combat Reworks - Stamina, Parrying, Dodging and Animation Cancels - 0.12.1 Sneak Peek!
updates.html:
Combat Reworks - Stamina, Parrying, Dodging and Animation Changes | 0.12.1 Sneak Peek!

Wands, Parrying, Specs, Swaps, Animation Cancels - Here's a look at what's coming in our next few updates.

We're making combat less clunky - here's a look at what's coming in our next few updates.

For a long time, we've been listening to feedback around combat - your steam reviews, your comments on Reddit and Discord, and replies on our socials, everywhere! We went back and forth, chatting to hundreds of you, combing through thousands of survey responses, and gathering info. One word kept coming up - clunky! Clunky clunky clunky.

We've boiled it down to some core principles. Here's what we want to address:

  • Blocking doesn't clearly or consistently reduce damage as expected.
  • Stamina management is a challenge.
  • You want to quick-switch and quick-cast more fluidly.
  • Switching ammo types in combat is punishing.
  • Weapon Specs should feel stronger, and more impactful to use.
  • You can't move while casting skill spells.
  • You want to really punish enemies for parrying them.
  • Fall damage hurts.

Right - let's fix that. Enter: The Core Improvements Team.

In our July update, 0.12.1, we'll be deploying the following changes. There's plenty of content, and the Agility skill, too. We won't get into those yet, we want to focus on Combat today.

  • With the introduction of the Mystic Forge in 0.12, we're adding the functionality to Upgrade Masterworks and Weapons to higher tiers using "Upgrade Cores".
  • Swapping to a 2H weapon and then back to a 1H weapon will automatically re-equip your off-hand item too.
  • We're adding a radial hotwheel for both Controller and Keyboard + Mouse users to speed up selecting primary items, as well as adding the quick cast shortcut for either a spell OR an item.
  • We've had a few reports of players losing the ability to Jump, either due to action inputs going missing, or poor network performance. We've ironed out some creases to make jumping even nicer, as well as the improvements to air control and vertical height already live with 0.12.0.
  • You'll be able to cycle through your runes/arrows in mid combat to save you having to open your inventory.
  • Jumping will cost 10 stamina, down from 20 - reducing further when Agility levels are reached.
  • Fall damage has been rebalanced to start later. As part of the Agility Skill launching with this update, you'll have access to perks that make this even more lenient, as well as a breakfall mechanic that will allow you to absorb damage from higher falls.
    • Leggings of Lightness, Mounts and Windstep should each be unaffected by this, so your general won't change!
  • We're making good progress on improving performance, additional ambient VFX and tons of optimisation for Fog, trees, grass and even the coastline. All of that is intended to make the experience more stable/smooth for you to focus on what you do best. Smacking the living daylights out of goblins.
  • We're also adding more to the existing jump to improve its "ledge forgiveness" - as in, if you walk off a ledge, there's a small window of time for you to jump before you cartoonishly plummet to your demise. There's more to come with agility, but we'll speak to that separately.

But that's not all! With 1.0's release, we're also adding even more:

  • Camera-relative aiming will become the default controller input.
    • Where your camera is looking will be where your attacks and spells will go.
    • This is currently set to where your character is facing, but is a toggle. We're flipping the default, but anyone who has selected an option will keep their preference.
  • Damage Telegraph Time
    • Improvements to responsiveness when telegraphing attacks between server and client.
    • Reducing the number of "phantom hits" you get from just-killed enemies, and making your damage output much more in line with what's on screen.
  • We're reducing the Block animation and starting the block window earlier, which means you'll be able to block more often, and more effectively.
    • We're also improving the UI to show the damage mitigated.
  • We've heard your feedback around casting and switching spells mid-fight. Starting with 0.12.1, you'll be able to WALK (not run) during Tempest Shield, Surge, Enchant Weapons and Spectral Arrow skill spell casts.
  • You'll be able to highlight a Skill Spell as your "Quick Cast" - like quick prayers in Old School and RuneScape!
    • This will also give you a little bit of protection while you cast to stop you getting interrupted while you cast this particular spell.
  • We're adding extra refinement to camera shake (optional toggle) and feedback on hits.
  • Players will be able to attack while sprinting as a combo opener.
  • Parrying successfully will grant you 50% of your max stamina back.
  • Parrying successfully with allow you to land a single, cinematic Visceral Attack, with a camera adjustment so you can savour the satisfying hit.
  • Stamina costs across weapon types will be rebalanced, as well as shield stamina costs.
  • You'll be able to animation cancel from combat actions.
  • You'll be able to animation cancel Skill Spells by blocking or dodging.
  • You'll be able to animation cancel Magic Attacks by blocking or dodging.
  • Increased duration of Enchant Weapon and Spectral Arrows
  • Reduced Cooldown for Tempest Shield and Snare
  • Early-exit cancels for bow and spell attacks.
  • Dire Wolf attacks shortened so they can't hit you while fully sprinting away from them.
  • We're adding 9 enemy variations to Brynmoor, Ghornfell, Fellhollow and Dowdun Reach, with new attacks that will apply debuff effects - poison, shock, wither rot, etc.

Mum Was Right, I Am Special

The Old School RuneScape classic, the Special Attack bar, is also coming to Dragonwilds.

Players familiar with RuneScape will be familiar with how this will work already, but as of 1.0, Special Attacks will consume a portion of the player's special attack bar. This allows us to strengthen some of these attacks and reduce their stamina costs so that they can be more powerful now that we can limit the frequency of these attacks. Your special attack bar will slowly recharge over time meaning players will want to ensure they time their attacks well to get the most out of their limited special attack potential! You will be able to use them less often, but they will feel more powerful with each use. Things like the Titan's Wrath and the Greatsword Special will hit harder, and be more of an active ability choice.

They'll feel less like "another move", and more like a conscious decision to use a Special Ability.

One Hit Wand-er

For 1.0, we're also adding a new magic weapon type... Wands!

Wands are a more mobile, fast-paced way to deal more damage at a comparatively lower damage output. These will still apply buildup of knockdowns, burns and slows that you expect from Air, Fire and Water magic. You'll be able to use wands to move more fluidly in combat and get around, but also hang back with a Staff and lay down more damage if you want!

All of this is in service of making a combat experience that feels truly brilliant, and has been designed around your feedback from the outset. We're so excited to share more with you soon - for now, we hope this is a reassurance that Combat is getting more improvements, and we hope you're excited to get your hands on it soon.

updates.title: Eye on Ashenfall - 0.12.1
updates.html:
Hello Adventurers! Dragonwilds' latest update before the Scorned Wilderness Raid arrives is coming to Steam Early Access soon! Let's get an early look at what it'll contain:

Agility

With the 0.12.1 release, we're delighted to be introducing a long-overdue addition to RuneScape: Dragonwilds - Agility! Our latest skill will allow you to build up your stamina and sculpt yourself into a speed machine. Across Ashenfall, you'll find SIX new stations with flags for you to interact with. There, you'll find a leaderboard of times, and a trail of orbs to gather along a fixed course. From there, you'll be able to continually repeat the courses over and over, improving your time, getting XP with every lap.

You'll earn rewards for completing Agility courses, and mastery of the courses will net you Gold Medals. You can throw those on your walls, like Pristine Fish from Fishing, as trophies to show everyone who's the boss of the course. Mastering the region's agility course will also grant you a gilded trimmed version of the regional cape as an extra reward.

Firstly, let's talk about passives:

You'll be able to gain XP passively while running across the world, too - but you won't get XP on mounts. Stop cheating and get those knees up! As you level up through the Agility Skill tree, you will passively consume less Stamina while you sprint.

At levels 50 and 75, you'll also unlock passive increases to your maximum carry weight.

You'll also be able to use Agility Shortcuts to make use of Kebbit Burrows situated across the world. They'll be dotted on your map, and you can dig them up to open up tunnels to cut across side routes in the world. In early Agility levels, you might take damage when failing to squeeze through unharmed, so be careful using the shortcuts on low HP.

At higher levels, you'll start to break your falls from higher up by rolling out of them to avoid taking as much damage. Fatal falls will still kill you though.

The skill tree also, of course, comes with its own Skill Spells and unlocks.

Windstep is now an Agility skill spell, rather than a Runecrafting skill spell.

At higher levels, Windstep will also cause you to send out a blast of air when you land, sending enemies to the floor.

So, you can run further, carry more and scoot across the world in shortcuts. But that's being fast - not agile.

How about... an aerial dash? A short, horizontal dash to cross small gaps and add extra evasive manoeuvres during combat?

Sounds good. What if we gave you... a second jump? You'll be able to jump, jump again in mid-air and then dash horizontally to get over and around enemies. Pretty cool, right?

You'll also be able to use a new skill spell - Recall.

Leave a runic marker on the ground, and then recast to teleport back to the initial marking spot - great for quickly grabbing something urgently and getting out of danger. If you fall to your death while tethered, you'll also teleport back, and the tether will be consumed.

All of this is built to make you faster, leaner and meaner - and we'll be factoring it in moving forwards in how we design exploration, puzzles and more. So don't start thinking you'll be able to make an Agility Pure account - it's time to do some cardio.

The Great Body Robbery

Our longest Secondary Quest to date can be found in Bloodblight Swamp - an unfortunate experiment has rendered the Good* Doctor* Fenkenstrain in a bit of a pickle. You'll need to help him out. Your rewards are a new club weapon that's shockingly good, and a buildable decoration: the Pylon. This functional decoration will generate an area of effect in a radius around it that intercepts lightning strikes to allow you to build in places known for... inclement weather.

We're adding a radial hotwheel for both Controller and Keyboard + Mouse users to speed up selecting primary items, as well as adding the quick cast shortcut for either a spell OR an item.

Swapping to a 2H weapon and then back to a 1H weapon will automatically re-equip your off-hand item too.

Stability changes are coming to make jumping more consistent in suboptimal networking conditions that led to losing the ability to jump in some circumstances.

You'll be able to cycle through your runes/arrows in mid combat to save you having to open your inventory.

Jumping will cost 10 stamina, down from 20 - reducing further when Agility levels are reached.

Leggings of Lightness, Mounts and Windstep should each be unaffected by this, so your general mobility won't change!

We're making good progress on improving performance, additional ambient VFX and tons of optimisation for Fog, trees, grass and even the coastline. All of that is intended to make the experience more stable/smooth for you to focus on what you do best. Smacking the living daylights out of goblins.

We're also adding more to the existing jump to improve its "ledge forgiveness" - as in, if you walk off a ledge, there's a small window of time for you to jump before you cartoonishly plummet to your demise.

Combat and Movement Improvements

  • We're adding a radial hotwheel for both Controller and Keyboard + Mouse users to speed up selecting primary items, as well as adding the quick cast shortcut for either a spell OR an item.
  • Swapping to a 2H weapon and then back to a 1H weapon will automatically re-equip your off-hand item too.
  • Stability changes are coming to make jumping more consistent in suboptimal networking conditions that led to losing the ability to jump in some circumstances.
  • You'll be able to cycle through your runes/arrows in mid combat to save you having to open your inventory.
  • Jumping will cost 10 stamina, down from 20 - reducing further when Agility levels are reached.
    • Leggings of Lightness, Mounts and Windstep should each be unaffected by this, so your general mobility won't change!
  • We're making good progress on improving performance, additional ambient VFX and tons of optimisation for Fog, trees, grass and even the coastline. All of that is intended to make the experience more stable/smooth for you to focus on what you do best. Smacking the living daylights out of goblins.
  • We're also adding more to the existing jump to improve its "ledge forgiveness" - as in, if you walk off a ledge, there's a small window of time for you to jump before you cartoonishly plummet to your demise.

Visual Fidelity

We've done a bit of a pass over the starting areas (Brynmoor and Ghornfell) with an emphasis on visual improvements, performance and clarity. We've improved how trees will look nicer at a distance, the visual clarity of moss and fog, our existing grass and foliage to include more flowers, and we've improved performance at lower ends of the settings.

We've revisited night sky visuals, volumetric fog across the world, storm weather visuals and we've also added additional ambient VFX across the region and along the coastline.

Bug Fixes

The 0.12.1 update will contain the following fixes:

  • We're resolving an issue where Axes were dealing incorrect damage to trees.
    • We misplaced a decimal. Oops!
    • We'll be reverting this to its intended value with 0.12.1, alongside several other bugfixes to woodcutting, including Splinter and Axetral Projection removing stumps.
    • This was giving people disproportionate XP based on the damage dealt - we're putting values back to where they should be!
  • Fixed an issue where Axtral Projection upgrades would not chop down all intended/highlighted trees.
  • Fixed an issue where Splinter would destroy tree stumps if used on an adjacent log.
  • Fixed an issue where the Yew Farming Plots did not snap in building modes correctly.
  • Fixed an issue where Rune Vents would appear full for clients in multiplayer worlds even when depleted.
  • Fixed an issue introduced in Umbral Sands where game music would loop repeatedly, primarily triggered upon respawning.
  • Fixed an bug where summoning Buddy in a wall would cause the game to crash.
    • Get it? Bug? Becau- oh, forget it.
  • Resolved an issue where a part of the Burning Spire zone where the player could fall through Lava.
  • Fixed an issue where returning to the main menu after dying would respawn the player back at the location of death.
  • Fixed an issue where Potion Effects would be removed between game sessions/on logout.
  • Fixed an issue where Lodestone teleports placed on the edges of the map could only be used one-way as they would fail to be displayed on the map.
  • Fixed an issue where the search area on the map for the "Saga of the Adventurer" Quest Step was incorrectly aligned.
  • Fixed an issue where Wild Jade Vines would die to poison in the Toxic Swamp.
  • Resolved an issue where Ascension Cores weren't displayed correctly in the Mystic Forge of the crafting menu.
  • Fixed an issue with the TokTz-Mej-Tal staff would not consume runes on attack.
  • Fixed an issue with some items would display a white square placeholder depiction.
  • Resolved an issue where the Right Stick on controllers would not turn the camera within a 30% radius in some contexts.
  • Fixed an issue where some shaded areas would let Scorch stack up to 500% without triggering.
    • That's probably going to leave a mark.
  • Tweaked the lighting in the Velgar Arena to improve visibility when fighting him at night.
  • Fixed an issue where the Spellwheel would not show descriptions for spells as a client in Multiplayer worlds.
  • Fixed an issue where the Fire Cape would refill Stamina even if the enemy was not afflicted with burns.
  • Fixed an issue where the Kharidian Inner Corner 45° Stairs would be unclimbable.
  • Fixed an issue where players could walk under a specific Sand Dune.
  • Fixed an issue where an Air Anima vent was situated inside a pillar within the Umbral Sands.
  • Fixed an issue where the Chamber barrier in the Contact! quest would be invisible at very low, low and medium graphics settings.
  • Fixed an issue with the Special Attack of Hammer weapons which could stunlock Lesser Dragons.
  • Fixed an issue where the "Shrimp Catcher" quest completion would not contribute to the Achievement "Brynmoor Helper".
  • Fixed an issue where the Kalphite Queen would respawn in an invisible state after being defeated.
  • Fixed an issue where the Kalphite Queen's Sting Attack would become angulated.
  • Fixed an issue where the dunes behind the Kalphite Queen Vault had missing collision.
  • Fixed an issue where the ground atop the Cave of Screams was missing collission.
  • Fixed an issue where there was a small invisible barrier blocking pathing in the Dunes of Uzzer when moving on foot.
  • Fixed an issue where Quicksand and its VFX were showing in areas that weren't actually quicksand.
  • Fixed an issue where a Sanguine Urn icon was incorrectly placed in the Bloodblight Swamp.
  • Fixed an issue where users could get stuck in a small spot in the Burning Spire.
  • Fixed an issue where Desert Weed did not have any healthy growth stage assets when planted. It looks as healthy as it is, now!
  • Fixed an issue where part of a rock surface in the Burning Spire would behave like lava and damage the player when walking on it.
  • Fixed an issue where the Menaphite Desert Cape was missing a Journal Entry.
  • Fixed an issue where the Rapid Growth Skill Spell had a placeholder icon in the Spellbook
  • Fixed an issue where collision remained on the Zi Core quest item after it had been collected.
  • Fixed an issue where Korean Subtitles were not showing correctly during the opening cutscene.
  • Fixed an issue where the Skills Necklace has an unclear description in the interface.
  • Fixed an issue where Localised text for the Construction Skill bonuses was not displayed correctly.
  • Fixed an issue where completing a quest for Lagra, Alcarrid's Butcher would not yield rewards if the player's inventory was full.
  • Fixed an issue with the Yew Shortbow when fully drawn back causing visual clutter.
  • Fixed an issue where the Fishing Minigame could not have the keybinds rebound.
  • Fixed an issue where Bones to Peaches would not mention the stack limit is limited to 10.
  • Fixed an issue where the Blue Dragon was incorrectly labelled as "Lesser Blue Dragon" instead.
  • Fixed an issue where Stamina would instantly regenerate after jumping when wearing the full set of Wizard Robes.
  • Fixed an issue with a typo in the Hall of Heroes Journal Entry.
  • Fixed an issue where Miniaturized Mushrooms in the Dunes of Uzzer could not be gathered.
  • Fixed an issue where Torches in the doorways in Umbral Sands were unnaturally bright.
  • Fixed an issue where attempting to cast Fishnado on a Net Fishing Spot would show an incorrect error message: "Your fish has escaped!"
  • Fixed an issue where Green Dragons' flame attack VFX were not aligned to their mouths properly.

updates.title: Eye on Ashenfall - 0.12.0
updates.html:
Umbral Sands arrives tomorrow! Brace yourself to battle your way to Fuzan under the cursed sun.

Hello Adventurers! We're back with yet another Major Update - tomorrow, we release the Umbral Sands!

We're also on sale from NOW until June 25th, at 30% off!

Explore an entire new region, inspired by the iconic deserts of mainland Gielinor, and battle across the desert with its dynamic weather systems, seeking shelter, shade and shadow to progress! Battle your way through the Fight Cave to earn the right to challenge Fuzan, and return to the Fight Cave to repeat the challenge for more rewards including rare materials and rewards. Yew, Adamant and Red Dragonhide crafting materials are available, allowing you to craft an additional tier of gear, alongside powerful Vestiges for each combat style.

There's going to be new bosses for you to take on including Fuzan, the new Dragon General, but Fuzan is not alone. Amongst other named bosses, you'll also be able to find keys to access the Nightmare Crucible, a challenging arena that throws the worst of Ashenfall at you.

Form a fragile alliance with the scattered tribes of the Moon Garou, aided by the Jackal-headed God of the Underworld, Icthlarin! Complete quests for the Garou to earn access to new resources, rewards and cosmetics.

Steam Achievements are here! At last, you get another bar to fill and another number to go up.

Woodcutting and Mining Skill Trees will be filled out to 99 with new spells, recipes, perks and rewards!

We've got tons of new music, ambience and soundscapes for your listening pleasure, so don't touch that dial now, we're just getting started.

Let's dive into what's coming in - spoilers ahead, so tread carefully.

New Features

The Umbral Sands region has been added. Fell the Black Knight Titan to pass beyond the gates and enter the Umbral Sands...

3 new vaults have been added in the Umbral Sands region.

Environmental hazards have been added:

  • Sunscorch: Prolonged exposure to the sun will wither you away. The Scorch debuff, once applied, causes hydration to deplete rapidly. Build shelter, stick to shade, or adventure in the dawn and dusk to avoid the worst of the Sun's fiery wrath.
  • Quicksand: Areas of treacherous sand will subsume any poor adventurer who missteps when exploring. You'll need to find a way over these spots.

The Fight Cave has been added. At the end of the questline, you will be able to take on the Fight Cave to challenge Fuzan. Earn your reward and bring down the last obstacle between you and the Dragon Queen, Kuldra.

New Items

Adamant Ore has been added, and with it, new items.

  • 4 New Tools:
    • Spade
    • Watering Can
    • Pickaxe
    • Logging Axe
  • 8 New Weapons:
    • Crossbow
    • Dagger
    • Greataxe
    • Greatsword
    • Hammer
    • Mace
    • Sword
  • 1 New Armour Set
  • 1 New Shield
  • Adamant Ammunition for ranged weapons.

    Yew Wood can be found across the Umbral Sands:

  • Added the Yew Fishing Rod
  • Added 3 New Weapons
    • Yew Shortbow
    • Yew Longbow
    • Yew Stock for Crossbow

      Infinity Cloth can be spun:

  • Added Infinity Robes

    Red Dragonhide can be tanned and crafted with:

  • Added Red Dragonhide armour.

4 Vestige Armour Sets have been added to the game: Magic:

  • Lunar Garou
  • Desert Robes

    Ranged:

  • Kalphite Carapace

    Melee:

  • Obsidian

New Buildings

We talked about this in a newspost recently in more detail! Your crafting stations will be deleted on login and you will need to replace them - your components will be refunded.

  • Blacksmith's Bench - Tools and Melee Weapons
  • Fletching Bench - All Ranged Weaponry
  • Mystic Forge - Magic weapons and Vestiges
  • Armour Bench - All armour sets
  • Ore & Stone Storage - Unlocked at Mining Level 59
  • Lumber Storage - Unlocked at Woodcutting Level 59

    Additional Kharidian Building Pieces have been added.

New Enemies

Added the following Bosses and Mini-bosses:

  • Fuzan
  • Tok-Xil
  • Red Dragon
  • The Kalphite Queen

    Added the following enemies:

Kalphites:

  • Kalphite Worker
  • Kalphite Solider
  • Kalphite Guardian

KotHaar:

  • KotHaar-Xil
  • KotHaar-Kal
  • KotHaar-Ket

Wildlife:

  • Desert Kebbit
  • Goat
  • Vulture

Steam Achievements

There's a heap of new achievements being added! We're not spoiling the list for you, but there's more to come with later updates. For now, enjoy the 43 (fourty-three!) achievements to dig into. Good luck, adventurers.

New Skill Progression for Mining and Woodcutting

Mining has been populated from levels 50-99.

  • New Spell 51- Divine Rock : Turn 5 ore on the ground into a personal mining vein for your continued use.
  • Recipe 59 - Ore & Stone Storage: Unlocks Ore & Stone Storage building piece for you to stash your goodies.
  • Perk 69 - Ultimate Burst: Increased Rocksplosion area of effect. Nice.
  • Perk 71- Accelerated Veins: Chance for Divine Rock (Level 51) to drop gemstones.
  • Perk 74 - Ingot Weight Reduction: Reduces the weight of ingots by 50%

    Woodcutting has been populated from levels 50-99.

  • New Spell 52 - Trunk Totem: Transmute scattered trees into a single totem.
  • Recipe 59 - Lumber Storage: New buildable piece with high storage capacity for logs & planks.
  • Perk 67 - Wood Weight Reduction: Reduce the carry weight of wood by 50%.
  • Recipe 78 - Lumber Backpack: Increases woodcutting XP, increases rare drop chances and reduces wood weight when worn. You guys wanted a backpack, right?
  • Perk 88 - Axtral Projection Upgrade: Upgrades to 3 spectral axes for bigger Area of Effect. Chop chop!

The Nightmare Crucible

Chills. Anyway, find Engrams around the Umbral Sands to gain access to the Nightmare Crucible, an ancient Dragonkin experiment pitting you against the biggest and baddest monsters Ashenfall can throw at you. This challenge, boss-rush style mode will pit you against enemies and reward you with rare rewards - Ascension Cores, which will be used for powerful upgrades ahead of the Scorned Wilderness' release.

New Mount

  • Players will be able to earn the Magic Carpet mount through Moon Garou quests.
  • Added customised variations for both the Terrorbird and the Magic Carpet.
    • You will need to complete The Wild Hunt quest in Fellhollow to access the mount even if you unlock customisation options.

New UI

New UI menus for:

  • Character Screen
  • Skills Menu
  • Spell book
  • Mounts
  • Spell Wheel

Character Re-customisation

  • Players can now edit character customisation at character select - change your look to fit the mood!

Adjusted Jump

  • Players will now have more forward momentum at the start of the jump. You currently have less rotation in the air, but you have more control during the jump.
  • You should now be able to jump over walls and ledges you are against!

Additional Updates

We're also adding:

  • Advanced Tannery:
    • For making better leathers!
  • The Fermentation Barrel:
    • Allows you to upgrade Tier 3 Potions into more powerful Tier 4 potions.
  • We're adding traders across ALL of Ashenfall for you to trade with!
    • These will accept some of your materials and spare loot in exchange for stuff in their shops.

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed an issue where Terrorbirds would randomly dismount the player while moving.
  • All items that stack can now stack to 99.
  • Fixed a bug which caused the Emberwood Village barrier in Fellhollow to come back after being destroyed, and vault progress was being lost despite having been completed.
  • Resolved an issue where casting Humidify on Diseased Plants would automatically consume a Plant Cure if one was available in the player's inventory.
  • Fixed an issue where the Last Played tab in the Server Selection only showed servers joined by that character, rather than all previous server joins.
  • Fixed an issue where a post between Emberwood and Dragon's Run in Fellhollow had unexpected sunlight passing through the fog. Begone, light!
  • Resolved a bug where Rune Vents would not properly show the fact that they were depleted for clients in multiplayer worlds.
  • Fixed an issue where changes to in-game font sizes would not persist after closing the game.
  • Cape Hooks now correctly swap capes.
  • Resolved an issue where attempting to delete a character would end up deleting the first character from list in some instances.
  • Stones outside of the Saradomin Temple can be picked up again as intended. Woo! Free stones!
  • Titans Wrath can no longer be enchanted by swapping to it during casting.

Tomorrow with launch we'll be sharing a Known Issues live page that we'll be updating throughout the week with Vital Information of issues we're tracking!

You know the usual - follow our socials (Twitter, BSky, Instagram, Facebook, Twitch, YouTube and TikTok!) and get involved with Reddit and join the Discord. As always, we love seeing your comments and feedback, and we're very excited to see you in-game tomorrow.

Until then, be good, and we'll see you in Ashenfall!

updates.title: Health and Wardstones Rework - What's Changing
updates.html:
We're changing how Food and Drink work. Wardstones and Wardshield are being removed. Hello Adventurers - with the release of 0.12.0, we're changing how Food and Drink work. Here's what's changing:

  • Wardstones and Wardshield is being removed.
  • In their place, you will instead increase your total HP by finding Constitution shrines around the world.
  • Food will now instantly restore HP, as well as provide other perks.
  • Healing potions will be removed (stat pots are staying).

Let's get into why.

Wardshield

Damage will now go directly to your health. The core issue with Wardshield as a mechanic was that it placed too much weight on the armour you were wearing. As we added new content and higher level enemies, we reached a point where the Wardshield bar became the only viable source of survivability. Once it was gone, even a single hit from a stronger enemy could kill you outright. It offered an additional layer of protection that scales with your armour, making each material upgrade feel more powerful than the last, but you have to actively engage with that system to benefit from it, otherwise it's empty health that we're balancing around but not giving you outright.

We looked at two options - leaning into Wardshield, outscaling the base health bar and rendering HP largely irrelevant, or move towards a system where your single HP pool scales over time. We chose the latter, because it's easier to balance and tune around. Being able to steadily increase your health outside of armour means you have a clearer path to get stronger even when you're struggling.

This ALSO, as an important note, moves us closer to your expectations of what you'd get in RuneScape, where HP is just HP, and you grow that pool of HP as you progress. Speaking of health progression...

Max HP

Players (that's you!) will now be able to increase their maximum HP beyond 100. Your health will reflect your growth throughout your journey, getting stronger all the time - so how do you get more HP? Introducing... the Constitution Shrine. These shrines are situated across Ashenfall, by someone or something. These are rewards for exploring, and key progression milestones. If you're finding shrines, you're doing something right. Stack those shrines up and your journey to become a Dragon Slayer legend will be a lot easier.

I tick eat those

We're shifting the focus away from healing potions. They feel a lot less RuneScapey than the combination of "Stat Pots" and cooked food in your inventory, so we're turning our attention towards our latest skill - Fishing. Food will now serve as a key driver in healing a significant chunk of your HP, quickly. Fish, following RuneScape, will be best in class at healing - in terms of sheer HP Value - other foods types have buffs. This also has the desired outcome of making sure that fishing has a fundamental place in the core gameplay loop, like farming does, and makes satiety and thirst less of a "meter to fill" and more a system that should organically be topped up by your play. Please remember to drink water, adventurers, I can't stress it enough.

Your existing potions will still exist but will be disassembled on use, rather than consumed. You'll get your components back, and won't have to disassemble them one by one!

I don't know what's going on with adventurers on mainland Gielinor, but those folks can stomach a truly horrifying amount of Karambwan without taking a break. We've not got Karambwans on Ashenfall, but we are removing the existing animation that comes with consuming food, drinks and potions in-game, to remove the friction with currently trying to heal during combat. There will be a brief cooldown between consumptions to prevent you stuffing even the slightest of wounds with a whole meat pie (do not try this, please), but you will no longer be prevented from eating when you fill up your sustenance bar. Instead of healing at the end of an existing 2 second animation, you'll receive the healing immediately and then have a short cooldown before your next snack.

You will be able to continue eating and healing even if your sustenance is at 100.

We're exploring this change as a way to deepen our connection to our RuneScape roots, offer more player power through natural gameplay progression, and make Fishing an even more integral part of your experience. Balancing and values on this are not final so we're eager to take on feedback and make adjustments with future updates.

As always, we're all ears, so let us know thoughts and discuss more in our official Discord and Reddit. We've got support for French, German and LATAM Communities with dedicated spaces within our Discord, so come and say Hallo or Bonjour while you're at it.

Check out our Socials (Twitter, BSky, Instagram, Facebook, Twitch, YouTube and TikTok), too!

Looking for LATAM socials? We've got Instagram Español, Instagram Brasil, TikTok Español, TikTok Brasil, Facebook Español and Facebook Brasil!

updates.title: Dragonwilds' Price Isn't Changing
updates.html:
"We've been continually humbled by your support, and we've decided not to raise the price of RuneScape: Dragonwilds following our 1.0 release - it will stay at £24.99 or $29.99."

Since we launched into Early Access, we've been extremely proud of the amazing work that has gone into RuneScape: Dragonwilds. So many of you have taken the plunge into Ashenfall, and with every update we are humbled by the number of you trying out Dragonwilds, recommending it to friends and leaving reviews on Steam. The feedback has been incredible, and the game continues to improve with every update, guided and informed by our vision, and your feedback, working together in harmony.

RuneScape: Dragonwilds is not stopping at our 1.0 release, and we will continue to deliver monthly updates to you as the game grows.

The game, containing the entirety of Kuldra's Saga and the Free Updates around it, is staying the same price once 1.0 releases. £24.99, or $29.99.

Dragonwilds' success is because of the invaluable participation of our Early Access players, but also thanks to the support and excitement shared by the countless number of fans waiting for Kuldra's Saga to be complete before you took the plunge with us. We hope this small gesture goes some way to showing our endless appreciation for your support and belief.
