We'll also be launching our next Update in the coming Winter - one we're naming Luminance. This, much like the minor updates, is free, too. We'll share more about our 2027 plans once we've delivered our 1.0 release, and you can tune into our Summit at RuneFest to hear more about 2027 and the next Saga in Ashenfall's story.

updates.title: Eye on Ashenfall - 0.11.2
updates.html:
Runecrafting fixes, a free Community Cape, Hide Helmet and Durability Rebalancing!

Our monthly update is arriving Tuesday 19th May, and we're happy with the Runecrafting feedback we received, so it's coming into this update. We'll get into that. We've also got a big chunk of fixes, and of course, more quest content heading your way.

Incoming Content

  • We've added a new quest: "A Melody Remembered".
    • A mysterious jewellery box lays on an abandoned desk in the Stormtouched Highlands. There's a riddle printed on the lid, and a strange recess in it.
    • Completion of this quest will reward you with a new piece of equipment.
  • There's a new activity for you - keep your eyes peeled for Statues of Saradomin can be found dotted around the world.
    • Track down the clues and earn a reward that shows your loyalty and faith.

Runecrafting Changes

We dove into this initially in the Runecrafting Changes Proposal, but here's what we've parsed through the discussion and what we've settled on.

More Runes, More Often

We're lowering the base Rune conversion ratio from 1:10 → 1:5.

1:10 Conversions will still be available by completing High Attunement difficulty when performing the minigame.

Anima vents will now produce 1:10 output ratios.

Concentrated Anima Vents will offer even bigger bonuses.

  • 100 Runes per standard anima vent, up from 40.
  • 300 Runes from a concentrated vent, up from 80.

When you just want runes now and are not fussed about getting maximum XP gains, Auto Crafting will now give the 5:1 ratio of runes, at 25% of the base XP earned. This auto-crafting will yield 10:1 ratio if you have the relevant skill perk (e.g. level 23 for Air Runes).

We've set the respawn time of Rune Essence and their resource yield to scale with over 4 players in a world. 20% more resources with 5 players, and a slightly reduced respawn time with 6 players.

Teleport Costs

We've brought down teleport costs by half on average. This, combined with the propotionally higher access to Law Runes in the early game makes moving from the same spot everyone builds a house in in Bramblemead Valley to somewhere a bit more ambitious is less punishing to lodestone around from! We also looked at how much carry weight affects the calculation. For example, if you've got 388 carry weight and you want to travel from the very tippy-top northern-most point in Fellhollow, all the way back to the lodestone in the Saradomin Temple, this will now cost 58 Law Runes. Even being several times over the carry limit will now not cost you 1000 Law Runes, you'll be able to shift your stuff with limited cost.

Attunement

Attunement should now be visually clearer, with a numerical indicator showing the exact number of runes you'll receive - and the number will tick down to show when you need to fix cracks in the runes!

Attunement rewards are 33/66/100% bonus runes depending on the difficulty.

Bonus Rune loss when cracks appear is now consistent across difficulties, so fixing those runes is still a priority, but not devastating if unchecked for a second.

Attunements should take 25% less time than before. Same output, just faster.

Skill Tree Perks

Skill tree perks now increase the yield of autocrafting runes to match the attunement yields.

Features

  • We've added the winning design from our Community Cape Contest - congratulations to SuizzyOwl for the amazing design! Please check out the full list of entries here.
    • The cape will be available at the Crafting Table for all players! Pick up some Ash Logs to unlock the crafting bench and the cape will be available.
  • We have now added a toggle setting to "Hide Helmet" for players in the in-game settings menu. This will hide the visual aspect of the Headwear, but you will still be able to benefit from its effects.
  • Spades and Nets have had their durability values reconfigured. The time it takes to break tools is now much more in line with expectations. No sudden durability drops!
  • Fishing activities now trigger music as intended. Lovely.

Fixes

  • You can now skip the Jagex logo cutscene upon startup.
    • We'll judge you though, that dragon looks so cool.
  • Players who unlocked the Farmers Hat prior to a hotfix we deployed can now retroactively gain the recipe by speaking to the Scarecrow.
  • Resolved an issue where only one node was damaged by a tool despite damage floaties showing multiple hits.
  • Fixed a bug where the Compost Bin would only accept Dwellberries that had already been dried. Juicy.
  • The entrance to Dowdun had two torches positioned right on top of each other - thanks to community member arkamos.odc for reporting this!
  • Fixed an issue where in-game chat would require "Enter" to be input twice to open the chat after the first use.
  • Resolved an issue where Cows, Chickens and Kebbits would still not aggro onto a player once they had been attacked.
  • Fixed an issue with "Cook's Assistant" where exiting dialogue with the Cow after feeding it wheat would consume the wheat without progressing the quest.
  • The "Advert-Inna-Bottle" now correctly specifies that the Arrow Grabba collects "Arrows and Bolts" to accurately define that it works with both.
  • Fixed an issue where Trees would not respawn when too close to player constructions due to the larger blocking radius.
  • Fixed an issue where the "Return to the Dreaming Stone" and "Defeat the Gatekeeper" quest objectives lacked an objective marker.
  • Fixed an issue where Ghost Mode incorrectly depicted the Stone Range as built, rather than in it's ghostly, unfinished form. Oooh, spooky.
  • Fixed an issue where Fishing Potions did not display correct tooltips.
  • We've updated the Sugar Rush perk's icon and description, you lucky little cooks, you.
  • Patched various holes and collision meshes in Dowdun. Gosh, it's like this place is falling into chaos or something...
  • Resolved an issue where controller menus within the settings screen could sometimes cause a crash.

We hope you're excited about this update - let us know thoughts and discuss more in our official Discord and Reddit. We've got support for French, German and LATAM Communities with dedicated spaces within our Discord, so come and say Hallo or Bonjour while you're at it.

Check out our Socials (Twitter, BSky, Instagram, Facebook, Twitch, YouTube and TikTok), too!

Looking for LATAM socials? We've got Instagram Español, Instagram Brasil, TikTok Español, TikTok Brasil, Facebook Español and Facebook Brasil! Until next time, have fun, be good, and we'll see you in Ashenfall.

updates.title: Eye on Ashenfall - 0.11.1
updates.html:
The One Where They Add Fishing

Hello adventurers! It's been a few weeks since we launched Dowdun Reach, and we're celebrating our 1-year anniversary with you in style!

This one's reel good, so let's catch you up on what you'll be hooked on for the next 99 levels! Cast your eyes over this.

Fishing

Hooray! We're launching Fishing today with a dozen fish types to catch. Have a chat with the Wise Old Man in Brynmoor (awww, it's good to be back - simpler times, eh?) to start your quest and get Fishing! Starting out, it'll be just a net and a dream, like the noobs over on the mainland, but as you progress, you'll climb the levels and start reely getting into it.

Fishing launches with 3 new skill spells for you - Fishing Frenzy, Infernal Rod and Fishnado. No prizes for guessing what that one does.

Fishing Frenzy: A fishing node springs to life with a significantly increased number of fish in the water.

Infernal Rod: Infuse your fishing rod with the power of fiery anima and cook your catches on contact.

Fishnado: Plunge a storm of magic into the water and catapult a hearty helping of fish into the air, and right into your backpack. Might need to wash your pockets out after this one, it'll start to smell.

You'll be able to cook (and burn!) fish to stock up your storage with plenty of fish. In the event that you pocket a Pristine Fish, you'll be able to craft a decorative Fishing Trophy out of it, and proudly mount it on your wall! They don't sing though. Do we say "Sorry" or "You're welcome"?

And, of course - reaching Level 99 in the Skill will allow you to craft the Fishing Skill Cape. Time to get hooking and cooking!

Quests and Activities

We've added a selection of new quests that channel the classic RuneScape feeling that you've been asking for - we heard you!

Added three new quests: Cook's Assistant, Room With Garou and Animal Magnetism.

Cook's Assistant: Slopfinger, the overworked Goblin, is desperate to make an impression. A cake should do the trick. The reward for your work is a recipe for a Victoria Sponge Cake that provides a buff for 5 minutes that reduces your fatigue drain rate!

Animal Magnetism: You're a long way from Draynor Manor - but Manktongue the Goblin has found an advert in a bottle with a recipe for something he calls the "Arrow Grabba". Find the materials he needs, get the parts and you'll be able to craft something you can place on your back which will... accumulate arrows you've fired in a radius around you.

A Room With Garou: The Elder Garou has lost his eyesight with age. Looking to see out the later years of life in a quiet, tranquil place, the Garou is looking for help from a young pup with the know-how to build a home. They can't tell if you're a Garou or not, but they trust you to help them.

We've also added new activities for you to get stuck into:

Scarecrow Scavening: Find a strange Scarecrow pointing out something - follow the clues, piece together the sketches and slowly unravel the mystery. Completing the trail will next you the new Farmer Hat. Dashing!

Buried Treasure: We've got a few more secrets stashed away for you to dig up, including rewards including new torches.

More Updates

Masterwork Weapons

Two Masterwork Weapons are getting updated with NEW Special Attacks with this update - Unleash the unholy fires of the Zamorak's wrath with the Zamorakian Staff, and cleave your enemies asunder with the Titan's Wrath special attack. Ignite your blade and let the rampage begin - kills will extend this ability's duration.

Enemy Aggression

Chickens, Cows and Kebbits will now no longer attack the player unprovoked. Just in time for you to stand around not getting attacked while you patiently fish. You're welcome!

Auto Run

You'll be able to toggle on the feature where you can now automatically sprint to save you a button press!

Auto Magnetise Items

You'll be able to toggle on the feature where nearby items in the world are pulled to you from a short distance to reduce the number of inputs required.

Rune Stacks

Rune Stack caps have been raised to 9,999. We added a nice round 9000 to that limit. Fill 'em up!

Black Metal Drop Rates

We've heard your feedback around Black Metal drop rates. We’ve doubled the drop rates of Zamorak Warrior Packs from Elite Black Knights, and Zamorakian Warrior Packs now guarantee a Black Metal Salvage drop. We’ve also increased the rate at which Black Metal Scraps drop from these.

Assorted Fixes

Resolved an issue where using "Sort" in chests would make some items disappear. Itemo reappearus!

  • Fire magic hitsplats no longer get stuck in the world.
  • Fixed an issue causing the Ring of Life to work incorrectly in Dedicated Servers.
  • Runecrafting decorations no longer give Runecrafting XP. Stop that, those things are fragile you know!
  • Patched various holes in Dowdun Reach.

Known Issues

We've got a few pieces that are on our radar that we're still investigating and/or have fixes lined up for.

  • The Staff of Subjugation may fall through the landscape if dropped in certain conditions.
  • We're targeting a hotfix for this as soon as possible!
  • Ava's Attractor will not collect arrows if you have disabled Auto-Magnetise World Items in the Settings Menu.
  • Ava's Attractor can be placed on Cape Racks, Hooks and Mannequins but currently sits further from the decoration than desired.
  • The tooltip for the Victoria Sponge Cake is not visible, but it reduces the drain rate of Fatigue by 25%.
  • When attempting to use a fishing net of the correct tier for the region, an error message occurs stating "Unable to catch fish, net tier is too low" - this is incorrect, and the net will function as intended. The text string will be getting fixed with our next minor update. Feel free to ignore it!

Bug Fixes

  • The Lesser Dragons' Spiral Fire attack deals the right amount of damage to the player - which is to say, tons.
  • Controller prompts and Focus now switch correctly when a Controller is plugged in while in a Crafting menu.
  • Fixed an issue affecting a Lorebook in Brynmoor being impossible to interact with.
  • Fixed an issue where the progress wheel in the UI for the Processing Stations would not function correctly.
  • Fixed a bug where a buried chest could be interacted with through the ground.
  • Tuned down Anima Vent volume in Dowdun Reach.
  • Fixed an issue where dying in the elevator near the Demon Gate of Dowdun Reach would cause Gravestones to respawn in mid-air.
  • Resolved an issue where casting the Eye of Oculus skill spell in the Saradomin Temple would push the camera under the map.

updates.title: 0.11 is live now! Enter Dowdun Reach...
updates.html:
Dowdun Reach is now available in the game! Head through Fellhollow to face down the Madness of Zamorak...

Dowdun Reach

Dowdun Reach is now available in the game! Head through Fellhollow to face down the Madness of Zamorak...

Added four new quests: Black Knight's Fortress, Wanted!, Biohazard and What's Theirs Is Mine.

Added new building pieces and decorations, including thatched roofing, chandeliers and stained glass windows.

Skilling

Runecrafting has been reworked to support a new skilling activity - using the Rune Altar will give players the option to "Attune" runes or "Autocraft".

Attuning runes will grant bonus runes and XP, so get involved!

Anima vents have started to emerge across Ashenfall for players to interact with.

Raised the skill cap of all existing skills to 99. This does not include higher tier content which will be expanded upon in future updates, but you can already climb through the levels and claim your capes if you want to show off your commitment to the grind.

Miscellaneous

Dedicated Servers are now available. We've reworked the front-end user flow to get you in-game with up to 5 friends smoothly!

We've refactored the Quest UI.

New characters will be able to select a range of new hairstyles upon creation - character editing is coming in with the next major update (0.12.0)

Various bugfixes and stability changes.

Controller

We're continuing to refine our controller settings and keybinds as we progress through Early Access, and today we're updating a range of inputs and keybind for inventory management:

Tap LT: Drop Item / Transfer Item Hold RT: Destroy Item Hold Face Button: Split Stack Tap LB/RB: Toggle Inventory Tab Tap L3: Sort the focused inventory tab. (Chest/Storage Inventory) Tap Y: Fill Chest Stacks (Chest/Storage Inventory) Hold Y: Take all items from Chest.

Bug Fixes

Gameplay

Community Reported Fixes
  • Sealed Wooden Crate and Stacked Wooden Crate recipes were not unlockable in Standard Mode.
  • Resolved an issue where Pumpkin foods would have their Lifeward Restoration interrupted by sleeping.
  • Fixed a blocker that prevented players initiating the "Dragon Slayer" Quest if they started "Growing Pains" but have not yet completed it.
  • Fixed an issue that caused the Oak/T2 Stair Variants or Oak/T2 Small Wall to unlock at Level 18 Construction.
  • Fixed an issue where teleporting across the map via lodestone would cause Mount Animations and VFX would break.
  • Resolved an issue where Custom Worlds with 2x Damage would cause Axetral Projection to destroy the stumps as well as the trees.
  • Fixed an issue where users could not place decorations on top of tables without the table being placed on a Foundation.
General Fixes
  • Fixed an issue where opening the Spellbook with Q caused some users to experience performance dips as the spellbook opened.
  • Fixed an issue where characters walking up stairs would "tremor" or move unnaturally.
  • Resolved an issue where Vault Guardians would target traps if they took damage from them, and would not refocus aggro onto players. No infighting!
  • Fixed an issue where Personal Chests can't be linked or set to private in certain circumstances.

Environment

Community Reported Fixes
  • Fixed an issue where players could fall through a small gap at the border of Silverthorn Keep's outer walls.
  • Resolved an issue where Chests in the Swamp and Waterfall caves were invisible to clients in a multiplayer world.
  • Fixed a spot that obstructed access to an Iron Ore Node north of Coalridge Pass in Fellhollow.

Audio

Community Reported Fixes
  • Fixed an issue where Mounts would double up SFX when dismounted.
  • Fixed an issue with Windstep where game audio could slowdown.

updates.title: 0.11.0.3 is live! - XP Curve Rebalance and Level 99 Cap Raised
updates.html:
We've applied a hotfix to rebalance xp values from levels 92-99. The XP required to reach Level 99 is now over double the original value.

  • If you have not already reached the new upper limit of 99, your skill level will be changed to reflect the new curve.
    • The skillcape perk becomes locked again if you are now below level 99.
    • If you had a skillcape equipped prior to the update and the hotfix goes live, you will still have it equipped:
      • You will NOT be able to unequip it by RIGHT CLICKING.
      • You CAN replace the cape by right clicking another cape to equip it instead.
      • If you try and RE-EQUIP a skill cape after the change, you will not be able to.
  • If you place the cape on an armour mannequin, you will be able to leave the cape on the mannequin even when swapping armours.
    • You can take the cape OFF the mannequin by dragging it to your inventory, but it will not let you equip it until you reach 99 again.

Dedicated Servers WILL require a restart to apply this patch.

We STRONGLY ADVISE that you patch as soon as the update is live.

updates.title: Eye on Ashenfall - 0.10
updates.html:
0.10 is here! Fellhollow, Farming and so much more. Let’s get stuck into this one, shall we?

Fellhollow

The Fellhollow region has been added to the game.

This region is accessible to the north of Ghornfell. Speak to the Wise Old Man after completing “Dragon Slayer” to enter the region and get started.

11 new enemy types have been added, found within the Fellhollow region.

We’re not listing them all here because you’ll get scared.

Added new vaults to the map within the Fellhollow region.

NPCs can be located within the Fellhollow region with new quests for the player to complete.

Added two new NPCs, Death and Postie Pete

Added Death’s Shop, a new in-game store where players can exchange resources with Death himself for rewards.

He’s a busy skeleton, but he’s also not stupid enough to leave souls on the table. What do you think he does with them?

Added new material progression tier – Tier 5.

Includes Steel Armour, Green Dragonhide and Splitbark armour.

Added new Vestige rewards.

Added a new debuff/status effect: Withering.

Players can become Withered and experience Soul Rifting when exposed to too much Wither Rot.

Cleansing pools in the region will allow the player to remove the debuff and cleanse the effect.

Added a new Tier 3 Building Kit – the Castle Kit.

Includes foundations, walls, stairs, floors, doorways, windows, everything a growing base needs!

Added new food to the world spawns.

New foods include Pumpkin, Watermelon, Wheat and Tomatoes in the overworld

Added recipes utilising these new ingredients.

Mounts

Added Mounts to the game.

Surprise! We’ve been keeping this a secret.

Players will be able to summon and ride a mount, in this case a Terrorbird, around the overworld to expedite travel.

Farming

Added the Farming Skill up to level 65.

Added new processing stations: Compost Bin, Water Barrel, Raincatcher Barrel and Oak, Ash and Willow Farming Plots!

Added Plant Cure, craftable by combining Animal Bone with Weeds.

Seeds will now spawn in hostile AI loot pack drop tables.

Added the Composting mechanic when using the Compost Bin station.

All of the following foods can be added to the compost bin to turn into compost:

  • Any farmable produce
  • Any plant or meat
  • Any cooked or burned food
  • Weeds

Added new tools: Shovel, Compost Bucket, Secateurs and Watering Can

Added Wood, Bronze and Steel variants of the Shovel and Watering Can.

Added the ability to plant and grow trees from seed at Level 20 Farming.

Added the Skill Spell “Uproot”

Uproot everything in a radius, collecting all gatherable food produce.

Added the Skill Spell Upgrade: Increasing the radius of Uproot.

Added the Skill Spell “Humidify”

Conjure forth a raincloud that rolls forward, watering all Farming Plots in its path.

Added the Skill Spell Upgrade: Humidify’s rain now also cures any plants it comes into contact with.

Existing Kwuarm sources, including enemy packs, will now be replaced with Kwuarm seeds for farming.

Added buildable decorations including the Scarecrow.

Combat

We've adjusted several aspects of combat balancing based on player feedback - most notably:

  • We were previously combining damage scaling off of projectile AND weapon type meaning that the damage numbers were scaling more rapidly than other combat types. Yes, that means we're nerfing the Crystal Bow. A lot.
    • Crystal Bow Changes:
      • Stamina cost increased from 30 to 65
      • "Force" from initial hit reduced from 600 (holy moly) to 50.
        • This means that there's a much lower "hit react" to this in successive hits, which means you won't be able to stun-lock enemies when you hit them.
      • Initial hit damage reduced by 50%.
  • Burning status effect damage has been rebalanced.
  • "Attack Steering" feature has been implemented.
    • There's a grace period once you start an attack to adjust your melee and ranged attack rotations to make Melee Combat and Bow Quickshots feel more fluid and responsive. It'll feel great, even if you don't notice it right away!

Bug Fixes

Multiple fixes for rare crashes

Spells placed in the spellbook can now be removed.

Begone, seventh slot of Axetral Projection!

Radial Progress Bar will now correctly display progress when processing Dirty Water.

Proggers in the chat.

Fixes to accessing (or not accessing!) content in Creative Mode.

Reduced likelihood of Gravestones spawning in unrecoverable locations.

Don’t push your luck though, Death is here and he’s clearly not in the mood to do you any more favours.

Stamina will now regenerate during conversations.

We know Vannaka might leave some of you breathless but not like that.

The “Special Attack” for the Crystal Bow now responds to the players’ aim more accurately.

Fixes to triggers for gameplay effects in a few vaults.

The signal down there must be dreadful, in all fairness.

Fixes for music starting or stopping incorrectly in a range of locations.

Improvements to the character creation and Steam invite flow.

Fixes to the building stability system.

Fixes to General Velgar’s weaknesses and resistances.

Poison and Burning status messages no longer replicate incorrectly.

The fire might be a hint, no need for us to repeat ourselves.

This is our first Major Update for RuneScape: Dragonwilds, and we are especially proud of the work that has gone into making this the update that it is. We're very excited for you to get into game and try this for yourselves. We'll be talking to you throughout the release week, and we have lots more to show you, but on behalf of the entire RuneScape: Dragonwilds team:

Thank you for making this year, and our game, so special. Merry Wintumber, and a happy new year - if you survive…

npcs.name: Abraxus The Eternal
npcs.lead: Abraxus The Eternal is an undead NPC that is featured in the What Remains is Written secondary quest. To start the quest, you must have the full necromancer robes and a ghostspeak amulet from the crumbling well in Bramblemead Village.

npcs.name: Advert-Inna-Bottle
npcs.lead: An Advert-Inna-Bottle is both an NPC and an item, once the player interacts with the NPC first. Both the NPC and the item are related to the quest, Animal Magnetism, where reading it reveals that it is a message from Ava with the ingredients on how to craft Ava's accumulator.

npcs.name: Aidan
npcs.lead: Aidan was a fire-touched Amalgamated Wild Knight who died by sacrificing himself to save his brothers whilst hunting a beast in a poisonous fog. Shortly after his death, his brothers-in-arms bore his name in honour of his sacrifice.

npcs.name: Ansel
npcs.lead: Ansel was a Wild Knight and solitary wanderer who travelled across Ashenfall, journeying to its highest peaks and deepest crevices. He made use of the Summon Shelter spell to find comfort in the most remote and inhospitable regions. He died after resting in the Bloodblight Swamp , where the spell offered no protection against the poison.

npcs.name: Archmage Alric
npcs.lead: Archmage Alric was the leader of the Zamorakian magi at Dowdun Reach and a senior figure within the Children of Shadows. He served as Archmage to Lord Rasmodel until losing authority over the keep's dreaming stone in the wake of a closed-door confrontation. His covert efforts to circumvent that loss eventually allowed demons to bleed directly into the walls of the fortress.

npcs.name: Armadyl
npcs.lead: Armadyl is the god of justice. He is an ascended from the world of , and is known for having slain his rival, Bandos, in the Sixth Age. He believes in an idealistic universe where gods and mortals live in harmony, with gods acting as benevolent guides rather than as rulers; however, since the God Wars, he has shown willingness to kill warmongering gods and/or their followers only if necessary.

npcs.name: Ashien
npcs.lead: Ashien was a legendary Garou druid and one of the first to wield a blightwood staff. According to the legend, she was given a quest by the goddess, Lougrim, to defeat a demon located in the swamps.

npcs.name: Auburn Ocelot
npcs.lead: The Auburn Ocelot was the leader of a faction of bandits that would hurl expensive arrows that were not known to Brynmoor to rob the nearby villagers for their coins. However, the coins were far less valuable than the arrows, but the bandits intended to cause a confused terror on the villagers' faces. The Auburn Ocelot later died from a small rat carrying a virulent plague. He was cremated and buried in a remote location to avoid infecting anyone.

npcs.name: Avisk
npcs.lead: Avisk was an Dragonkin with the elemental power of air who lived on Ashenfall and was part of a group of Dragonkin who broke away from their main kin in defiance of their traditions. Among this group were Lacrussa, Rasthin, Viika, and Brakka, with Avisk serving as a calming presence during their early settlement of Ashenfall.

npcs.name: Bandos
npcs.lead: Bandos was the God of War, often called the "Big High War God" by his followers, which primarily consisted of less-intelligent races. Once a mortal member of an unnamed extinct species that valued fighting to the death, he ascended after killing the former god of his own world. During the , Bandos joined a temporary alliance with Saradomin and Armadyl to combat Zamorak. After Guthix's death, Bandos returned to Gielinor to restart the war, but was met by Armadyl. Now embracing peace, Armadyl built a to stop Bandos' warmongering. In a final confrontation, Armadyl killed the god of war and ended a deity who once suffered so greatly from war himself.

npcs.name: Beartach - The Merchant
npcs.lead: Beartach - The Merchant is a Moon Garou found in the Umbral Sands, in the Manafem clan camp within the Manafem Plains. To access his shop, players must have completed the Rogue Trader reputation quest. Full access to his shop requires the completion of the Song of the Ancients, Scaling Difficulties, and Beast in the Sand reputation quests.

npcs.name: Bilegut
npcs.lead: Bilegut is an imprisoned goblin who can be found caged next the Outlook Ruins north-east of Zanik in the Bramblemead Valley.

npcs.name: Brakka
npcs.lead: Brakka was a dragonkin scientist and architect who migrated to Ashenfall with other members of his kin. Known for his architectural genius and scientific advancements, he was responsible for creating many of the dragons that would later populate the continent, including the fearsome General Velgar.

npcs.name: Brassica Prime
npcs.lead: Brassica Prime is the god of cabbages. In his early years, he gifted all of Ashenfall with cabbages and eventually taught them how to fry them as well. However, many villagers in Ashenfall are not sure why there was a god of cabbages, and his whereabouts are unknown. Legends tells of his origin being within Ashenfall, being discovered by Guthix while exploring the region. Other legends teaches how he shaped creation itself by mixing together the base of vitamins.

npcs.name: Caratacus
npcs.lead: Caratacus the Elder is an old Garou located in the north-western part of the Fractured Plains, outside of the Stormtouched Highlands. Speaking with them starts the secondary quest A Room With A Garou.

npcs.name: Cathan
npcs.location:
* Front entrance of Velgar's Rise
* Front of the three standing stones (Post Dragon Slayer)
* Front of the entrance to Dowdun Reach
npcs.lead: Cathan was a rookie adventurer who travelled to Ashenfall with Zanik, Vannaka, Doric and the Wise Old Man, and survived the initial expedition to the continent. Before his journey to Ashenfall, he was trained by Vannaka after losing a leg in a childhood misadventure.

npcs.name: Commander Zilyana
npcs.lead: Commander Zilyana is a character who appears alongside the Scorned Wilderness.

npcs.name: Count Valingard
npcs.lead: Count Valingard is a member of the Brynmoor's nobility during the Third Age. During the Third Age, Saradominist missionaries arrived on Ashenfall, seeking refuge and converts to recruit. This may imply that Count Valingard may be a member of the Saradominists.

npcs.name: Cow (Cook's Assistant)
npcs.lead: The cow in the Cook's Assistant quest is an NPC that allows the player to collect a bucket of milk, as long as the player selects the "Feed it some wheat" option.

npcs.name: Cynthia Valtis
npcs.lead: Cynthia Valtis was a Saradominist wizard who pushed the boundaries of spellcasting, other than common and familiar spells. She prevented the famine in Brynmoor by transforming twigs into carrots, and created a cool breeze with wind and water magic combined. However, she experimented with ill-advised fire magic, sending her travelling across Ashenfall. It is unknown whether she survived the experiment.

npcs.name: Dahnu
npcs.lead: Dahnu was a naturally gifted archer who learned how to use a bow made of a deceased deer's antlers. She was raised by Gahl, a garou druid after the Human-Garou War, where nearby goblins that took over many garou settlements tortured her while in her infant years. After Gahl slaughtered the torturous goblins, he raised her like his own. However, Dahnu was unable to learn the druid spells at first, so Gahl picked up deer antlers and created a bow that would later become Dahnu's primary weapon. Over a few years, Dahnu defeated the prior monarch with reason and wit, making Gahl and her people proud. During the Dragon Rebellion, Velgar slaughtered all of the garou nearby, eventually taking her life in the process.

npcs.name: Death (Grim Reaper)
npcs.lead: Harold Death Esquire, better known as Death or the Grim Reaper, is a legendary who is responsible for harvesting the souls of the dead in Gielinor. Death is located in the Forgotten Temple for the adventurer(s) to assist them in dealing with the undead in Fellhollow and Imaru. Death offers a reward for assisting him. He'll lead the players to speak with Postie Pete before entering Fellhollow.

npcs.name: Derien
npcs.lead: Derien was a Wind-touched Amalgamated Human. Derien entered an archery contest, using his amalgam powers to win, guiding his arrows through the air. Shortly thereafter, the tournament was cancelled his victory further added to the tension between the "Pure" humans and the Amalgamated .

npcs.name: Doctor Fenkenstrain
npcs.lead: Doctor Fenkenstrain is a character who is featured in The Great Body Robbery secondary quest. They are a long-lost relative of , who asks the Player to assist them in making a body for him. While he does not share what happened to him and the situation he is in, he hints that a certain chicken is responsible for it. In an ironic twist of fate, he now has the body of a chicken after the quest.

npcs.name: Domri - The Merchant
npcs.lead: Domri - The Merchant is a Moon Garou found in the Umbral Sands, in the Alcarrid camp within the Alcarrid Oasis.

npcs.name: Doric
npcs.location:
* Temple Woods
* Fractured Plains
* East of Lake of Lost Souls
* The Nexus
npcs.lead: Doric is a who travelled to Ashenfall with Zanik, the Wise Old Man, Vannaka and Cathan. He is first introduced in the game as the survival tutor for crafting and teaches the player about their rest, hydration, and sustenance systems. After the tutorial, he can be found in the Fractured Plains, Fellhollow and Dowdun Reach.

npcs.name: Edna
npcs.lead: Edna is an NPC that requires the player to bring her one silver bar, one fine thread, one sacred oil, and six soul fragments.

npcs.name: Elidinis
npcs.lead: Elidinis is the Menaphite goddess of Fertility and Growth, and is heavily associated with the and the moon. She is the mother of Icthlarin and . She is mentioned in Icthlarin's Little Helper, called the River Goddess, River Mother and Goddess of the River. According to Lehran - The Archaeologist, Elidinis is said to be a garou, but older scrolls said she appeared human.

npcs.name: Eric
npcs.lead: Eric was briefly mentioned in the torn journal page lore scrap. In the lore scrap, the author (whose name is unknown), Eva, Eric, and the driver transporting the group, were all escaping from presumably the garou since they were travelling near the Fractured Plains at night. The author caught a glimpse of yellow eyes in the distance after Eva instinctively cast flames into the woods. Eric was dragged into the tree line, yelling for help before his cries were suddenly stopped.

npcs.name: Eva
npcs.lead: Eva was a wizard who was briefly mentioned in the torn journal page lore scrap. In the lore scrap, the author (whose name is unknown), the driver of the unknown vehicle, Eva, and Eric were escaping from presumably the garou since they were travelling near the Fractured Plains at night. The author caught a glimpse of yellow eyes in the distance after Eva instinctively cast flames into the woods. From the light of the fire Eva cast from her staff, they saw them as "wolves that walk on two legs". Unfortunately, the presumed garou caught Eva after killing the driver first, killing her on the spot. However, they left the author to run for their life.

npcs.name: Finn
npcs.location: South-east of the Wise Old Man at Bramblemead Valley
npcs.lead: Finn is a deceased adventurer who comes back as a ghost during the night. He was one of the earliest adventurers who attempted to escape Velgar by hiding in a cave. This proved to be a mistake as the dragon knew of his location and cornered him, killing him. He moves on when his name is remembered at the Temple Woods' church shrine. His ghost can be found inside a cave to the south-east of the Wise Old Man after starting Restless Ghosts. The player will need an axe and a Woodcutting level of 20 to clear the vines blocking the entrance of the cave, as well as the ability to cast Windstep or to build a path up to the cave.

npcs.name: Frode
npcs.lead: Frode was a fire-touched Amalgamated Wild Knight archer that is known for wielding the blightwood longbow. He is known to be very skilled with the bow, so that he never returned empty-handed. His siblings would always send him to hunt in the woods before every great gathering, and he would always come back with a feast.

npcs.name: Gahl
npcs.lead: Gahl was a garou druid who survived during the Human-Garou War, where many of the garou were killed. Nearby garou villages were turned into ruins and were occupied by goblins, as Gahl would see. However, he saw nearby goblins torturing a newborn garou in her ruinous crib. Gahl slaughtered the goblins and took the newborn with him, raising her with his love. He named the newborn, Dahnu, and realized she was not magically skilled and could not learn his druid spells. However, Gahl created a bow using antlers from a deer and taught her how to hunt with a bow. Dahnu was naturally gifted whilst using the bow and would defeat the prior monarch later on, making her people thrive and her father proud.

npcs.name: Glass Knife
npcs.lead: Glass Knife is an alias for a serial killer who was active in Bramblemead Village during the early days of the Schism during the Third Age. As a blacksmith by trade and the wife of a village elder, she used her social position to avoid proper justice for her crimes.

npcs.name: Gothren Actillian
npcs.lead: Gothren Actillian was a blacksmith known for his obsession with blurite and his pioneering work with blurite weaponry.

npcs.name: Guthix
npcs.lead: Guthix was the god of balance and one of the first beings to arrive on Gielinor. He was a Naragi, a race of intelligent humanoid people, and the only member of the race to survive the God War of his home. This event caused him to detest divine beings, believing that worlds could only survive without divine influence.

npcs.name: Hedric - The Hunter
npcs.lead: Hedric - The Hunter is a Moon Garou located in Umbral Sands, within the Manafem Plains' camp. He is one of the few NPCs needed to interact with for the Icthlarin's Little Helper quest.

npcs.name: Henrietta
npcs.lead: Henrietta is a witch who was known for using her powers to combine a toadflax herb with the amphibian of its namesake. The result was a monster that killed five people before being put down. Henrietta's whereabouts are unknown.

npcs.name: Hokistix
npcs.lead: Hokistix is a druid who was known for bringing the wild jade vines to Ashenfall. After bringing the wild jade vine to Ashenfall, Hokistix was forced to live near the edge of the city. The wild jade vine's lore scrap infers that Hokistix was eaten by one of the wild jade vines, explaining his disappearance.

npcs.name: Iasadair - The Merchant
npcs.lead: Iasadair - The Merchant is a Moon Garou found in the Umbral Sands, in the Uzzer clan camp within the Dunes of Uzzer. To access his shop, players must have completed the Rogue Trader reputation quest. Full access requires completion of the Uzzer clan reputation quests.

npcs.name: Icthlarin
npcs.lead: Icthlarin is the Menaphite god of the dead, son of and Elidinis, and one of the four major gods of the . He is first mentioned by Death on several occasions during Withering Heights, and later appears within Umbral Sands, within the clan Alcarrid in Alcarrid Oasis. He requests that the Adventurer(s) help gain each of the garou tribes' trust so that he could repair his mother's mirror, so that the lair of Fuzan could be accessed.

npcs.name: Imaru
npcs.lead: Imaru the Soul-Eater is an undead blue dragon infused with the wild anima of Ashenfall and the energy of the by drinking from the . She was one of Kuldra's generals, who rules over Fellhollow, a boss monster who was introduced with the 0.10 update.

npcs.name: Kay
npcs.lead: Kay is a deceased adventurer who comes back as a ghost during the night. They were one of the earliest adventurers who were killed by Velgar during their trip through Ashenfall. They move on when their name is remembered at the Temple Woods' church shrine. Their ghost can be found in the Whispering Swamp south-east of the abyssal demon spawn area in the quest Restless Ghosts.

npcs.name: Kessel
npcs.lead: Kessel was a fire-touched Amalgamated Wild Knight. Kessel was known to favour a bronze greatsword over the bows and daggers of her peers. Famously, Kessel would set her greatsword alight during battle, hefting the flaming blade with surprising efficiency for its size.

npcs.name: Kethren
npcs.lead: Kethren was a wizard in Brynmoor, tasked with shadowing the nearby miners to see if he could help with their tedious tasks of mining ores. Kethren thought of a way of speeding up the process using magic and created a spell that had chaotic instability, turning an ore cluster into smaller pieces. His whereabouts are unknown.

npcs.name: King Raluh
npcs.lead: King Raluh was a mighty warrior who received the Skullsplitter from Lougrim, the moon goddess. With the Skullsplitter, this weapon was capable of destroying any foe that stood in King Raluh's way. It is also unknown if the weapon was just a fable, but many young garou would create weapons to match the strength of the supposed weapon. King Raluh's whereabouts are unknown.

npcs.name: King Rolthar
npcs.lead: King Rolthar was presumably a garou king who was not only mighty but also loved by his villagers. He sought after foes that seemed greater than him to seek the praise of his villagers. Rolthar was successful in doing so, and he chose to face Velgar, the strongest in the realm at the time. To prepare for this fight, he crafted a challenge horn and also an iron greatsword (presumably), which was meant to shatter armoured scales. However, Velgar's scales were too solid and he overpowered Rolthar, killing him as he held onto his greatsword. Velgar showed his respect by carrying Rolthar's lifeless body back to the villagers and said, "This warrior is the pride of your people, give him a burial worthy of his strength".

npcs.name: Kuldra
npcs.lead: Queen Kuldra, also known as the Dragon Queen and the God Eater, is an ancient black dragon with five heads. She is the leader of the dragons ruling over the continent of Ashenfall, and the current High Queen for some of the garou. She is the boss of the Scorned Wilderness raid, and the final boss for Kuldra's Saga.

npcs.name: Lacrussa
npcs.lead: Lacrussa was a dragonkin scientist and a former assistant of , who resided in Ashenfall and was known for her experiments with dragons and magical technology. Her legacy is particularly tied to the dragonkin vaults and the creation of the colossal wyrms whose bones now litter the Stormtouched Highlands. Lacrussa had the elemental power of ice.

npcs.name: Lagra - The Butcher
npcs.lead: Lagra - the Butcher is a Moon Garou located in the camp within Alcarrid Oasis within Umbral Sands. They are one of the many NPCs needed to interact with for the Icthlarin's Little Helper quest.

npcs.name: Lazina
npcs.location: Bottom of the Windmill at Temple Woods
npcs.lead: Lazina is a deceased adventurer who appears as a ghost during the night. She is an early explorer from Al Kharid who took on the adventure of Ashenfall with her brother for fame and glory. She was a blade for hire and claimed to be a swordmaster supreme. She was vanquished by Velgar the moment she arrived. She moves on when her name is remembered at the Temple Woods' church shrine. Her ghost can be found next to the to the windmill in the Temple Woods during the quest, Restless Ghosts.

npcs.name: Leander
npcs.lead: Leander was Bramblemead Village's head chef, who was known for making big cauldrons of hearty stew. The aroma and taste of the stew would make all the villagers feel at home, or would make villagers feel like they're at a campfire with friends.

npcs.name: Lehran - The Archaeologist
npcs.lead: Lehran - The Archaeologist is a Moon Garou located within the Dunes of Uzzer camp in Umbral Sands. They are one of the few NPCs to interact with in order to progress Icthlarin's Little Helper.

npcs.name: Lougrim
npcs.lead: Lougrim was the goddess of the moon and primordial hunt to the garou. She came from another world of silver and silence, and left it through a doorway that opened when a grieving god wandered into it. Her transformation into the goddess of the hunt completely altered her original form. She is said to also have a history with Bandos, where the god of war wanted revenge against her and the garou.

npcs.name: Mallory
npcs.lead: Mallory was a wizard whose memory was excellent, but lacked the power of his spells. He climbed through the ranks only by seniority and was never respected by his peers. One day, he focused his power to create the Magical Focus, and refined it further to increase the caster's magic powers. After sharing his newfound spell with his peers, Mallory's mentor killed him and claimed his knowledge. However, the mentor was later found to be swallowed and digested by a dragon.

npcs.name: Manktongue
npcs.location: Building in the southwestern corner of the Fractured Plains
npcs.lead: Manktongue is a Goblin who starts the quest Animal Magnetism, and is involved in Cook's Assistant. He can be found in the south-western corner of the Fractured Plains.

npcs.name: Mayev
npcs.lead: Mayev was a Moon Garou hunter, recorded as the first in Ashenfall to wear red dragonhide. She made the armour from the remains of Vakar, a red dragon she had raised from a hatchling and considered a friend, following a garou tradition of wearing the hide and bones of a fallen warrior as a mark of honour.

npcs.name: Meya
npcs.lead: Meya was a female Wild Knight mentioned in the memorials found in the quest Heartstrings. Meya fell in love with an unnamed elven bard and eventually died of old age, while the elf lived on due to having much longer life-spans than humans.

npcs.name: Mia Larsdottir
npcs.lead: Mia Larsdottir was the first human on Ashenfall to become Amalgamated. She was murdered with a bronze dagger, and her killer was never brought to justice, although many suspected that she was killed by her father, who was ashamed of her. She was not given a proper funeral; her body was instead left out in the forest.

npcs.name: Mirror
npcs.lead: The mirror is an NPC featuring in the secondary quest, Mirror, Mirror. They were once a person who was trapped by a necromancer as punishment, thus trapped in a mirror until the player arrives to help them free.

npcs.name: Mittens
npcs.lead: Mittens was a cat that supposebly owned blacksmith Gothren Actillian in Bramblemead. He lived in Gothren's forge and played a crucial role in developing blurite weaponry.

npcs.name: Mouldfinger
npcs.lead: Mouldfinger was a goblin smith who forged the chieftain's blade. Although she never wanted to be chief, as she content with being a background character, she ended up creating a simple blade that both sturdy and strong enough that her fellow goblins believed it must have been a special blade. Because of this, she was challenged by her fellow goblins but slew them effortlessly with her blade, causing the goblins to make her chieftain against her wishes.

npcs.name: Muncher
npcs.lead: Muncher is Death's faithful pet skeletal hellhound, who appears right besides him in the Forgotten Temple. He cannot be interacted with.

npcs.name: Nightingale
npcs.lead: Nightingale was a highwaywoman of Bramblemead who robbed caravans and tax collectors during the village's final years and distributed the proceeds among its people. She was killed by the assassin Moragrin, who was hired by the nobility of Brynmoor and who proved to be her elder sister.

npcs.name: Noggin
npcs.lead: Noggin was an outcast who wore a sack over his head because he was always looked at as ugly by the locals of Bramblemead Valley. He fled to the nearby forest, still wearing his sack, when he found a lost villager. Over time, the lost villager and Noggin fell in love and planned to marry each other. However, she wanted Noggin to remove his sack over his head, but his face was nowhere to be found upon removing the sack. Noggin disappeared, leaving behind his clothes on the floor, frightening the lost villager. Noggin's face appears on scarecrows and training dummies across Ashenfall to this day.

npcs.name: OffalFoot
npcs.lead: OffalFoot can be found deep beneath the grove, trying to catch fish with a spear attached to a fishing rod. If you help him, he will bite into the fish and say that there is a shiny rock inside. He will then give it to you. (After update 1.0, you will need a fishing rod for this.)

npcs.name: Old Book
npcs.lead: An old book is an NPC that is found inside a small cave inside Coalridge Pass in Fellhollow. Players will need to enter a cave that's at the bottom of the ridge and cast Rocksplosion at the granite node on top of the coal node once inside the cave. This will expose the old book, which players can find a dust-covered sketchbook needed for the quest, Even More Restless Ghosts.

npcs.name: Olis
npcs.lead: Olis was a fire-touched Amalgamated Wild Knight that invented the dwellberry crunchies. It was said that he was not a very good chef, but that did not stop the Wild Knights from being particularly fond of his invention. He is one of the chefs of the Wild Knights, along with Orik the Bear, better known for his culinary expertise.

npcs.name: Orik the Bear
npcs.lead: Orik the Bear was a fire-touched Amalgamated Wild Knight. Orik was known to cook dishes for the other Wild Knights, such as the dwellberry glazed roast flank. He excelled in making the dwellberry-glazed roast flank, so that other Wild Knights would seek him out at the gatherings, just to taste his culinary expertise. Orik is one of the Wild Knight chefs along with Olis, a practicing chef that created the dwellberry crunchies.

npcs.name: Paint-Spattered Ghost
npcs.location: North East of the Lake of Lost Souls, most western part of Coalridge Pass.
npcs.lead: The paint-spattered ghost a spirit of a deceased human, who got incinerated by a dragon and remains in in a ruined dragonkin structure north east of the Lake of Lost Souls, most western part of Coalridge Pass. They speak about how boring the afterlife is, and how they wish to draw, but their sketchbook is with their husband. Locating the book is required to complete one of the tasks for Even More Restless Ghosts

npcs.name: Parcel Pete
npcs.lead: Parcel Pete, is Postie Pete's brother who also works for . He makes an appearance in the end of Letters for the Dead quest, where it is revealed that Parcel had stolen Pete's letter as a prank.

npcs.name: Postie Pete
npcs.lead: Postie Pete is a skull serving as a postman for the in , carrying a satchel around in his mouth. He is north of the Forgotten Temple, where he gives players information on how to enter Fellhollow through soul rifting. Players may speak with him to start the secondary quest, Letters for the Dead. He also appears in Dowdun Reach selling vestiges.

npcs.name: Pulpknuckle
npcs.location: Building in the southwestern corner of the Fractured Plains
npcs.lead: Pulpknuckle is a Goblin who creates a magnet for the player during the quest Animal Magnetism if provided with an iron bar and 5 law runes.

npcs.name: Putrilius
npcs.lead:
Putrilius is a demon currently inhabiting the body of a rooster at the top of The Grand Hall. Reaching them takes some platforming and a fight with a Black Knight Warrior and a Black Knight Sniper on some rafters. Putrilius cannot be attacked, and their only dialogue is "Bwak?"
After the quest Biohazard, Putrilius offers to exchange 10 Corrupted Essence for 50 infernal fragments.

npcs.name: Ramus Lumen
npcs.lead: Ramus Lumen was a wizard and member of the Wizard's Guild on Ashenfall. A statue dedicated to him can be found at the guild, and serves as the starting point for the Highlighting the Problem quest. The statue contains a magical recording of a mysterious voice, which is most likely the voice of Ramus Lumen, indicating that he had knowledge of how to create a staff of light.

npcs.name: Rasthin
npcs.lead: Rasthin was a female dragonkin who settled in Ashenfall alongside Lacrussa, Brakka, Viika, and Avisk. Rasthin is known for advocating patience among the dragonkin settlers of Ashenfall, her mastery of fire, and her magnificent, ornate robes. She ruled over subjects who regarded her with both devotion and fear.

npcs.name: Ravanna
npcs.lead: Ravanna is a necromancer who arrived on Ashenfall while fleeing from pirates. She formed a partnership with Ulv, a Wild Knight, and together they protected the forests around Bramblemead.

npcs.name: Reminiscing Ghost
npcs.location: In the ruined building north of Hope's Fall.
npcs.lead: The reminiscing ghost is a spirit of a deceased elderly human who remains in the ruin just north of Hope's Fall. They talk about their granddaughter, Edra, and how they wish they had a clay doll to remember her by, recalling the times they would create some for their granddaughter every time they visited, which is required to complete one of the tasks for Even More Restless Ghosts

npcs.name: Sadia Vulketra
npcs.lead: Sadia Vulketra was a member of the Children of Shadows, a Zamorakian order that settled in Fellhollow. She is credited as the first person to forge steel armour in Fellhollow, working alongside an Amalgamated blacksmith named Vesk, one of her many lovers.

npcs.name: Saradomin
npcs.lead: Saradomin, also known as the Lord of Light, is the god of order, and one of the deities of Gielinor. Once a human justiciar on the world of Teregard, he ascended after prolonged exposure an elder artefacts, known as the Locator, also called the Elder Crown. Though he is largely benevolent and wants what he believes is best for humanity, which has prospered greatly across the universe as a result of his influence, his temper has historically led him to commit acts of warmongering and violence that he now regrets. He is traditionally aligned against Zamorak, with followers of each of the gods coming into conflict often.

npcs.name: Shady Ghost
npcs.location: Next the shrine to Armadyl, south west of Emberwood
npcs.lead: The shady ghost is a spirit that can be interacted with during and after the Withering Heights quest. They are one of the three suspects that you must speak to in order to find out if they committed the crime or are innocent. They are innocent, with the actual murderer being the snickering ghost.

npcs.name: Shana
npcs.lead: Shana was a Bramblemead villager who could not become a wizard, since her enchantments always carried an excess amount of energy and had no way of controlling her power. However, she finally succeeded in controlling her powers whilst creating the leggings of lightness. While wearing the leggings of lightness, Shana could not only carry more items around the village, but it kept her warm during the cold and windy periods. Over time, the leggings of lightness insulated so much heat that Shana had to find another way to control the overheating problem. Thus, she presumably used her powers again and accidentally burnt down her house in the process.

npcs.name: Shatterfang
npcs.lead: Shatterfang was a notorious alpha wolf who terrorized Bramblemead during the time when humans inhabited Ashenfall. Known for his cunning and cruelty, he was responsible for one of the most devastating wolf attacks in the settlement's history.

npcs.name: Shaun
npcs.lead: Shaun is a quest NPC located in Fellhollow. They are part of the Letters for the Dead and are the ones who holds the missing letter. Once you speak with them and take the letter, they will disappear, along with the rest of the other sheep.

npcs.name: Simon
npcs.lead: Simon is a quest NPC located in Fellhollow. They are part of the Letters for the Dead, Once you speak with Shaun and take the letter, they will disappear, along with the rest of the other sheep.

npcs.name: Sir Lear
npcs.lead: Sir Lear was a White Knight Paladin that discovered the potential of the iron mace. He used the mace to crush goblin warriors, druids, and thanes. With the iron mace, Sir Lear was a symbol of as he battled on with other Paladins and other White Knights.

npcs.name: Sir Percival Lateef
npcs.lead: Sir Percival Lateef was a of , who arrived to Ashenfall before it was discovered by the world.

npcs.name: Slopfinger
npcs.location: Building in the southwestern corner of the Fractured Plains
npcs.lead: Slopfinger is a Goblin chef who can be spoken to start the Cook's Assistant quest. Despite needing the ingredients to bake a cake, he has you bake it for him.

npcs.name: Snickering Ghost
npcs.location: Next the shrine to Armadyl, south west of Emberwood
npcs.lead: The snickering ghost is a spirit that can be interacted with during and after the Withering Heights quest. They are one of the three suspects that you must speak to in order to find out if they committed the crime or are innocent. He is the murderer; all the clues will point to him.

npcs.name: Snotpit
npcs.lead: Snotpit was a goblin in Dowdun Reach featured in the Black Knight's Fortress quest. Players used talk to him to receive a hint about where the password is and how to retrieve the cookbook from them to trade it to Spittletoe.

npcs.name: Spitfoot
npcs.lead: Spitfoot is a goblin character who plays a role in Cathan's plan to defeat Velgar. Spitfoot is first mentioned in Cathan's journals, where Cathan writes about waiting for Spitfoot to bring him keys while he is a prisoner of the goblins. These keys would grant access to "the blue-flamed door in the swamps", which Cathan believes holds the secret to destroying Velgar.

npcs.name: Spittletoe
npcs.lead: Spittletoe is a goblin located in Dowdun Reach. They are featured in the Black Knight's Fortress quest as one of the NPCs who has a shard of the Dreaming Stone. Players must have Maple Sap in their inventory to talk to Spittletoe.

npcs.name: Steve
npcs.lead: Steve is a quest NPC located in Fellhollow. They are part of the Letters for the Dead, Once you speak with Shaun and take the letter, they will disappear, along with the rest of the other sheep.

npcs.name: Stuart
npcs.lead: Stuart is a quest NPC located in Fellhollow. They are part of the Letters for the Dead, Once you speak with Shaun and take the letter, they will disappear, along with the rest of the other sheep.

npcs.name: Suspicious Ghost
npcs.location: Next the shrine to Armadyl, south west of Emberwood
npcs.lead: The suspicious ghost is a spirit that can be interacted with during and after the Withering Heights quest. They are one of the three suspects that you must speak to in order to find out if they committed the crime or are innocent. They are innocent, with the actual murderer being the snickering ghost.

npcs.name: Suspicious Skeleton
npcs.lead: The suspicious skeleton is an quest NPC in Fellhollow that you interact with during the Letters for the Dead.

npcs.name: The Cairn
npcs.lead: The Cairn was a member of the Bronze Guard who wielded a bronze mace, defending the alliance of both Guthix and Saradomin. He was known as a mountain of a man for using the bronze mace very effectively against anyone who defied the alliance, swinging the mace with a force of justice. At some point, The Cairn was asked by an unknown entity to turn his fury against the priests of Guthix. The Cairn then lowered his weapon, as he was loyal to the alliance.

npcs.name: Ulv
npcs.lead: Ulv was a Wild Knight warrior during the period of garou-human conflicts. He was cast out from his village for his quiet nature and survived by hunting small prey such as rabbits and chickens using daggers fashioned from bone. He would whittle small carvings of animals from fallen branches. He sold excess meat at market to purchase simple tools and clothing.

npcs.name: Valas - The Blacksmith
npcs.lead: Valas - The Blacksmith is a Moon Garou located in Umbral Sands, within the Alcarrid Oasis' camp. He is one of the few NPCs needed to interact with for the Icthlarin's Little Helper quest.

npcs.name: Valerius
npcs.lead: Valerius is a Zamorakian mage part of the Black Knight's Fortress quest.

npcs.name: Vannaka
npcs.location:
* Temple Woods
* Stormtouched Highlands
* Bleakfields Valley
* The Library
npcs.lead: Vannaka is a who travelled to Ashenfall with Zanik, the Wise Old Man, Doric, and Cathan.

npcs.name: Velgar
npcs.lead: General Velgar, also known as the Big High War God by the goblins after witnessing Bandos retreat from Velgar, is one of Queen Kuldra's generals and most feared disciples. His lair, Velgar's Rise, is located in the Fractured Plains.

npcs.name: Vemmeck
npcs.lead: Vemmeck was a fire-touched Amalgamated Wild Knight commander. He led a siege with the goblins against a northern garou stronghold alongside Sir Lear, a White Knight paladin. With the goblins, Wild, and White Knights, they were almost victorious over the garou stronghold. However, a garou druid held all three forces at bay.

npcs.name: Vesk
npcs.lead: Vesk was an Amalgamated blacksmith who worked alongside Sadia Vulketra to forge the first steel armour in Fellhollow; He was one of her many lovers.

npcs.name: Viika
npcs.lead: Viika is a dragonkin seer who came to Ashenfall with their sibling Lacrussa and other dragonkin, including Rasthin and Avisk. As a seer, Viika experiences time differently from other dragonkin, often existing in moments of their life other than the present. This often results in cryptic and sometimes incomprehensible predictions of the future.

npcs.name: Warren
npcs.location: Bramblemead Valley, Ruined building south-east of the Wise Old Man
npcs.lead: Warren is a deceased adventurer who comes back as a ghost during the night. He was one of the earliest adventurers who came to Bramblemead Valley in the hope of rebuilding a farmstead. He was instead murdered by goblins, and in his death resents them. He moves on when his name is remembered at the Temple Woods' church shrine. His ghost can be found in a ruined building just south-east of the Wise Old Man during the quest, Restless Ghosts.

npcs.name: Windswept Ghost
npcs.location: Emberwood village, north-west of the Emberwood standing stone
npcs.lead: The windswept ghost a spirit of a deceased human who remains in Emberwood village. They talk about how they had poured his life in creating a home for himself, only for it to be gone, and requests others to builds them 4 walls and a roof, which is required to complete one of the tasks for Even More Restless Ghosts.

npcs.name: Wise Old Man
npcs.location:
* Temple of Saradomin
* Bramblemead Village
* Velgar's Rise (After defeating Velgar)
* Entrance to Fellhollow (After completing Dragon Slayer)
* The Courtyard (after completing Withering Heights)
npcs.lead: Dionysius, also known as the Wise Old Man, is a legendary sage and mighty adventurer who travelled to Ashenfall with Zanik, Vannaka, Doric, and Cathan. After their ship was wrecked by General Velgar, the adventurers would gather materials and activate an inactive lodestone, where they would contact the mainland for reinforcement. He would greet the newly arrived adventurer to Ashenfall and be their mentor during their progress through the continent.

npcs.name: Wormelbow
npcs.lead: Wormelbow is a caged goblin found in the ruins of the Adventurer's Guild in Bramblemead Valley.

npcs.name: Zamorak
npcs.lead: Zamorak is the god of chaos and one of the deities of Gielinor. Originally a general in Zaros' armies, he ascended after stabbing Zaros with the staff of Armadyl, instigating the . Though he is often viewed as evil by other religions, he thinks of himself as a champion of self-liberation and personal growth via chaos and conflict. During the conflicts in the Third Age, some garou were captured by Zamorakian forces and subjected to vampyric experiments. These experiments created werewolves, leaving Vannaka to search for his ancestors.

npcs.name: Zanik
npcs.location:
* Temple Woods
* Bramblemead Valley
* Bleakfields Valley
* Under The Courtyard
* Umbral Sands
npcs.lead: Zanik is a adventuring goblin from the mainland who travelled to Ashenfall along with Cathan, Vannaka, Doric, and the Wise Old Man. She has a remarkable history as the first of her people to explore the surface world and interact with humans.
